docs.title: The bibliofabric family
docs.text:
Python client libraries for scholarly metadata APIs, built on one core: bibliofabric owns HTTP, authentication, retries, rate limiting, paging, batch retrieval, identifier normalization, and typed resource clients. Each client library adds only what is specific to its API. All ship async clients alongside generated sync twins (<Name>SyncClient) and py.typed. They live in one uv workspace at github.com/utsmok/bibliofabric (packages/<name>); this site documents all of them. Three client libraries are published on PyPI. Eleven more Wave 1 libraries are built in the workspace and wait for their first release; the second table lists them.

Package API PyPI Install bibliofabric (core framework, no API) pypi.org/project/bibliofabric uv add bibliofabric aireloom OpenAIRE Graph API (V4), Scholexplorer pypi.org/project/aireloom uv add aireloom aletheca OpenAlex pypi.org/project/aletheca uv add aletheca stavrophora Crossref REST API pypi.org/project/stavrophora uv add stavrophora

docs.title: Wave 1 libraries
docs.text:
These packages are complete and tested but not yet published on PyPI. Until their first release they install from the workspace only. The Wave 1 roster lists the upstream API of each one, and the deferred list records what each one leaves out.

Package API PyPI rorifer ROR (research organizations and funders) not published zenotheca Zenodo REST API and OAI-PMH not published dataphora DataCite REST API and public GraphQL not published opcitato OpenCitations Index and Meta APIs not published hodoi DOI registration agency lookup, content negotiation, and Handle records not published scholiast Semantic Scholar Graph, Recommendations, and Datasets APIs not published orchis ORCID Public API v3.0 not published europaea Europe PMC REST web services and annotations API not published quiddita Wikidata (action API, REST API, and SPARQL) not published diurnalia DOAJ (open access journals and articles) not published seriatim ISSN Portal not published

docs.text:
Wave 2 adds specialist sources. These libraries are built and not yet published.

Package API PyPI archeion arXiv API not published prodromus bioRxiv and medRxiv API not published

docs.title: Which package do I need?
docs.text:
• You want records from OpenAIRE (research products, projects, organizations, persons, Scholix links): use aireloom.
  • You want records from OpenAlex (works, authors, institutions, funders, sources): use aletheca.
  • You want records from Crossref (works, journals, funders, members): use stavrophora.
  • You want records from ROR: use rorifer.
  • You want records from Zenodo: use zenotheca.
  • You want records from DataCite: use dataphora.
  • You want citation links from OpenCitations: use opcitato.
  • You want to resolve a DOI (registration agency, metadata, or Handle record): use hodoi.
  • You want records from Semantic Scholar: use scholiast.
  • You want records from ORCID: use orchis.
  • You want records from Europe PMC: use europaea.
  • You want records from Wikidata: use quiddita.
  • You want records from DOAJ: use diurnalia.
  • You want records from the ISSN Portal: use seriatim.
  • You want preprints from arXiv: use archeion.
  • You want preprints from bioRxiv or medRxiv: use prodromus.
  • You are building a client for another scholarly API in this style: build on bibliofabric. Start with the Building a client guide (and the client quick start) covering settings, auth, dialects, unwrappers, resource hooks, sync twins, and monorepo registration.
  • You want to see planned API clients and the canonical entity fusion architecture: explore the Roadmap & Architecture section, including the 2025–2026 academic API catalogs, Wave 1 starter specs, and fusion blueprint.

Requires Python 3.12 or newer. See the contributing guide to set up the workspace and run the test and lint gates.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: The bibliofabric monorepo hosts the bibliofabric core and one client library per API (aireloom, aletheca, stavrophora, and more) in a single uv workspace under packages/<name>/. Requires Python 3.12+ and uv.

docs.title: Set up your environment
docs.text:
Run everything from the monorepo root:

git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/bibliofabric.git
cd bibliofabric
uv sync --all-packages --all-groups

This installs every workspace package in editable mode along with the dev (pytest, pytest-asyncio, pytest-httpx, ruff, ty, unasync) and docs (mkdocs, mkdocs-material, mkdocstrings) dependency groups.

docs.title: Async sources and generated _sync/ twins
docs.text:
For every package, async modules under packages/<name>/src/<name>/_async/ and packages/<name>/tests/_async/ are the single source of truth. Never hand-edit generated _sync/ files; regenerate them with scripts/unasync.py:

uv run python scripts/unasync.py                  # regenerate all packages
uv run python scripts/unasync.py --package <name> # regenerate one package

See Writing a client with sync support for the sync-twin rules.

docs.title: Quality gates
docs.text:
Every pull request must pass the same gates CI runs:

uv run python scripts/unasync.py --check
uv run ruff check
uv run ruff format --check
uv run ty check packages/*/src packages/*/tests scripts/unasync.py
uv run pytest
uv run mkdocs build --strict

Useful local helpers:

  • uv run ruff check --fix / uv run ruff format — apply lint fixes and formatting.
  • uv run pytest packages/<name>/tests — run a single package's offline unit suite (pytest-httpx).
  • uv run pytest -m live_api — run live API smoke tests (deselected by default; reads credentials from .env files that are git-ignored).
  • uv run mkdocs serve — preview the documentation site locally.

The dev group pins ty and ruff versions so local checks match CI.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Use uv for all commands (uv run, uv sync); never bare python or pip.
  • Add type hints on all public signatures; ty must pass with zero diagnostics and zero suppression comments (# ty: ignore / # type: ignore).
  • Use stdlib logging with module loggers (no loguru); format debug logs with %s and redact credentials via bibliofabric.utils.sanitize_url and sanitize_headers.
  • Validation failures raise bibliofabric.ValidationError with the offending payload attached.
  • User-facing changes get a Keep a Changelog entry in packages/<name>/CHANGELOG.md.
  • Write small, focused, conventional commits (feat:, fix:, docs:, chore:, ...), short and imperative, with no AI attribution.

docs.title: Wave 1 packages
docs.text:
The eleven Wave 1 packages (rorifer through seriatim) are finished client libraries that wait for their first PyPI release. The Wave 1 roster lists them with their upstream APIs.

In a test, build settings with every credential field explicit, for example OrchisSettings(_env_file=None, access_token=None). The _env_file=None argument stops the .env file from loading, but it does not hide variables that the shell exports, so the suite must pass in both situations.

docs.title: Submit a pull request
docs.text:
1. Branch from main.
  2. Push your branch and open a pull request against utsmok/bibliofabric.
  3. Reference related issues (e.g. Closes #123).

docs.title: AIREloom
docs.text: AIREloom is a Python client (async and generated sync twin) for the OpenAIRE Graph API and the Scholexplorer API. It is built on the shared bibliofabric core, which provides retries, rate limiting, and pagination; AIREloom adds the OpenAIRE query dialect, typed filter models, and response parsing.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv add aireloom

Python 3.12 or later is required.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import asyncio

from aireloom import AireloomClient


async def main() -> None:
    async with AireloomClient() as client:
        page = await client.research_products.search(query="quantum dots", page_size=10)
        for product in page.results:
            print(product.id, product.mainTitle)


asyncio.run(main())

Without credentials the client is anonymous. For the registered-service quota, set AIRELOOM_OPENAIRE_CLIENT_ID and AIRELOOM_OPENAIRE_CLIENT_SECRET (environment variables or a .env file); the client then fetches a bearer token from the OpenAIRE Keycloak endpoint and reuses it until it expires. Setting only one of the two raises ConfigurationError. You can also set AIRELOOM_OPENAIRE_REFRESH_TOKEN (or pass refresh_token=) for OAuth2 refresh-token authentication, or pass an explicit auth_strategy= (auth= is kept as a deprecated alias).

docs.title: Sync usage
docs.text:
AIREloom ships two variants of every client class. The async code is the single source of truth; the sync twins are generated from it with unasync and committed.

Async Sync AireloomClient AireloomSyncClient ResearchProductsResource SyncResearchProductsResource ScholixResource SyncScholixResource

Use the async client inside asyncio applications. Use the sync client in scripts and notebooks, or from code that runs inside a running event loop: it uses httpx.Client, time.sleep, and threads, and never starts or touches an event loop.

from aireloom import AireloomSyncClient

with AireloomSyncClient() as client:
    page = client.research_products.search(query="quantum dots", page_size=10)
    for product in page.results:
        print(product.id, product.mainTitle)

Both variants take the same parameters, raise the same errors, retry and page the same way, and enforce the same rate limits. Every resource attribute of AireloomSyncClient (research_products, projects, organizations, data_sources, persons, scholix) exposes the matching Sync* resource class.

docs.title: The client
docs.text:
Attribute Resource Host client.research_products V4 research products plus link helpers Graph client.projects V4 projects Graph client.organizations V4 organizations Graph client.data_sources V4 data sources Graph client.persons V4 persons Graph client.research_products.search_links V3 relations between products Graph client.scholix Scholexplorer Links (V3, V2 for linkProvider) Scholexplorer

Every entity resource supports search, iterate, collect, first, count, facets, and group_by. get(id) reads the V3 by-id route because V4 has none. See the usage pages for each resource family.

docs.title: aireloom.AireloomClient
docs.text:
Bases: BaseApiClient

Client for the OpenAIRE Graph API (V4) and the Scholexplorer API.

Entity resources are available as typed attributes; single-entity lookups go through the V3 by-id routes because V4 has none. Authentication resolves in the constructor: set openaire_refresh_token / refresh_token for OAuth2 refresh-token access, or set both openaire_client_id and openaire_client_secret (settings, AIRELOOM_OPENAIRE_CLIENT_ID / AIRELOOM_OPENAIRE_CLIENT_SECRET, or client_id / client_secret) for OAuth2 client-credentials access against the Keycloak token endpoint; partial client credentials raise :class:ConfigurationError, and without credentials the client is anonymous. An explicit auth_strategy always wins.

The Scholix resource talks to the Scholexplorer host through a second internal client that shares settings and credentials but throttles itself to one request per second. See the package README and docs for usage examples of both the async and the sync variants.

Source code in packages/aireloom/src/aireloom/_async/client.py 
class AireloomClient(BaseApiClient):
    """Client for the OpenAIRE Graph API (V4) and the Scholexplorer API.

    Entity resources are available as typed attributes; single-entity lookups
    go through the V3 by-id routes because V4 has none. Authentication
    resolves in the constructor: set ``openaire_refresh_token`` /
    ``refresh_token`` for OAuth2 refresh-token access, or set both
    ``openaire_client_id`` and ``openaire_client_secret`` (settings,
    ``AIRELOOM_OPENAIRE_CLIENT_ID`` / ``AIRELOOM_OPENAIRE_CLIENT_SECRET``, or
    ``client_id`` / ``client_secret``) for OAuth2 client-credentials access
    against the Keycloak token endpoint; partial client credentials raise
    :class:`ConfigurationError`, and without credentials the client is
    anonymous. An explicit ``auth_strategy`` always wins.

    The Scholix resource talks to the Scholexplorer host through a second
    internal client that shares settings and credentials but throttles itself
    to one request per second. See the package README and docs for usage
    examples of both the async and the sync variants.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        settings: AireloomSettings | None = None,
        auth: AuthStrategy | None = None,
        *,
        auth_strategy: AuthStrategy | None = None,
        base_url: str | None = None,
        scholix_base_url: str | None = None,
        mailto: str | None = None,
        client_id: str | None = None,
        client_secret: str | None = None,
        refresh_token: str | None = None,
        http_client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Build the client from settings, resolving credentials immediately.

        ``settings`` defaults to :func:`aireloom.config.get_settings`, which
        reads ``AIRELOOM_*`` environment variables and ``.env``. Keyword
        overrides (``base_url``, ``scholix_base_url``, ``mailto``,
        ``client_id``, ``client_secret``, ``refresh_token``) take precedence
        over ``settings``. Pass ``auth_strategy`` for a custom auth strategy
        (``auth`` is a deprecated alias).
        """
        if auth is not None and auth_strategy is not None:
            raise ConfigurationError(
                "Pass either 'auth_strategy' or the deprecated 'auth' parameter, "
                "not both."
            )
        if auth is not None:
            warnings.warn(
                "The 'auth' parameter is deprecated; use 'auth_strategy' instead.",
                DeprecationWarning,
                stacklevel=2,
            )
            explicit_auth: AuthStrategy | None = auth
        else:
            explicit_auth = auth_strategy

        resolved = settings or get_settings()
        overrides: dict[str, str] = {}
        if base_url is not None:
            overrides["base_url"] = base_url
        if scholix_base_url is not None:
            overrides["scholix_base_url"] = scholix_base_url
        if mailto is not None:
            overrides["mailto"] = mailto
        if client_id is not None:
            overrides["openaire_client_id"] = client_id
        if client_secret is not None:
            overrides["openaire_client_secret"] = client_secret
        if refresh_token is not None:
            overrides["openaire_refresh_token"] = refresh_token
        if overrides:
            resolved = resolved.model_copy(update=overrides)
        strategy = (
            explicit_auth if explicit_auth is not None else _resolve_auth(resolved)
        )
        super().__init__(
            base_url=resolved.base_url,
            settings=resolved,
            unwrapper=OpenAireUnwrapper(),
            auth=strategy,
            http_client=http_client,
        )
        self._scholix_api = BaseApiClient(
            base_url=resolved.scholix_base_url,
            settings=resolved.model_copy(
                update={
                    "max_requests_per_second": resolved.scholix_max_requests_per_second
                }
            ),
            unwrapper=ScholixUnwrapper(),
            auth=strategy,
        )
        auth_label = (
            "anonymous" if isinstance(strategy, NoAuth) else type(strategy).__name__
        )
        logger.debug("%s initialized (%s).", type(self).__name__, auth_label)

    async def request(
        self,
        method: str,
        path: str,
        *,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        json: Any | None = None,
        data: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        content: str | bytes | None = None,
        headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
        timeout: float | httpx.Timeout | None = None,
        retry: bool | None = None,
        follow_redirects: bool | None = None,
    ) -> httpx.Response:
        """Send a request through the core retry pipeline.

        V4 accepts ``mailto`` for polite-pool admission (V3 rejects it), so the
        configured contact address is attached to ``v4/`` requests only.
        """
        effective_params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = params
        if path.lstrip("/").startswith("v4/") and self._settings.mailto:
            if params is None:
                effective_params = {"mailto": self._settings.mailto}
            elif isinstance(params, Mapping):
                if "mailto" not in params:
                    effective_params = {"mailto": self._settings.mailto, **params}
            else:
                qp = httpx.QueryParams(params)
                if "mailto" not in qp:
                    effective_params = qp.set("mailto", self._settings.mailto)
        return await super().request(
            method,
            path,
            params=effective_params,
            json=json,
            data=data,
            content=content,
            headers=headers,
            timeout=timeout,
            retry=retry,
            follow_redirects=follow_redirects,
        )

    @functools.cached_property
    def _links(self) -> LinksResource:
        return LinksResource(self)

    @functools.cached_property
    def research_products(self) -> ResearchProductsResource:
        """Search, iterate, and batch-fetch research products; links helpers."""
        return ResearchProductsResource(self, self._links)

    @functools.cached_property
    def projects(self) -> ProjectsResource:
        """Search and iterate OpenAIRE projects."""
        return ProjectsResource(self)

    @functools.cached_property
    def organizations(self) -> OrganizationsResource:
        """Search and iterate OpenAIRE organizations."""
        return OrganizationsResource(self)

    @functools.cached_property
    def data_sources(self) -> DataSourcesResource:
        """Search and iterate OpenAIRE data sources."""
        return DataSourcesResource(self)

    @functools.cached_property
    def persons(self) -> PersonsResource:
        """Search and iterate OpenAIRE persons."""
        return PersonsResource(self)

    @functools.cached_property
    def scholix(self) -> ScholixResource:
        """Search Scholix links on the Scholexplorer host (V3, V2 for linkProvider)."""
        return ScholixResource(self._scholix_api)

    async def aclose(self) -> None:
        """Close both the Graph and the Scholix HTTP clients."""
        try:
            await super().aclose()
        finally:
            await self._scholix_api.aclose()

docs.text:
Bases: BaseApiSettings

Tunable client behavior for the OpenAIRE Graph and Scholexplorer APIs.

Every field can be set through an environment variable prefixed with AIRELOOM_ (for example AIRELOOM_OPENAIRE_CLIENT_ID) or a .env file in the working directory.

Source code in packages/aireloom/src/aireloom/config.py 
class AireloomSettings(BaseApiSettings):
    """Tunable client behavior for the OpenAIRE Graph and Scholexplorer APIs.

    Every field can be set through an environment variable prefixed with
    ``AIRELOOM_`` (for example ``AIRELOOM_OPENAIRE_CLIENT_ID``) or a ``.env``
    file in the working directory.
    """

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        env_prefix="AIRELOOM_",
        env_file=".env",
        env_file_encoding="utf-8",
        extra="ignore",
    )

    base_url: str = DEFAULT_GRAPH_BASE_URL
    scholix_base_url: str = DEFAULT_SCHOLIX_BASE_URL

    # OAuth2 client credentials (registered service) or refresh token. Without
    # credentials the client stays anonymous; partial client credentials raise
    # ConfigurationError.
    openaire_client_id: str | None = None
    openaire_client_secret: str | None = None
    openaire_refresh_token: str | None = Field(default=None, repr=False)
    token_url: str = DEFAULT_TOKEN_URL

    # D-15: OpenAIRE allows about 7200 requests per rolling hour.
    max_requests_per_second: float | None = 2.0
    max_concurrency: int = 4

    # The Scholexplorer host sends no rate-limit headers, so self-throttle.
    scholix_max_requests_per_second: float | None = 1.0

docs.text:
Bases: GraphResource[ResearchProduct]

V4 research products endpoint: search, iterate, count, facets, group_by.

get(id) reads the V3 by-id route because V4 has no by-id endpoints. Batch lookups use OR expressions over id and ids.doi.

Source code in packages/aireloom/src/aireloom/_async/resources.py 
class ResearchProductsResource(GraphResource[ResearchProduct]):
    """V4 research products endpoint: search, iterate, count, facets, group_by.

    ``get(id)`` reads the V3 by-id route because V4 has no by-id endpoints.
    Batch lookups use OR expressions over ``id`` and ``ids.doi``.
    """

    path = "v4/research-products"
    model = ResearchProduct
    filters_model = ResearchProductsFilters
    sort_fields = frozenset(
        {
            "relevance",
            "publication_date",
            "date_of_collection",
            "citation_count",
            "influence",
            "popularity",
            "impulse",
        }
    )
    batch_size = 50

    def __init__(self, client: BaseApiClient, links: LinksResource) -> None:
        super().__init__(client)
        self._links = links

    def record_keys(self, entity: ResearchProduct, field: str) -> list[str]:
        if field == "ids.doi":
            # Deduplicated records carry several DOIs; batch_get keeps the requested one.
            return [normalize_doi(doi) for doi in entity.all_dois]
        return super().record_keys(entity, field)

    async def batch_get_by_doi(
        self,
        dois: list[str] | tuple[str, ...],
        *,
        batch_size: int | None = None,
        concurrency: int = 4,
    ) -> dict[str, ResearchProduct]:
        """Fetch research products for many DOIs in bounded, concurrent chunks.

        Keys are bare, lowercased DOIs; missing DOIs are absent from the
        result. The request goes out as ``filter=ids.doi:a|b|c``.
        """
        normalized = list(dict.fromkeys(normalize_doi(doi) for doi in dois))
        return await self.batch_get(
            normalized, field="ids.doi", batch_size=batch_size, concurrency=concurrency
        )

    async def by_orcid(self, orcid: str, *, limit: int = 100) -> list[ResearchProduct]:
        """Return research products whose authorship carries ``orcid``.

        Accepts any spelling ``bibliofabric.ids.normalize_orcid`` handles
        (bare, dashed, or an ``https://orcid.org/`` URL); the filter sends
        the hyphenated form via the V4 ``authorships.author.orcid`` field and
        paginates via cursor when ``limit`` exceeds 100.
        """
        page_size = min(limit, self.dialect.max_page_size) if limit > 0 else None
        return await self.collect(
            ResearchProductsFilters(authorships_author_orcid=normalize_orcid(orcid)),
            limit=limit,
            page_size=page_size,
        )

    async def get_fields(
        self,
        ids: Sequence[str],
        fields: Sequence[str],
        *,
        batch_size: int | None = None,
        concurrency: int = 4,
    ) -> list[ResearchProduct]:
        """Sparse-fetch ``fields`` for known ids in bounded, concurrent chunks.

        Combines the V4 ``select`` parameter with an ``id`` OR-filter (at most
        50 ids per chunk). The returned records carry only the requested
        fields; every other model field stays at its default.
        """
        selected = [field.strip() for field in fields if field and field.strip()]
        if not selected:
            raise ConfigurationError("get_fields() requires at least one field name.")
        size = self.batch_size if batch_size is None else batch_size
        if size <= 0 or size > MAX_OR_VALUES:
            raise ConfigurationError(
                f"batch_size must be between 1 and {MAX_OR_VALUES}, got {size}."
            )
        if concurrency <= 0:
            raise ConfigurationError(
                f"concurrency must be positive, got {concurrency}."
            )
        wanted = list(
            dict.fromkeys(norm for raw in ids if (norm := self.normalize_id(raw)))
        )
        if not wanted:
            return []
        chunks = [wanted[start : start + size] for start in range(0, len(wanted), size)]

        async def fetch_chunk(chunk: list[str]) -> list[ResearchProduct]:
            page = await self.search(
                {"id": chunk}, select=selected, page_size=len(chunk)
            )
            return page.results

        chunk_results = await run_bounded(fetch_chunk, chunks, concurrency)
        return [record for group in chunk_results for record in group]

    async def search_links(
        self,
        filters: LinksFilters | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        page: int | None = None,
        page_size: int | None = None,
    ) -> Page[Relation]:
        """Fetch one page of relations from the Graph links route."""
        return await self._links.search(filters, page=page, page_size=page_size)

    def iterate_links(
        self,
        filters: LinksFilters | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        page_size: int | None = None,
        limit: int | None = None,
        on_error: OnError = "raise",
        failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] | None = None,
        on_page: Callable[[int, str | None], Any] | None = None,
    ) -> AsyncIterator[Relation]:
        """Iterate over all relations matching ``filters``, 99 per page.

        See :class:`LinksResource` for the missing-sort hazard of this
        page-based route.

docs.text:
Sparse-fetch fields for known ids in bounded, concurrent chunks.

Combines the V4 select parameter with an id OR-filter (at most 50 ids per chunk). The returned records carry only the requested fields; every other model field stays at its default.

Source code in packages/aireloom/src/aireloom/_async/resources.py 
async def get_fields(
    self,
    ids: Sequence[str],
    fields: Sequence[str],
    *,
    batch_size: int | None = None,
    concurrency: int = 4,
) -> list[ResearchProduct]:
    """Sparse-fetch ``fields`` for known ids in bounded, concurrent chunks.

    Combines the V4 ``select`` parameter with an ``id`` OR-filter (at most
    50 ids per chunk). The returned records carry only the requested
    fields; every other model field stays at its default.
    """
    selected = [field.strip() for field in fields if field and field.strip()]
    if not selected:
        raise ConfigurationError("get_fields() requires at least one field name.")
    size = self.batch_size if batch_size is None else batch_size
    if size <= 0 or size > MAX_OR_VALUES:
        raise ConfigurationError(
            f"batch_size must be between 1 and {MAX_OR_VALUES}, got {size}."
        )
    if concurrency <= 0:
        raise ConfigurationError(
            f"concurrency must be positive, got {concurrency}."
        )
    wanted = list(
        dict.fromkeys(norm for raw in ids if (norm := self.normalize_id(raw)))
    )
    if not wanted:
        return []
    chunks = [wanted[start : start + size] for start in range(0, len(wanted), size)]

    async def fetch_chunk(chunk: list[str]) -> list[ResearchProduct]:
        page = await self.search(
            {"id": chunk}, select=selected, page_size=len(chunk)
        )
        return page.results

    chunk_results = await run_bounded(fetch_chunk, chunks, concurrency)
    return [record for group in chunk_results for record in group]

class OrganizationsResource(GraphResource[Organization]):
    """V4 organizations endpoint: search, iterate, count, facets, group_by.

    ``get(id)`` reads the V3 by-id route because V4 has no by-id endpoints.
    """

    path = "v4/organizations"
    model = Organization
    filters_model = OrganizationsFilters

    async def find_variants(
        self,
        names: Sequence[str],
        *,
        country: str | None = None,
        page_size: int | None = None,
    ) -> list[Organization]:
        """Search each name fragment and return deduplicated organizations.

        Records are deduplicated by exact ``id`` keeping the first match;
        ``pending_org_::`` records are kept on purpose. They carry
        organization-project links that the canonical merged record lost,
        which makes them the main source of undercounted org-project
        links, so callers decide how to merge them.
        """
        filters = {"country": country} if country else None
        found: dict[str, Organization] = {}
        for name in names:
            page = await self.search(filters, query=name, page_size=page_size)
            for org in page.results:
                found.setdefault(org.id, org)
        return list(found.values())

class ScholixResource:
    """Scholix link search over the Scholexplorer host (V3 default, V2 fallback).

    Backed by a dedicated internal API client for ``api.scholexplorer.openaire.eu``
    that shares the Graph client's credentials and settings but throttles
    itself to one request per second (the host sends no rate-limit headers).

    V3 is the default surface. Queries carrying ``linkProvider`` are routed to
    V2 because V3 silently ignores ``linkProvider``. Queries carrying
    ``from_date`` or ``to_date`` raise :class:`ConfigurationError` because V3
    returns zero rows for date filters and V2 silently ignores date parameters.
    """

    def __init__(self, client: BaseApiClient) -> None:
        self._v3 = ScholixV3Links(client)
        self._v2 = ScholixV2Links(client)
        self._client = client

    @staticmethod
    def _has_date_filter(filters: ScholixFilters | Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> bool:
        if filters is None:
            return False
        if isinstance(filters, ScholixFilters):
            return filters.from_date is not None or filters.to_date is not None
        return any(
            filters.get(key) is not None
            for key in ("from", "to", "from_date", "to_date")
        )

    @classmethod
    def _reject_date_filter(
        cls, filters: ScholixFilters | Mapping[str, Any] | None
    ) -> None:
        if cls._has_date_filter(filters):
            raise ConfigurationError(
                "Scholexplorer does not support 'from_date'/'to_date' filtering "
                "(V3 returns zero rows for 'from'/'to' and V2 silently ignores "
                "date parameters). Remove 'from_date'/'to_date' from filters and "
                "filter results by 'link_publication_date' client-side, or query "
                "Graph V4 research products with 'from_publication_date' / "
                "'to_publication_date'."
            )

    @staticmethod
    def _has_link_provider(filters: ScholixFilters | Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> bool:
        if filters is None:
            return False
        if isinstance(filters, ScholixFilters):
            return filters.linkProvider is not None
        return filters.get("linkProvider") is not None

    def _select_target(
        self, filters: ScholixFilters | Mapping[str, Any] | None
    ) -> _ScholixLinks:
        self._reject_date_filter(filters)
        if self._has_link_provider(filters):
            return self._v2
        return self._v3

    async def search_links(
        self,
        filters: ScholixFilters | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        page: int | None = None,
        page_size: int | None = None,
    ) -> Page[ScholixRelationship]:
        """Fetch one page of links as typed records.

        Queries with ``linkProvider`` route to V2 (V3 silently ignores it);
        everything else goes to V3. Passing ``from_date`` or ``to_date`` raises
        :class:`ConfigurationError`.
        """
        target = self._select_target(filters)
        return await target.search(filters, page=page, page_size=page_size)

    def iterate_links(
        self,
        filters: ScholixFilters | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        page_size: int | None = None,
        limit: int | None = None,
        on_error: OnError = "raise",
        failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] | None = None,
        on_page: Callable[[int, str | None], Any] | None = None,
    ) -> AsyncIterator[ScholixRelationship]:
        """Iterate over all matching links, 99 per page.

        See :meth:`search_links` for V2/V3 routing rules and date-filter
        rejection. The route has no cursor, so page windows are not pinned; the
        iterator stops on an empty page or when the reported total has been
        fetched.
        """
        target = self._select_target(filters)
        return target.iterate(
            filters,
            page_size=page_size,
            limit=limit,
            on_error=on_error,
            failures=failures,
            on_page=on_page,
        )

    async def search_links_v2(
        self,
        filters: ScholixFilters | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        page: int | None = None,
        page_size: int | None = None,
    ) -> Page[ScholixRelationship]:
        """Fetch one page of links from the V2 endpoint.

        Passing ``from_date`` or ``to_date`` raises :class:`ConfigurationError`
        because V2 silently ignores date parameters.
        """
        self._reject_date_filter(filters)
        return await self._v2.search(filters, page=page, page_size=page_size)

    def iterate_links_v2(
        self,
        filters: ScholixFilters | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        page_size: int | None = None,
        limit: int | None = None,
        on_error: OnError = "raise",
        failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] | None = None,
        on_page: Callable[[int, str | None], Any] | None = None,
    ) -> AsyncIterator[ScholixRelationship]:
        """Iterate over all matching links from the V2 endpoint.

        Passing ``from_date`` or ``to_date`` raises :class:`ConfigurationError`
        because V2 silently ignores date parameters.
        """
        self._reject_date_filter(filters)
        return self._v2.iterate(
            filters,
            page_size=page_size,
            limit=limit,
            on_error=on_error,
            failures=failures,
            on_page=on_page,
        )

    async def list_link_providers(
        self, name: str | None = None
    ) -> list[ScholixLinkProvider]:
        """List Scholexplorer link providers (V2)."""
        params = {"name": name} if name is not None else None
        response = await self._client.request("GET", "v2/LinkProvider", params=params)
        payload = self._client.parse_json(response)
        return [
            validate_model(
                ScholixLinkProvider, entry, request=response.request, response=response
            )
            for entry in _records(payload)
        ]

    async def list_link_publishers(
        self, *, in_target: bool = True, name: str | None = None
    ) -> list[ScholixPublisher]:
        """List publishers of source or target objects (V2)."""
        path = "v2/LinkPublisher/inTarget" if in_target else "v2/LinkPublisher/inSource"
        params = {"name": name} if name is not None else None
        response = await self._client.request("GET", path, params=params)
        payload = self._client.parse_json(response)
        return [
            validate_model(
                ScholixPublisher, entry, request=response.request, response=response
            )
            for entry in _records(payload)
        ]

    async def get_kpi(self) -> str:
        """Return the Scholexplorer Prometheus KPI document."""
        response = await self._client.request("GET", "kpi/getKPI")
        return response.text

docs.text:
Bases: SyncBaseApiClient

Client for the OpenAIRE Graph API (V4) and the Scholexplorer API.

Entity resources are available as typed attributes; single-entity lookups go through the V3 by-id routes because V4 has none. Authentication resolves in the constructor: set openaire_refresh_token / refresh_token for OAuth2 refresh-token access, or set both openaire_client_id and openaire_client_secret (settings, AIRELOOM_OPENAIRE_CLIENT_ID / AIRELOOM_OPENAIRE_CLIENT_SECRET, or client_id / client_secret) for OAuth2 client-credentials access against the Keycloak token endpoint; partial client credentials raise :class:ConfigurationError, and without credentials the client is anonymous. An explicit auth_strategy always wins.

The Scholix resource talks to the Scholexplorer host through a second internal client that shares settings and credentials but throttles itself to one request per second. See the package README and docs for usage examples of both the async and the sync variants.

Source code in packages/aireloom/src/aireloom/_sync/client.py 
class AireloomSyncClient(SyncBaseApiClient):
    """Client for the OpenAIRE Graph API (V4) and the Scholexplorer API.

    Entity resources are available as typed attributes; single-entity lookups
    go through the V3 by-id routes because V4 has none. Authentication
    resolves in the constructor: set ``openaire_refresh_token`` /
    ``refresh_token`` for OAuth2 refresh-token access, or set both
    ``openaire_client_id`` and ``openaire_client_secret`` (settings,
    ``AIRELOOM_OPENAIRE_CLIENT_ID`` / ``AIRELOOM_OPENAIRE_CLIENT_SECRET``, or
    ``client_id`` / ``client_secret``) for OAuth2 client-credentials access
    against the Keycloak token endpoint; partial client credentials raise
    :class:`ConfigurationError`, and without credentials the client is
    anonymous. An explicit ``auth_strategy`` always wins.

    The Scholix resource talks to the Scholexplorer host through a second
    internal client that shares settings and credentials but throttles itself
    to one request per second. See the package README and docs for usage
    examples of both the async and the sync variants.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        settings: AireloomSettings | None = None,
        auth: AuthStrategy | None = None,
        *,
        auth_strategy: AuthStrategy | None = None,
        base_url: str | None = None,
        scholix_base_url: str | None = None,
        mailto: str | None = None,
        client_id: str | None = None,
        client_secret: str | None = None,
        refresh_token: str | None = None,
        http_client: httpx.Client | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Build the client from settings, resolving credentials immediately.

        ``settings`` defaults to :func:`aireloom.config.get_settings`, which
        reads ``AIRELOOM_*`` environment variables and ``.env``. Keyword
        overrides (``base_url``, ``scholix_base_url``, ``mailto``,
        ``client_id``, ``client_secret``, ``refresh_token``) take precedence
        over ``settings``. Pass ``auth_strategy`` for a custom auth strategy
        (``auth`` is a deprecated alias).
        """
        if auth is not None and auth_strategy is not None:
            raise ConfigurationError(
                "Pass either 'auth_strategy' or the deprecated 'auth' parameter, "
                "not both."
            )
        if auth is not None:
            warnings.warn(
                "The 'auth' parameter is deprecated; use 'auth_strategy' instead.",
                DeprecationWarning,
                stacklevel=2,
            )
            explicit_auth: AuthStrategy | None = auth
        else:
            explicit_auth = auth_strategy

        resolved = settings or get_settings()
        overrides: dict[str, str] = {}
        if base_url is not None:
            overrides["base_url"] = base_url
        if scholix_base_url is not None:
            overrides["scholix_base_url"] = scholix_base_url
        if mailto is not None:
            overrides["mailto"] = mailto
        if client_id is not None:
            overrides["openaire_client_id"] = client_id
        if client_secret is not None:
            overrides["openaire_client_secret"] = client_secret
        if refresh_token is not None:
            overrides["openaire_refresh_token"] = refresh_token
        if overrides:
            resolved = resolved.model_copy(update=overrides)
        strategy = (
            explicit_auth if explicit_auth is not None else _resolve_auth(resolved)
        )
        super().__init__(
            base_url=resolved.base_url,
            settings=resolved,
            unwrapper=OpenAireUnwrapper(),
            auth=strategy,
            http_client=http_client,
        )
        self._scholix_api = SyncBaseApiClient(
            base_url=resolved.scholix_base_url,
            settings=resolved.model_copy(
                update={
                    "max_requests_per_second": resolved.scholix_max_requests_per_second
                }
            ),
            unwrapper=ScholixUnwrapper(),
            auth=strategy,
        )
        auth_label = (
            "anonymous" if isinstance(strategy, NoAuth) else type(strategy).__name__
        )
        logger.debug("%s initialized (%s).", type(self).__name__, auth_label)

    def request(
        self,
        method: str,
        path: str,
        *,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        json: Any | None = None,
        data: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        content: str | bytes | None = None,
        headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
        timeout: float | httpx.Timeout | None = None,
        retry: bool | None = None,
        follow_redirects: bool | None = None,
    ) -> httpx.Response:
        """Send a request through the core retry pipeline.

        V4 accepts ``mailto`` for polite-pool admission (V3 rejects it), so the
        configured contact address is attached to ``v4/`` requests only.
        """
        effective_params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = params
        if path.lstrip("/").startswith("v4/") and self._settings.mailto:
            if params is None:
                effective_params = {"mailto": self._settings.mailto}
            elif isinstance(params, Mapping):
                if "mailto" not in params:
                    effective_params = {"mailto": self._settings.mailto, **params}
            else:
                qp = httpx.QueryParams(params)
                if "mailto" not in qp:
                    effective_params = qp.set("mailto", self._settings.mailto)
        return super().request(
            method,
            path,
            params=effective_params,
            json=json,
            data=data,
            content=content,
            headers=headers,
            timeout=timeout,
            retry=retry,
            follow_redirects=follow_redirects,
        )

    @functools.cached_property
    def _links(self) -> SyncLinksResource:
        return SyncLinksResource(self)

    @functools.cached_property
    def research_products(self) -> SyncResearchProductsResource:
        """Search, iterate, and batch-fetch research products; links helpers."""
        return SyncResearchProductsResource(self, self._links)

    @functools.cached_property
    def projects(self) -> SyncProjectsResource:
        """Search and iterate OpenAIRE projects."""
        return SyncProjectsResource(self)

    @functools.cached_property
    def organizations(self) -> SyncOrganizationsResource:
        """Search and iterate OpenAIRE organizations."""
        return SyncOrganizationsResource(self)

    @functools.cached_property
    def data_sources(self) -> SyncDataSourcesResource:
        """Search and iterate OpenAIRE data sources."""
        return SyncDataSourcesResource(self)

    @functools.cached_property
    def persons(self) -> SyncPersonsResource:
        """Search and iterate OpenAIRE persons."""
        return SyncPersonsResource(self)

    @functools.cached_property
    def scholix(self) -> SyncScholixResource:
        """Search Scholix links on the Scholexplorer host (V3, V2 for linkProvider)."""
        return SyncScholixResource(self._scholix_api)

    def close(self) -> None:
        """Close both the Graph and the Scholix HTTP clients."""
        try:
            super().close()
        finally:
            self._scholix_api.close()

    access rights, countries, subjects, indicators, instances, Open Access
    flags, subtype-specific fields, and typed relationship lists. Inherits
    ``id`` from ``BaseEntity``.
    """

    originalIds: SafeList[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    pids: SafeList[Pid] = Field(default_factory=list)
    type: ResearchProductType | None = None
    mainTitle: SafeStr = ""
    subTitle: SafeStr = ""
    otherTitles: SafeList[str] = Field(default_factory=list)

    bestAccessRight: SafeBestAccessRight = Field(default_factory=BestAccessRight)

    subjects: SafeList[Subject] = Field(default_factory=list)
    container: SafeContainer = Field(default_factory=Container)
    geoLocations: SafeList[GeoLocation] = Field(default_factory=list)

    # Open Access fields
    isGreen: bool | None = None
    green: bool | None = None
    isInDiamondJournal: bool | None = None
    inDiamondJournal: bool | None = None
    openAccessColor: str | None = None
    publiclyFunded: bool | None = None
    eoscIfGuidelines: SafeList[EoscIfGuideline] = Field(default_factory=list)

    # Subtype-specific fields (Software)
    codeRepositoryUrl: str | None = None
    documentationUrls: SafeList[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    programmingLanguage: str | None = None

    # Subtype-specific fields (Dataset)
    size: str | None = None
    version: str | None = None

    # Subtype-specific fields (Other)
    contactPeople: SafeList[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    contactGroups: SafeList[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    tools: SafeList[str] = Field(default_factory=list)

    # Relationship fields
    collectedFrom: SafeList[CfHbKeyValue] = Field(default_factory=list)
    projects: SafeList[ProductProject] = Field(default_factory=list)
    organizations: SafeList[ProductOrganization] = Field(default_factory=list)
    communities: SafeList[ProductCommunity] = Field(default_factory=list)
    links: SafeList[RelatedRecord] = Field(default_factory=list)

    # ── Computed fields ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

    @computed_field
    @property
    def doi(self) -> str | None:
        """First DOI from the pids list."""
        return extract_pid_by_scheme(self.pids, "doi")

    @computed_field
    @property
    def all_dois(self) -> list[str]:
        """All DOI values from the pids list."""
        return extract_all_pids_by_scheme(self.pids, "doi")

    @computed_field
    @property
    def is_open_access(self) -> bool:
        """True when the best access right is OPEN."""
        return self.bestAccessRight.label.upper() == "OPEN"

    @computed_field
    @property
    def open_access_url(self) -> str | None:
        """URL of the first instance whose access right is OPEN."""
        for inst in self.instances:
            if (
                inst.accessRight
                and inst.accessRight.label
                and inst.accessRight.label.upper() == "OPEN"
                and inst.urls
            ):
                return inst.urls[0]
        return None

    @computed_field
    @property
    def citation_count(self) -> int | None:
        """Citation count from indicators, if available."""
        return self.indicators.citationImpact.citationCount

    @computed_field
    @property
    def publication_year(self) -> int | None:
        """Year parsed from publicationDate."""
        if self.publicationDate:
            try:
                return int(self.publicationDate[:4])
            except ValueError:
                return None
        return None

    @computed_field
    @property
    def journal_name(self) -> str | None:
        """Container / journal name, or None when empty."""
        return self.container.name or None

    @computed_field
    @property
    def author_names(self) -> list[str]:
        """Non-empty full names of all authors."""
        return [a.fullName for a in self.authors if a.fullName]

    @computed_field
    @property
    def license(self) -> str | None:
        """First non-empty license string found across instances."""
        for inst in self.instances:
            if inst.license:
                return inst.license
        return None

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        parts = []
        if self.mainTitle:
            parts.append(self.mainTitle[:80])
        if self.publication_year:
            parts.append(f"({self.publication_year})")
        if self.doi:
            parts.append(f"DOI:{self.doi}")
        return " | ".join(parts) if parts else f"ResearchProduct(id={self.id!r})"

            except ValueError:
                return None
        return None

            try:
                return int(self.endDate[:4])
            except ValueError:
                return None
        return None

        parts = []
        if self.title:
            parts.append(self.title[:80])
        if self.code:
            parts.append(f"[{self.code}]")
        if self.funder_name:
            parts.append(f"funded by {self.funder_name}")
        return " | ".join(parts) if parts else f"Project(id={self.id!r})"

    @field_validator("keywords", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def parse_keywords_string(cls, v: Any) -> Any:
        """Split a delimited keyword string (comma or semicolon) into a list."""
        if isinstance(v, str):
            stripped = v.strip()
            if not stripped:
                return []
            for delimiter in (",", ";"):
                if delimiter in stripped:
                    return [
                        part.strip()
                        for part in stripped.split(delimiter)
                        if part.strip()
                    ]
            return [stripped]
        return v

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
AIREloom re-exports the bibliofabric exceptions; every error derives from BibliofabricError:

Exception Raised when NotFoundError the API answers 404 AuthError token fetch or authentication fails RateLimitError the API answers 429 after retries TimeoutError the request exceeds the timeout NetworkError connection or DNS failure ValidationError a response record fails model validation ConfigurationError invalid client usage, such as an unknown sort field

ValidationError carries the raw record. Pass on_error="skip" and a failures list to search or collect to keep going past bad records and inspect them afterwards.

docs.title: Retries
docs.text: The core retries transient failures: 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504 responses, plus network errors, with exponential backoff, and it honors the Retry-After header. By default every idempotent method retries (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, DELETE); the client sends no mutating requests of its own.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text:
According to the OpenAIRE API terms, authenticated requests allow up to 7,200 requests per rolling hour (2 req/s), while unauthenticated requests are documented at 60 requests per hour (though live V4 responses currently report x-ratelimit-limit: 7199).

Client defaults follow the 7,200 req/hour allowance:

  • Graph host: at most 2 requests per second, 4 concurrent requests
  • Scholexplorer host: at most 1 request per second (no rate-limit headers, so the client self-throttles)

Change them through settings:

settings = AireloomSettings(max_requests_per_second=1.0, max_concurrency=2)
client = AireloomClient(settings=settings)

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Set AIRELOOM_OPENAIRE_CLIENT_ID and AIRELOOM_OPENAIRE_CLIENT_SECRET for OAuth2 client-credentials access, or AIRELOOM_OPENAIRE_REFRESH_TOKEN (or refresh_token=) for refresh-token access. Setting only one of client ID or client secret raises ConfigurationError. The client posts to the Keycloak token endpoint, caches the bearer token until shortly before it expires, and serializes concurrent fetches. Without credentials, or with an explicit auth_strategy= (auth= is a deprecated alias), the client behaves accordingly; an explicit strategy always wins.

The legacy https://aai.openaire.eu/oidc/token endpoint was retired on 2026-11-02 and returns 410 Gone; the default token URL already points at the Keycloak realm endpoint.

docs.title: Polite pool
docs.text: Set mailto in the settings to attach your contact address to every V4 request for polite-pool admission. V3 routes reject mailto, so the client attaches it to V4 requests only.

docs.title: Upstream quirks
docs.text: Behavior of the OpenAIRE and Scholexplorer services that the client works around or documents. All of these were observed against the live services.

docs.title: V4 page_size, offset, and OR-list caps
docs.text:
• page_size must be between 1 and 100 (in both offset and cursor modes); larger values return HTTP 400.
  • Offset-based paging is limited to offset <= 10,000 (max_offset=10_000); use cursor paging (iterate() or cursor="*") for larger datasets.
  • A single V4 filter field accepts at most 50 pipe-separated OR values (OpenAIRE Graph 1.6.0+); larger lists return HTTP 400.

AIREloom enforces all three caps client-side (GRAPH_DIALECT.max_page_size = 100, GRAPH_DIALECT.max_offset = 10_000, and 50-value OR check raising ConfigurationError).

docs.title: Scholix V3 linkProvider and date-filter limitations
docs.text:
• /v3/Links does not declare linkProvider and silently ignores it; /v2/Links filters by linkProvider properly. AIREloom routes queries carrying linkProvider to /v2/Links automatically.
  • /v3/Links accepts from and to but returns zero rows for every tested date value. /v2/Links has no from/to parameters at all and silently ignores them (returning unfiltered links). Passing from_date or to_date to Scholix search or iterate methods raises ConfigurationError immediately so callers never receive silent zero-row or unfiltered results; filter results by link_publication_date client-side instead, or query Graph V4 research products with from_publication_date / to_publication_date.

docs.title: V4 group_by totals are uneven
docs.text: The V4 group_by aggregation mode reports counts per value together with a header numFound, but the numbers come from different aggregation paths and are not guaranteed to agree; per-value counts can also differ from what a plain search for that value reports. Treat group_by output as a rough distribution, not an exact breakdown.

docs.title: Graph links and Scholix routes silently truncate at 100
docs.text: On /v3/research-products/links and Scholexplorer /v2/Links & /v3/Links, a page size of 100 or more silently returns 10 results without an error. The client caps page sizes for these routes at 99.

docs.title: Graph links pages are not pinned
docs.text: The links route has no cursor or sort, so a page window only makes sense if the upstream ordering is stable. If the ordering changes between requests, relations can be skipped or duplicated. The iterator stops on an empty page or at the reported total, which bounds the walk but cannot prevent shifts.

docs.title: V3 by-id routes need raw colons
docs.text: The /v3/{entity}/{id} routes expect prefix::suffix identifiers with the colons unencoded; percent-encoding them returns 404. The client leaves colons in place.

docs.title: V4 group_by responds with an empty result list
docs.text: In group_by mode the API returns the facet counts and an empty results array, even though numFound still counts matching records. The client reads the counts from the facets block and ignores the record list.

docs.title: Scholexplorer sends no rate-limit headers
docs.text: There is no 429 feedback to pace against, so the Scholix client self-throttles to one request per second.

docs.title: Links
docs.text:
The /v3/research-products/links route returns relations between research products as individual query parameters (not the V4 filter expression).

from aireloom import LinksFilters

page = await client.research_products.search_links(
    LinksFilters(relation="IsSupplementTo", sourceType="publication"),
    page=0,
    page_size=99,
)
page.results  # list[Relation]
page.total  # totalLinks from the header

async for relation in client.research_products.iterate_links(limit=1000):
    ...

Pages are 0-indexed and page sizes cap at 99; sizes of 100 or more silently return 10 results (see upstream quirks). The route requires one of the pid, publisher, or type parameters; a bare query returns 400.

The route has no cursor and no sort parameter, so page windows are not pinned: if the upstream ordering changes between requests, pages can shift and relations can be skipped or duplicated. The iterator stops on an empty page or when the reported total has been fetched, which bounds the walk but cannot remove that hazard.

info = await client.research_products.get_relations_info()
info[0].relation  # "Cites"
info[0].inverse  # "IsCitedBy"
info[0].description

docs.title: Relation vocabulary
docs.text:
from aireloom import RELATION_INVERSES, RelationName, relation_inverse

relation_inverse("Cites")  # "IsCitedBy"
relation_inverse("IsRelatedTo")  # "IsRelatedTo" (symmetric)
relation_inverse("nonsense")  # None

The vocabulary is static data mirroring the relations-info payload: RelationName is the union of both directions, and RELATION_INVERSES/relation_inverse() map each name to its inverse without a live request.

docs.title: Projects, organizations, data sources, persons
docs.text:
These four resources share the research-product machinery: one V4 filter expression, the same search/iterate/count helpers, and V3 by-id lookups. They differ in filter fields, sort fields, and models.

from aireloom import (
    DataSourcesFilters,
    OrganizationsFilters,
    PersonsFilters,
    ProjectsFilters,
)

page = await client.projects.search(
    ProjectsFilters(funder="EC", project_status="ongoing"), page_size=25
)
org = await client.organizations.get("wtso__________::1234")
sources = await client.data_sources.search(
    DataSourcesFilters(jurisdiction="Governmental"), page_size=10
)
persons = await client.persons.search(
    PersonsFilters(given_name="Ada", last_name="Lovelace")
)

To fetch many people by ORCID, use batch_get_by_orcid. It sends one request per 50 iDs and returns a dict keyed by the hyphenated ORCID; iDs without a person record are absent.

people = await client.persons.batch_get_by_orcid(
    ["0000-0002-5965-6560", "https://orcid.org/0000-0003-1219-1775"]
)

docs.title: Sort fields
docs.text:
Only these fields sort. Anything else raises ConfigurationError before a request is sent:

  • research products: relevance, publication_date, date_of_collection, citation_count, influence, popularity, impulse
  • projects: relevance, start_date, end_date
  • organizations, data sources, persons: relevance

Directions are asc/desc; the default direction depends on the field. sort="relevance" sorts by match score for free-text queries.

docs.title: Valid filter fields
docs.text: The filter models list exactly the fields the V4 endpoints accept; extra attributes are rejected by pydantic. The dotted aliases mirror the API field names (organizations.id, compatibility.name, collected_from.id). Unknown V4 fields raise a server-side error, which is how the models stay honest.

docs.title: Counts and aggregations
docs.text:
n = await client.projects.count()
by_status = await client.projects.group_by("project_status")
facets = await client.organizations.facets("country", page_size=1)

docs.title: Organization name variants
docs.text:
orgs = await client.organizations.find_variants(
    ["universiteit twente", "university of twente"], country="NL"
)

Each fragment becomes one free-text search; results are deduplicated by exact id, keeping the first occurrence. Records with pending_org_:: identifiers are kept on purpose: they carry organization-project links that the canonical merged record lost, which makes them the main source of undercounted org-project links. Merging them is the caller's decision.

docs.title: Research products
docs.text: client.research_products queries /v4/research-products. All criteria go into one V4 filter expression; see the filter syntax below.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
from aireloom import ResearchProductsFilters

page = await client.research_products.search(
    ResearchProductsFilters(type="publication", is_green=True),
    query="graph neural networks",
    sort="citation_count:desc",
    select=["id", "mainTitle", "publicationDate"],
    page_size=50,
)
page.total  # numFound from the response header
page.results  # list[ResearchProduct]
page.next_cursor  # cursor for iterate/resume

docs.title: Filter syntax
docs.text:
Each set field becomes one field:value entry:

  • a model attribute with a dotted alias sends the dotted name (ids_doi sends ids.doi);
  • list values join with | (OR within one field), commas between fields are AND;
  • a leading ! negates, > and < compare on numeric and date fields;
  • booleans encode as true/false.
ResearchProductsFilters(
    subjects=["chemistry", "biology"],  # subjects:chemistry|biology
    impact_citation_count=">100",  # impact.citation_count:>100
    oa_color="!gold",  # oa_color:!gold
)

Plain dictionaries work the same way: search({"type": "dataset", "language": "!ger"}).

docs.title: Iterate
docs.text:
iterate walks all matches at 100 per page and stops when the API stops returning nextCursor or echoes the current cursor:

async for product in client.research_products.iterate(
    ResearchProductsFilters(type="dataset"), limit=500
):
    ...

Pass on_page(number, next_cursor) to checkpoint progress, and feed a saved cursor back through cursor= to resume an interrupted harvest.

docs.title: Single record
docs.text:
product = await client.research_products.get("doi_dedup___::<identifier>")

get reads /v3/research-products/{id}; colons in the identifier stay unencoded.

docs.title: Batch lookups
docs.text:
by_id = await client.research_products.batch_get(["id_1", "id_2"])
by_doi = await client.research_products.batch_get_by_doi(
    ["10.1038/nature12373", "https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1234"]
)

DOIs are normalized before lookup and as result keys; missing DOIs are absent from the result. Requests go out in chunks of 50 as OR expressions.

docs.title: By author ORCID
docs.text:
works = await client.research_products.by_orcid(
    "https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0097", limit=50
)

Any ORCID spelling works (bare, dashed, or URL); the request uses the hyphenated form in the authorships.author.orcid V4 filter and returns a plain list capped at limit (automatically paginating via cursor when limit exceeds 100).

docs.title: Sparse batch fetch
docs.text:
records = await client.research_products.get_fields(
    ["06cdd3ff4700::3c8734759ca685b966b1d737c37daeed"],
    ["id", "mainTitle", "publicationDate"],
)

Sends concurrent chunks of up to 50 IDs combining an id OR-filter with the V4 select parameter. Records carry only the requested fields, so this is the cheap way to enrich local rows; unknown field names are the caller's responsibility.

docs.title: Aggregations
docs.text:
counts = await client.research_products.group_by("type")
facets = await client.research_products.facets("type", "result_hosts", page_size=1)

group_by fetches no records; facets fetches records plus aggregations, so bound it with page_size. See upstream quirks for the uneven group_by totals.

docs.title: Relations
docs.text: search_links, iterate_links, and get_relations_info use the separate /v3/research-products/links route; see Links.

docs.title: Scholix
docs.text:
client.scholix searches Scholexplorer, the OpenAIRE service for scholarly links. It talks to api.scholexplorer.openaire.eu through a second internal client that shares the Graph client's credentials and throttles itself to one request per second, because the host sends no rate-limit headers.

from aireloom import ScholixFilters

page = await client.scholix.search_links(
    ScholixFilters(sourcePid="10.1038/nature12373"), page_size=25
)
page.results  # list[ScholixRelationship]

The API requires one of sourcePid, targetPid, sourcePublisher, targetPublisher, sourceType, or targetType; a bare query returns 400.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
V3 is the default endpoint. Queries with linkProvider are routed to V2 automatically because /v3/Links silently ignores linkProvider whereas /v2/Links filters by it:

page = await client.scholix.search_links(
    ScholixFilters(sourcePid="10.1038/nature12373", linkProvider="Crossref")
)

Passing from_date or to_date to search_links, iterate_links, search_links_v2, or iterate_links_v2 raises ConfigurationError immediately: V3 returns zero rows for date filters and V2 silently ignores date parameters (see upstream quirks). Filter results by link_publication_date client-side, or query Graph V4 research products with from_publication_date / to_publication_date.

search_links_v2 and iterate_links_v2 force the V2 endpoint directly.

docs.title: Providers and publishers
docs.text:
providers = await client.scholix.list_link_providers()
publishers = await client.scholix.list_link_publishers(in_target=True, name="Elsevier")
kpi = await client.scholix.get_kpi()  # Prometheus text

The provider and publisher helpers use the V2 routes.

docs.title: Aletheca
docs.text: Aletheca is a Python client for the OpenAlex API, built on bibliofabric. It types all nine native entity endpoints (works, authors, sources, institutions, topics, keywords, publishers, funders, awards) plus the /locations per-copy index and /links citation-graph endpoint with Pydantic models and serializes OpenAlex filter syntax for you. It ships an async client and a generated sync twin with the same API.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv add aletheca

Requires Python 3.12 or newer.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
OpenAlex works without a key, but unkeyed traffic shares a $0.10/day per-IP budget and cannot use cursor paging past the first page. A free key raises the budget to $1/day. Request one at openalex.org/settings/api, then export it:

export ALETHECA_API_KEY="your-key"

By default the key travels as the api_key query parameter. Set ALETHECA_AUTH_SCHEME=bearer to send it as an Authorization: Bearer header instead. See errors, retries, and rate limits for budgets and pacing.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import asyncio
from aletheca import AlethecaClient


async def main():
    async with AlethecaClient() as client:
        work = await client.works.get("W2741809807")
        print(work.title, work.publication_year)

        page = await client.works.search(
            {"is_oa": True, "publication_year": 2024},
            query="photosynthesis",
            select=["id", "title"],
        )
        print(page.total, len(page.results))

        async for author in client.authors.iterate(
            {"last_known_institutions.id": "I1290904741"}
        ):
            print(author.display_name)


asyncio.run(main())

Every resource client exposes get(), search(), iterate(), collect(), first(), count(), sample(), group_by(), and iterate_group_by(). The works client adds OpenAlex-specific helpers: batch_get_by_doi(), batch_get_by_openalex_id(), citing(), referenced(), oa_pdf_urls(), search_scoped(), and corpus=/include_parts=/include_pulled=/rerank= controls. The client itself offers free autocomplete() and rate_limit() endpoints, plus last_rate_limit_headers after responses.

docs.title: Sync usage
docs.text:
AlethecaSyncClient is generated from the async source and behaves the same: same parameters, errors, retries, paging, and rate limits. The resource twins are WorksSyncClient, AuthorsSyncClient, and so on, one *SyncClient class per endpoint. The sync client uses plain httpx.Client and never starts or touches an event loop, so it works in scripts, in Jupyter, in threads, and when called from inside a running event loop.

from aletheca import AlethecaSyncClient

with AlethecaSyncClient() as client:
    work = client.works.get("W2741809807")
    print(work.title, work.publication_year)

    page = client.works.search(
        {"is_oa": True}, query="photosynthesis", select=["id", "title"]
    )
    print(page.total, len(page.results))

    for author in client.authors.iterate(
        {"last_known_institutions.id": "I1290904741"}, limit=5
    ):
        print(author.display_name)

Use the async client in asyncio applications and for many concurrent requests. Use the sync client everywhere else. Both read ALETHECA_API_KEY and the other ALETHECA_* settings the same way.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: AlethecaSettings loads from environment variables prefixed with ALETHECA_: ALETHECA_API_KEY, ALETHECA_AUTH_SCHEME, ALETHECA_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND, ALETHECA_MAX_CONCURRENCY, ALETHECA_RATE_LIMITS (JSON, default {"semantic": 1.0}), ALETHECA_TIMEOUT, ALETHECA_MAX_RETRIES, ALETHECA_MAX_RETRY_WAIT, ALETHECA_USER_AGENT. The legacy ALETHECA_OPENALEX_API_KEY name still works.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• One usage page per resource family: start with works.
  • Errors, retries, and rate limits.
  • Upstream quirks observed in the live OpenAlex API.
  • The API reference is generated from the source.

docs.title: Errors, retries, and rate limits
docs.text:
Every error inherits from BibliofabricError (re-exported from aletheca), and carries the failed httpx.Request and, when available, the httpx.Response.

BibliofabricError
├── APIError                     # any other 4xx/5xx; body holds the parsed JSON
│   ├── NotFoundError            # 404
│   └── RateLimitError           # 429
├── AuthError                    # 401 and 403
├── NetworkError                 # DNS, connection refused, reset
├── TimeoutError                 # also a builtin TimeoutError
├── ConfigurationError           # bad input caught client-side
└── ValidationError              # a record failed model validation

Catch specific types where you can react, and BibliofabricError as a last resort:

from aletheca import NotFoundError, RateLimitError

try:
    work = await client.works.get("W0000000000")
except NotFoundError:
    ...
except RateLimitError as e:
    print(e.body)  # parsed JSON error payload, or None

Error strings redact credential query parameters, so printing them never leaks your key.

docs.title: Client-side guards
docs.text:
Some mistakes fail before any request is sent, with a ConfigurationError:

  • More than 100 pipe-joined values in one filter.
  • Basic paging past OpenAlex's 10,000-result ceiling (page * per_page > 10,000), combining page with cursor, page < 1, or page_size <= 0.
  • A corpus value outside core/expansion/all on works.search().
  • A sample() size outside 1 to 10,000.
  • An unknown search_scoped() scope, autocomplete() entity type, or auth_scheme.

A record that fails model validation raises ValidationError with the raw payload (raw), the pydantic error (error), and the model name (model_name). In search(), batch_get(), iterate(), and collect(), pass on_error="skip" to drop bad records and collect them in a failures list instead.

docs.title: Retries
docs.text:
The client retries 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504 responses plus network errors and timeouts. A Retry-After header is honored when present; otherwise it waits with jittered exponential backoff, capped at ALETHECA_MAX_RETRY_WAIT (default 60 seconds). The number of attempts is ALETHECA_MAX_RETRIES (default 3).

One OpenAlex-specific veto: a 429 whose body carries reason: "daily_budget" is not retried, because it cannot succeed before the UTC midnight reset and retrying would only burn budget.

docs.title: Rate limits and budgets
docs.text:
OpenAlex meters requests in dollars per day, not requests per day. There is no polite pool: mailto is ignored.

Access Daily budget Cursor paging No key $0.10/day per IP First page only Free key $1/day Full cursor paging

Request types cost differently: plain list requests are cheapest, free-text search costs more (about 10x), and semantic search has its own per-second cap of 1 request. Content downloads cost the most.

Check your remaining budget for free:

status = await live_or_keyed_client.rate_limit()
print(status.rate_limit.daily_remaining_usd)

rate_limit() reads the key from settings and never stores the echoed key value. Every HTTP response also updates client.last_rate_limit_headers with any x-ratelimit-* headers returned by OpenAlex.

docs.title: Credit and cost headers
docs.text:
Every response tells you what the request cost and what is left of the daily budget. client.last_rate_limit_headers holds these headers from the most recent response, with lower-case names and string values. OpenAlex sent the following headers on 2026-11-28:

Header Meaning Example x-ratelimit-credits-used Credits the request used. A single-record lookup by id uses 0, and a list request uses 1. 1 x-ratelimit-cost-usd Cost of the request in US dollars. 0.0001 x-ratelimit-limit Daily budget in credits. 10000 x-ratelimit-remaining Credits left today. 9999 x-ratelimit-limit-usd Daily budget in US dollars. 1 x-ratelimit-remaining-usd Dollars left today. 0.9999 x-ratelimit-prepaid-remaining-usd Prepaid balance in US dollars. 0 x-ratelimit-onetime-remaining Remaining one-time credits. 0 x-ratelimit-reset Seconds until the budget resets at UTC midnight. 77578

OpenAlex also lists X-RateLimit-Credits-Required and X-RateLimit-Cost-Required-USD in Access-Control-Expose-Headers. They were absent from successful responses; the names suggest that they report the price of a request that the budget cannot cover.

Read the cost of each request after it returns:

page = await client.works.search({"publication_year": 2024})
headers = client.last_rate_limit_headers
print(headers.get("x-ratelimit-cost-usd"), headers.get("x-ratelimit-remaining-usd"))

The headers describe the last response only. Under concurrent requests, read them right after the call you want to measure, or call rate_limit() for the authoritative daily totals.

docs.title: Client-side pacing
docs.text: Aletheca spaces requests to a default of 10 per second with at most 5 concurrent requests, and caps search.semantic requests to 1 per second via its "semantic" rate class. Change these with ALETHECA_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND, ALETHECA_MAX_CONCURRENCY, and ALETHECA_RATE_LIMITS.

docs.title: Keyless 401s
docs.text: The most common 401 is cursor paging without a key. Aletheca replaces the opaque upstream body with an AuthError that names the fix: get a free key and set ALETHECA_API_KEY (or pass api_key= to AlethecaClient). A keyed client keeps the upstream message.

docs.title: aletheca.AlethecaSettings
docs.text:
Bases: BaseApiSettings

OpenAlex-specific client settings.

Inherits timeout, max_retries, max_retry_wait, max_requests_per_second, max_concurrency, rate_limits, user_agent and mailto from :class:bibliofabric.config.BaseApiSettings and sets OpenAlex defaults (10 req/s, concurrency 5, semantic search 1 req/s).

The polite pool no longer exists: since February 2026 OpenAlex ignores mailto and meters unkeyed traffic at $0.10/day per IP. A free API key raises the budget to $1/day and is required for cursor paging beyond the first page. Get one at https://openalex.org/settings/api.

openalex_api_key (and env ALETHECA_OPENALEX_API_KEY) is accepted at runtime as a deprecated alias for api_key; typed callers should pass api_key= directly.

docs.title: Resource clients
docs.text: Each resource client inherits the generic operations from bibliofabric.ResourceClient (get, search, iterate, collect, first, count, batch_get) through aletheca._async.dialect.OpenAlexResourceClient. Only class-specific members are shown here.

docs.title: aletheca._async.works.WorksClient
docs.text:
Bases: OpenAlexResourceClient[Work]

Client for the /works endpoint.

Adds the works-only query features: corpus/include_pulled/ include_parts, corpus-aware sample(), the scoped search.* parameters, and DOI-based batch retrieval.

docs.title: search(filters=None, *, query=None, sort=None, select=None, page=None, page_size=None, cursor=None, on_error='raise', failures=None, params=None, corpus=None, include_parts=None, include_pulled=None, rerank=False) async
docs.text:
Search works; accepts the works-only corpus controls.

corpus selects which works answer: core (default upstream) excludes pulled and part works, expansion is the expansion set, all is everything. include_parts/include_pulled re-add those subsets to core. Note that a is_pulled/is_retracted filter re-includes pulled works on its own.

rerank=True reorders the top 100 of a relevance-sorted search (costs 10 extra credits and requires the relevance sort a query gives you); page.meta["reranked"] reports whether it applied.

docs.title: search_scoped(text, *, scope='title_and_abstract', filters=None, params=None, **kwargs) async
docs.text:
Search works under one scoped search.* parameter.

Scopes: title, title_and_abstract, title_abstract_keywords, exact (supports wildcards and proximity operators), and semantic (embedding search; max 50 results, 1 request/second, and only its whitelisted filters combine). Only one search parameter is allowed per request; a search costs 10 credits.

docs.title: sample(n, *, seed=None, filters=None, query=None, sort=None, select=None, page=None, page_size=None, cursor=None, on_error='raise', failures=None, params=None, corpus=None, include_parts=None, include_pulled=None, rerank=False) async
docs.text:
Return a random sample of up to n works (max 10,000).

Pass seed for reproducibility, and works-only corpus / include_parts / include_pulled / rerank controls. Page.total reports the sample size, not the size of the filtered corpus.

docs.title: batch_get_by_doi(dois, *, batch_size=None) async
docs.text:
Fetch works by DOI, batched as pipe-joined OR filters.

DOIs are normalized (URL prefixes stripped, lowercased) and split into chunks of batch_size (default 100, the OpenAlex OR cap). Returns {normalized doi: Work}; DOIs not found are absent.

docs.text:
Return downloadable PDF URLs for a work, best OA copy first.

Reads pdf_url from best_oa_location, then primary_location, then the remaining locations; duplicates keep their first position. Returns [] when no location carries a PDF. OpenAlex's own paid PDF copies (content_urls.pdf) are not included.
