class BaseApiSettings(BaseSettings):
    """Tunable client behavior, loaded from environment variables and ``.env``."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore"
    )

    timeout: float = Field(default=30.0, gt=0)
    connect_timeout: float | None = Field(default=None, gt=0)
    """Optional TCP/TLS connect timeout in seconds (``> 0``); defaults to ``timeout``."""
    follow_redirects: bool = False
    """Whether owned ``httpx`` clients follow HTTP 3xx redirects."""
    max_retries: int = Field(default=3, ge=0)
    max_retry_wait: float = Field(default=60.0, ge=0)
    max_requests_per_second: float | None = Field(default=None, gt=0)
    """Requests per second of the ``"default"`` rate class."""
    max_concurrency: int = Field(default=10, gt=0)
    rate_limits: dict[str, float | None] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    """Requests per second per rate class (D-19).

    The ``"default"`` class comes from :attr:`max_requests_per_second`; keys
    here add further classes (for example ``{"single": 10.0, "list": 3.0}``)
    that a client's overridden ``rate_class`` assigns per request. Setting a
    class to ``None`` disables pacing for that class. Each class gets its own
    minimum-interval gate; the concurrency bound is shared.
    """
    user_agent: str | None = None
    mailto: str | None = None

    @field_validator(
        "timeout", "connect_timeout", "max_retry_wait", "max_requests_per_second"
    )
    @classmethod
    def _validate_finite_float(cls, value: float | None) -> float | None:
        if value is not None and not math.isfinite(value):
            raise ValueError("must be a finite number")
        return value

    @field_validator("rate_limits")
    @classmethod
    def _validate_rate_limits(
        cls, value: dict[str, float | None]
    ) -> dict[str, float | None]:
        for rate_class, rate in value.items():
            if rate is not None and (not math.isfinite(rate) or rate <= 0):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"rate_limits[{rate_class!r}] must be positive and finite or None, "
                    f"got {rate!r}"
                )
        return value

    def effective_user_agent(self) -> str:
        """Return ``user_agent`` or the default built from package metadata.

        The default has the form ``<package>/<version> (+<homepage>;
        mailto:<mailto>)``. ``mailto`` is included only when set, and the
        parenthesized part is omitted when neither homepage nor mailto exists.
        """
        if self.user_agent is not None:
            return self.user_agent
        package = type(self).__module__.partition(".")[0]
        version = "0.0.0"
        homepage = ""
        try:
            dist = distribution(package)
            version = dist.version
            for entry in dist.metadata.get_all("Project-URL") or []:
                name, _, url = entry.partition(",")
                if name.strip().lower() == "homepage":
                    homepage = url.strip()
                    break
            if not homepage:
                homepage = dist.metadata.get("Home-page") or ""
        except PackageNotFoundError:
            pass
        if homepage or self.mailto:
            inner = "; ".join(
                part
                for part in (homepage, f"mailto:{self.mailto}" if self.mailto else "")
                if part
            )
            return f"{package}/{version} (+{inner})"
        return f"{package}/{version}"

docs.title: Status mapping
docs.text:
request() and stream() raise on any status >= 400:

Status Exception 404 NotFoundError 429 RateLimitError (carries retry_after when sent) 401, 403 AuthError (carries body when JSON) others APIError

Network failures raise NetworkError; timeouts raise TimeoutError (also a builtin TimeoutError). Every exception exposes .status_code, .request, and .response when available. APIError and AuthError expose .body with the parsed JSON error payload and include a concise, sanitized summary of the upstream body in str(err), so callers see details like OpenAlex's reason=daily_budget immediately. Custom credential query parameters declared by an auth strategy (redacted_query_params) are scrubbed from both logs and exception strings.

docs.title: Retries
docs.text:
By default (retry=None), automatic retries apply to idempotent HTTP methods (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, DELETE) and cover 429, 500, 502, 503, 504, network failures, and timeouts, up to settings.max_retries (default 3, meaning four attempts). Non-idempotent methods (POST, PATCH) are not retried automatically unless the caller passes retry=True (for example on read-only POST batch endpoints). Pass retry=False to disable retries for a single call.

When the server sends Retry-After (seconds or HTTP date), the wait honors it capped at settings.max_retry_wait; otherwise the client uses jittered exponential backoff with the same cap.

For auth strategies that expose invalidate_token() (ClientCredentialsAuth, RefreshTokenAuth), HTTP 401 triggers one automatic token invalidation and retry before raising AuthError.

To veto retries, override is_retryable(response) on the client. A non- retryable 429 surfaces immediately as RateLimitError:

class FooClient(BaseApiClient):
    def is_retryable(self, response: httpx.Response) -> bool:
        if response.status_code == 429:
            try:
                body = response.json()
            except ValueError:
                body = None
            if isinstance(body, dict) and body.get("reason") == "daily_budget":
                return False
        return super().is_retryable(response)

Override on_response(response) to inspect every HTTP response (including rate-limit headers or timings) before error statuses are raised.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: Three settings throttle the client: max_requests_per_second sets the "default" rate class, rate_limits adds per-class rates (routed via rate_class(request)), and max_concurrency bounds requests in flight (default 10) and sizes the owned httpx connection pool. Set a class rate to None to disable spacing for that class. The limiter reserves each caller's pacing slot and sleeps before acquiring a concurrency slot, so waiting callers of one class never starve another class.

docs.title: Configuration and validation failures
docs.text:
Passing unsupported search parameters (query, select, sort, cursor, or page) for a resource's QueryDialect, or exceeding QueryDialect.max_offset, raises ConfigurationError immediately before any HTTP request is sent.

Records that fail pydantic validation raise ValidationError carrying the rejected payload in raw (use bibliofabric.validate_model() on custom endpoints for the same wrapping). search(), batch_get(), iterate(), and collect() can tolerate bad records with on_error="skip", failures=my_list; each skipped record is appended to failures as a (raw_record, exception) pair.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
All exceptions derive from BibliofabricError and carry the request and response of the failed call when available. APIError and its subclasses also carry body, the parsed JSON error payload (or None), so callers can read fields like OpenAlex's reason.

BibliofabricError
├── ConfigurationError
├── AuthError                 # 401/403, token fetch failure
├── NetworkError              # DNS failure, connection refused
├── TimeoutError              # also a builtin TimeoutError
├── ValidationError           # response record failed pydantic validation
└── APIError                  # other error statuses
    ├── NotFoundError         # 404
    └── RateLimitError        # 429

ValidationError carries raw (the rejected payload), error (the pydantic exception), and model_name. get() and search() raise it; iterate() raises it by default and drops bad records with on_error="skip", collecting them in failures.

Error strings redact credential query parameters such as api_key and token values from URLs.

class BibliofabricError(Exception):
    """Base class for all bibliofabric errors."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        message: str,
        *,
        request: httpx.Request | None = None,
        response: httpx.Response | None = None,
        redacted_query_params: Collection[str] = (),
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.message = message
        self.response = response
        self.request = request if request is not None else _extract_request(response)
        self._redacted_query_params: frozenset[str] = frozenset(redacted_query_params)

    @property
    def status_code(self) -> int | None:
        """HTTP status code of the response, when available."""
        return self.response.status_code if self.response is not None else None

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        extra = self._redacted_query_params
        message = sanitize_url(self.message, extra_params=extra)
        request = _extract_request(self.response) or self.request
        if self.response is not None:
            if request is not None:
                return (
                    f"{message} (status: {self.response.status_code}, "
                    f"URL: {sanitize_url(request.url, extra_params=extra)})"
                )
            return f"{message} (status: {self.response.status_code})"
        if request is not None:
            return f"{message} (URL: {sanitize_url(request.url, extra_params=extra)})"
        return message

def validate_model[M: BaseModel](
    model: type[M],
    data: Any,
    *,
    request: httpx.Request | None = None,
    response: httpx.Response | None = None,
) -> M:
    """Validate ``data`` against ``model``, wrapping failures in :class:`ValidationError`."""
    try:
        return model.model_validate(data)
    except PydanticValidationError as error:
        raise ValidationError(
            f"Failed to validate {model.__name__}: {error}",
            raw=data,
            error=error,
            model_name=model.__name__,
            request=request,
            response=response,
        ) from error

docs.title: bibliofabric.ids
docs.text:
Canonical identifier normalization shared by bibliofabric-family clients.

Clients add API-specific encoding on top of these normalizers; the normalizers themselves never URL-encode. Each one strips the resolver URLs and scheme prefixes its identifier is written with and returns the canonical form. A value that does not match the known shape comes back stripped and tidied, so unvetted API fields can pass through without raising.

Return the ISBN in ISBN-13 form without hyphens (9780306406157).

A valid ISBN-10 converts to its 978-prefixed ISBN-13 with a recomputed check digit. Any other value comes back compacted: hyphens and spaces removed, uppercased.

def normalize_isbn(value: str) -> str:
    """Return the ISBN in ISBN-13 form without hyphens (``9780306406157``).

    A valid ISBN-10 converts to its ``978``-prefixed ISBN-13 with a recomputed
    check digit. Any other value comes back compacted: hyphens and spaces
    removed, uppercased.
    """
    compact = _compact(strip_url_prefix(value, _ISBN_PREFIXES))
    if not _is_valid_isbn_10(compact):
        return compact
    stem = f"978{compact[:-1]}"
    return f"{stem}{_isbn_13_check_digit(stem)}"

        and compact[:-1].isdigit()

def strip_url_prefix(value: str, prefixes: Iterable[str]) -> str:
    """Remove the first matching prefix (case-insensitive) and trim whitespace."""
    stripped = value.strip()
    for prefix in prefixes:
        if stripped.lower().startswith(prefix.lower()):
            return stripped[len(prefix) :].strip()
    return stripped

docs.title: Paging
docs.text:
Paging behavior is declared once per API in a frozen QueryDialect and shared by all resource clients of that API (or overridden per instance via ResourceClient(..., dialect=...)).

DIALECT = QueryDialect(
    page_size_param="per_page",  # None for unpaged APIs (e.g. OpenCitations)
    max_page_size=200,
    default_page_size=25,
    page_param="page",  # None when the API has no page numbers
    page_start=1,  # 0 for OpenAIRE links and Scholix
    offset_param=None,  # "offset" for Crossref; replaces page_param
    max_offset=None,  # optional cap enforced on page/offset paging
    cursor_param=None,  # "cursor" enables cursor paging
    cursor_start="*",
    sort_param="sort",
    query_param=None,  # free-text search parameter
    select_param=None,  # field selection parameter
    iterate_page_size=100,  # page size iterate() uses when the caller passes none; falls back to default_page_size
    count_page_size=0,  # page size count() requests; 0 for APIs that return totals with zero rows
)

iterate() uses cursor paging when cursor_param is set; otherwise it walks page numbers (page_param) or offsets (offset_param, where page N becomes offset=(N - page_start) * page_size). When page_param, offset_param, and cursor_param are all None, iterate() fetches once and stops.

Passing query, select, sort, cursor, or page when the corresponding dialect parameter is None, or exceeding max_offset in page/offset mode, raises ConfigurationError before sending any request.

search() returns a generic Page[E]:

Field Meaning results Validated entities total Total matches, or None when the API does not report it next_cursor Cursor for the next page, or None page The requested page number meta The raw envelope minus the results (facets, group-by)

docs.title: QueryDialect dataclass
docs.text:
Declares the query parameter names and paging rules of an API.

Set a parameter name to None when the API does not support the feature: page_size_param=None omits the page-size parameter (for example unpaged APIs such as OpenCitations), page_param=None means the API has no page numbers, offset_param routes paging through an offset instead, max_offset caps page/offset depth, and cursor_param enables cursor paging, which takes precedence over page and offset paging in iterate(). Set cursor_start=None for APIs whose first cursor request omits the cursor parameter (e.g. token-based bulk search).

Source code in packages/bibliofabric/src/bibliofabric/paging.py 
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class QueryDialect:
    """Declares the query parameter names and paging rules of an API.

    Set a parameter name to ``None`` when the API does not support the
    feature: ``page_size_param=None`` omits the page-size parameter (for
    example unpaged APIs such as OpenCitations), ``page_param=None`` means
    the API has no page numbers, ``offset_param`` routes paging through an
    offset instead, ``max_offset`` caps page/offset depth, and
    ``cursor_param`` enables cursor paging, which takes precedence over page
    and offset paging in ``iterate()``. Set ``cursor_start=None`` for APIs
    whose first cursor request omits the cursor parameter (e.g. token-based
    bulk search).
    """

    page_size_param: str | None = "per_page"
    max_page_size: int = 100
    default_page_size: int = 25
    iterate_page_size: int | None = None
    """Page size ``iterate()`` uses when the caller passes none; falls back to ``default_page_size``."""
    count_page_size: int = 1
    """Page size ``count()`` requests (e.g. ``0`` for APIs supporting zero-row count queries)."""
    page_param: str | None = "page"
    page_start: int = 1
    offset_param: str | None = None
    max_offset: int | None = None
    """Maximum allowed offset for page/offset paging; ``None`` means unbounded."""
    cursor_param: str | None = None
    cursor_start: str | None = "*"
    sort_param: str | None = "sort"
    query_param: str | None = None
    select_param: str | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.max_page_size <= 0:
            raise ConfigurationError(
                f"QueryDialect.max_page_size must be positive, got {self.max_page_size}."
            )
        if not 0 < self.default_page_size <= self.max_page_size:
            raise ConfigurationError(
                f"QueryDialect.default_page_size must be between 1 and "
                f"{self.max_page_size}, got {self.default_page_size}."
            )
        if (
            self.iterate_page_size is not None
            and not 0 < self.iterate_page_size <= self.max_page_size
        ):
            raise ConfigurationError(
                f"QueryDialect.iterate_page_size must be between 1 and "
                f"{self.max_page_size}, got {self.iterate_page_size}."
            )
        if not 0 <= self.count_page_size <= self.max_page_size:
            raise ConfigurationError(
                f"QueryDialect.count_page_size must be between 0 and "
                f"{self.max_page_size}, got {self.count_page_size}."
            )
        if self.max_offset is not None and self.max_offset <= 0:
            raise ConfigurationError(
                f"QueryDialect.max_offset must be positive, got {self.max_offset}."
            )

docs.title: Resources
docs.text:
ResourceClient[E] is a generic client for one API endpoint. Declare the endpoint path, the entity model, and the query dialect; override hook methods where the API deviates from the defaults. Both path= and dialect= may also be overridden per instance in the constructor.

class Works(ResourceClient[Work]):
    path = "works"
    model = Work
    dialect = DIALECT

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
• get(id, *, select=None, params=None) fetches one entity (str or int id); a 404 raises NotFoundError.
  • exists(id) sends a HEAD request and returns True or False (on 404).
  • search(filters, ..., on_error="raise", failures=None) fetches one page and returns a Page[E] with results, total, next_cursor, page, and meta. Filters accept a pydantic model or a plain dict. Passing unsupported dialect parameters (query, select, sort, cursor, or page) or exceeding dialect.max_offset raises ConfigurationError before any request is sent.
  • iterate(...) yields entities across pages. It uses cursor paging when the dialect has a cursor_param, otherwise page or offset paging (or fetches once for unpaged dialects where page_param and offset_param are None). It stops at limit, on an empty page, or when there is no next cursor. on_page(page_number, next_cursor) checkpoints progress; passing a saved cursor back via cursor= resumes a cursor-mode harvest.
  • first(...) returns the first matching entity (defaulting page_size=1), or None.
  • count() reads the unwrapper total from a minimal page.
  • batch_get(ids, field="id", select=None, batch_size=None, concurrency=4, on_error="raise", failures=None) normalizes and deduplicates ids, fetches them in concurrent chunks (capped at dialect.max_page_size), and returns a dict keyed by normalized id. Missing ids are absent from the result.

On the default on_error="raise" path, search(), batch_get(), and iterate() bulk-validate each page or chunk with a lazily cached TypeAdapter(list[E]) per subclass, falling back to per-record validation only when a record fails so ValidationError.raw still attaches the offending record.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
Override these methods on subclasses:

  • build_filter_params(filters) — filter serialization (OpenAlex joins filters into one filter parameter).
  • format_sort(sort) — sort parameter shape (Crossref splits sort/order).
  • build_batch_params(field, values) — batch OR syntax (OpenAlex and OpenAIRE use pipe-separated values in one filter parameter; Crossref repeats keys like doi:a,doi:b).
  • _fetch_batch_chunk(field, chunk, *, select=None) — chunk transport for batch_get; override for POST-batch APIs (such as Semantic Scholar) or path-encoded batch endpoints while keeping chunking, deduplication, concurrency, validation, on_error/failures, and keying.
  • normalize_id(value) — canonical identifier form (DOIs via bibliofabric.ids.normalize_doi).
  • record_keys(entity, field) — normalized keys an entity matches in batch_get.
  • item_path(id) — single-entity path; the default URL-encodes the id.
  • default_params() — query parameters sent with every list request (search(), iterate(), count(), and each batch_get chunk). Returns {} by default. Filter parameters and caller-supplied params= take precedence, so the hook is for API-wide requirements such as Europe PMC's format=json.
  • search_path(query) — route for search, iterate(), count(), and batch requests. The default returns self.path. Override it for APIs that carry the query in the path (DOAJ's /search/journals/{query}). With such an override, query= is accepted even when dialect.query_param is None; otherwise that combination raises ConfigurationError. query is None for count() without a query and for batch chunks.

params= is the escape hatch for API extras (facets, sample, seed); typed wrappers for those belong on resource subclasses.

docs.title: bibliofabric._async.resources
docs.text:
Generic typed resource client over a BaseApiClient.

Subclass :class:ResourceClient per endpoint: declare path, model, and dialect, then override the hook methods where the API deviates from the defaults (filter syntax, sort format, batch parameter shape, constant query parameters, list route, id handling).

docs.title: ResourceClient
docs.text:
Typed client for one API resource.

Class attributes:

  • path: endpoint path relative to the client's base URL, e.g. "works". Pass path= to the constructor for routes bound to a parent id, e.g. "members/297/works".
  • model: the pydantic model a single entity validates against.
  • dialect: the :class:QueryDialect of the API (usually shared); may also be overridden per instance via dialect=.
  • filters_model: optional declaration of the accepted filter model.
  • batch_size: ids per batch_get chunk; 0 disables batch_get.
Source code in packages/bibliofabric/src/bibliofabric/_async/resources.py 
class ResourceClient[E: BaseModel]:
    """Typed client for one API resource.

    Class attributes:

    - ``path``: endpoint path relative to the client's base URL, e.g. ``"works"``.
      Pass ``path=`` to the constructor for routes bound to a parent id,
      e.g. ``"members/297/works"``.
    - ``model``: the pydantic model a single entity validates against.
    - ``dialect``: the :class:`QueryDialect` of the API (usually shared); may
      also be overridden per instance via ``dialect=``.
    - ``filters_model``: optional declaration of the accepted filter model.
    - ``batch_size``: ids per ``batch_get`` chunk; ``0`` disables ``batch_get``.
    """

    path: str
    model: type[E]
    dialect: ClassVar[QueryDialect]
    filters_model: ClassVar[type[BaseModel] | None] = None
    batch_size: ClassVar[int] = 50
    _list_adapter: ClassVar[TypeAdapter[Any] | None] = None
    _list_adapter_model: ClassVar[type[BaseModel] | None] = None

    def __init__(
        self,
        client: BaseApiClient,
        *,
        path: str | None = None,
        dialect: QueryDialect | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._client = client
        if path is not None:
            self.path = path
        if dialect is not None:
            self.__dict__["dialect"] = dialect

    # --- hooks ---------------------------------------------------------

    def build_filter_params(
        self, filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None
    ) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Convert filter criteria into query parameters.

        The default dumps pydantic models (excluding ``None`` fields, using
        aliases), skips ``None`` entries in plain mappings, formats booleans as
        lowercase ``"true"``/``"false"``, and stringifies other values. Override
        for APIs that encode filters as a single structured parameter.
        """
        if filters is None:
            return {}
        if isinstance(filters, BaseModel):
            dumped = filters.model_dump(exclude_none=True, by_alias=True)
        else:
            dumped = {key: value for key, value in filters.items() if value is not None}
        params: dict[str, str] = {}
        for key, value in dumped.items():
            if isinstance(value, bool):
                params[str(key)] = "true" if value else "false"
            elif isinstance(value, str):
                params[str(key)] = value
            else:
                params[str(key)] = str(value)
        return params

    def format_sort(self, sort: str | Sequence[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Convert a sort request into query parameters.

        The default sends ``<sort_param>: <value>``, joining sequences with a
        comma. Override for APIs that split field and direction into separate
        parameters (e.g. ``{"sort": "score", "order": "desc"}``).
        """
        if self.dialect.sort_param is None:
            return {}
        value = sort if isinstance(sort, str) else ",".join(sort)
        return {self.dialect.sort_param: value}

    def build_batch_params(self, field: str, values: Sequence[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Build the query parameters for one ``batch_get`` chunk.

        The default repeats the key once per value. Override for APIs that
        require an OR-list syntax in a single parameter.
        """
        return {field: list(values)}

    def default_params(self) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
        """Query parameters sent with every list, ``count()``, and batch request.

        Override for APIs that need a constant parameter on list routes (for
        example Europe PMC's ``format=json``, whose default is XML). Filter
        parameters and caller-supplied ``params`` take precedence.
        """
        return {}

    def search_path(self, query: str | None) -> str:
        """Return the list route for a search, ``count()``, or batch request.

        The default is :attr:`path`. Override for APIs that carry the query in
        the path instead of a query parameter (for example DOAJ's
        ``/search/journals/{query}``). Such an override makes ``query=``
        valid on a dialect whose ``query_param`` is ``None``. ``query`` is
        ``None`` for ``count()`` without one and for batch chunks.
        """
        return self.path

    async def _fetch_batch_chunk(
        self,
        field: str,
        chunk: list[str],
        *,
        select: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], httpx.Response]:
        """Fetch raw records for one ``batch_get`` chunk.

        The default issues a ``GET`` using :meth:`build_batch_params` and
        unwraps records via ``unwrapper.results``. Override for APIs that use
        ``POST`` batch bodies (for example Semantic Scholar) or path-encoded
        batch endpoints while inheriting chunking, deduplication, concurrency,
        validation, ``on_error`` handling, and keying from :meth:`batch_get`.
        """
        query_params: dict[str, Any] = {
            **self.default_params(),
            **self.build_batch_params(field, chunk),
        }
        if self.dialect.page_size_param is not None:
            query_params[self.dialect.page_size_param] = len(chunk)
        if select is not None:
            if self.dialect.select_param is None:
                raise ConfigurationError(
                    f"{type(self).__name__} does not support field selection "
                    "(dialect.select_param is None)."
                )
            if select:
                query_params[self.dialect.select_param] = ",".join(select)
        response = await self._client.request(
            "GET", self.search_path(None), params=query_params
        )
        records = self._client.unwrapper.results(self._client.parse_json(response))
        return records, response

    def normalize_id(self, value: str) -> str:
        """Canonicalize an identifier before use in paths, batches, and keys."""
        return value.strip()

    def record_keys(self, entity: E, field: str) -> list[str]:
        """Return every normalized ``field`` value of ``entity``.

        ``batch_get`` keys each entity by whichever of these values was
        requested, so records carrying several ids (for example deduplicated
        records with many DOIs) land under the id the caller asked for.
        Override when the values live somewhere other than ``entity.<field>``.
        """
        value = getattr(entity, field, None)
        if value is None:
            value = getattr(entity, "id", None)
        values = value if isinstance(value, list) else [value]
        return [self.normalize_id(str(item)) for item in values if item is not None]

    def item_path(self, id: str | int) -> str:
        """Return the single-entity path for ``id``, URL-encoding it."""
        normalized = self.normalize_id(str(id))
        if not normalized:
            raise ConfigurationError(
                f"{type(self).__name__}.item_path requires a non-empty id."
            )
        return f"{self.path.rstrip('/')}/{quote(normalized, safe='')}"

    # --- operations ----------------------------------------------------

    async def get(
        self,
        id: str | int,
        *,
        select: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> E:
        """Fetch one entity by id; 404 raises :class:`NotFoundError`."""
        query_params: dict[str, Any] = {}
        if select is not None:
            if self.dialect.select_param is None:
                raise ConfigurationError(
                    f"{type(self).__name__} does not support field selection "
                    "(dialect.select_param is None)."
                )
            if select:
                query_params[self.dialect.select_param] = ",".join(select)
        if params is not None:
            query_params.update(params)
        response = await self._client.request(
            "GET",
            self.item_path(id),
            params=query_params or None,
        )
        body = self._client.parse_json(response)
        data = self._client.unwrapper.item(body)
        return self._validate(
            data, request=_response_request(response), response=response
        )

    async def exists(self, id: str | int) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` when ``id`` exists (HTTP HEAD); 404 returns ``False``."""
        try:
            await self._client.request("HEAD", self.item_path(id))
        except NotFoundError:
            return False
        return True

    async def search(
        self,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        query: str | None = None,
        sort: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
        select: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        page: int | None = None,
        page_size: int | None = None,
        cursor: str | None = None,
        on_error: OnError = "raise",
        failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> Page[E]:
        """Fetch one page of results as a typed :class:`Page`.

        ``params`` is the escape hatch for API extras (facets, ``sample``,
        ``seed``); typed wrappers for them belong on client subclasses.
        Records that fail validation raise :class:`ValidationError` by default,
        or are skipped and recorded in ``failures`` with ``on_error="skip"``.
        """
        _check_on_error(on_error)
        query_params = self._search_params(
            filters=filters,
            query=query,
            sort=sort,
            select=select,
            page=page,
            page_size=page_size,
            cursor=cursor,
            params=params,
        )
        response = await self._client.request(
            "GET", self.search_path(query), params=query_params
        )
        body = self._client.parse_json(response)
        unwrapper = self._client.unwrapper
        results = self._validate_records(
            unwrapper.results(body),
            on_error=on_error,
            failures=failures,
            request=_response_request(response),
            response=response,
        )
        effective_page = page
        if (
            effective_page is None
            and cursor is None
            and (
                self.dialect.offset_param is not None
                or self.dialect.page_param is not None
            )
        ):
            effective_page = self.dialect.page_start
        return Page(
            results=results,
            total=unwrapper.total(body),
            next_cursor=unwrapper.next_cursor(body),
            page=effective_page,
            meta=unwrapper.meta(body),
        )

    def iterate(
        self,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        query: str | None = None,
        sort: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
        select: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        page_size: int | None = None,
        limit: int | None = None,
        cursor: str | None = None,
        on_error: OnError = "raise",
        failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] | None = None,
        on_page: Callable[[int, str | None], Any] | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> AsyncIterator[E]:
        """Iterate over all matching entities.

        Uses cursor paging when ``dialect.cursor_param`` is set, otherwise page
        or offset paging. Stops at ``limit``, on an empty page, or when the
        unwrapper reports no next cursor. ``on_page(page_number, next_cursor)``
        checkpoints progress; passing a saved cursor back via ``cursor=``
        resumes a cursor-mode harvest. Records that fail validation raise
        :class:`ValidationError`, or are dropped and recorded in ``failures``
        with ``on_error="skip"``.
        """
        _check_on_error(on_error)
        if limit is not None and limit < 0:
            raise ConfigurationError(f"limit must be non-negative, got {limit}.")
        if cursor is not None and self.dialect.cursor_param is None:
            raise ConfigurationError(
                f"{type(self).__name__} does not support cursor paging "
                "(dialect.cursor_param is None)."
            )
        if self.dialect.cursor_param is not None:
            return self._iterate_cursor(
                filters=filters,
                query=query,
                sort=sort,
                select=select,
                page_size=page_size,
                limit=limit,
                cursor=cursor,
                on_error=on_error,
                failures=failures,
                on_page=on_page,
                params=params,
            )
        return self._iterate_pages(
            filters=filters,
            query=query,
            sort=sort,
            select=select,
            page_size=page_size,
            limit=limit,
            on_error=on_error,
            failures=failures,
            on_page=on_page,
            params=params,
        )

    async def collect(
        self,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        limit: int | None = None,
        query: str | None = None,
        sort: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
        select: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        page_size: int | None = None,
        cursor: str | None = None,
        on_error: OnError = "raise",
        failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] | None = None,
        on_page: Callable[[int, str | None], Any] | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> list[E]:
        """Collect ``iterate()`` output into a list, optionally bounded."""
        collected: list[E] = [
            entity
            async for entity in self.iterate(
                filters,
                query=query,
                sort=sort,
                select=select,
                page_size=page_size,
                limit=limit,
                cursor=cursor,
                on_error=on_error,
                failures=failures,
                on_page=on_page,
                params=params,
            )
        ]
        return collected

    async def first(
        self,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        query: str | None = None,
        sort: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
        select: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        page_size: int | None = 1,
        cursor: str | None = None,
        on_error: OnError = "raise",
        failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> E | None:
        """Return the first matching entity, or ``None`` when there is none."""
        results = await self.collect(
            filters,
            limit=1,
            query=query,
            sort=sort,
            select=select,
            page_size=page_size,
            cursor=cursor,
            on_error=on_error,
            failures=failures,
            params=params,
        )
        return results[0] if results else None

    async def count(
        self,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        query: str | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> int:
        """Return the total number of matching entities, fetching a minimal page."""
        dialect = self.dialect
        cursor = (
            dialect.cursor_start
            if dialect.cursor_param is not None
            and dialect.page_param is None
            and dialect.offset_param is None
            else None
        )
        query_params = self._search_params(
            filters=filters,
            query=query,
            page_size=dialect.count_page_size,
            cursor=cursor,
            params=params,
        )
        response = await self._client.request(
            "GET", self.search_path(query), params=query_params
        )
        return self._client.unwrapper.total(self._client.parse_json(response)) or 0

    async def batch_get(
        self,
        ids: Sequence[str],
        *,
        field: str = "id",
        select: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        batch_size: int | None = None,
        concurrency: int = 4,
        on_error: OnError = "raise",
        failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, E]:
        """Fetch entities for many ids in bounded, concurrent chunks.

        Ids are normalized with :meth:`normalize_id` and deduplicated, split
        into chunks of ``batch_size`` (capped at ``dialect.max_page_size``),
        fetched concurrently under ``concurrency``, and returned keyed by
        normalized id. Missing ids are absent from the result. Each entity is
        keyed by the requested ids found among :meth:`record_keys`. Records
        that fail validation raise :class:`ValidationError` by default, or are
        skipped and recorded in ``failures`` with ``on_error="skip"``.
        """
        _check_on_error(on_error)
        if batch_size is None:
            size = self.batch_size
            if size <= 0:
                raise ConfigurationError(
                    f"{type(self).__name__}.batch_get is disabled (batch_size={size})."
                )
        else:
            if batch_size <= 0:
                raise ConfigurationError(
                    f"batch_size must be positive, got {batch_size}."
                )
            size = batch_size
        if concurrency <= 0:
            raise ConfigurationError(
                f"concurrency must be positive, got {concurrency}."
            )
        effective_size = min(size, self.dialect.max_page_size)
        keys = list(dict.fromkeys(self.normalize_id(value) for value in ids))
        if not keys:
            return {}
        chunks = [
            keys[start : start + effective_size]
            for start in range(0, len(keys), effective_size)
        ]

        async def fetch_chunk(
            chunk: list[str],
        ) -> tuple[dict[str, E], list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]]]:
            records, response = await self._fetch_batch_chunk(
                field, chunk, select=select
            )
            requested = set(chunk)
            chunk_results: dict[str, E] = {}
            chunk_failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] = []
            entities = self._validate_records(
                records,
                on_error=on_error,
                failures=chunk_failures if failures is not None else None,
                request=_response_request(response),
                response=response,
            )
            for entity in entities:
                for key in self.record_keys(entity, field):
                    if key in requested:
                        chunk_results[key] = entity
            return chunk_results, chunk_failures

        chunk_outputs = await run_bounded(fetch_chunk, chunks, concurrency)
        results: dict[str, E] = {}
        for chunk_results, chunk_failures in chunk_outputs:
            results.update(chunk_results)
            if failures is not None:
                failures.extend(chunk_failures)
        return results

    # --- internals -----------------------------------------------------

    def _search_params(
        self,
        *,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None,
        query: str | None = None,
        sort: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
        select: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        page: int | None = None,
        page_size: int | None = None,
        cursor: str | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        dialect = self.dialect
        if isinstance(filters, str):
            raise ConfigurationError(
                f"Got a string as filters ({filters!r}). Pass search text as "
                f"query={filters!r}; filters takes a filter model or a mapping."
            )
        if cursor is not None and dialect.cursor_param is None:
            raise ConfigurationError(
                f"{type(self).__name__} does not support cursor paging "
                "(dialect.cursor_param is None)."
            )
        if (
            page is not None
            and dialect.page_param is None
            and dialect.offset_param is None
        ):
            raise ConfigurationError(
                f"{type(self).__name__} does not support page/offset paging "
                "(dialect.page_param and dialect.offset_param are both None)."
            )
        if (
            query is not None
            and dialect.query_param is None
            and self.search_path(query) == self.search_path(None)
        ):
            raise ConfigurationError(
                f"{type(self).__name__} does not support free-text query "
                "(dialect.query_param is None and search_path ignores it)."
            )
        if select is not None and dialect.select_param is None:
            raise ConfigurationError(
                f"{type(self).__name__} does not support field selection "
                "(dialect.select_param is None)."
            )
        if sort is not None and dialect.sort_param is None:
            raise ConfigurationError(
                f"{type(self).__name__} does not support sorting "
                "(dialect.sort_param is None)."
            )
        query_params: dict[str, Any] = {
            **self.default_params(),
            **self.build_filter_params(filters),
        }
        size = (
            dialect.default_page_size
            if page_size is None
            else min(page_size, dialect.max_page_size)
        )
        if dialect.page_size_param is not None:
            query_params[dialect.page_size_param] = size
        if cursor is not None and dialect.cursor_param is not None:
            query_params[dialect.cursor_param] = cursor
        elif dialect.offset_param is not None:
            effective_page = dialect.page_start if page is None else page
            offset = (effective_page - dialect.page_start) * size
            if dialect.max_offset is not None and offset > dialect.max_offset:
                raise ConfigurationError(
                    f"Requested offset {offset} exceeds QueryDialect.max_offset "
                    f"({dialect.max_offset})."
                )
            query_params[dialect.offset_param] = offset
        elif dialect.page_param is not None:
            effective_page = dialect.page_start if page is None else page
            offset = (effective_page - dialect.page_start) * size
            if dialect.max_offset is not None and offset > dialect.max_offset:
                raise ConfigurationError(
                    f"Requested offset {offset} exceeds QueryDialect.max_offset "
                    f"({dialect.max_offset})."
                )
            query_params[dialect.page_param] = effective_page
        if query is not None and dialect.query_param is not None:
            query_params[dialect.query_param] = query
        if select and dialect.select_param is not None:
            query_params[dialect.select_param] = ",".join(select)
        if sort is not None:
            query_params.update(self.format_sort(sort))
        if params is not None:
            query_params.update(params)
        return query_params

    def _get_list_adapter(self) -> TypeAdapter[list[E]]:
        cls = type(self)
        adapter = cls.__dict__.get("_list_adapter")
        if adapter is None or cls.__dict__.get("_list_adapter_model") is not self.model:
            list_type: Any = GenericAlias(list, (self.model,))
            adapter = TypeAdapter(list_type)
            cls._list_adapter = adapter
            cls._list_adapter_model = self.model
        return cast(TypeAdapter[list[E]], adapter)

    def _validate(
        self,
        data: dict[str, Any],
        *,
        request: httpx.Request | None = None,
        response: httpx.Response | None = None,
    ) -> E:
        return validate_model(self.model, data, request=request, response=response)

    def _validate_records(
        self,
        records: list[dict[str, Any]],
        *,
        on_error: OnError,
        failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] | None,
        request: httpx.Request | None = None,
        response: httpx.Response | None = None,
    ) -> list[E]:
        """Validate a page or chunk of records.

        Uses the lazily cached ``TypeAdapter(list[E])`` on the ``on_error="raise"``
        fast path, falling back to per-record :meth:`_validate` only when
        validation fails so ``ValidationError.raw`` still carries the offending
        record.
        """
        if not records:
            return []
        if on_error == "raise":
            try:
                return self._get_list_adapter().validate_python(records)
            except PydanticValidationError:
                for record in records:
                    self._validate(record, request=request, response=response)
                raise  # pragma: no cover
        validated: list[E] = []
        for record in records:
            entity = self._parse_or_handle(
                record,
                on_error=on_error,
                failures=failures,
                request=request,
                response=response,
            )
            if entity is not None:
                validated.append(entity)
        return validated

    def _parse_or_handle(
        self,
        record: dict[str, Any],
        *,
        on_error: OnError,
        failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] | None,
        request: httpx.Request | None = None,
        response: httpx.Response | None = None,
    ) -> E | None:
        """Validate a record; on failure raise, or skip and record it."""
        try:
            return self.model.model_validate(record)
        except PydanticValidationError as error:
            if on_error == "skip":
                if failures is not None:
                    failures.append((record, error))
                logger.warning(
                    "Skipping record that failed %s validation: %s",
                    self.model.__name__,
                    error,
                )
                return None
            return validate_model(
                self.model, record, request=request, response=response
            )

    async def _iterate_cursor(
        self,
        *,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None,
        query: str | None,
        sort: str | Sequence[str] | None,
        select: Sequence[str] | None,
        page_size: int | None,
        limit: int | None,
        cursor: str | None,
        on_error: OnError,
        failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] | None,
        on_page: Callable[[int, str | None], Any] | None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None,
    ) -> AsyncIterator[E]:
        if limit == 0:
            return
        dialect = self.dialect
        if page_size is None:
            page_size = dialect.iterate_page_size
        current = cursor if cursor is not None else dialect.cursor_start
        page_number = 0
        fetched = 0
        while True:
            query_params = self._search_params(
                filters=filters,
                query=query,
                sort=sort,
                select=select,
                page=None,
                page_size=page_size,
                cursor=current,
                params=params,
            )
            response = await self._client.request(
                "GET", self.search_path(query), params=query_params
            )
            body = self._client.parse_json(response)
            unwrapper = self._client.unwrapper
            results = unwrapper.results(body)
            next_cursor = unwrapper.next_cursor(body)
            if next_cursor == current:  # Solr-style APIs echo the cursor when exhausted
                next_cursor = None
            page_number += 1
            stopped = False
            req = _response_request(response)
            if on_error == "raise":
                batch = results[: limit - fetched] if limit is not None else results
                entities = self._validate_records(
                    batch,
                    on_error="raise",
                    failures=None,
                    request=req,
                    response=response,
                )
                for entity in entities:
                    yield entity
                    fetched += 1
                    if limit is not None and fetched >= limit:
                        stopped = True
                        break
            else:
                for record in results:
                    entity = self._parse_or_handle(
                        record,
                        on_error=on_error,
                        failures=failures,
                        request=req,
                        response=response,
                    )
                    if entity is None:
                        continue
                    yield entity
                    fetched += 1
                    if limit is not None and fetched >= limit:
                        stopped = True
                        break
            await _fire_on_page(on_page, page_number, next_cursor)
            if stopped or not results or next_cursor is None:
                return
            current = next_cursor

    async def _iterate_pages(
        self,
        *,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None,
        query: str | None,
        sort: str | Sequence[str] | None,
        select: Sequence[str] | None,
        page_size: int | None,
        limit: int | None,
        on_error: OnError,
        failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] | None,
        on_page: Callable[[int, str | None], Any] | None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None,
    ) -> AsyncIterator[E]:
        if limit == 0:
            return
        if page_size is None:
            page_size = self.dialect.iterate_page_size
        has_paging = (
            self.dialect.page_param is not None or self.dialect.offset_param is not None
        )
        page = self.dialect.page_start
        fetched = 0
        seen = 0
        while True:
            query_params = self._search_params(
                filters=filters,
                query=query,
                sort=sort,
                select=select,
                page=page if has_paging else None,
                page_size=page_size,
                params=params,
            )
            response = await self._client.request(
                "GET", self.search_path(query), params=query_params
            )
            body = self._client.parse_json(response)
            unwrapper = self._client.unwrapper
            results = unwrapper.results(body)
            total = unwrapper.total(body)
            seen += len(results)
            stopped = False
            req = _response_request(response)
            if on_error == "raise":
                batch = results[: limit - fetched] if limit is not None else results
                entities = self._validate_records(
                    batch,
                    on_error="raise",
                    failures=None,
                    request=req,
                    response=response,
                )
                for entity in entities:
                    yield entity
                    fetched += 1
                    if limit is not None and fetched >= limit:
                        stopped = True
                        break
            else:
                for record in results:
                    entity = self._parse_or_handle(
                        record,
                        on_error=on_error,
                        failures=failures,
                        request=req,
                        response=response,
                    )
                    if entity is None:
                        continue
                    yield entity
                    fetched += 1
                    if limit is not None and fetched >= limit:
                        stopped = True
                        break
            await _fire_on_page(on_page, page, None)
            if (
                stopped
                or not has_paging
                or not results
                or (total is not None and seen >= total)
            ):
                return
            page += 1

async def batch_get(
    self,
    ids: Sequence[str],
    *,
    field: str = "id",
    select: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    batch_size: int | None = None,
    concurrency: int = 4,
    on_error: OnError = "raise",
    failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, E]:
    """Fetch entities for many ids in bounded, concurrent chunks.

    Ids are normalized with :meth:`normalize_id` and deduplicated, split
    into chunks of ``batch_size`` (capped at ``dialect.max_page_size``),
    fetched concurrently under ``concurrency``, and returned keyed by
    normalized id. Missing ids are absent from the result. Each entity is
    keyed by the requested ids found among :meth:`record_keys`. Records
    that fail validation raise :class:`ValidationError` by default, or are
    skipped and recorded in ``failures`` with ``on_error="skip"``.
    """
    _check_on_error(on_error)
    if batch_size is None:
        size = self.batch_size
        if size <= 0:
            raise ConfigurationError(
                f"{type(self).__name__}.batch_get is disabled (batch_size={size})."
            )
    else:
        if batch_size <= 0:
            raise ConfigurationError(
                f"batch_size must be positive, got {batch_size}."
            )
        size = batch_size
    if concurrency <= 0:
        raise ConfigurationError(
            f"concurrency must be positive, got {concurrency}."
        )
    effective_size = min(size, self.dialect.max_page_size)
    keys = list(dict.fromkeys(self.normalize_id(value) for value in ids))
    if not keys:
        return {}
    chunks = [
        keys[start : start + effective_size]
        for start in range(0, len(keys), effective_size)
    ]

    async def fetch_chunk(
        chunk: list[str],
    ) -> tuple[dict[str, E], list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]]]:
        records, response = await self._fetch_batch_chunk(
            field, chunk, select=select
        )
        requested = set(chunk)
        chunk_results: dict[str, E] = {}
        chunk_failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] = []
        entities = self._validate_records(
            records,
            on_error=on_error,
            failures=chunk_failures if failures is not None else None,
            request=_response_request(response),
            response=response,
        )
        for entity in entities:
            for key in self.record_keys(entity, field):
                if key in requested:
                    chunk_results[key] = entity
        return chunk_results, chunk_failures

    chunk_outputs = await run_bounded(fetch_chunk, chunks, concurrency)
    results: dict[str, E] = {}
    for chunk_results, chunk_failures in chunk_outputs:
        results.update(chunk_results)
        if failures is not None:
            failures.extend(chunk_failures)
    return results

def build_filter_params(
    self, filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Convert filter criteria into query parameters.

    The default dumps pydantic models (excluding ``None`` fields, using
    aliases), skips ``None`` entries in plain mappings, formats booleans as
    lowercase ``"true"``/``"false"``, and stringifies other values. Override
    for APIs that encode filters as a single structured parameter.
    """
    if filters is None:
        return {}
    if isinstance(filters, BaseModel):
        dumped = filters.model_dump(exclude_none=True, by_alias=True)
    else:
        dumped = {key: value for key, value in filters.items() if value is not None}
    params: dict[str, str] = {}
    for key, value in dumped.items():
        if isinstance(value, bool):
            params[str(key)] = "true" if value else "false"
        elif isinstance(value, str):
            params[str(key)] = value
        else:
            params[str(key)] = str(value)
    return params

async def count(
    self,
    filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    *,
    query: str | None = None,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Return the total number of matching entities, fetching a minimal page."""
    dialect = self.dialect
    cursor = (
        dialect.cursor_start
        if dialect.cursor_param is not None
        and dialect.page_param is None
        and dialect.offset_param is None
        else None
    )
    query_params = self._search_params(
        filters=filters,
        query=query,
        page_size=dialect.count_page_size,
        cursor=cursor,
        params=params,
    )
    response = await self._client.request(
        "GET", self.search_path(query), params=query_params
    )
    return self._client.unwrapper.total(self._client.parse_json(response)) or 0

def format_sort(self, sort: str | Sequence[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Convert a sort request into query parameters.

    comma. Override for APIs that split field and direction into separate

Iterate over all matching entities.

Uses cursor paging when dialect.cursor_param is set, otherwise page or offset paging. Stops at limit, on an empty page, or when the unwrapper reports no next cursor. on_page(page_number, next_cursor) checkpoints progress; passing a saved cursor back via cursor= resumes a cursor-mode harvest. Records that fail validation raise :class:ValidationError, or are dropped and recorded in failures with on_error="skip".

def iterate(
    self,
    filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    *,
    query: str | None = None,
    sort: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    select: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    page_size: int | None = None,
    limit: int | None = None,
    cursor: str | None = None,
    on_error: OnError = "raise",
    failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] | None = None,
    on_page: Callable[[int, str | None], Any] | None = None,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> AsyncIterator[E]:
    """Iterate over all matching entities.

    Uses cursor paging when ``dialect.cursor_param`` is set, otherwise page
    or offset paging. Stops at ``limit``, on an empty page, or when the
    unwrapper reports no next cursor. ``on_page(page_number, next_cursor)``
    checkpoints progress; passing a saved cursor back via ``cursor=``
    resumes a cursor-mode harvest. Records that fail validation raise
    :class:`ValidationError`, or are dropped and recorded in ``failures``
    with ``on_error="skip"``.
    """
    _check_on_error(on_error)
    if limit is not None and limit < 0:
        raise ConfigurationError(f"limit must be non-negative, got {limit}.")
    if cursor is not None and self.dialect.cursor_param is None:
        raise ConfigurationError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} does not support cursor paging "
            "(dialect.cursor_param is None)."
        )
    if self.dialect.cursor_param is not None:
        return self._iterate_cursor(
            filters=filters,
            query=query,
            sort=sort,
            select=select,
            page_size=page_size,
            limit=limit,
            cursor=cursor,
            on_error=on_error,
            failures=failures,
            on_page=on_page,
            params=params,
        )
    return self._iterate_pages(
        filters=filters,
        query=query,
        sort=sort,
        select=select,
        page_size=page_size,
        limit=limit,
        on_error=on_error,
        failures=failures,
        on_page=on_page,
        params=params,
    )

def record_keys(self, entity: E, field: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return every normalized ``field`` value of ``entity``.

    ``batch_get`` keys each entity by whichever of these values was
    requested, so records carrying several ids (for example deduplicated
    records with many DOIs) land under the id the caller asked for.
    Override when the values live somewhere other than ``entity.<field>``.
    """
    value = getattr(entity, field, None)
    if value is None:
        value = getattr(entity, "id", None)
    values = value if isinstance(value, list) else [value]
    return [self.normalize_id(str(item)) for item in values if item is not None]

docs.text:
Fetch one page of results as a typed :class:Page.

params is the escape hatch for API extras (facets, sample, seed); typed wrappers for them belong on client subclasses. Records that fail validation raise :class:ValidationError by default, or are skipped and recorded in failures with on_error="skip".

async def search(
    self,
    filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    *,
    query: str | None = None,
    sort: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    select: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    page: int | None = None,
    page_size: int | None = None,
    cursor: str | None = None,
    on_error: OnError = "raise",
    failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] | None = None,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> Page[E]:
    """Fetch one page of results as a typed :class:`Page`.

    ``params`` is the escape hatch for API extras (facets, ``sample``,
    ``seed``); typed wrappers for them belong on client subclasses.
    Records that fail validation raise :class:`ValidationError` by default,
    or are skipped and recorded in ``failures`` with ``on_error="skip"``.
    """
    _check_on_error(on_error)
    query_params = self._search_params(
        filters=filters,
        query=query,
        sort=sort,
        select=select,
        page=page,
        page_size=page_size,
        cursor=cursor,
        params=params,
    )
    response = await self._client.request(
        "GET", self.search_path(query), params=query_params
    )
    body = self._client.parse_json(response)
    unwrapper = self._client.unwrapper
    results = self._validate_records(
        unwrapper.results(body),
        on_error=on_error,
        failures=failures,
        request=_response_request(response),
        response=response,
    )
    effective_page = page
    if (
        effective_page is None
        and cursor is None
        and (
            self.dialect.offset_param is not None
            or self.dialect.page_param is not None
        )
    ):
        effective_page = self.dialect.page_start
    return Page(
        results=results,
        total=unwrapper.total(body),
        next_cursor=unwrapper.next_cursor(body),
        page=effective_page,
        meta=unwrapper.meta(body),
    )

docs.title: Sync usage
docs.text:
Every bibliofabric-based client ships two variants. The async code is the single source of truth; the sync twins are generated from it with unasync at dev time and committed.

Async Sync What it is BaseApiClient SyncBaseApiClient HTTP lifecycle: retries, pacing, auth, error mapping ResourceClient SyncResourceClient typed per-endpoint operations (get, search, iterate, batch_get) FooClient FooSyncClient a concrete client entry point

Everything the package root exports is exported for both variants; import from the package root, not from bibliofabric._async or bibliofabric._sync directly.

docs.title: When to use which
docs.text: Use the async variant inside asyncio applications (web servers, harvesters with concurrent requests). Use the sync twin in scripts, notebooks, and code that runs inside a running event loop: the sync path uses httpx.Client, time.sleep, and threads, and never starts or touches an event loop.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# async
async with StavrophoraClient(mailto="you@example.org") as client:
    work = await client.works.get("10.1038/nature12373")

# sync
with StavrophoraSyncClient(mailto="you@example.org") as client:
    work = client.works.get("10.1038/nature12373")

Both variants take the same parameters, raise the same errors, retry and page the same way, and enforce the same rate limits.

docs.title: Guarantees
docs.text:
• Generated files carry the header Generated by scripts/unasync.py; do not edit and are committed. CI fails (uv run python scripts/unasync.py --check) when a generated file is stale; pre-commit runs the same check.
  • Every behavior test in tests/_async/ is generated into tests/_sync/, so each behavior is verified against both variants.
  • Client authors keep their own packages' docs and quick starts showing both variants; see "Writing a client with sync support".

docs.title: Response unwrapping
docs.text:
ResponseUnwrapper is the protocol that makes bibliofabric API-agnostic. A client implements it to teach the framework how to navigate its API's JSON envelope: where result records live, how to read a single item, the total, the next cursor, and the remaining metadata.

class FooUnwrapper:
    def results(self, body):
        return body.get("results", [])

    def item(self, body):
        return body

    def total(self, body):
        return body.get("total")

    def next_cursor(self, body):
        return body.get("next_cursor")

    def meta(self, body):
        return {k: v for k, v in body.items() if k != "results"}

No inheritance is required; any object with these five methods satisfies the protocol.

docs.title: JSON:API unwrapping
docs.text:
JsonApiUnwrapper in bibliofabric.unwrap is a ready-made ResponseUnwrapper for JSON:API envelopes, as served by DataCite:

from bibliofabric import JsonApiUnwrapper

unwrapper = JsonApiUnwrapper(cursor_param="page[cursor]")
  • results() returns the data list members that are objects: raw JSON:API resource objects with id, type, attributes, and relationships.
  • item() returns the single data object, or {} when there is none.
  • total() returns meta.total when it is an integer.
  • next_cursor() reads the cursor_param query parameter from the links.next URL.
  • meta() returns the envelope minus data.

class JsonApiUnwrapper:
    """Read a JSON:API envelope (``data``, ``meta``, ``links``).

    Args:
        cursor_param: Name of the cursor query parameter that ``links.next``
            carries on later pages (``"page[cursor]"`` for DataCite).

    Records are the raw JSON:API resource objects (``id``, ``type``,
    ``attributes``, ``relationships``); a client that models flat records
    subclasses this and reshapes them. The total is ``meta.total``, and
    :meth:`meta` returns the rest of the envelope (``meta``, ``links``,
    ``included``).
    """

    def __init__(self, cursor_param: str = "page[cursor]") -> None:
        self._cursor_param = cursor_param

    def _data(self, body: Any) -> Any:
        return body.get("data") if isinstance(body, dict) else None

    def results(self, body: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Return the ``data`` members that are objects, in order."""
        data = self._data(body)
        if not isinstance(data, list):
            return []
        return [item for item in data if isinstance(item, dict)]

    def item(self, body: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Return the single ``data`` object, or ``{}`` when it is not one."""
        data = self._data(body)
        return data if isinstance(data, dict) else {}

    def total(self, body: Any) -> int | None:
        """Return ``meta.total`` when it is an integer."""
        meta = body.get("meta") if isinstance(body, dict) else None
        total = meta.get("total") if isinstance(meta, dict) else None
        if isinstance(total, int) and not isinstance(total, bool):
            return total
        return None

    def next_cursor(self, body: Any) -> str | None:
        """Return the cursor query parameter value of ``links.next``, if any."""
        links = body.get("links") if isinstance(body, dict) else None
        next_url = links.get("next") if isinstance(links, dict) else None
        if not isinstance(next_url, str):
            return None
        values = parse_qs(urlsplit(next_url).query).get(self._cursor_param, [])
        return values[0] if values and values[0] else None

    def meta(self, body: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Return the envelope minus ``data``."""
        if not isinstance(body, dict):
            return {}
        return {key: value for key, value in body.items() if key != "data"}

    if isinstance(total, int) and not isinstance(total, bool):
        return total
    return None
