docs.title: Building a client on bibliofabric
docs.text:
This guide walks through creating a new scholarly API client package on bibliofabric 0.8 — from workspace layout and settings to authentication, paging, unwrapping, resource hooks, sync-twin generation, testing, and release registration.

For the rules governing generated synchronous twins (_sync/), see Writing a client with sync support; this page focuses on the full client architecture and bibliofabric 0.8 API surface.

docs.title: 1. Package Layout
docs.text:
Keep pure code (settings, dialect, unwrapper, models, identifier helpers) at the package root and put every I/O module under _async/. Never hand-edit _sync/; scripts/unasync.py generates it from _async/.

packages/<pkg>/
  pyproject.toml
  CHANGELOG.md
  README.md
  src/<pkg>/
    py.typed
    __init__.py          # re-exports async + generated sync names
    config.py            # BaseApiSettings subclass + get_settings()
    dialect.py           # QueryDialect instance(s)
    unwrapper.py         # ResponseUnwrapper implementation
    models/              # Pydantic models (pure)
    _async/
      __init__.py
      client.py          # BaseApiClient subclass
      resources.py       # ResourceClient[E] subclasses (or resources/*.py)
    _sync/               # GENERATED by scripts/unasync.py
  tests/
    _async/              # pytest-httpx tests (source of truth)
    _sync/               # GENERATED by scripts/unasync.py

See Writing a client with sync support for _concurrency primitives (sleep, Lock, Limiter, run_bounded, maybe_await), naming conventions (FooClient → FooSyncClient, WorksResource → SyncWorksResource), and [tool.unasync] overrides.

docs.title: 2. Configuration (BaseApiSettings)
docs.text:
Subclass BaseApiSettings with a unique env_prefix so environment variables never collide across sibling libraries, and expose an lru_cache-backed get_settings():

from functools import lru_cache

from pydantic import Field
from pydantic_settings import SettingsConfigDict

from bibliofabric import BaseApiSettings


class ExampleSettings(BaseApiSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        env_prefix="EXAMPLE_", env_file=".env", extra="ignore"
    )

    api_key: str | None = None
    timeout: float = Field(default=30.0, gt=0)
    connect_timeout: float | None = Field(default=10.0, gt=0)
    follow_redirects: bool = False
    max_requests_per_second: float | None = Field(default=5.0, gt=0)
    rate_limits: dict[str, float | None] = Field(
        default_factory=lambda: {"search": 2.0, "single": 10.0}
    )


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def get_settings() -> ExampleSettings:
    return ExampleSettings()

Inherited behaviors worth knowing:

  • follow_redirects (default False) and connect_timeout (default None, falling back to timeout) apply automatically when BaseApiClient creates an owned httpx client.
  • httpx.Limits auto-size from max_concurrency (max_connections=max(20, max_concurrency * 2), max_keepalive_connections=max(10, max_concurrency)).
  • rate_limits pairs with BaseApiClient.rate_class(request) for per-endpoint pacing under a shared concurrency bound; setting a class to None disables pacing for that class.
  • effective_user_agent() builds <package>/<version> (+<homepage>; mailto:<mailto>) automatically from your package metadata when user_agent is unset.

docs.title: 3. Authentication (AuthStrategy)
docs.text:
Pick one of the built-in strategies (each implements both async_authenticate / async_close and sync authenticate / close):

Strategy When to use NoAuth() Public APIs (default) HeaderAuth(name, value) Static credential headers (e.g. x-api-key, crossref-api-key, Client-Id) QueryParameterAuth(key_name, key_value) Credential query parameters (e.g. api_key, email) StaticTokenAuth(token) Pre-issued Authorization: Bearer <token> BasicAuth(username, password) HTTP Basic (Authorization: Basic <b64>, e.g. DataCite Member writes) ClientCredentialsAuth(client_id, client_secret, token_url, *, scope=None, token_auth_method="basic", ...) OAuth2 client-credentials flow with monotonic expiry cache; pass token_auth_method="post" when the token endpoint expects form-body credentials (e.g. ORCID) RefreshTokenAuth(token_url, refresh_token, *, client_id=None, client_secret=None, scope=None, ...) OAuth2 refresh-token flow with automatic refresh-token rotation

docs.title: Automatic 401 Refresh & Secret Redaction
docs.text:
• 401 retry-once: Any strategy implementing invalidate_token() -> None (including ClientCredentialsAuth and RefreshTokenAuth) triggers automatic token invalidation and a single retry on HTTP 401 inside both request() and stream().
  • Custom secret redaction: If you write a custom AuthStrategy, declare redacted_query_params: frozenset[str] and/or redacted_headers: frozenset[str] (lowercase header names). BaseApiClient scrubs those values from debug logs and all BibliofabricError strings automatically.

docs.title: 4. Query Dialect (QueryDialect)
docs.text:
Declare paging, sorting, search, and field-selection rules once in a frozen QueryDialect:

from bibliofabric import QueryDialect

DIALECT = QueryDialect(
    page_size_param="per_page",  # None for unpaged APIs (e.g. OpenCitations)
    max_page_size=200,
    default_page_size=25,
    iterate_page_size=200,  # optional larger page size for iterate()
    count_page_size=0,  # 0 when the API supports zero-row count queries
    page_param="page",  # None if page numbers are unsupported
    page_start=1,  # 0 for zero-based APIs
    offset_param=None,  # e.g. "offset" or "start"; replaces page_param
    max_offset=10_000,  # optional hard cap; raises ConfigurationError if exceeded
    cursor_param="cursor",  # takes precedence over page/offset in iterate()
    cursor_start="*",  # set None if the first request omits the cursor param
    sort_param="sort",
    query_param="q",
    select_param="select",
)

Key bibliofabric 0.8 dialect details:

  • page_size_param=None omits the page-size parameter altogether (useful for unpaged endpoints like OpenCitations or fixed-page-size APIs like ROR v2).
  • cursor_start=None sends the initial cursor request without the cursor parameter (needed by token-based APIs such as Semantic Scholar bulk search or ClinicalTrials.gov pageToken).
  • max_offset guards page and offset paging before sending a request, raising ConfigurationError instead of triggering an upstream 400/500.
  • count_page_size controls what count() requests (default 1; set to 0 for APIs that return totals with zero rows).
  • Per-instance override: Pass dialect=... to ResourceClient(...) when one endpoint differs from the rest of the API (for example Zenodo's 25 unauth vs. 100 auth max_page_size, or Semantic Scholar's bulk vs. standard search).

docs.title: 5. Response Unwrapper (ResponseUnwrapper)
docs.text:
Implement the 5-method ResponseUnwrapper protocol to teach bibliofabric how to read your API's JSON envelope:

from typing import Any


class ExampleUnwrapper:
    def results(self, body: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        return list(body.get("results", []))

    def item(self, body: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return dict(body)

    def total(self, body: Any) -> int | None:
        meta = body.get("meta")
        return meta.get("count") if isinstance(meta, dict) else None

    def next_cursor(self, body: Any) -> str | None:
        meta = body.get("meta")
        return meta.get("next_cursor") if isinstance(meta, dict) else None

    def meta(self, body: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {k: v for k, v in body.items() if k != "results"}

For JSON:API envelopes (DataCite's shape), you do not need a custom unwrapper. JsonApiUnwrapper from bibliofabric.unwrap implements the protocol with cursor_param="page[cursor]"; see Unwrapping responses.

docs.title: 6. API Client (_async/client.py)
docs.text:
Subclass BaseApiClient to wire base_url, settings, unwrapper, auth, resource attributes, and optional HTTP lifecycle hooks:

import httpx

from bibliofabric import AuthStrategy, BaseApiClient, HeaderAuth, NoAuth

from ..config import ExampleSettings, get_settings
from ..unwrap import ExampleUnwrapper
from .resources import WorksResource


class ExampleClient(BaseApiClient):
    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        settings: ExampleSettings | None = None,
        auth: AuthStrategy | None = None,
        http_client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        resolved = settings or get_settings()
        effective_auth = auth
        if effective_auth is None:
            effective_auth = (
                HeaderAuth("x-api-key", resolved.api_key)
                if resolved.api_key
                else NoAuth()
            )
        super().__init__(
            base_url="https://api.example.org/v1",
            settings=resolved,
            unwrapper=ExampleUnwrapper(),
            auth=effective_auth,
            http_client=http_client,
        )
        self.last_credits_used: str | None = None
        self.works = WorksResource(self)

    def rate_class(self, request: httpx.Request) -> str:
        return "search" if request.url.path.endswith("/works") else "single"

    def on_response(self, response: httpx.Response) -> None:
        # Invoked after every HTTP response, before status errors raise.
        self.last_credits_used = response.headers.get("X-RateLimit-Credits-Used")

    def is_retryable(self, response: httpx.Response) -> bool:
        # Veto retries for non-transient 429s (e.g. exhausted daily budget).
        if response.status_code == 429:
            try:
                if response.json().get("reason") == "daily_budget":
                    return False
            except ValueError:
                pass
        return super().is_retryable(response)

Useful BaseApiClient capabilities for custom endpoints:

  • default_headers: Override this property (a Mapping[str, str], default {}) to pin one representation for a whole API. These headers go out with every request() and stream() call, and per-call headers= entries win, matched case-insensitively:

python @property def default_headers(self) -> dict[str, str]: return {"Accept": "application/vnd.orcid+json"} - request(..., follow_redirects=True | False | None): Default None keeps settings.follow_redirects. Pass False to get the 3xx response itself so you can read its Location header. Pass True to follow redirects, including to another host (needed for content negotiation through doi.org). - request(..., retry=True | False | None): Default retry=None retries only idempotent methods (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, DELETE). Pass retry=True for read-only POST batch/search endpoints, or retry=False to disable retries for a single call. - stream(method, path, ...): Async context manager (sync context manager on SyncBaseApiClient) for downloading files or bulk dumps incrementally with auth, rate limiting, on_response(), single-retry 401 refresh, and typed error mapping. - parse_json(response) / get_json(path, ...): Decode JSON while mapping malformed payloads to APIError.

docs.title: 7. Resource Clients (_async/resources.py)
docs.text:
Subclass ResourceClient[E] per endpoint and override only the hooks where your API deviates from the defaults:

from collections.abc import Sequence
from typing import Any

import httpx

from bibliofabric import ResourceClient, normalize_doi, validate_model

from ..dialect import DIALECT
from ..models import Work


class WorksResource(ResourceClient[Work]):
    path = "works"
    model = Work
    dialect = DIALECT
    batch_size = 500

    def normalize_id(self, value: str) -> str:
        return normalize_doi(value)

    async def _fetch_batch_chunk(
        self,
        field: str,
        chunk: list[str],
        *,
        select: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], httpx.Response]:
        # Override chunk transport for POST-batch APIs while inheriting
        # chunking, deduplication, concurrency, validation, on_error, and keying.
        params = {"fields": ",".join(select)} if select else None
        response = await self._client.request(
            "POST",
            f"{self.path}/batch",
            params=params,
            json={"ids": chunk},
            retry=True,
        )
        raw = self._client.parse_json(response)
        records = [item for item in raw if isinstance(item, dict)]
        return records, response

Key ResourceClient[E] details:

  • Hook checklist: build_filter_params(), format_sort(), build_batch_params(), _fetch_batch_chunk(), normalize_id(), record_keys(), item_path(), default_params(), and search_path().
  • default_params(): Returns a Mapping[str, Any] (default {}) sent as query parameters with every list request (search(), iterate(), count(), and each batch_get chunk). Filter parameters and caller-supplied params= take precedence, so the hook is for API-wide requirements such as Europe PMC's format=json:

python def default_params(self) -> dict[str, str]: return {"format": "json"} - search_path(query): Returns the route for search, iterate(), count(), and batch requests. The default returns self.path. Override it when the API carries the query in the path, as DOAJ does with /search/journals/{query}. With such an override, query= is accepted even when dialect.query_param is None; without one, that combination raises ConfigurationError. The hook receives None for count() without a query and for batch chunks. - Validation & on_error: On the default on_error="raise" path, search(), iterate(), and batch_get() bulk-validate each page/chunk using a lazily cached TypeAdapter(list[E]) per subclass, falling back to per-record validation only on error so ValidationError.raw still carries the offending payload. Callers can pass on_error="skip" and a failures=[] list to collect bad records without aborting a harvest. - Custom endpoints & validate_model(): When writing custom resource methods outside get()/search(), validate payloads with validate_model(Model, data, request=response.request, response=response) so Pydantic errors consistently raise bibliofabric.ValidationError.

docs.title: 8. Exports (__init__.py)
docs.text:
Re-export both async and generated sync classes from your package root so users never import from _async or _sync directly:

from ._async.client import ExampleClient
from ._async.resources import WorksResource
from ._sync.client import ExampleSyncClient
from ._sync.resources import SyncWorksResource
from .config import ExampleSettings, get_settings

docs.title: 9. Testing & Quality Gates
docs.text:
Write offline unit tests in packages/<pkg>/tests/_async/ using pytest-httpx (never import asyncio in _async tests; use bibliofabric._async._concurrency primitives if testing concurrency). Running scripts/unasync.py mirrors your async tests into tests/_sync/ automatically.

Mark any live-network smoke tests with @pytest.mark.live_api (deselected by default in pytest).

Offline fixtures come from trimmed live payloads. One payload per model is not enough to trust its field types. Before you call the models done, pull a few hundred real records through the client with iterate(..., on_error="skip", failures=failures) and check that the failures list stays empty. A model typed from a single record can reject most real records, for example a keyword field typed as a list of objects where the API serves plain strings.

Before opening a pull request, run every gate from the monorepo root:

uv run python scripts/unasync.py --package <pkg>
uv run python scripts/unasync.py --check
uv run ruff check
uv run ruff format --check
uv run ty check packages/*/src packages/*/tests scripts/unasync.py
uv run pytest packages/<pkg>/tests
uv run mkdocs build --strict

ty must pass with zero diagnostics and zero suppression comments (# ty: ignore / # type: ignore).

docs.title: 10. Monorepo Registration Checklist
docs.text:
When adding a new client package to utsmok/bibliofabric:

  1. Workspace & packaging: Create packages/<pkg>/pyproject.toml depending on bibliofabric>=0.8,<0.9 (with py.typed, Python >=3.12, and optional [tool.unasync]), then run uv lock and uv sync --all-packages --all-groups so the root uv.lock includes the new workspace member.
  2. Root pytest config: List packages/<pkg>/tests in the root pyproject.toml [tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths.
  3. Sync generation: Run uv run python scripts/unasync.py --package <pkg> and commit the generated _sync/ and tests/_sync/ modules.
  4. Documentation (mkdocs.yml):
  5. Add "packages/<pkg>/src" to plugins.mkdocstrings.handlers.python.paths.
  6. Add packages/<pkg>/src/<pkg> to watch:.
  7. Add the package's docs under docs/<pkg>/ and register it under nav: plus docs/index.md.
  8. CI matrix (.github/workflows/ci.yml): Add <pkg> to the test.strategy.matrix.package list so every PR tests Python 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14.
  9. Changelog & PyPI publishing:
  10. Maintain Keep a Changelog entries in packages/<pkg>/CHANGELOG.md.
  11. Configure a PyPI Trusted Publisher (OIDC) for <pkg> pointing to utsmok/bibliofabric, workflow ci.yml, environment pypi.
  12. Pushing a tag named <pkg>-v<version> validates pyproject.toml, builds the wheel/sdist, publishes to PyPI via OIDC, and creates a GitHub Release from packages/<pkg>/CHANGELOG.md.

docs.title: dataphora
docs.text: dataphora is a Python client for the DataCite REST API, built on bibliofabric. It types the public read routes for DOIs, clients, providers, repositories, prefixes, prefix assignments, activities, and events, flattens the JSON:API envelope so record fields sit at the top level of each model, and sends queries to the public GraphQL API. It ships an async client and a generated sync twin with the same API.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv sync --all-packages

The package is not yet published on PyPI. The command runs in a checkout of the bibliofabric workspace and installs dataphora with the bibliofabric 0.8 it needs. uv add dataphora works once the package is on PyPI. Requires Python 3.12 or newer.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Public reads need no login and no key. The client never sends credentials. Routes that need a login (DOI writes, media, usage reports, draft and registered records, API keys) are not wrapped; see upstream quirks.

Anonymous traffic is metered at 500 requests per 5 minutes. The client paces itself at 1.5 requests per second by default.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import asyncio
from dataphora import DataphoraClient


async def main():
    async with DataphoraClient() as client:
        doi = await client.dois.get("10.5438/0012")
        print(doi.title, doi.resource_type, doi.client_id)

        page = await client.dois.search(
            {"client-id": "cern.zenodo", "resource-type-id": "dataset"},
            query="photosynthesis",
            select=["doi", "titles"],
        )
        print(page.total, len(page.results))

        async for record in client.dois.iterate({"prefix": "10.5438"}, limit=10):
            print(record.doi, record.created)


asyncio.run(main())

Every resource client exposes get(), exists(), search(), iterate(), collect(), first(), and count(). The clients, providers, and prefixes clients add totals() for DOI production statistics and a dois() helper that reads the DOIs of one account or prefix. Start with the DOIs page.

docs.title: Sync usage
docs.text:
DataphoraSyncClient is generated from the async source and behaves the same: same parameters, errors, retries, paging, and rate limits. It uses plain httpx.Client and never starts or touches an event loop.

from dataphora import DataphoraSyncClient

with DataphoraSyncClient() as client:
    doi = client.dois.get("10.5438/0012")
    print(doi.title, doi.publicationYear)

    for record in client.providers.search(page_size=5):
        print(record.symbol, record.displayName)

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: DataphoraSettings loads from environment variables prefixed with DATAPHORA_: DATAPHORA_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND (default 1.5), DATAPHORA_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 3), DATAPHORA_TIMEOUT (default 30), DATAPHORA_MAX_RETRIES (default 3), DATAPHORA_MAX_RETRY_WAIT, DATAPHORA_USER_AGENT, and DATAPHORA_MAILTO.

docs.title: dataphora._async.dois.DoisClient
docs.text:
Bases: DataphoraDoiClient[DataphoraDoi]

Client for the /dois endpoint.

Generic operations (get, exists, search, iterate, collect, first, count) come from :class:bibliofabric.ResourceClient. iterate() walks with page[cursor] so it can pass the 10,000-record limit of numbered paging; cursor walks always run in created ascending order.

docs.title: activities(doi) async
docs.text:
Return the provenance activities of one DOI, newest first.

The route pages like every list route, so the method reads every page of up to 1000 records. The links.next link of these pages points at the global /activities route, so the method numbers the pages itself and stops at the first 10,000 records, the limit of numbered paging.

docs.title: dataphora._async.dois.ActivitiesClient
docs.text:
Bases: DataphoraDoiClient[DataphoraActivity]

Client for the global /activities endpoint.

For the activities of one DOI, prefer :meth:DoisClient.activities; this client lists and fetches activities across all DOIs. The route accepts page[size], page[number], and page[cursor]. Without a login its id and ids[] filters answer nothing, so the client has no typed filter model; narrow a search with query and quote a value that contains a slash (query='"10.5438/0012"'), because the bare value is a 400. Fetch one activity with get().

docs.title: dataphora._async.graphql.GraphqlClient
docs.text:
The public GraphQL API of DataCite.

The schema covers the same records as the REST API (works, persons, organizations, repositories, funders, prefixes, and events) and adds the connections between them. Queries need no credentials. The schema also lists three mutations (createClaim, deleteClaim, and updateUserProfile); they need a bearer token and are out of scope.

DataCite will retire the GraphQL API in July 2027 and asks its users to move to the REST API (announced on the DataCite support portal). New code should use the REST resources of this client.

docs.title: dataphora.filters.DoiFilters
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Filter model for the /dois route.

state is findable, registered, or draft. Without a login the API ignores registered and draft and answers as for findable. affiliation-id and funded-by take ROR ids, funder-id a Crossref Funder ID, and user-id an ORCID iD, bare or as a URL. Date filters (created, registered, published) take a year or a comma-separated list of years. field-of-science takes the plain label (natural sciences). has-citations, has-references, has-parts, has-part-of, has-versions, has-version-of, has-views, and has-downloads take a minimum count (1); true does not work for them, while it does for has-person, has-affiliation, has-organization, and has-funder. random=true draws random records, and sample_group="client" draws one random record per client account (a slow query, about two minutes on 2026-11-28). sample_size did not change the number of records on 2026-11-28; the page size decides how many of the drawn records come back.

docs.title: dataphora.dialect
docs.text:
DataCite query dialect constants.

DATACITE_DIALECT tells bibliofabric how DataCite names its query parameters. The resource-client base that consumes these constants lives in :mod:dataphora._async.dialect (its sync twin is generated from it).

Verified against the live API and the DataCite reference on 2026-11-28:

  • The default page size is 25; page[size] accepts 0 to 1000.
  • Numbered paging (page[number]) can reach the first 10,000 records of a query only. Beyond that the API answers with the last reachable page again instead of an error, so the resource clients raise ConfigurationError first. page[cursor] paging has no depth limit and always walks in created ascending order.

docs.title: DataCite REST API upstream quirks
docs.text: Facts below were verified against the live API at https://api.datacite.org with curl in November 2026, one to two requests per second, roughly sixty requests during the study and a small live test run. They shape choices in this client and the upstream documentation does not always state them.

docs.title: Paging
docs.text:
• The default is numbered paging with page[number] and page[size]. page[size] accepts 1 to 1000; 1001 clamps down to 1000.
  • Numbered paging can only reach the first 10,000 records of a query. Beyond that, DataCite returns 400 and tells you to switch to cursor paging.
  • Cursor paging starts at page[cursor]=1. links.next in the response carries the encoded next cursor; following it walks the whole result set.
  • A cursor walk always sorts by created ascending, whatever sort says.
  • count() and single-record requests work over either mode; the client uses numbered paging for search() and cursor paging for iterate() and collect().

docs.title: Query syntax
docs.text:
• Full-text search uses query= and matches indexed metadata. Filters are one query parameter per criterion, not one filter object: client-id=, provider-id=, consortium-id=, prefix=, schema-version=, state=, affiliation-id=, affiliation-country=, funded-by=, resource-type-id=, created=, registered=, published=, and has-views= among others.
  • Unknown query parameters are silently ignored. A typo in a filter yields an unfiltered result, not an error.
  • List values join with commas and mean OR; different keys mean AND.
  • sort accepts relevance, name, created, updated, published, view-count, download-count, citation-count, and title, each reversible with a leading -. Sorting by publicationYear is silently ignored.
  • Sparse fieldsets use fields[dois]=doi,titles (route-named). include= accepts client and media on DOI routes.
  • fields[dois] honors some attribute names (doi, titles, publicationYear, publisher, schemaVersion) but silently drops others, among them resourceTypeGeneral: even fields[dois]=resourceTypeGeneral returns empty attributes. Do not rely on sparse fieldsets for the general resource type.

docs.title: Attributes DataCite trims or varies
docs.text:
• Older records carry affiliations as bare strings; the models wrap those as {"name": ...}.
  • publisher can be a string or an object with name, publisherIdentifier, and scheme fields.
  • metadataVersion is a number on current records and a string on old ones.
  • Affiliation identifiers, publisher identifiers, and registration-agency details are omitted unless the request passes affiliation=true, publisher=true, or detail=true. detail=true additionally adds xml, viewsOverTime, citationsOverTime, and relationship counts.
  • The JSON:API type of a DOI record is dois, and relationship names use client, provider, media, and repository.

docs.title: Routes that behave differently than documented
docs.text:
• GET /dois/{id}/views, /downloads, and /url return 404. They belong to the login-only MDS and Usage Reports APIs, not the REST API. The client does not wrap them; use the DOI attributes or events instead.
  • GET /dois/{id}/media returns 404 anonymously, and an Accept: application/vnd.api+json request answers with an empty data: [], so it is useless without a login and is not wrapped.
  • GET /prefixes/totals answers 204 No Content without a client-id parameter and a JSON array with one entry per prefix with it (verified 2026-11-28). prefixes.totals() therefore requires a client id.
  • /clients/totals and /providers/totals are public but are bare JSON arrays of {id, title, count, temporal, states} entries, not JSON:API envelopes, and they are unpaged (about 1.5 MB and 0.6 MB).
  • /client-prefixes and /provider-prefixes records carry only createdAt and updatedAt; prefix, client, and provider are relationships.
  • /events records use hyphenated attribute names (subj-id, relation-type-id, citation-type, occurred-at); the spec text spells occured-at without the first r, and older fixtures use that form.
  • The unfiltered /events route stalls for tens of seconds; filter it (for example doi=) and it answers in seconds.
  • HEAD /dois/{id} works and returns 200, so the framework default exists() needs no override.
  • Unknown DOI ids return 404 with a JSON:API errors body.

docs.title: GraphQL API
docs.text:
• POST /graphql answers without a login, with the Accept: application/vnd.api+json header that the client sends on every request (verified 2026-11-27).
  • A rejected query (an unknown field, a wrong argument type) answers 400 with an errors list. A field that fails (a record that does not exist) answers 200 with an errors list and data: null. The client raises APIError for both and attaches the body.
  • Introspection is open: __schema lists 69 fields of the Query type on 2026-11-27. The id argument of work has the type ID!.
  • The support portal had no page for the GraphQL API on 2026-11-27. The endpoint and its schema are the reference.

docs.title: Traffic limits
docs.text:
• No rate-limit headers are sent. DataCite documents 500 requests per 5 minutes for anonymous callers; this client paces itself at 1.5 requests per second.
  • api.datacite.org serves neither the swagger UI nor an OpenAPI document; the machine-readable reference lives in the DataCite support portal.

docs.title: Clients
docs.text:
The clients resource reads the repository accounts that register DOIs. Ids are lowercase symbols such as datacite.datacite or cern.zenodo.

record = await client.clients.get("datacite.datacite")
record.symbol
record.clientType  # "repository" or "periodical"
record.issn.electronic
record.domains

docs.title: Searching
docs.text:
from dataphora import ClientFilters

page = await client.clients.search(
    ClientFilters(client_type="repository", year="2024"),
    query="zenodo",
    select=["name", "symbol"],
)

page.meta carries the facet counts (years, providers, client types).

docs.title: DOIs of one client
docs.text:
page = await client.clients.dois("cern.zenodo", page_size=25)

dois() sends the same request as the /clients/{id}/dois route: a /dois search filtered by client-id. All search() keyword arguments (query, sort, select, cursor, and friends) forward.

docs.title: Production statistics
docs.text:
totals = await client.clients.totals()
totals[0].id
totals[0].count
totals[0].temporal["this_year"][0].count
totals[0].states[0].count

totals() reads /clients/totals. The response is one unpaged entry per client (several megabytes), so cache it if you call it repeatedly.

docs.title: Prefix assignments
docs.text:
Each prefix assignment pairs one prefix with one client. The prefix and the account are relationships; the resource itself only carries timestamps.

page = await client.client_prefixes.search(page_size=50)
assignment = page.results[0]
assignment.relationships["prefix"].data.id
assignment.relationships["client"].data.id

docs.title: DOIs
docs.text: The dois resource reads DataCite DOI records. Anonymous reads see findable records only; registered and draft states need a login.

docs.title: Fetching one DOI
docs.text:
doi = await client.dois.get("10.5438/0012")
doi.title
doi.resource_type  # resourceTypeGeneral, for example "Text"
doi.publicationYear
doi.client_id  # repository account that registered the DOI
doi.provider_id  # DataCite member behind that account
doi.creators[0].name
doi.relationships["references"]

get() accepts bare DOIs and https://doi.org/ links, in any case. exists() answers True or False with one HEAD request. An unknown DOI raises NotFoundError.

docs.title: Searching
docs.text:
page = await client.dois.search(
    {"client-id": "cern.zenodo", "resource-type-id": "dataset"},
    query="photosynthesis",
    sort="-updated",
    select=["doi", "titles", "publicationYear"],
    page_size=100,
)
page.total, page.results, page.next_cursor, page.meta

search() pages with page[number], which DataCite limits to the first 10,000 records of a query. page.meta carries the raw envelope with its facet counts.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Pass a DoiFilters model or a plain mapping. Values that are lists join with commas, which DataCite reads as OR; different keys AND.

from dataphora import DoiFilters

filters = DoiFilters(
    prefix=["10.5438", "10.5281"],
    resource_type_id="text",
    schema_version="4",
    affiliation_id="https://ror.org/006hf6230",
    funded_by="https://ror.org/01cwqze88",
    created="2024,2025",
    has_affiliation=True,
)
page = await client.dois.search(filters)

DataCite silently ignores unknown query parameters, so a typo in a mapping returns an unfiltered result. The typed model fields are the safety net. Date filters take years, not ISO timestamps.

docs.title: Paging deep result sets
docs.text:
iterate() and collect() walk with page[cursor], which has no depth limit. Cursor walks always run in created ascending order, whatever sort says.

async for record in client.dois.iterate(filters):
    ...

records = await client.dois.collect(filters, limit=1000)

count() returns meta.total with a one-record request.

docs.title: Per-DOI activities
docs.text:
activities = await client.dois.activities("10.5438/0012")
activities[0].action  # "create", "update"
activities[0].version
activities[0].changes  # attribute name -> [old, new]

The global /activities route is available through client.activities with the same generic operations. The prov:* attribute keys land in model_extra.

docs.title: Extras the API trims by default
docs.text:
DataCite omits some attributes unless the request asks for them. Forward the flags with params=:

doi = await client.dois.get("10.5438/0012", params={"detail": "true"})
page = await client.dois.search(params={"affiliation": "true", "publisher": "true"})

detail=true adds xml, viewsOverTime, citationsOverTime, and the relationship counts; affiliation=true and publisher=true add identifier details that schema 4.3+ records carry.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The events resource reads the citation, reference, view, and download event log that DataCite feeds from DOI landing pages and Content Negotiation. Events are write-once records with no update or delete.

from dataphora import EventFilters

page = await client.events.search(
    EventFilters(doi="10.5438/0012", citation_type="journal-article"),
    page_size=100,
)
event = page.results[0]
event.subj_id  # landing page or DOI the event happened on
event.obj_id  # target of a citation or reference
event.relation_type_id  # "is-referenced-by", "is-cited-by", "views", ...
event.occurred_at  # None on older records, which carry occured_at instead
event.source_id  # "datacite-crossref", "datacite-usage", ...
event.total
event.relationships["subj"].data.id
page.meta["facets"]

Attribute aliases mirror the upstream hyphenated names (subj-id, obj-id, relation-type-id, source-id, message-action, source-token). The date exists under two spellings: older records carry the spec spelling occured-at and recent records carry occurred-at, so the model has the two fields occured_at and occurred_at.

docs.title: Always pass a filter
docs.text: The unfiltered /events route walks the full history and stalls for tens of seconds. Give the search at least one criterion, for example doi=, source-id=, or relation-type-id=.

docs.title: Counting by facet
docs.text:
page = await client.events.search(
    EventFilters(doi="10.5438/0012"),
    page_size=1,
)
page.meta["citation-count"]  # total citation count
page.meta["facets"]["relation-type-id"]
page.meta["facets"]["source"]

With page_size=1 the envelope meta answers "how many and of what kind" in one request; count() returns the plain number.

docs.title: GraphQL
docs.text:
The graphql resource sends queries to the public GraphQL API of DataCite at https://api.datacite.org/graphql. Its schema covers the same records as the REST routes (works, persons, organizations, repositories, funders, prefixes, and events) and the connections between them, so one query can fetch a work together with its creators, its repository, and its citing works. Queries need no login.

data = await client.graphql.query(
    """
    query($id: ID!) {
      work(id: $id) {
        doi
        titles { title }
        creators { name }
        publicationYear
        citationCount
        repository { uid name }
      }
    }
    """,
    {"id": "https://doi.org/10.5438/0012"},
)
work = data["work"]
print(work["doi"], work["citationCount"])

docs.title: The answer is plain data
docs.text:
The answer follows the query, so query() returns the data object as plain dictionaries and lists. The client does not validate it. Ask for the fields you need. The id argument of a work is its DOI as a URL (https://doi.org/10.5438/0012).

An introspection query lists the schema: the 69 fields of the Query type and their arguments, such as the published, registrationAgency, repositoryId, and userId filters of the list fields.

schema = await client.graphql.query(
    "{ __schema { queryType { fields { name args { name } } } } }"
)

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: DataCite reports a rejected query (an unknown field, a wrong argument type) with status 400. It reports a field that fails (a record that does not exist) with status 200 and an errors list. Both raise APIError. Its body holds the answer of DataCite with every error message and its path.

docs.title: Mutations need a token
docs.text: Mutations need a bearer token and are not part of this client. See the deferred list in the roadmap for the condition that unblocks them.

docs.title: Media and other account routes
docs.text: Several DataCite routes answer 404 or 401 for anonymous callers and need an account. dataphora does not wrap them; this page records what they are and why they are out of scope, verified against the live API in November 2026.

docs.title: Media (/dois/{id}/media)
docs.text: The media route lists or stores the content URLs behind a DOI. Anonymous requests get 404; with Accept: application/vnd.api+json the answer is an empty data: [], which makes the route useless without a login, and the JSON list form needs an authenticated MDS session. DataphoraDoi already exposes the public contentUrl, url, and media attribute values that DataCite ships on the DOI record itself, which covers most read needs.

docs.title: Usage statistics (/dois/{id}/views and /dois/{id}/downloads)
docs.text: These per-DOI routes do not exist in the REST API; they return 404. Counts live in the DOI attributes instead (viewsOverTime, downloadsOverTime, viewCount when detail=true) and in the events resource (relation-type-id views and downloads). Full monthly reports use the separate Usage Reports API, which is login-only.

docs.title: URL resolution (/dois/{id}/url)
docs.text: This route belongs to the login-only MDS API, not the REST API, and returns 404 anonymously. Read the url attribute of a DataphoraDoi instead.

docs.title: DOI writes (create, update, delete, publish)
docs.text: All DOI mutations need DataCite account credentials and the MDS or REST write endpoints. dataphora covers reads only; writes are out of scope until test credentials exist.

docs.title: Prefix totals
docs.text: GET /prefixes/totals answers 204 No Content without a client-id parameter. client.prefixes.totals(client_id) sends that parameter and returns the statistics; see Prefixes.

docs.title: Prefixes
docs.text: The prefixes resource lists the DOI prefixes (10-prefixed strings such as 10.5438) and their assignment ledger. A prefix record itself carries almost nothing; its assignments point at the provider and clients that use it.

docs.title: Browsing prefixes
docs.text:
record = await client.prefixes.get("10.5438")
record.prefix

from dataphora import PrefixFilters

page = await client.prefixes.search(PrefixFilters(state="unallocated"))
page = await client.prefixes.search(prefix="10.52")

docs.title: DOIs of one prefix
docs.text:
page = await client.prefixes.dois("10.5438", page_size=25)

dois() sends a /dois search filtered by prefix, the same request the /prefixes/{id}/dois route serves. All search() keyword arguments forward.

docs.title: Who holds a prefix
docs.text:
The ledger lives in two resources, and both carry only createdAt and updatedAt; the prefix, the client, and the provider are relationships.

page = await client.client_prefixes.search(page_size=50)
assignment = page.results[0]
assignment.relationships["prefix"].data.id
assignment.relationships["client"].data.id

page = await client.provider_prefixes.search(page_size=50)
page.results[0].relationships["provider"].data.id

docs.title: Production statistics
docs.text:
totals = await client.prefixes.totals("cern.zenodo")
totals[0].id  # "10.5281"
totals[0].count
totals[0].states[0].count

totals() reads /prefixes/totals with the required client-id parameter: one unpaged entry per prefix of the client, with the same count, temporal, and states fields as the client and provider totals. Pass a list of client ids to cover several clients. Without client-id the route answers 204 No Content, so the method requires it.

docs.title: Providers
docs.text:
The providers resource reads the DataCite members and consortium organizations that manage clients and prefixes. Ids are lowercase symbols such as datacite or cern.

record = await client.providers.get("datacite")
record.displayName
record.memberType  # "direct_member", "consortium", ...
record.region  # "EMEA", "AMER", "APA"
record.rorId

docs.title: Searching
docs.text:
from dataphora import ProviderFilters

page = await client.providers.search(
    ProviderFilters(member_type="consortium", region="EMEA"),
    select=["symbol", "displayName", "country"],
)

docs.title: DOIs of one provider
docs.text:
page = await client.providers.dois("datacite", page_size=25)

dois() sends a /dois search filtered by provider-id, the same request the /providers/{id}/dois route serves. All search() keyword arguments forward.

docs.title: Production statistics
docs.text:
totals = await client.providers.totals()
totals[0].id
totals[0].temporal["last_year"][0].count

totals() reads /providers/totals. The response is one unpaged entry per provider, several hundred kilobytes.

docs.title: Prefix assignments
docs.text:
The provider side of the prefix ledger lives in client.provider_prefixes; each record carries only timestamps, with the prefix and provider as relationships.

page = await client.provider_prefixes.search(page_size=50)
page.results[0].relationships["prefix"].data.id

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text:
The repositories resource is a view of the client accounts restricted to clientType: repository. Periodicals are excluded, so this is the catalog for indexing repositories. Ids are lowercase symbols such as cern.zenodo.

record = await client.repositories.get("cern.zenodo")
record.symbol
record.re3data  # re3data id, for example "r3d100010468"
record.opendoar
record.software  # repository software, when known
record.certificate  # for example "Core Certified Repository"
record.issn.print

docs.title: Searching
docs.text:
from dataphora import RepositoryFilters

page = await client.repositories.search(
    RepositoryFilters(year="2024"),
    query="arxiv",
    select=["name", "re3data", "opendoar"],
)

page.meta carries facet counts by year, certificate, software, and country.

docs.title: DOIs of one repository
docs.text:
page = await client.repositories.dois("cern.zenodo", page_size=25)

dois() sends a /dois search filtered by client-id, the same request the /repositories/{id}/dois route serves. All search() keyword arguments forward. For periodical accounts use client.clients.dois() instead.

docs.title: diurnalia
docs.text:
diurnalia is not yet published on PyPI; until its first release it installs from the bibliofabric workspace.

diurnalia is a Python client for the DOAJ API v4, built on bibliofabric. It types the journal and article search routes with Pydantic models, resolves journals by ISSN and articles by DOI, and enforces the paging limits the API imposes. It ships an async client and a generated sync twin with the same API. The search routes need no credentials.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv add diurnalia

Requires Python 3.12 or newer.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import asyncio
from diurnalia import DiurnaliaClient


async def main():
    async with DiurnaliaClient() as client:
        journal = await client.journals.get("1932-6203")
        print(journal.title, journal.publisher_name)

        page = await client.journals.search(query="title:plos")
        print(page.total, [journal.title for journal in page.results])

        article = await client.articles.get("10.3389/fpubh.2020.00115")
        print(article.doi)


asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Journals covers the journal record, search, sorting, and the ISSN lookup.
  • Articles covers the article record and the DOI lookup.
  • Upstream quirks lists what the live API does differently from its documentation.

docs.title: Articles
docs.text: client.articles talks to /api/v4/search/articles/{query} and /api/v4/articles/{id} and returns Article models. The index holds about 14 million articles, but like every DOAJ route the search serves at most 1000 records per query. Harvest everything through the DOAJ public data dump.

docs.title: Get one article by DOI
docs.text:
article = await client.articles.get("10.3389/fpubh.2020.00115")
article = await client.articles.get("https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2020.00115")
found = await client.articles.exists("10.3389/fpubh.2020.00115")

get() runs the search route with the doi: clause and accepts a bare DOI and a DOI URL. DOAJ answers a DOI without a record with an envelope of zero results, which the client turns into NotFoundError.

docs.title: Get one article by record id
docs.text:
full = await client.articles.get_by_id(article.id)

get_by_id() runs the record route with the DOAJ record id that every search result carries as id. The record holds the fields of a search result plus es_type and an admin block with in_doaj and publisher_record_id. An id without a record raises NotFoundError.

docs.title: The record model
docs.text:
Field Content id The DOAJ record id title bibjson.title doi The DOI from bibjson.identifier, or None issns The ISSNs of the publishing journal bibjson The full article metadata; see below admin in_doaj and publisher_record_id on records from the record route, None on search results created_date, last_updated Record timestamps es_type article on records from the record route, None on search results

Selected bibjson fields:

Field Content title, abstract Title and abstract text author Entries with name, affiliation, and orcid identifier Entries with type (doi, eissn, pissn) and id journal The journal block: title, publisher (a plain string), country, language, issns, volume, number link Entries with type (fulltext, abstract), url, and content_type (PDF, HTML, ePUB, XML) year, month Publication date as strings keywords, subject Keywords and LCC classification entries

Fields DOAJ adds later are kept in model_extra.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
page = await client.articles.search(
    query='title:"food insecurity" AND year:2020', page_size=50
)
page.total  # 14038837 for the match-all query on 2026-11-27
page.results  # up to 50 Article records

The short field names are title, doi, issn, publisher, and abstract. iterate(), collect(), first(), and count() behave as on the journals page, with the same 1000-record cap.

docs.title: Journals
docs.text: client.journals talks to /api/v4/search/journals/{query} and /api/v4/journals/{id} and returns Journal models. DOAJ has no journal listing route, so searches and ISSN lookups go through the search route. One query reaches at most 1000 records, so a full registry harvest uses the journal CSV export.

docs.title: Get one journal by ISSN
docs.text:
journal = await client.journals.get("1932-6203")
journal = await client.journals.get("19326203")  # compact spelling
found = await client.journals.exists("1932-6203")

get() runs the search route with the issn: clause and accepts the grouped and the compact spelling and an ISSN URL. The clause matches the print and the electronic ISSN, because DOAJ indexes both in one field. A journal that does not carry the ISSN raises NotFoundError.

docs.title: Get one journal by record id
docs.text:
full = await client.journals.get_by_id(journal.id)

get_by_id() runs the record route with the DOAJ record id that every search result carries as id. The record holds the fields of a search result plus es_type, last_manual_update, and in_doaj in admin. An id without a record raises NotFoundError.

docs.title: The record model
docs.text:
Field Content id The DOAJ record id, such as 2fdf1470373343b7bd4f825179c685f5 title bibjson.title issns The print and electronic ISSNs that are set publisher_name bibjson.publisher.name bibjson The full journal metadata; see the table below admin Editorial flags. A search result carries ticked; a record from the record route also carries in_doaj created_date, last_updated, last_manual_update Record timestamps; last_manual_update appears on records from the record route es_type journal on records from the record route, None on search results

Selected bibjson fields:

Field Content title, alternative_title Journal names publisher name and country (ISO 3166 code) pissn, eissn The ISSNs license Entries with type (CC BY, CC BY-NC, and so on), the by/nc/nd/sa flags, and url language, keywords Lists of ISO 639 codes and keywords subject Classification entries with scheme (LCC), code, and term oa_start, boai The year the journal went fully open access, and the BOAI flag apc, other_charges, waiver Charge policies, each with a has_* flag, the APC max price list, and a url editorial, copyright, plagiarism, preservation, deposit_policy, pid_scheme Policies and services, each with flags and URLs article How article licenses are displayed (license_display, example URL) ref Journal links: aims and scope, author instructions, OA statement, license terms

Fields DOAJ adds later are kept in model_extra.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
page = await client.journals.search(
    query='language:EN AND license:"CC BY"', sort="title:asc", page_size=50
)
page.total  # 23831 for the match-all query on 2026-11-27
page.results  # up to 50 Journal records
page.page  # the page number
page.meta  # the envelope: pageSize, timestamp, query, last/next/prev URLs

iterate(), collect(), first(), and count() build on the same route. iterate() pages at pageSize=50 and stops at total; a page beyond the 1000-record cap raises ConfigurationError before a request is sent.

docs.title: Sorting
docs.text: sort= takes field or field:direction with asc (the default) and desc. The field uses the dot notation (sort=bibjson.title:desc). An unknown sort field answers 400. Fields that hold multiple values sort by their smallest value.

docs.title: Every journal as CSV
docs.text:
DOAJ publishes a CSV export of every journal at https://doaj.org/csv, which redirects to a file on Amazon S3. On 2026-11-28 it held 23,672 journals in 52 columns and was about 26 MB. download_csv() streams it to a file, and iter_journal_csv() reads it row by row.

from diurnalia import iter_journal_csv

path = await client.journals.download_csv("doaj_journals.csv")
for row in iter_journal_csv(path):
    row["Journal title"], row["Journal EISSN (online version)"]

Each row is a dict keyed by the column headers as DOAJ writes them, and every value is a string. The full journal and article data dumps are not public: DOAJ grants access case by case and the dump routes answer 401 without it.

The search routes need no credentials. The client sends Accept: application/json on every request and paces requests at half of the documented limit of two per second by default.

docs.title: diurnalia.DiurnaliaSettings
docs.text:
Bases: BaseApiSettings

DOAJ-specific client settings.

Inherits timeout, max_retries, max_retry_wait, max_requests_per_second, max_concurrency, user_agent and mailto from :class:bibliofabric.config.BaseApiSettings and sets DOAJ defaults (1 request per second, concurrency 2). The search routes need no credentials; write routes that need an admin key are out of scope.

docs.title: diurnalia.JournalsClient
docs.text:
Bases: DiurnaliaResourceClient[Journal]

Client for the /search/journals route.

DOAJ has no journal listing; every read goes through a search. One query reaches at most 1000 records (page and page size combined). For the whole registry, :meth:download_csv fetches the public CSV export of every journal.

docs.title: download_csv(dest) async
docs.text:
Stream the public CSV export of every DOAJ journal to dest.

The export holds one row per journal with 52 columns (2026-11-28) and is about 26 MB. Read it with :func:diurnalia.iter_journal_csv. Creates parent directories, overwrites an existing file, and returns the path.

docs.title: get(id, *, select=None, params=None) async
docs.text:
Return the journal with a given ISSN.

Accepts the grouped (1932-6203) and the compact (19326203) spelling and an ISSN URL. The search matches the print and the electronic ISSN, because DOAJ indexes both in one field. Raises NotFoundError when no journal carries the ISSN.

Client for the /search/articles route.

The route indexes about 14 million articles, but like the journals route it serves at most 1000 records per query. Harvest everything through the DOAJ public data dump instead.

Accepts a bare DOI (10.3389/fpubh.2020.00115) and a DOI URL. Raises NotFoundError when no article carries the DOI; DOAJ answers such a search with a 200 envelope of zero results.

docs.title: diurnalia.issn_query(issn)
docs.text:
Return the issn: clause for a journal ISSN.

Accepts the grouped (1932-6203) and the compact (19326203) spelling and an ISSN URL. The clause matches the print and the electronic ISSN of a journal, because DOAJ indexes both in one field.

docs.title: diurnalia.doi_query(doi)
docs.text:
Return the doi: clause for an article DOI.

Accepts a bare DOI (10.3389/fpubh.2020.00115) and a DOI URL. DOAJ escapes the forward slash of a DOI itself, so the clause can carry the plain DOI.

docs.title: diurnalia.iter_journal_csv(path)
docs.text:
Yield one dict per journal row of a downloaded DOAJ journal CSV.

The keys are the column headers of the export as DOAJ writes them, for example "Journal title", "Journal ISSN (print version)", and "Journal EISSN (online version)". Every value is a string; an empty cell is "". The file is read row by row, so memory use stays flat.

docs.title: Upstream quirks
docs.text: Findings from about 65 requests against the live DOAJ API on 2026-11-27, with the API documentation and its Swagger page as the reference. Where a quirk affects diurnalia, the behavior of the client is noted.

docs.title: One search envelope, two route prefixes
docs.text: /api/search/journals/{query} (legacy) and /api/v4/search/journals/{query} answer the same envelope: total, page, pageSize, timestamp, query, results, and last (plus next and prev from page 2 on). diurnalia wraps v4 only.

docs.title: Paging is capped at 1000 records
docs.text:
The API answers (page - 1) * pageSize + pageSize <= 1000 and rejects anything beyond with HTTP 400: "You cannot access results beyond 1000 records via this API" (it points to the public data dump). Verified: page 20 at pageSize=50 answers, page 21 answers 400, page 500 at pageSize=2 answers, page 501 answers 400, page 1000 at pageSize=1 answers. The cap is independent of the matched total; the match-all journal query reports 23831 records and the article query 14038837. diurnalia sets max_offset to 999 and raises ConfigurationError before sending a request beyond the cap.

pageSize is clamped silently: 51 and 100 both answer with pageSize: 50. The default is 10. page=0 is treated as page 1.

docs.title: The query lives in the path
docs.text: The search query is a path segment. A missing query is not allowed as an empty segment; * (URL-encoded %2A) works as match-all on both resources. bibliofabric carries queries as query parameters by default, so diurnalia overrides search_path().

docs.title: Query syntax
docs.text:
• Fielded queries work with the short names title, issn, publisher, license (journals) and title, doi, issn, publisher, abstract (articles), and with full dot notation such as bibjson.title. license:"CC BY" matches 12395 journals on 2026-11-27; license:cc-by matches none, so the license value needs its stored spelling.
  • AND, OR, ANDNOT, quoted phrases, and ranges (created_date:[2015-01-01 TO 2016-01-01], 889 journals) work.
  • Wildcards answer 400 with "Query contains disallowed Lucene features". The documentation also disables regex, fuzzy (~), and proximity searches.
  • issn:1932-6203 finds PLoS ONE, which carries it as an eISSN, so the field covers both ISSN kinds.
  • A syntactically strange query such as title:::x does not error; it answers 200 with 27 results.
  • sort takes field or field:direction and is echoed in the envelope. An unknown sort field answers 400. Sorting articles by bibjson.year answers 400 (verified 2026-11-27); title:asc on journals sorts case-insensitively.

docs.title: Identifier lookups go through search
docs.text:
There is no journal listing or article listing route, and no ISSN or DOI route. GET /api/v4/search/articles/doi:10.3389/fpubh.2020.00115 answers the article, and a made-up DOI answers 200 with total: 0, not 404. diurnalia raises NotFoundError on an empty envelope.

The record routes GET /api/v4/journals/{id} and GET /api/v4/articles/{id} take the DOAJ record id and answer 200 without a key (verified 2026-11-27). They hold more than a search result. A journal search result carries admin.ticked and es_type: null, and an article search result carries admin: null. A record from the record route carries es_type (journal or article) and admin with in_doaj, and an article record also carries publisher_record_id. An id without a record answers 404 with {"status": "not_found"}. get_by_id() wraps both routes.

docs.title: Rate limit
docs.text: The documentation states a rate limit of two requests per second on all API routes, with bursts of up to five queued requests. diurnalia defaults to 1 request per second and concurrency 2.

docs.title: Write routes and admin key
docs.text: POST /api/applications, GET/PUT/DELETE /api/applications/{id}, POST /api/articles, GET/PUT/DELETE /api/articles/{id}, and the bulk upload routes (/api/bulk/articles, /api/bulk/applications) need an API key that only publishers have. The applications search route answers 401 without a key ("An API Key is required to access this"). diurnalia wraps none of these.

docs.title: Records
docs.text:
• Search results and id-route records carry id, bibjson, admin, created_date, last_updated; search results also carry es_type: null.
  • Journal ISSNs are top-level bibjson.pissn/bibjson.eissn; article ISSNs live in bibjson.identifier (type doi, eissn, pissn) and in bibjson.journal.issns.
  • The journal bibjson.publisher is an object (name, country); the article bibjson.journal.publisher is a plain string.
  • The v4.0.1 release notes state that the article API normalizes identifier types to lower case and ignores unmanaged types.

docs.title: europaea
docs.text:
europaea is not yet published on PyPI; until its first release it installs from the bibliofabric workspace.

europaea is a Python client for the Europe PMC REST web services, the annotations API, and the grants API, built on bibliofabric. It types the article search (cursor paging, sorting, resultType=lite|core), the per-article routes, annotations, grants, profiles, and the preprint subset with Pydantic models. It ships an async client and a generated sync twin with the same API. The APIs need no credentials.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv add europaea

Requires Python 3.12 or newer.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import asyncio
from europaea import EuropaeaClient


async def main():
    async with EuropaeaClient() as client:
        page = await client.search.search(
            query="DOI:10.1038/nature12373", result_type="core", page_size=1
        )
        article = page.results[0]
        print(article.title, article.cited_by_count)

        references = await client.articles.references(
            "MED:23903748", page=1, page_size=5
        )
        print(references.total, [ref.title for ref in references.results])

        annotations = await client.annotations.by_article_ids(
            "MED:23903748", type="Chemicals"
        )
        print(annotations[0].annotations[0].exact)

        async for record in client.search.iterate(query="nanodiamond", page_size=100):
            print(record.id, record.source)


asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Sync usage
docs.text:
The generated EuropaeaSyncClient has the same methods without async and await:

from europaea import EuropaeaSyncClient

with EuropaeaSyncClient() as client:
    page = client.search.search(query="DOI:10.1038/nature12373", result_type="core")
    print(page.results[0].title)

    for record in client.search.iterate(query="nanodiamond", page_size=100):
        print(record.id, record.source)

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
EuropaeaSettings loads from environment variables prefixed with EUROPAEA_ and from a .env file in the working directory. EUROPAEA_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND (default 3) and EUROPAEA_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 2) set the request pace. Europe PMC publishes no rate limit, so these defaults are a courtesy. The shared fields of bibliofabric.config.BaseApiSettings also apply, such as EUROPAEA_TIMEOUT, EUROPAEA_MAX_RETRIES, EUROPAEA_MAX_RETRY_WAIT, and EUROPAEA_USER_AGENT.

A search can take about ten seconds. The shared timeout default of 30 seconds covers that.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Search covers the query string, resultType, sorting, and cursor paging.
  • Articles covers article records, full text, references, citations, and data links.
  • Annotations covers the annotations API.
  • Grants, profiles, and preprints covers the grants API and the profile and preprint searches.
  • Upstream quirks lists what the live API does differently from its documentation.
  • The API reference is generated from the source.

docs.title: Annotations
docs.text: client.annotations talks to the annotations API at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/annotations_api, a separate service from the REST web services. Every method sends format=JSON.

docs.title: Annotations of articles
docs.text:
records = await client.annotations.by_article_ids(
    ["MED:23903748", "PMC:PMC4221854"], type="Chemicals"
)
for record in records:
    for annotation in record.annotations:
        print(annotation.exact, annotation.tags[0].name)

by_article_ids takes one article id or a list (comma-joined into the articleIds parameter) and returns one ArticleAnnotations record per article. Optional filters: type (annotation type such as Chemicals, Diseases, Taxonomy), sub_type, section (a JATS section such as Methods), and provider.

docs.title: Annotations of entities, providers, and relationships
docs.text:
The other routes page with cursor marks (a float) and return AnnotationPage models; next_cursor_mark is None once the API reports exhaustion.

page = await client.annotations.by_entity("aspirin", page_size=100)
while page.next_cursor_mark is not None:
    for record in page.articles:
        ...
    page = await client.annotations.by_entity(
        "aspirin", cursor=page.next_cursor_mark, page_size=100
    )

await client.annotations.by_provider("Europe PMC", page_size=100)
await client.annotations.by_relationship("aspirin", "heart", page_size=100)
await client.annotations.by_section(type="Diseases", page_size=100)

by_provider takes a provider name such as Europe PMC, OpenTargets, or HES-SO_SIB; an unknown name answers 400. by_section covers the whole annotation store without a filter, so it requires at least type or section and raises ConfigurationError otherwise.

docs.title: Articles
docs.text: client.articles covers the article record and its sibling routes. Combined ids use the SOURCE:ID form (MED:23903748, PMC:PMC4221854, PPR:...).

docs.title: One record
docs.text:
article = await client.articles.get("MED:23903748")
print(article.title, article.cited_by_count)
print(article.journal_info.journal.title)
print(article.author_list.author[0].author_id.value)  # ORCID

found = await client.articles.exists("MED:23903748")

get() requests resultType=core and raises NotFoundError for an unknown id. exists() sends GET, because the gateway answers HEAD with 405.

docs.title: Full text and supplementary files
docs.text:
document = await client.articles.full_text_xml("PMC13810549")
print(document.xml[:200])  # JATS article XML as text

book = await client.articles.book_xml("NBK32884")
if book.message:
    print(book.message, book.is_open_access)

bundle = await client.articles.supplementary_files("PMC13810549")
# bytes of a ZIP archive

full_text_xml and book_xml return an XmlDocument wrapper around the answer text; typed JATS parsing is out of scope. Both routes answer 404 for articles without open access full text, and the book route answers HTTP 200 with a wrapper document (its message and isOpenAccess land on the model) when the id is valid but not open access. supplementary_files returns the raw ZIP archive bytes; pass include_inline_image=True to add the inline images.

docs.title: References and citations
docs.text:
Both routes page with page and pageSize and return Citation models with total set to the list size of the article.

references = await client.articles.references("MED:23903748", page=1, page_size=25)
citations = await client.articles.citations("MED:23903748", page=1, page_size=25)
print(references.total, citations.total)

docs.title: Links
docs.text:
db_links = await client.articles.database_links("MED:23903748", page_size=25)

data_links = await client.articles.data_links("MED:23903748")
category = data_links.data_link_list.category[0]
print(category.name, category.category_link_count)
link = category.section[0].linklist.link[0]
print(link.target.title, link.relationship_type.name)

labs = await client.articles.labs_links("MED:23903748")
for provider in labs.links_count_list.provider:
    print(provider.provider_name, provider.links_count)

database_links returns the curated cross-references as paged DatabaseLink records. data_links returns one envelope of Category entries (Altmetric, BioStudies, and others) with the link records inside; category and obtained_by narrow it. labs_links returns per-provider link counts.

docs.title: Status updates
docs.text:
response = await client.articles.status_updates(["PPR:PPR324115", "MED:23903748"])
print(response.metrics.articles_with_status_update)
for article in response.articles_with_status_update or []:
    print(article.ext_id, article.status_updates)

This is the article status monitor (POST /status-update-search): it reports the status changes Europe PMC recorded for the queried articles, for example preprints that received a published version. Articles without updates are counted in metrics but do not appear in the answer list; only tracked articles (mostly preprints that later were published in a journal) carry updates.

docs.title: Evaluations
docs.text:
response = await client.articles.evaluations("MED:23903748")
print(response.evaluation_list.evaluation)

docs.title: Grants (the Grist API)
docs.text:
client.grants talks to the grants RESTful (Grist) API, a separate service that holds the grants of the Europe PMC funders.

response = await client.grants.search("malaria", page=1)
print(response.hit_count)  # the API reports it as a string
for record in response.record_list.record:
    print(record.grant.id, record.grant.funder.name, record.person.family_name)

records = await client.grants.iterate("ga:Wellcome Trust", limit=10)  # 10 pages

search returns the typed GrantsResponse envelope; the route pages with page and has no page-size parameter. iterate walks pages until the record list empties, bounded by limit pages when given. Grist wants the parameters glued to the query path (get/query=malaria&format=json&page=1); the client builds that URL.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
response = await client.profiles.profile('AUTH:"Kucsko G"')
for source in response.profile_list.source:
    print(source.name, source.count)

profile is one request, not paged: it reports the article counts per source (MED, PMC, PPR, and others), publication type, and subset for a query. profile_type accepts all, lite, or core; synonym=True expands MeSH synonyms.

docs.title: Preprints
docs.text:
Europe PMC indexes preprints under the PPR source. client.preprints is the search resource scoped to that source: it wraps every query in SRC:PPR AND (...).

page = await client.preprints.search(query="nanodiamond", page_size=25)
print(page.total, page.results[0].source)  # PPR

async for record in client.preprints.iterate(page_size=100):
    print(record.id)

docs.title: Search
docs.text: client.search talks to /search. Every method sends format=json and returns :class:Page objects whose records are SearchResult models.

docs.title: One page
docs.text:
page = await client.search.search(
    query="nanodiamond AND OPEN_ACCESS:Y", result_type="core", page_size=25
)
print(page.total)  # hitCount
print(page.next_cursor)  # nextCursorMark
print(page.results[0].title)
  • query is a Europe PMC query string: free text, field queries (DOI:, PMCID:, AUTH:, SRC:PMC), boolean operators, and parentheses.
  • result_type is "lite" (scalar metadata), "core" (adds abstract, keywords, MeSH headings, grants, chemicals, full text URLs, and more), or "idlist", "json", "xml", "dc". The model accepts all shapes; unknown fields are kept on the model.
  • synonym=True expands query terms with MeSH synonyms.
  • sort is an expression such as "CITED desc", "P_PDATE_D asc", or "PDATE desc". The client rejects expressions whose field is not one of CITED, P_PDATE_D, PDATE, AUTHOR_ID, or RELEVANCE.
  • page_size is capped at 1000, the maximum the API accepts.

docs.title: Iterate everything
docs.text:
The search pages with cursorMark tokens. nextCursorMark repeats unchanged once the result list is exhausted, and the framework stops on that.

async for record in client.search.iterate(
    query="cancer", result_type="lite", page_size=1000
):
    print(record.id, record.source)

# resume later from a saved cursor
async for record in client.search.iterate(query="cancer", cursor=saved_cursor):
    ...

A search can take several seconds. The client default timeout is 30 seconds.
