docs.text: total = await client.search.count(query="SRC:PPR AND TITLE:nanodiamond")

docs.title: Search over POST
docs.text:
POST /searchPOST is the same search with the parameters in a form-encoded body. search_post() mirrors search(), and cursor paging works on the route, so iterate_post() mirrors iterate().

page = await client.search.search_post(query="cancer", result_type="core")
async for record in client.search.iterate_post(query="cancer", page_size=1000):
    print(record.id)

docs.title: Index terms
docs.text:
fields = await client.search.fields()
# ["ACCESSION_ID", "ABSTRACT", ...]

client.profiles.fields() returns the same list as a typed FieldsResponse model.

docs.title: Upstream quirks
docs.text: Findings from about 70 requests against the live Europe PMC services on 2026-11-27, with the RESTful web service documentation, the OpenAPI document at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/v3/api-docs, the annotations API page, and the grants API page as references. Where a quirk affects europaea, the behavior of the client is noted.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
• pageSize accepts at most 1000; a larger value answers HTTP 404 with {"errCode": 404, "errMsg": "Invalid page size provided. Valid size is between 1 and 1000"}.
  • Search pages with cursorMark tokens (opaque base64); the first request uses cursorMark=*. nextCursorMark repeats unchanged once the result list is exhausted; the framework cursor iteration stops on that.
  • sort takes field asc|desc with the fields CITED, P_PDATE_D, PDATE, AUTHOR_ID, and RELEVANCE. The query=... sort_cited:y spelling from the documentation also works.
  • synonym=true|false is echoed in the request envelope.
  • A search can take several seconds; one SRC:PMC AND OPEN_ACCESS:Y search took about ten seconds. The client timeout default of 30 seconds covers it.
  • The search service answers transient HTTP 503 (Search service is temporarily unavailable) for some requests. The framework retry policy retries it.

docs.title: Article records and per-article routes
docs.text:
• /article/{source}/{id} wraps the record in a result key alongside hitCount and the request echo. The unwrapper returns the record.
  • fullTextXML and supplementaryFiles take a bare id (PMC13810549, NBK32884), not the SOURCE:ID form. fullTextXML answers 404 for articles without open access full text (MED/23903748 answers 404; the PMC twin of the same article also has no JATS full text).
  • bookXML answers HTTP 200 with a namespace-heavy wrapper document that carries <message>Article is not either Open Access article or a valid NBK/PM ID</message> and <isOpenAccess>N</isOpenAccess> for a book without open access XML. The client raises NotFoundError on that shape.
  • XML routes need Accept: application/xml (or anything but JSON): fullTextXML answers 406 to Accept: application/json. The client overrides the per-request header.
  • references, citations, and databaseLinks page with page and pageSize (pageSize=1000 works on references). The request echo of citations and databaseLinks does not reflect the requested page (offSet stays 1); the records are still the requested page.
  • The routes are /{source}/{id}/databaseLinks (curated, database, page, pageSize parameters) and /{source}/{id}/datalinks (lowercase, not paged, category, obtainedBy parameters). dataLinks (camelCase) answers 404.
  • datalinks answers dataLinkList.Category with nested Section and Linklist.Link records whose keys are PascalCase (Name, Title, LinkProvider). The models alias them.
  • labsLinks returns per-provider link counts and also pages with page and pageSize.
  • evaluations/{source}/{id} returns evaluationList.evaluation, empty for most articles.
  • These routes do not exist in the current service (all answer 404 on 2026-11-27, and none appears in the OpenAPI document): comments, correctionsAndErratum, and textMinedTerms (with or without a type suffix). Comments and corrections are part of the core record (commentCorrectionList); text-mined terms moved to the annotations API.
  • The /preprint/{source}/{id} routes that older documentation lists (fullTextXML, annotations, supplementaryFiles, references, citations, databaseLinks, datalinks, labsLinks) all answer 404 (verified 2026-11-27). A preprint record is available through /article/PPR/{id}, and /{id}/supplementaryFiles works for a preprint id. /article/PPR/{id}/references answers 404, and /{id}/fullTextXML answers 500 for a preprint id.

docs.title: The POST search and the status monitor (verified 2026-11-27)
docs.text:
• POST /searchPOST is the GET search with the parameters (query, resultType, synonym, cursorMark, pageSize, sort, format) in an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body. Without format=json in the body the route answers XML. cursorMark paging works identically (verified with a two-page walk). europaea wraps it as search_post() and iterate_post().
  • POST /status-update-search takes Content-Type: application/json with a body {"ids": [{"src": "PPR", "extId": "PPR324115"}, ...]} and answers {"metrics": {...}, "articlesWithStatusUpdate": [...]}. metrics counts queried, found, without update, with update, and articlesNotFound. Articles with updates carry src, ext_ID, title, firstPublishDate, statusUpdates (for example ["PUBLISHED_VERSION_AVAILABLE"]), and links (SELF, PUBLISHED_ARTICLE; the href values can literally start with "null", as in nullMED/35166174).
  • The route returns data only for articles the status monitor tracks. 8 requests over 2026-11-27: 25 recent PPR records and 40 random PMC records answered 0 updates; 30 PPR records from 2020 answered 14 with updates (preprints that received a published version). Recent preprints and journal articles do not carry updates, so an empty articlesWithStatusUpdate is a normal answer, not an error. europaea wraps it as client.articles.status_updates().

docs.title: Annotations API
docs.text:
• annotationsByArticleIds takes comma-joined articleIds (MED:23903748 or PMC:PMC4221854) and answers a JSON list of per-article records.
  • annotationsByEntity (parameter entity), annotationsByProvider (parameter provider), annotationsByRelationship (parameters firstEntity and secondEntity), and annotationsBySectionAndOrType page with a float cursorMark and answer {cursorMark, nextCursorMark, articles}. Exhaustion is signaled with nextCursorMark of -1.0, which the client maps to None.
  • annotationsByProvider rejects unknown provider names with 400 and lists the valid names in the error message.
  • annotationsBySectionAndOrType without any filter returns the whole annotation store (a test request with only section=Methods answered about 24 MB). The client requires type or section.

docs.title: Grants (Grist) API
docs.text:
• The query endpoint is https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/GristAPI/rest/get/query=<q>&format=json&page=N. The parameters must be glued to the path with &. With a ? query string (...query=malaria?format=json) the route content-negotiates and answers 406 for Accept: application/json, and answers XML otherwise; the format=json parameter is ignored in that position.
  • A pageSize query parameter is concatenated into the query string (Query: "pageSize=2malaria"). The route has no page size.
  • The answer keys are PascalCase (HitCount, Request, RecordList) and HitCount is a JSON string.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text: The Europe PMC documentation publishes no rate limit and no hard request limit for unauthenticated callers. europaea defaults to 3 requests per second and a concurrency of 2 out of courtesy, and keeps the framework timeout default of 30 seconds because a search can take about ten seconds.

docs.title: hodoi
docs.text:
The package is not yet published on PyPI. Until the first release, install it from a checkout of the bibliofabric workspace, where uv sync --all-packages installs it together with the bibliofabric 0.8 it needs.

hodoi is a Python client for the DOI System proxy server at doi.org, built on bibliofabric. It looks up the registration agency of a DOI, reads the Handle.net record behind it, returns the redirect a DOI resolves to, and retrieves metadata through content negotiation in every representation Crossref, DataCite, and mEDRA serve. It ships an async client and a generated sync twin with the same API. The proxy needs no credentials.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv sync --all-packages

Run the command from the root of the bibliofabric workspace checkout. It requires Python 3.12 or newer.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import asyncio
from hodoi import CSL_JSON, HodoiClient


async def main():
    async with HodoiClient() as client:
        print(await client.agency("10.1038/nature12373"))
        item = await client.content("10.1038/nature12373", CSL_JSON)
        print(item.title)
        print(await client.landing_url("10.1038/nature12373"))


asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Sync usage
docs.text:
The generated HodoiSyncClient has the same methods without async and await:

from hodoi import CSL_JSON, HodoiSyncClient

with HodoiSyncClient() as client:
    record = client.handle("10.1038/nature12373")
    item = client.content("10.1038/nature12373", CSL_JSON)
    print(item.title)

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: HodoiSettings loads from environment variables prefixed with HODOI_ and from a .env file in the working directory. HODOI_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND (default 2) and HODOI_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 2) set the request pace, HODOI_TIMEOUT (default 60) sets the timeout, and HODOI_FOLLOW_REDIRECTS (default off) decides whether a request follows the resolver's 302. doi.org publishes no rate limit, so the pace is a courtesy. The other shared fields of bibliofabric.config.BaseApiSettings also apply, such as HODOI_MAX_RETRIES, HODOI_MAX_RETRY_WAIT, and HODOI_USER_AGENT.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Registration agencies covers the /ra/ lookup, single and batched.
  • Handles covers the handle records, the landing URLs, the redirect of a DOI, and its redirect targets.
  • Metadata covers content negotiation and its media types.
  • The API reference is generated from the source, and upstream quirks lists what the live service does, verified on 2026-11-27 and 2026-11-28.

docs.title: Registration agencies
docs.text: Every DOI is registered with exactly one registration agency (RA). The proxy answers GET /ra/{doi} with a JSON list that names it. client.agencies() sends that request and returns AgencyAnswer models.

docs.title: One DOI
docs.text:
answer = await client.agency("10.1038/nature12373")
print(answer.DOI, answer.RA)  # 10.1038/nature12373 Crossref

The argument can be a bare DOI, a https://doi.org/ URL, or a doi: string. The client strips the wrapper and sends the rest. It does not reject a malformed string, because the proxy answers a malformed string with status: "Invalid DOI" instead of an error. A query string or fragment in the URL is cut first, as in https://doi.org/10.1038/nature12373?from=mail.

docs.title: Many DOIs
docs.text:
answers = await client.agencies(
    ["10.1038/nature12373", "10.5281/zenodo.1238808", "10.1400/56174"]
)
print([(answer.DOI, answer.RA) for answer in answers])
# Crossref, DataCite, mEDRA

agencies() joins the DOIs with commas into one request. A request holds at most 100 DOIs (hodoi.RA_BATCH_SIZE) and stays under 4000 path characters (hodoi.RA_MAX_PATH_CHARS), so a list of long DOIs takes more, smaller requests. The result order follows the request order across requests.

A longer URL would fail. The proxy answered HTTP 414 (URI Too Long) for a 500-DOI request.

docs.title: Unknown and malformed DOIs
docs.text:
The proxy answers HTTP 200 in every case. A known DOI carries RA; an unknown or malformed one carries a status string instead:

Input Answer Known DOI RA is the agency name (Crossref, DataCite, mEDRA, ...) Unregistered DOI status is DOI does not exist Malformed string status is Invalid DOI Unknown prefix status is Unknown

AgencyAnswer models both shapes. RA is None when status is set. Nothing raises for an unknown or malformed DOI. Decide from answer.RA or answer.status.

Two inputs raise before a request is sent. An empty list raises ConfigurationError, and so does a blank DOI.

docs.title: Encoding in the path
docs.text: The client percent-encodes every DOI before it enters the path, because the proxy decodes the path before it matches the DOI. 10.1000/a#b travels as /ra/10.1000/a%23b. A comma inside a DOI travels as %2C, so it does not split the list.

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
Field Content DOI The DOI as echoed by the proxy RA The agency name, or None for a status answer status The error string, or None for a known DOI

Unknown extra fields pass through (extra="allow"). Every entry of the answer is validated. A body that is not a list raises ConfigurationError, and an entry that is not an object raises ValidationError.

docs.title: Handles
docs.text: A DOI is a Handle System identifier. The proxy exposes the underlying record at GET /api/handles/{doi}, and client.handle() types it as HandleRecord.

docs.title: Read a record
docs.text:
record = await client.handle("10.1038/nature12373")
print(record.responseCode)  # 1
for value in record.values:
    print(value.index, value.type, value.data.format)
# 1 URL string
# 700050 700050 string
# 100 HS_ADMIN admin

The argument can be a bare DOI or a DOI URL. Anything that is not a DOI name raises ConfigurationError before a request is sent. The client percent-encodes the DOI for the path, so a suffix with parentheses, angle brackets, colons, or a semicolon needs no extra work:

sici = "10.1002/(SICI)1097-4636(199823)43:3<338::AID-JBM16>3.0.CO;2-B"
record = await client.handle(sici)
print(
    record.values[0].data.value
)  # https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/(SICI)...

An unknown DOI answers HTTP 404 (responseCode 100), which raises NotFoundError. A record that exists but has no values answers responseCode 200 with an empty values list. A filter that matches no value answers the same way.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
record = await client.handle("10.1038/nature12373", type="URL")
record = await client.handle("10.1038/nature12373", index=[1, 100])
record = await client.handle("10.1038/nature12373", type=["URL", "HS_ADMIN"])
record = await client.handle("10.1038/nature12373", auth=True, cert=True)

type and index restrict the returned values. Each takes one value or a list. A list is sent as repeated parameters, and the proxy returns the values that match any of them. A blank entry raises ConfigurationError before a request is sent.

auth=True bypasses the proxy cache and asks the primary handle server. The proxy caches values for up to 24 hours, so a freshly changed URL can be stale without it. cert=True asks the primary server for an authenticated answer.

docs.title: The record model
docs.text:
Field Content responseCode 1 success, 100 handle not found, 200 values not found handle The DOI as echoed by the proxy values List of HandleValue entries message Error explanation, on failures

Each HandleValue has index, type, data (a HandleValueData with format and value), ttl in seconds, and an ISO 8601 timestamp. The format is string for the common text values, admin for HS_ADMIN (the value parses into a HandleAdminValue), and base64, hex, vlist, or site for the rarer shapes. Anything the client does not type passes through as extra fields.

docs.title: Landing URLs
docs.text:
url = await client.landing_url("10.1038/nature12373")
# https://www.nature.com/articles/nature12373

landing_url() reads the URL entry of the record and returns it without fetching the landing page. It raises ConfigurationError when the record has no URL value.

docs.title: The redirect of a DOI
docs.text:
response = await client.resolve("10.1038/nature12373")
print(response.status_code, response.headers["location"])
# 302 https://www.nature.com/articles/nature12373

resolve() sends GET https://doi.org/{doi} for text/html and returns the proxy's 302 as an httpx.Response. The Location header holds the landing page URL, and the body is a small HTML page titled "Handle Redirect". Redirects stay off unless the HODOI_FOLLOW_REDIRECTS setting is on, so the response is the 302 itself. An unknown DOI answers 404, which raises NotFoundError.

docs.title: The redirect targets of a DOI
docs.text:
for location in await client.locations("10.1038/nature12373"):
    print(location.mode, location.http_role, location.href)
# legacy None https://www.nature.com/articles/nature12373
# None conneg https://api.crossref.org/v1/works/10.1038%2Fnature12373/transform

locations() sends GET https://doi.org/{doi}?action=showurls. The proxy answers an XML listing with one location element for every URL it could redirect to. An ordinary DOI has two entries. The landing page carries mode="legacy" and a numeric weight. The metadata server of the registration agency carries http_role="conneg" and a href_template, in which {hdl} stands for the DOI. A DOI with multiple resolution lists its further locations.

Field Content href The URL mode legacy for the landing page, otherwise None weight The proxy's preference as a string http_role conneg for the metadata server, otherwise None href_template The URL pattern of the metadata server

Every other attribute of the element passes through as an extra field. An unknown DOI answers 404, which raises NotFoundError.

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text:
Content negotiation turns a plain DOI URL into a metadata endpoint. Send an Accept header to GET https://doi.org/{doi}, and the resolver redirects to the data server of the registration agency, which answers the metadata in the requested format. client.content() sends the request, follows the redirect, and parses the answer.

from hodoi import BIBTEX, CSL_JSON, HodoiClient

async with HodoiClient() as client:
    item = await client.content("10.1038/nature12373", CSL_JSON)
    print(item.title, item.container_title)

    bib = await client.content("10.1038/nature12373", BIBTEX)
    print(bib)

docs.title: The media type catalog
docs.text:
Import the strings from hodoi.media_types instead of typing them by hand:

Constant Media type Crossref DataCite mEDRA CSL_JSON application/vnd.citationstyles.csl+json yes yes yes DATACITE_JSON application/vnd.datacite.datacite+json no yes no DATACITE_XML application/vnd.datacite.datacite+xml no yes no SCHEMAORG_JSONLD application/vnd.schemaorg.ld+json no yes no UNIXREF_XML application/vnd.crossref.unixref+xml yes no no UNIXSD_XML application/vnd.crossref.unixsd+xml yes no no ONIX_DOI_XML application/vnd.medra.onixdoi+xml no no yes BIBTEX application/x-bibtex yes yes yes RIS application/x-research-info-systems yes yes yes BIBLIOGRAPHY text/x-bibliography yes yes yes RDF_XML application/rdf+xml yes no yes TURTLE text/turtle yes no yes

AGENCY_SUPPORT carries the same matrix as data. The matrix was checked against one DOI of each agency on 2026-11-28. It differs from the table of the DOI Foundation page for RIS and for the two RDF formats. See upstream quirks.

Requesting a type the agency does not serve raises APIError with the agency's error body, for example a DataCite DOI with UNIXREF_XML or a Crossref DOI with SCHEMAORG_JSONLD. The status is 406 in most cases.

docs.title: Parsed and text representations
docs.text:
content() parses the three JSON media types into models. CSL_JSON becomes a CslItem, DATACITE_JSON a DataciteRecord, and SCHEMAORG_JSONLD a SchemaOrgThing. Each model pins the identity fields and allows every other field through, because all three schemas are large and open. Every other media type returns its text unchanged (BibTeX, RIS, the XML dialects, formatted citations).

A media type may carry parameters. The client reads the type before the semicolon, so f"{CSL_JSON}; charset=utf-8" parses like CSL_JSON.

When the agency answers HTTP 204, content() returns None.

docs.title: The un-parsed bytes
docs.text:
raw() returns the bytes of the answer instead of a model or text. With the default setting it returns the body of the resolver's 302, a small HTML page titled "Handle Redirect" that links to the data server of the agency. The method returns bytes only. To read the Location header of the redirect, call resolve().

Pass follow_redirects=True to receive the bytes of the metadata itself:

payload = await client.raw("10.1038/nature12373", CSL_JSON)  # body of the 302
payload = await client.raw(
    "10.1038/nature12373", CSL_JSON, follow_redirects=True
)  # CSL JSON bytes

The HODOI_FOLLOW_REDIRECTS setting is off by default. content() always follows the redirect, and raw() follows it only when the setting is on or you pass follow_redirects=True.

docs.title: Reference pages
docs.text:
• DOI Foundation, DOI content negotiation: the format matrix and response codes.
  • Crossref, Content negotiation: the Crossref formats and how the resolver redirects to the /transform route.
  • mEDRA answers content negotiation from its own server, data.medra.org. The DOI Foundation page documents its ONIX for DOI type.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text: Generated from the source with mkdocstrings.

docs.title: hodoi.HodoiClient
docs.text:
Bases: BaseApiClient

Client for the DOI System proxy server at https://doi.org.

The proxy needs no credentials. It resolves DOIs (resolve, locations), looks up registration agencies (/ra/), serves Handle.net records (/api/handles/), and negotiates metadata representations on plain DOI URLs (content, raw).

Redirects stay off by default so a caller can inspect the resolver's 302 response. :meth:content turns them on for the request it sends.

docs.title: agencies(dois) async
docs.text:
Return the registration agency of one or many DOIs.

Sends GET /ra/{doi} with the DOIs joined by commas. A request carries at most :data:~hodoi.dialect.RA_BATCH_SIZE DOIs and stays under :data:~hodoi.dialect.RA_MAX_PATH_CHARS characters, so a long list takes several requests. Every entry arrives as HTTP 200: known DOIs carry RA, unknown ones a status string, both modeled as :class:~hodoi.models.AgencyAnswer. The result order follows the request order across requests. The argument takes a bare DOI, a DOI URL, or a doi: string; anything else is sent as given, and the proxy answers Invalid DOI.

docs.title: agency(doi) async
docs.text: Return the registration agency answer for one DOI.

docs.title: handle(doi, *, index=None, type=None, auth=False, cert=False) async
docs.text:
Return the Handle.net record of a DOI.

Sends GET /api/handles/{doi} and validates the answer into :class:~hodoi.models.HandleRecord. index and type restrict the returned values; each takes one value or a list, and the proxy answers the values that match any of them. auth=True bypasses the proxy cache and asks the primary handle server; cert=True asks for an authenticated answer from it. An unknown DOI answers HTTP 404, which raises :class:bibliofabric.exceptions.NotFoundError.

docs.title: landing_url(doi) async
docs.text:
Return the landing page URL stored in the DOI's handle record.

Reads the URL entry of the record without fetching the landing page itself. A DOI whose record has no URL value raises :class:bibliofabric.exceptions.ConfigurationError; :meth:locations lists the URLs of a multiple-resolution DOI.

docs.title: resolve(doi) async
docs.text:
Return the proxy's answer to GET https://doi.org/{doi}.

The request asks for text/html, so the proxy answers 302 with the landing page URL in the Location header and a small HTML body titled "Handle Redirect". Redirects follow the follow_redirects setting (off by default), so the response is the 302 itself unless the setting is on. An unknown DOI answers 404, which raises :class:bibliofabric.exceptions.NotFoundError.

docs.title: locations(doi) async
docs.text:
Return every URL the proxy could redirect a DOI to.

Sends GET https://doi.org/{doi}?action=showurls, the proxy's XML listing. An ordinary DOI has two entries: the landing page (mode="legacy") and the registration agency's metadata server (http_role="conneg", with a href_template). A multiple-resolution DOI lists its further locations. An unknown DOI answers 404, which raises :class:bibliofabric.exceptions.NotFoundError.

docs.title: content(doi, media_type) async
docs.text:
Return the negotiated metadata representation for a DOI.

Sends GET https://doi.org/{doi} with the given Accept header and follows the resolver's redirect to the registration agency's data server. The three JSON media types parse into typed models (:class:~hodoi.models.CslItem for :data:~hodoi.media_types.CSL_JSON, :class:~hodoi.models.DataciteRecord for :data:~hodoi.media_types.DATACITE_JSON, :class:~hodoi.models.SchemaOrgThing for :data:~hodoi.media_types.SCHEMAORG_JSONLD); every other media type (BibTeX, RIS, the XML dialects, a formatted citation) returns as text. The answer is None when the agency reports 204, which means that no metadata is available. A media type the agency does not answer raises :class:bibliofabric.exceptions.APIError with its HTTP 406.

docs.title: raw(doi, media_type, *, follow_redirects=None) async
docs.text:
Return the un-parsed bytes of a negotiated representation.

follow_redirects=None keeps the client setting (off), so the bytes are the resolver's 302 body ("Handle Redirect"); pass follow_redirects=True to receive the agency's metadata bytes. To read the Location header of the 302, use :meth:resolve.

docs.title: hodoi.HodoiSettings
docs.text:
Bases: BaseApiSettings

DOI System client settings.

Inherits timeout, max_retries, max_retry_wait, max_requests_per_second, max_concurrency, user_agent, mailto and follow_redirects from :class:bibliofabric.config.BaseApiSettings and sets DOI defaults (2 req/s, concurrency 2, timeout 60 s). No credentials exist for doi.org.

follow_redirects stays False: the resolver answers metadata requests with a 302 whose body and Location header point at the registration agency's data server. Pass follow_redirects=True per request (the client does this for content()), or set it to True here to follow redirects globally.

docs.title: hodoi.models.AgencyAnswer
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

One entry of the GET /ra/{doi} JSON list.

A known DOI carries the registration agency name in RA (for example Crossref, DataCite, mEDRA). An unknown or malformed DOI has RA=None and a status string (DOI does not exist, Invalid DOI, or Unknown). The HTTP status is 200 in every case.

docs.title: hodoi.models.HandleRecord
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

The JSON object of GET /api/handles/{doi}.

responseCode 1 means success; 100 means handle not found (then the proxy answers HTTP 404 and message explains which part failed). 200 means values not found, which arrives as HTTP 200 with no values.

docs.title: hodoi.models.HandleValue
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

One entry of a handle record.

type is URL for the landing page link, HS_ADMIN for the administrator entry, HS_ALIAS for an alias, or a numeric type such as 700050. ttl is the cache time in seconds; the timestamp is an ISO 8601 string.

docs.title: hodoi.models.HandleValueData
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

The data object of one handle value.

format is one of string, base64, hex, admin, vlist, or site. value is the decoded string for the first three formats, an :class:HandleAdminValue for admin, and the raw extra fields carry the rarer vlist and site shapes.

docs.title: hodoi.models.HandleAdminValue
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

The value of an HS_ADMIN entry: the administrator handle.

docs.title: hodoi.models.CslItem
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

One CSL JSON item (application/vnd.citationstyles.csl+json).

docs.title: hodoi.models.DataciteRecord
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

One DataCite JSON record (application/vnd.datacite.datacite+json).

docs.title: hodoi.models.SchemaOrgThing
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

One schema.org JSON-LD document (application/vnd.schemaorg.ld+json).

docs.title: hodoi.models.RedirectLocation
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

One location element of the proxy's redirect listing.

href is the URL. The proxy sends mode="legacy" and a numeric weight for the landing page, http_role="conneg" and href_template for the registration agency's metadata server, and other attributes for the locations of a multiple-resolution DOI. Every attribute stays, as the string the proxy sends.

docs.title: hodoi.normalize_doi(value) cached
docs.text:
Return the bare DOI for a DOI, DOI URL, or doi: string.

Accepts 10.1038/nature12373, https://doi.org/10.1038/nature12373, http://dx.doi.org/10.1038/nature12373, and doi:10.1038/nature12373. Anything else raises :class:bibliofabric.exceptions.ConfigurationError.

docs.title: hodoi.doi_path(doi)
docs.text:
Return doi percent-encoded for the path of a doi.org URL.

The DOI 10.1000/res#test becomes 10.1000/res%23test, the form the proxy resolves (see the DOI Resolution Documentation, section 2).

docs.title: hodoi.ra_chunks(dois)
docs.text:
Group percent-encoded DOIs into the comma-separated bodies of /ra/ paths.

A chunk holds at most :data:RA_BATCH_SIZE DOIs and stays under :data:RA_MAX_PATH_CHARS characters, so long DOIs form more, smaller requests. A single DOI that is longer than the budget travels alone.

docs.title: hodoi.strip_doi_form(value)
docs.text:
Strip DOI URL and doi: wrappers without validating the result.

A URL wrapper carries the DOI percent-encoded, as in https://doi.org/10.1000/res%23test; the function decodes it. In a URL a raw ? starts the query string and a raw # the fragment, so both are cut, as in https://doi.org/10.1038/nature12373?from=x. A bare DOI keeps them, because both are legal characters of a DOI name. The /ra/ route answers malformed strings itself (Invalid DOI), so the lookup sends whatever it gets after the wrapper is removed.

docs.title: hodoi.parse_locations(text)
docs.text:
Parse the XML of ?action=showurls into :class:RedirectLocation.

The proxy answers <locations><location ... /></locations> with every URL it could redirect to. Raises :class:ConfigurationError for a body that is not that document, and :class:ValidationError for a location without an href.

docs.title: Upstream quirks
docs.text:
Findings from about 60 requests against the live DOI System proxy (doi.org) on 2026-11-27, from further requests on 2026-11-28 that checked the encoding of DOIs in the path, the handle filters, the redirect of a DOI, the redirect listing, and the full format matrix, and from the reference pages. Where a quirk affects hodoi, the behavior of the client is noted.

Reference pages used:

  • DOI Foundation factsheet, DOI Resolution Documentation (proxy routes, /ra/ and the REST API, response codes, query parameters).
  • DOI Foundation, DOI content negotiation (format matrix, response codes, redirect behavior).
  • Crossref, Content negotiation.

docs.title: The /ra/ lookup
docs.text:
• The answer is a JSON list with one {DOI, RA} object per requested DOI, even for a single DOI. The factsheet documents the route as https://doi.org/doiRA/; /ra/ answers identically, and both were verified. hodoi uses /ra/.
  • Every answer has HTTP 200. A known DOI carries RA; an unknown DOI carries status: "DOI does not exist", a malformed string status: "Invalid DOI", and an unknown prefix status: "Unknown" (the last one from the factsheet; not exercised live). hodoi models both shapes in AgencyAnswer and raises nothing.
  • Prefix-only strings work. /ra/10.7334 answers RA: "Crossref", and /ra/10.3205 answers RA: "DataCite".
  • Comma-separated DOIs go into one path segment. Lists of 100, 150, and 200 short DOIs were accepted (entries echoed in request order, mixed known and unknown). A 500-DOI URL answered HTTP 414 with an HTML error page. The proxy decodes each DOI after it splits the path, so a literal comma separates two DOIs and %2C inside one DOI does not. hodoi chunks at 100 DOIs and at 4000 path characters; the path limit of the proxy is not documented.
  • ?pretty=true answers the same JSON indented (verified 2026-11-28). hodoi does not send it.
  • Agency names observed live: Crossref, DataCite, mEDRA (the mEDRA DOI 10.1400/56174 was found by probing known mEDRA prefixes).

docs.title: Encoding in the path
docs.text: • The proxy percent-decodes the path before it matches the DOI (verified 2026-11-28). A DOI whose suffix has <, >, ;, (, ), #, ?, or a space resolves when those characters are percent-encoded, and a non-ASCII suffix travels as percent-encoded UTF-8. hodoi sends every DOI percent-encoded through doi_path(), and it decodes a DOI URL before it encodes the DOI again.

docs.title: Content negotiation
docs.text:
• A metadata request (any Accept except text/html) answers 302 with a small HTML body titled "Handle Redirect" whose only link is the data server of the agency. The link is https://api.crossref.org/v1/works/{urlencoded doi}/transform for Crossref, https://data.crosscite.org/{urlencoded doi} for DataCite, and https://data.medra.org/{urlencoded doi} for mEDRA. hodoi's content() follows this redirect; raw() returns the 302 body itself unless redirects are on.
  • Without an Accept header, with text/html, or with Accept: */* (verified 2026-11-28), the 302 points at the publisher landing page instead. The redirect body is the same small HTML page. An unknown DOI answers 404 with an HTML page. hodoi's resolve() sends Accept: text/html and returns the 302.
  • HEAD behaves like GET at the resolver. It answers 302 with the same Location header and no body, for both metadata and landing-page requests.
  • The full format matrix was checked on 2026-11-28 with one DOI of each agency. The table of the DOI Foundation page differs for RIS, which mEDRA serves, and for RDF XML and Turtle, which DataCite does not serve. hodoi follows the live answers in AGENCY_SUPPORT.
Agency HTTP 200 Other answers Crossref (10.1038/nature12373) CSL JSON, Unixref XML, Unixsd XML, BibTeX, RIS, text/x-bibliography, RDF XML, Turtle 406 with a text/plain body (No acceptable resource available.) for DataCite JSON, DataCite XML, schema.org JSON-LD, and ONIX for DOI DataCite (10.5281/zenodo.1238808) CSL JSON, DataCite JSON, DataCite XML, schema.org JSON-LD, BibTeX, RIS, text/x-bibliography 406 with an application/json body for Unixref XML, Unixsd XML, ONIX for DOI, and Turtle; 422 with a text/plain body (The request could not be processed.) for RDF XML mEDRA (10.1400/56174) CSL JSON, ONIX for DOI, BibTeX, RIS, text/x-bibliography, RDF XML, Turtle 406 with an HTML error page from the mEDRA server for every other type
  • The content types carry parameters (; charset=utf-8 or charset=UTF-8). hodoi reads the media type from the Accept header it sent, not from the content type of the answer.
  • Crossref BibTeX answers start with a leading space (@article{...}). hodoi returns the text unchanged; strip before parsing.
  • Content negotiation returns one record at a time; there is no batch form.
  • An HTTP 204 answer was not observed live on either day. hodoi returns None for it.

docs.title: The Handle REST API
docs.text:
• GET /api/handles/{doi} answers {responseCode, handle, values} with HTTP 200. Values carry index, type, data ({format, value}), ttl (seconds, here always 86400), and an ISO 8601 timestamp. Types seen: URL (index 1), HS_ADMIN (index 100 or 700050-adjacent), and a numeric type 700050.
  • HS_ADMIN data is {"format": "admin", "value": {"handle": "0.na/10.1038", "index": 200, "permissions": "111111110010"}} on Crossref and {"handle": "10.admin/codata", "index": 300} on the DataCite record. hodoi parses it into HandleAdminValue.
  • ?type=URL and ?index=1 each restrict the values (verified; both returned only the URL entry). Repeated parameters work (verified 2026-11-28: type=URL&type=HS_ADMIN returned both entries). ?cert=true answered the same record with HTTP 200 (verified 2026-11-28). ?recursive=true was accepted and returned the full record; the factsheet does not list it. The factsheet also documents auth and a callback JSONP parameter. hodoi sends type, index, auth, and cert.
  • Unknown prefix: HTTP 404 with {"responseCode": 100, "message": "HandleException (SERVICE_NOT_FOUND) ...", "handle": ...}. A malformed handle string (/api/handles/nonsense): HTTP 404 with {"responseCode": 100, "handle": "nonsense"} and no message. hodoi raises NotFoundError on both; normalize_doi() rejects malformed strings client-side for handle().
  • Response code 200 (values not found) answers HTTP 200 with {"responseCode": 200, "handle": ..., "values": []} (verified 2026-11-28 with ?type=NOPE). hodoi returns the record with an empty values list.
  • ?pretty=true answers the same JSON indented (verified 2026-11-28). hodoi does not send it.

docs.title: The redirect of a DOI
docs.text: • GET https://doi.org/{doi} with Accept: text/html answers 302 to the landing page, with the "Handle Redirect" HTML body. hodoi's resolve() returns that response.

docs.title: The redirect listing
docs.text:
• GET https://doi.org/{doi}?action=showurls answers HTTP 200 and text/xml (verified 2026-11-28). The body is a <locations> element with one <location> element for every URL the proxy could redirect to. The landing page carries mode="legacy", weight="1.0", and href. The data server of the agency carries weight="0", http_role="conneg", href, and a href_template, in which {hdl} stands for the DOI. hodoi's locations() parses the listing into RedirectLocation models and keeps every attribute.
  • The demo DOI 10.1000/202 lists only its landing page, with no entry for a data server. An unknown DOI answers 404 with an HTML page.
  • ?noredirect answers an HTML page that shows the DOI name and its values. It is a web page and not an API, so hodoi leaves it out.

docs.title: Politeness and limits
docs.text:
• doi.org publishes no rate limit. The factsheet asks only for the standard proxy etiquette; there is no mailto polite pool for doi.org itself (unlike Crossref). hodoi defaults to 2 requests per second and concurrency 2.
  • The proxy caches handle values with a 24-hour TTL; a changed URL can be stale without auth=True.

docs.title: Quirks in the client's own tests
docs.text:
• The live mEDRA sample (10.1400/56174) has no RA change; its landing redirect went to digital.casalini.it, not to a medra.org page. landing_url() reads the handle record, so it is unaffected.
  • The DOI Foundation HTML handbook pages moved under /doi-handbook/; the old /doi_handbook/3_Resolution.html URL now redirects to a landing page. The content-negotiation factsheet at citation.doi.org/docs.html is the stable format matrix.

docs.title: opcitato
docs.text:
The package is not yet published on PyPI. Until the first release, install it from a checkout of the bibliofabric workspace, where uv sync --all-packages installs it together with the bibliofabric 0.8 it needs.

opcitato is a Python client for the OpenCitations Index API v2, the OpenCitations Meta API v1, and the SPARQL endpoint of each dataset, built on bibliofabric. It types the citation rows, the count rows, and the bibliographic metadata with Pydantic models, parses the multi-identifier strings into (scheme, value) pairs, validates the prefixed identifiers before a request is sent, and reads the CSV representation into the same models. It ships an async client and a generated sync twin with the same API. The APIs need no credentials.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv sync --all-packages

Run the command from the root of the bibliofabric workspace checkout. It requires Python 3.12 or newer.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import asyncio
from opcitato import OpcitatoClient


async def main():
    async with OpcitatoClient() as client:
        citations = await client.index.citations("doi:10.1108/jd-12-2013-0166")
        print(len(citations), citations[0].oci)

        count = await client.index.citation_count("doi:10.1108/jd-12-2013-0166")
        print("incoming citations:", count)

        records = await client.meta.metadata("doi:10.1007/978-1-4020-9632-7")
        print(records[0].title, records[0].pub_date)

        result = await client.index.sparql(
            "SELECT ?ci ?cited WHERE { "
            "?ci <http://purl.org/spar/cito/hasCitedEntity> ?cited } LIMIT 3"
        )
        for row in result.rows():
            print(row["ci"], row["cited"])


asyncio.run(main())

client.index exposes the six Index operations (citation(), citations(), references(), citation_count(), reference_count(), venue_citation_count()) and the Index SPARQL endpoint (sparql() and sparql_text()). client.meta exposes the three Meta operations (metadata(), author(), editor()) and the Meta SPARQL endpoint. Every operation answers with the complete result; neither API pages.

docs.title: Sync usage
docs.text:
OpcitatoSyncClient is generated from the async source and behaves the same. The sync client uses plain httpx.Client and never starts or touches an event loop, so it works in scripts, in Jupyter, in threads, and when called from inside a running event loop.

from opcitato import OpcitatoSyncClient

with OpcitatoSyncClient() as client:
    for record in client.meta.author("orcid:0000-0002-8420-0696"):
        print(record.pub_date, record.title)

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: OpcitatoSettings loads from environment variables prefixed with OPCITATO_ and from a .env file in the working directory. OPCITATO_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND (default 3, matching the documented limit of 180 requests per minute per IP address) and OPCITATO_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 3) set the request pace. The shared fields of bibliofabric.config.BaseApiSettings also apply, such as OPCITATO_TIMEOUT, OPCITATO_MAX_RETRIES, OPCITATO_MAX_RETRY_WAIT, and OPCITATO_USER_AGENT.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Index API covers citations, references, counts, the row-shaping parameters, and the SPARQL endpoints of both datasets.
  • Meta API covers metadata, authors, editors, and multi-id requests.
  • Upstream quirks lists what the live APIs do differently from their documentation, with the dates each fact was verified.
  • The API reference is generated from the source.

docs.title: Index API
docs.text: The Index API v2 (https://api.opencitations.net/index/v2) stores who cites whom. client.index exposes one method per documented operation; every method sends one GET and returns the complete result.

docs.title: Citations and references
docs.text:
citations(id) returns the incoming citations of one entity: every row records a reference in which the entity is cited. references(id) returns the outgoing references in the reference list of one entity.

rows = await client.index.citations("doi:10.1108/jd-12-2013-0166")
row = rows[0]
print(row.oci)  # "06012708740-06180334099"
print(
    row.citing
)  # "omid:br/06012708740 doi:10.53730/ijhs.v9n2.15534 openalex:W4411604700"
print(
    row.cited_identifiers
)  # [ParsedIdentifier(scheme='omid', value='br/06180334099'), ...]
print(row.creation, row.timespan, row.journal_sc, row.author_sc)

id is a prefixed identifier. The Index API accepts doi:, omid:, pmid:, issn:, and isbn:; the client rejects anything else, including bare DOIs and openalex: ids, with ConfigurationError before a request is sent. The model fields:

Field Meaning oci Open Citation Identifier of the citation, first-second. citing, cited Space-separated, prefixed identifiers of the two entities. creation Publication date of the citing entity; may be partial (2013, 2013-07). timespan XSD duration between the publication dates; may be negative (-P1Y1M16D). journal_sc, author_sc "yes"/"no" strings for a journal self-citation and an author self-citation.

An unknown identifier is not an error: the API answers 200 with [] and the method returns an empty list.

The client percent-encodes the identifier for the URL path, so a DOI that contains #, ?, parentheses, or angle brackets arrives whole. The server decodes the path before it looks up the identifier.

docs.title: One citation by OCI
docs.text:
citation(oci) returns the single citation with this Open Citation Identifier, or None. The prefix is optional: "oci:1-18" and "1-18" both work.

row = await client.index.citation("06101801781-06180334099")

docs.title: Counts
docs.text:
citation_count(id) and reference_count(id) return the number of incoming citations and outgoing references of one entity. venue_citation_count(issn) returns the incoming citations to all entities published in one venue; this operation accepts only issn: ids. An unknown identifier answers 200 with a zero row, which the methods return as 0. On 2026-11-27 the API answered [] for the same request instead; the methods return None for that body.

incoming = await client.index.citation_count("doi:10.1108/jd-12-2013-0166")
venue = await client.index.venue_citation_count("issn:0138-9130")

The JSON body carries the count as a string ({"count": "57"}) even though the documentation types it as int; the Count model coerces it.

docs.title: Row shaping
docs.text:
citations(), references(), and the Meta row operations accept four parameters that the server applies in this order:

  1. require: drop rows whose field is empty. A string or a list of field names; the parameter repeats.
  2. filter: keep rows matching a regular expression, or =, <, > with a value, as in creation:>2019-12. The parameter repeats.
  3. sort: asc(field) or desc(field), for example desc(creation).
  4. format: "json" (default) or "csv".
rows = await client.index.citations(
    "doi:10.1108/jd-12-2013-0166",
    require="creation",
    filter="creation:>2019-12",
    sort="desc(creation)",
)

With format="csv" the server returns its CSV table; the client parses it into the same models, because the CSV header repeats the JSON field names. The format parameter overrides the Accept header server-side, so the header alone never changes the representation.

docs.title: SPARQL
docs.text:
Each OpenCitations dataset has a SPARQL endpoint on a second host: https://sparql.opencitations.net/index for the Index dataset and https://sparql.opencitations.net/meta for the Meta dataset. sparql() sends a query and returns the SPARQL 1.1 Query Results JSON answer as a SparqlResult. sparql_text() returns the body of another representation as text.

result = await client.index.sparql(
    "SELECT ?ci ?citing ?cited WHERE { "
    "?ci <http://purl.org/spar/cito/hasCitingEntity> ?citing ; "
    "<http://purl.org/spar/cito/hasCitedEntity> ?cited } LIMIT 5"
)
for row in result.rows():
    print(row["ci"], row["citing"], row["cited"])
print(result.meta["result-size-total"])

SparqlResult keeps the whole answer: head.vars, results.bindings, boolean for an ASK query, and meta with the query time and the number of rows the server reports. results.bindings is a list of dictionaries from variable name to SparqlTerm. Each term has type (uri, literal, or bnode) and value; a literal also carries datatype and xml_lang when the server sends them. rows() flattens the bindings into a list of dictionaries from variable name to the term's string value. It returns [] for an ASK answer, where boolean holds the result.

sparql_text() asks for one of the other result formats through the Accept header. format is one of json, xml, csv, tsv, turtle (the default), or n-triples. Use this method for CONSTRUCT and DESCRIBE queries, because their answers are RDF documents: the endpoint answers Turtle when a CONSTRUCT query asks for JSON.

turtle = await client.index.sparql_text(
    "CONSTRUCT { ?ci <http://purl.org/spar/cito/hasCitingEntity> ?citing } "
    "WHERE { ?ci <http://purl.org/spar/cito/hasCitingEntity> ?citing } LIMIT 5"
)

Both methods send the query in the URL of a GET request by default. Pass method="POST" to send it in the body of a form request instead, which suits long queries. The timeout argument sets a per-request timeout in seconds.

An empty query or an unknown format raises ConfigurationError before a request is sent. A malformed query makes the server answer 400, which raises APIError. An answer that is not a SPARQL result document raises ValidationError.

docs.title: Meta API
docs.text: The Meta API v1 (https://api.opencitations.net/meta/v1) holds the bibliographic metadata of the documents involved in the citations of the OpenCitations Index. client.meta exposes one method per documented operation. The rows share the shape of MetadataRecord.

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text:
metadata(ids) returns the bibliographic metadata of one or more entities.

records = await client.meta.metadata("doi:10.1007/978-1-4020-9632-7")
record = records[0]
print(
    record.title, record.type, record.pub_date
)  # "Adaptive Environmental Management", "book", "2009"
print(record.identifiers)  # parsed from record.id
print(record.authors, record.editors)  # split from the semicolon lists

The accepted schemes are doi, issn, isbn, omid, openalex, pmid, and pmcid (wider than the Index API, which rejects openalex:). Several entities travel in one request: pass a list of identifiers, or a single string with the __ separator the API documents. One row comes back per entity found; an unknown identifier contributes no row, so an unknown single id answers with [].

Field Meaning id Space-separated, prefixed identifiers of the entity. title, pub_date, volume, issue, page, type Bibliographic fields; empty strings when unknown. author, editor Semicolon-separated person strings with bracketed ids, for example Peroni, Silvio [orcid:0000-0003-0530-4305 omid:ra/0614010840729]. venue Venue title followed by its identifiers in brackets. publisher Publisher name with its identifiers in brackets.

The identifiers, authors, and editors properties parse those packed strings into ParsedIdentifier entries and plain person strings.

docs.title: Authors and editors
docs.text:
author(id) returns the entities the person authored, editor(id) the entities the person edited. The identifier is an ORCID (orcid:0000-0002-8420-0696) or the OpenCitations id of a responsible entity (omid:ra/0601).

works = await client.meta.author("orcid:0000-0002-8420-0696")
for record in works:
    print(record.pub_date, record.title)

docs.title: Row shaping
docs.text: All three methods accept the same require, filter, sort, and format parameters as the Index API; see Index API. format="csv" parses into MetadataRecord rows like the JSON form.

docs.title: SPARQL
docs.text:
The Meta dataset has a SPARQL endpoint at https://sparql.opencitations.net/meta. client.meta.sparql() and client.meta.sparql_text() take the same arguments as their Index counterparts; see Index API.

result = await client.meta.sparql(
    "SELECT ?br ?title WHERE { "
    "?br <http://purl.org/dc/terms/title> ?title ; "
    "<http://prismstandard.org/namespaces/basic/2.0/publicationDate> ?date } LIMIT 5",
    method="POST",
)
for row in result.rows():
    print(row["br"], row["title"])

docs.title: opcitato.OpcitatoClient
docs.text:
Bases: BaseApiClient

Client for the OpenCitations Index API v2, the Meta API v1, and SPARQL.

The APIs need no credentials. The documented limit is 180 requests per minute per IP address, which the settings pace to 3 requests per second. OpenCitations hands out a free Access Token by email and uses it to count unique users; the token travels in an authorization header, and this client does not manage one. To send one, pass a prepared httpx.AsyncClient that carries the header. The client sends Accept: application/json on every request; format="csv" selects the CSV representation regardless of that header. The two SPARQL endpoints live on a second host and share the request pacing.

docs.title: opcitato._async.resources.IndexClient
docs.text:
The read operations of the OpenCitations Index API v2.

Every operation sends one GET and returns the complete result; the API has no paging. citations and references accept require, filter, sort, and format; filter entries look like creation:>2019-12 (a regular expression, or =, <, > with a value), and sort looks like desc(creation). The SPARQL endpoint of the Index dataset answers arbitrary queries through :meth:sparql and :meth:sparql_text.

docs.title: citation(oci) async
docs.text:
Return the one citation with this Open Citation Identifier.

oci is the two dash-separated numbers without the oci: prefix (06101801781-06180334099); a value with the prefix is accepted and stripped. Returns None when no citation carries the identifier.

docs.title: citation_count(id) async
docs.text:
Return the number of incoming citations of one entity.

An unknown identifier answers 0: the API returns a zero row with status 200 (verified 2026-11-28). None means the API answered an empty list, which it did for unknown identifiers on 2026-11-27.

docs.title: citations(id, *, require=None, filter=None, sort=None, format='json') async
docs.text:
Return the incoming citations of one entity.

Every row records a reference in which cited identifies the entity. id is a prefixed identifier (doi:, omid:, pmid:, issn:, or isbn:); an unknown identifier answers with an empty list. require drops rows whose field is empty, filter keeps matching rows, sort orders them, and format="csv" asks the server for the CSV representation.

docs.title: reference_count(id) async
docs.text:
Return the number of outgoing references of one entity.

An unknown identifier answers 0; see :meth:citation_count.

docs.title: references(id, *, require=None, filter=None, sort=None, format='json') async
docs.text:
Return the outgoing references of one entity.

Every row records a reference of the reference list in which citing identifies the entity. The parameters behave exactly as in :meth:citations.

docs.title: sparql(query, *, method='GET', timeout=None) async
docs.text:
Run a SPARQL SELECT or ASK query on the Index dataset.

The endpoint is https://sparql.opencitations.net/index. A SELECT answer fills results, and rows() on the result returns the bindings as plain strings. An ASK answer fills boolean. The meta member carries the query time and the number of rows.

method="POST" sends the query in the request body, which has no length limit. A malformed query answers 400 and raises :class:~bibliofabric.exceptions.APIError with the server's message in the body.

docs.title: sparql_text(query, *, format='turtle', method='GET', timeout=None) async
docs.text:
Run a SPARQL query and return the raw body as text.

format selects the representation through the Accept header: json, xml, csv, tsv, turtle, or n-triples. CONSTRUCT and DESCRIBE answers are RDF, so use this method for them: the endpoint answers Turtle for a CONSTRUCT query that asks for the JSON representation (verified 2026-11-28).

docs.title: venue_citation_count(issn) async
docs.text:
Return the number of incoming citations to a whole venue.

issn is an issn:-prefixed identifier; this is the only scheme the operation accepts. An unknown identifier answers 0; see :meth:citation_count.

docs.title: opcitato._async.resources.MetaClient
docs.text:
The read operations of the OpenCitations Meta API v1.

The rows share the shape of :class:~opcitato.models.MetadataRecord; missing values are empty strings. The row-shaping parameters behave as in the Index API. The SPARQL endpoint of the Meta dataset answers arbitrary queries through :meth:sparql and :meth:sparql_text.

docs.title: author(id, *, require=None, filter=None, sort=None, format='json') async
docs.text:
Return the entities the person with this identifier authored.

id is orcid:0000-0002-8420-0696 or the OpenCitations id of a responsible entity (omid:ra/0601).

docs.title: editor(id, *, require=None, filter=None, sort=None, format='json') async
docs.text:
Return the entities the person with this identifier edited.

id is an orcid: or omid:ra/ identifier, as in :meth:author.

docs.title: metadata(ids, *, require=None, filter=None, sort=None, format='json') async
docs.text:
Return the bibliographic metadata of one or more entities.

ids is one prefixed identifier or a list of them; the accepted schemes are doi, issn, isbn, omid, openalex, pmid, and pmcid. Several identifiers are packed into one request with the __ separator, and one answer row comes back per identifier found. An unknown identifier contributes no row.

docs.title: sparql(query, *, method='GET', timeout=None) async
docs.text:
Run a SPARQL SELECT or ASK query on the Meta dataset.

The endpoint is https://sparql.opencitations.net/meta. The answer follows the same shape as in :meth:IndexClient.sparql.

docs.title: sparql_text(query, *, format='turtle', method='GET', timeout=None) async
docs.text:
Run a SPARQL query and return the raw body as text.

The parameters behave exactly as in :meth:IndexClient.sparql_text.

docs.title: opcitato.dialect
docs.text:
OpenCitations dialect constants.

Both REST APIs are served by one host and are built with RAMOSE, so they share the row-shaping parameters (require, filter, sort, format, json) and the documented rate limit. Each dataset also has a SPARQL endpoint on a second host. The resource clients that consume these constants live in :mod:opcitato._async (their sync twins are generated from them).

docs.title: opcitato.ids.parse_identifiers(text)
docs.text:
Split a space-separated identifier string into typed identifiers.

"omid:br/06120344846 doi:10.1038/nature12373" becomes two :class:ParsedIdentifier entries. Raises :class:ConfigurationError when a part carries no scheme: prefix, because every identifier OpenCitations returns is prefixed and a bare part would hide an upstream format change.

docs.title: opcitato.ids.ParsedIdentifier dataclass
docs.text:
One prefixed identifier of an OpenCitations record.

scheme is the lowercase prefix (doi, omid, pmid, openalex, issn, isbn, pmcid, or orcid) and value the identifier without the prefix (an OMID keeps its br/ or ra/ part, as in br/06120344846).

docs.title: opcitato.ids.normalize_index_id(value)
docs.text:
Validate one Index API identifier for the URL path.

Accepts the schemes the Index API documents (omid, doi, pmid, issn, isbn) and returns the identifier percent-encoded. Raises :class:ConfigurationError for a bare id or an unsupported scheme, which the API would answer with 400.

docs.title: opcitato.ids.normalize_issn(value)
docs.text: Validate that value is an issn: id, as the venue count route needs.

docs.title: opcitato.ids.normalize_meta_ids(value)
docs.text:
Validate Meta identifiers and join them with the __ separator.

Accepts one identifier or a list of them (a single string may already carry the __ separator). Each identifier must use a scheme the Meta /metadata operation documents, and comes back percent-encoded. Raises :class:ConfigurationError otherwise.

docs.title: opcitato.ids.normalize_person_id(value)
docs.text:
Validate a Meta person identifier (orcid:... or omid:ra/...).

Raises :class:ConfigurationError for any other scheme.

docs.title: opcitato.ids.normalize_oci(value)
docs.text:
Normalize an Open Citation Identifier to its first-second form.

The oci: prefix is optional on input and is never sent, because the Index /citation/{oci} operation expects the bare numbers. Raises :class:ConfigurationError for any other shape.

docs.title: opcitato.csvparse.parse_csv_rows(text)
docs.text:
Parse an OpenCitations CSV table into row dictionaries.

Short rows are padded with empty strings, exactly like the JSON representation fills unknown fields with "". A None key (a row longer than the header) is dropped, because no model field can receive it.

docs.text:
Return the first row of the list.

Raises :class:NotFoundError when the list is empty, which is how the APIs answer an unknown identifier.

docs.title: meta(body)
docs.text: Return {}; a top-level list carries no envelope metadata.

docs.title: next_cursor(body)
docs.text: Return None; no operation of either API pages its results.

docs.text: Return the length of the result list (the complete result set).

docs.title: Models
docs.text: The models live in opcitato.models and are re-exported from the top-level package. They are plain Pydantic models with extra="allow".

docs.title: opcitato.models.Citation
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

One citation row of the Index API.

citing and cited hold the identifiers of the citing and the cited entity, space-separated and each prefixed with its scheme (omid:br/06120344846 doi:10.1038/nature12373 pmid:23903748). creation is the publication date of the citing entity in ISO format and may be partial (2013 or 2013-07). timespan is the XSD duration between the publication dates and can be negative (-P1Y1M16D). journal_sc and author_sc are "yes" or "no" strings that report a journal self-citation and an author self-citation.

docs.title: citing_identifiers property
docs.text: The identifiers of the citing entity, parsed from citing.

docs.title: cited_identifiers property
docs.text: The identifiers of the cited entity, parsed from cited.

docs.title: opcitato.models.Count
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

The one row a count operation returns.

The JSON representation carries the number as a string ({"count": "1806"}) even though the documentation types it as int; :attr:count coerces it.

docs.title: opcitato.models.MetadataRecord
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

One bibliographic metadata row of the Meta API.

id holds all known identifiers of the entity, space-separated and prefixed (doi:10.1038/nature12373 pmid:23903748 omid:br/06120344846). author and editor are semicolon-separated lists of person strings such as Peroni, Silvio [orcid:0000-0003-0530-4305 omid:ra/0614010840729]; venue is the venue title followed by its identifiers in brackets. Missing values are empty strings.

docs.title: identifiers property
docs.text: The identifiers of the entity, parsed from id.

docs.title: authors property
docs.text: The author field split into person strings.

docs.title: editors property
docs.text: The editor field split into person strings.

docs.title: opcitato.models.SparqlResult
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

A SPARQL 1.1 JSON result as the endpoints answer sparql-results+json.

A SELECT answer carries head and results. An ASK answer carries head and boolean. OpenCitations adds a meta object with the query time (query-time-ms) and the number of rows (result-size-total).

docs.title: rows()
docs.text:
Return the bindings as plain variable -> value strings.

An ASK answer has no bindings and returns []; read :attr:boolean for it.

docs.title: opcitato.models.SparqlTerm
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

One typed term of a result row.

type is uri, literal, or bnode. A literal can carry a datatype (an XSD datatype IRI) or a language tag (xml:lang in the payload, :attr:xml_lang on the model).

docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

The head member: the result variables.
