Bases: BaseModel

The results member with its bindings rows.

docs.title: Upstream quirks
docs.text: Findings from about 80 requests against the live OpenCitations APIs on 2026-11-27 (about 45 by an earlier probe, 23 in this study, and the live test runs), and from further requests on 2026-11-28 that checked the count routes for unknown ids, the encoding of ids in the path, and the two SPARQL endpoints. The reference is the Index API v2 documentation (version 2.2.0, 2025-04-15) and the Meta API v1 documentation (version 1.1.1, 2022-12-22). Where a quirk affects opcitato, the behavior of the client is noted.

docs.title: Limits and access
docs.text:
• Both APIs document a rate limit of 180 requests per minute per IP address (3 per second). No rate-limit headers are sent, so the limit cannot be read from responses; the client paces at 3 requests per second by default.
  • Both API documentations ask applications to send an OpenCitations Access Token in the authorization header. The token is free, optional, and lets OpenCitations count unique users. Neither documentation ties it to a higher limit. The client sends no token and manages none; a caller can pass a prepared httpx.AsyncClient that carries the header (verified offline).
  • https://opencitations.net/index/v2/... (without the api. host) answers 403. The canonical host is https://api.opencitations.net, which is the client default. The Retrieval API routes (https://opencitations.net/index/api/v2/citations/...) answer 200 on the www host but are a different, undocumented service; the client does not use them.

docs.title: The result is the whole list
docs.text:
• No operation pages. Every request returns the complete result of the query; one response can reach hundreds of kilobytes (a 658 KB response was cut off once by the network and httpx raised RemoteProtocolError; the framework retries network errors).
  • require, filter, sort, format, and json are server-side row operations that every operation accepts. The verified behavior: require=creation dropped one of 57 rows (the one with an empty creation date), filter=creation:>2019-12 kept 15 of 57, and sort=desc(creation) ordered by the string date, so partial dates (2020, 2020-03) sort before full dates within the same year.
  • format=csv works as a query parameter. An Accept: text/csv header alone does not change the representation; the format parameter has priority over the header. The CSV header repeats the JSON field names, so format="csv" parses into the same models.
  • The json=array(...)/json=dict(...) row transformations are documented but not exposed by the client.

docs.title: Identifier handling
docs.text:
• Index path ids must carry a scheme prefix. The documented shape is (omid|doi|pmid|issn|isbn):(.+). A bare DOI and an openalex: id answer 400 with a plain-text body such as HTTP status code 400: the value '10.1108/jd-12-2013-0166' is not valid for parameter 'id' in operation '/index/v2/citations/{id}'. Example: /index/v2/citations/doi:10.1108/jd-12-2013-0166. The client rejects both shapes before a request is sent; a 400 that slips through raises APIError.
  • Meta metadata accepts more schemes than the Index API: the documented shape also allows openalex, pmid, and pmcid, and openalex:W2159974629 answered 200 with the Nature 12373 metadata (verified 2026-11-27).
  • Several identifiers in one request are only a Meta feature. /meta/v1/metadata/{a}__{b} answered with one row per id (verified 2026-11-27). The Index operations document no multi-id form; citations/doi:A__doi:B answered [] even though both ids have citations, so the Index client sends one id per request.
  • The /citation/{oci} operation wants the bare first-second numbers without the oci: prefix. The client strips an optional prefix.
  • Citing and cited rows pack several schemes into one space-separated string. The live data carries omid:, doi:, openalex:, and pmid: (verified 2026-11-27).
  • The server percent-decodes the path before it looks up the identifier. The SICI DOI 10.1002/(SICI)1097-4636(199823)43:3<338::AID-JBM16>3.0.CO;2-B answered the same count when its parentheses, angle brackets, and semicolon arrived percent-encoded and when some of them arrived raw (verified 2026-11-28). httpx cuts a path at the first # or ?, so the client percent-encodes every character of an identifier other than / and :.
  • The Meta /author/{id} and /editor/{id} operations also accept an ORCID without the orcid: prefix, according to their documented shape. The client requires the prefix, as it does for every identifier.

docs.title: Values that differ from the documentation
docs.text:
• The count operations answer [{"count": "57"}]: the count travels as a string although the documentation types the field as int. The Count model coerces it.
  • journal_sc and author_sc are "yes"/"no" strings.
  • creation dates can be partial (2013, 2013-07); timespan can be negative (-P1Y1M16D).
  • The documentation claims that values are prefixed with [index name] => when data comes from several indexes; no such prefix appeared in any live payload on 2026-11-27. The models store the values as they arrive.

docs.title: Unknown identifiers and errors
docs.text:
• An unknown id is not an error. Row operations answer 200 with []. The count operations answered [] on 2026-11-27 and a zero row ([{"count": "0"}]) on 2026-11-28; the client returns None for the first answer and 0 for the second.
  • Rejected parameters answer 400 with a text/plain body, not JSON. The framework raises APIError for any status of 400 or above, before parsing the body.

docs.title: Routes that do not exist
docs.text: The Index operations /metadata/{id}, /citation-count-and-year/{id}, /citations-with-context/{id}, and source-scoped /index/v2/{source}/citations/{id} answered 404 on api.opencitations.net on 2026-11-27 and appear in neither API's documentation; the six documented Index operations and the three documented Meta operations are the complete surface. The Meta routes related, citation, journal, publisher, identifier, amount, and concept also answered 404 and are not documented.

docs.title: SPARQL endpoints
docs.text:
• Each dataset has a SPARQL endpoint: https://sparql.opencitations.net/index and https://sparql.opencitations.net/meta. The landing page at https://sparql.opencitations.net/ lists both; the REST API documentations do not mention them.
  • The endpoints answer SPARQL 1.1 Query Results XML unless the Accept header asks for another representation. application/sparql-results+json returns the JSON form with one addition: a meta member that carries query-time-ms and result-size-total. The SparqlResult model keeps it.
  • application/sparql-results+xml, text/csv, text/tab-separated-values, text/turtle, and application/n-triples select the other representations. An Accept type the endpoint does not serve answers 406. A CONSTRUCT query that asks for application/sparql-results+json answers Turtle.
  • A query travels in the query parameter of a GET request, in the form body of a POST request, or in an application/sparql-query body of a POST request. The client sends the query parameter by default and a form body for method="POST".
  • A malformed query answers 400 with a JSON body that carries an exception member. The framework raises APIError for the status.
  • An ASK query answers {"head": {}, "boolean": true} with no results member.

docs.title: Index API v1
docs.text: https://api.opencitations.net/index/v1/citations/{doi} still answers 200 (verified 2026-11-28). It takes a bare DOI and returns a subset of the v2 fields, with bare DOIs in citing and cited instead of the prefixed identifiers of v2. The client targets v2 only; the deferred list has the entry.

docs.title: orchis
docs.text:
orchis is not yet published on PyPI; until its first release it installs from the bibliofabric workspace.

orchis is a Python client for the ORCID Public API v3.0, built on bibliofabric. It types the record, person, activities, and search endpoints with Pydantic models and ships an async client with a generated sync twin. The public API answers reads without credentials.

The upstream references for this package are the Public API guide and the swagger document it links to. Facts in these pages were verified against the live API on 2026-11-27; see upstream quirks.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv add orchis

Requires Python 3.12 or newer.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
• Records: the record summary and its XML representation.
  • Person: the person section and its sub-sections.
  • Activities: the summary, the twelve sections, and single items.
  • Search: expanded search and the Solr-compatible route.
  • Upstream quirks: verified behavior that differs from what you might expect.
  • API reference: generated from the source.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import asyncio
from orchis import OrchisClient


async def main():
    async with OrchisClient() as client:
        record = await client.record.get("0000-0002-1694-233X")
        print(record.person.name.given_names.text)
        page = await client.expanded_search.search(
            query="family-name:Kucsko", page_size=10
        )
        print(page.total, [(r.given_names, r.family_names) for r in page.results])


asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Sync usage
docs.text:
The generated OrchisSyncClient has the same methods without async and await:

from orchis import OrchisSyncClient

with OrchisSyncClient() as client:
    work = client.activities.work("0000-0002-1694-233X", 145464015)
    print(work.title.title.text)

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: OrchisSettings loads from environment variables prefixed with ORCHIS_ and from a .env file in the working directory. The shared fields of bibliofabric.config.BaseApiSettings apply, such as ORCHIS_MAX_CONCURRENCY, ORCHIS_TIMEOUT, ORCHIS_MAX_RETRIES, and ORCHIS_USER_AGENT.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text: ORCID documents 12 requests per second for anonymous and public API callers and 24 for the member API, with a burst of 40. The client defaults to 4 requests per second; raise it with ORCHIS_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND.

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
A token lifts the daily read quota from 25,000 to 100,000 reads for a registered public API client. Give the client one of two things:

  • ORCHIS_ACCESS_TOKEN: a token you already hold. The client sends it as a bearer header.
  • ORCHIS_CLIENT_ID and ORCHIS_CLIENT_SECRET: the credentials of your public API client. The client mints a /read-public token at https://orcid.org/oauth/token on the first request, reuses it, and mints a new one after a 401.

ORCHIS_ACCESS_TOKEN wins when both are set. Setting only one of the client id and secret raises ConfigurationError.

settings = OrchisSettings(client_id="APP-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX", client_secret="...")
async with OrchisClient(settings=settings) as client:
    record = await client.record.get("0000-0002-1694-233X")

docs.title: Activities
docs.text: The activities summary (GET /{orcid}/activities) lists every section of the record. client.activities.get(orcid) validates it into ActivitiesSummary; a section the record does not use is None.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
Each section has a reader that hits the section route and returns its model, or None when the record has none of that kind.

Method Route Element model works(orcid) /{orcid}/works WorkSummary in WorksSection fundings(orcid) /{orcid}/fundings FundingSummary educations(orcid) /{orcid}/educations EducationSummary employments(orcid) /{orcid}/employments EmploymentSummary peer_reviews(orcid) /{orcid}/peer-reviews PeerReviewSummary distinctions(orcid) /{orcid}/distinctions DistinctionSummary invited_positions(orcid) /{orcid}/invited-positions InvitedPositionSummary memberships(orcid) /{orcid}/memberships MembershipSummary qualifications(orcid) /{orcid}/qualifications QualificationSummary research_resources(orcid) /{orcid}/research-resources ResearchResourceSummary services(orcid) /{orcid}/services ServiceSummary

Works, fundings, and peer reviews group their summaries in group lists; the affiliation-style sections use affiliation-group[].summaries[], where each summary is wrapped as {"education-summary": {...}} and so on. Every section model has a put_codes() helper that collects the put-codes you need for the single-item routes.

works = await client.activities.works("0000-0002-1694-233X")
print(works.put_codes()[:5])
for group in works.group:
    for summary in group.work_summary:
        print(summary.put_code, summary.title.title.text, summary.type)

docs.title: Single items
docs.text:
Each put-code has a full route that returns the complete element, not the summary.

Method Route Returns work(orcid, put_code) /{orcid}/work/{put-code} Work works_bulk(orcid, put_codes) /{orcid}/works/{code},{code},... list[Work], up to 100 codes per request funding(orcid, put_code) /{orcid}/funding/{put-code} Funding peer_review(orcid, put_code) /{orcid}/peer-review/{put-code} PeerReview education(orcid, put_code) /{orcid}/education/{put-code} parsed JSON object employment(orcid, put_code) /{orcid}/employment/{put-code} parsed JSON object affiliation_item(orcid, kind, put_code) /{orcid}/{kind}/{put-code} parsed JSON object

affiliation_item covers qualification, membership, service, distinction, invited-position, and research-resource. These six share one shape with the affiliation summaries, so the client returns the parsed JSON object instead of one model per kind.

works_bulk() fetches many full works in one request per 100 put codes, which is the fastest way to read every work of a record: take the put codes from works(orcid) and pass them in. A put code that ORCID does not know answers an error entry and is absent from the result.

work = await client.activities.work("0000-0002-1694-233X", 145464015)
print(work.title.title.text)  # Parsing and Matching Dates in VIAF
print(work.title.subtitle.text)  # Issue 26, 2014-10-21
print(work.journal_title.text)  # Code4Lib Journal
print(work.publication_date.iso())  # 2014-10-21
print(work.contributors.contributor[1].orcid.path)

funding = await client.activities.funding("0000-0002-1694-233X", 63665)
print(funding.organization.name)  # NSF Office of the Director
print(funding.organization.disambiguated_organization.identifier)

docs.title: Representations
docs.text:
client.activities.representation(orcid, suffix, accept) returns any route under the ORCID iD as text in another representation:

xml = await client.activities.representation("0000-0002-1694-233X", "work/145464015")

docs.title: Bulk data
docs.text: For a complete copy of the registry, ORCID publishes a public data file (a 17.4 GB tar.gz of XML for 2025) on orcid.figshare.com, documented under Working with the Public Data File. This package does not download or parse it.

docs.title: Person
docs.text:
The person section (GET /{orcid}/person) holds the name, other names, biography, researcher URLs, emails, addresses, keywords, and external identifiers. client.person.get(orcid) validates it into Person; each part also has its own route.

Method Route Notes personal_details(orcid) /{orcid}/personal-details name, other names, biography biography(orcid) /{orcid}/biography None when the record has none researcher_urls(orcid) /{orcid}/researcher-urls emails(orcid) /{orcid}/emails None when the record has none addresses(orcid) /{orcid}/address two-letter countries keywords(orcid) /{orcid}/keywords external_identifiers(orcid) /{orcid}/external-identifiers Scopus, ISNI, and so on other_names(orcid) /{orcid}/other-names item(orcid, kind, put_code) /{orcid}/{kind}/{put-code} one item as a parsed JSON object

item() reads one entry of address, keywords, other-names, researcher-urls, or external-identifiers by its put code. The section routes return the same entries in their lists.

person = await client.person.get("0000-0002-1694-233X")
print(person.name.family_name.text)  # Hickey
print([name.content for name in person.other_names.other_name])

urls = await client.person.researcher_urls("0000-0002-1694-233X")
for url in urls.researcher_url:
    print(url.url_name, url.url.text)

biography = await client.person.biography("0000-0002-1694-233X")
# None: this record has no biography (the API answers 404 with error code 9041)

Every element carries put-code, path, visibility, and its source, so you can tell a researcher-asserted claim from one imported by a client (source.source_client_id).

Names differ between sections: the person section uses given-names and family-name (singular), while expanded search uses given-names and family-names (plural). The models follow the API spelling, aliased to snake_case attributes.

docs.title: Records
docs.text:
The record summary route (GET /{orcid}/record) returns everything public in one document: the ORCID identifier, preferences, history, the person section, and the activities summary. client.record.get() validates it into OrchisRecord.

record = await client.record.get("0000-0002-1694-233X")

print(record.orcid_identifier.uri)  # https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1694-233X
print(record.history.creation_method)  # WEBSITE
print(record.history.claimed)  # True
print(record.person.name.given_names.text)  # Thomas B.
works = record.activities_summary.works
print(works.put_codes()[:5])

The identifier input is normalized: https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1694-233X, the compact form, and the bare hyphenated iD all work. client.record.exists(orcid) sends GET and returns False on 404.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text: record.person holds the full person section and record.activities_summary holds every activity section as it stood with the record. A section the record does not use is None. For fresh data, fetch the sections through client.person and client.activities, which hit their own routes.

docs.title: Other representations
docs.text:
The API answers XML for the same route with Accept: application/xml (and with no Accept header at all). client.record.representation(orcid) returns that body as text:

xml = await client.record.representation("0000-0002-1694-233X")
print(xml[:200])

application/ld+json answers 406 on the public API as of 2026-11-27, so no JSON-LD method exists.

docs.title: Values
docs.text:
ORCID wraps almost every scalar as {"value": ...}. The models expose wrapped text through the text property, and the module-level text() helper accepts any wrapper or None:

from orchis import text

print(record.person.name.credit_name)  # TextValue model or None
print(record.person.name.credit_name.text)  # unwrapped string or None
print(text(record.person.name.credit_name))  # same

Dates such as {"year": {"value": "2020"}} validate into FuzzyDate, whose iso() returns 2020, 2020-06, or 2020-06-15 depending on the parts the record carries.

ORCID-specific client settings.

Inherits timeout, max_retries, max_retry_wait, max_requests_per_second, max_concurrency, user_agent and mailto from :class:bibliofabric.config.BaseApiSettings and sets ORCID defaults (4 req/s, concurrency 4). docs.title: Search
docs.text: ORCID exposes one Solr index through two routes. Both accept the same query syntax and the rows and start parameters, which the client maps through the bibliofabric paging dialect (page_size and page, with start as a zero-based offset).

docs.title: Expanded search
docs.text:
/expanded-search/ answers one expanded profile per result: names, credit name, other names, emails, and institutions. client.expanded_search inherits the generic search(), iterate(), collect(), first(), and count() operations.

page = await client.expanded_search.search(
    query="family-name:Kucsko", page_size=10, page=2
)
print(page.total)  # num-found from the API
print(page.page)  # 2
for result in page.results:
    print(result.orcid_id, result.given_names, result.family_names)
    print(result.institution_name)

async for result in client.expanded_search.iterate(
    query="family-name:Kucsko", page_size=50, limit=200
):
    print(result.orcid_id)

A page past the total answers {"expanded-result": null, "num-found": N}, which becomes an empty result list. Keep rows at 100 or below: rows=1000 makes the server answer HTTP 500 with a Solr exception (verified 2026-11-27).

docs.title: Solr search
docs.text:
/search/ answers the same index with one orcid-identifier per result and no profile fields.

page = await client.search.search(query="family-name:Kucsko", page_size=10)
print(page.total, [r.orcid_identifier.path for r in page.results])

docs.title: CSV search
docs.text:
/csv-search/ answers the same index as CSV text with a header row. fields picks the columns through the fl parameter; without it ORCID answers nine columns (orcid, email, given-names, family-name, given-and-family-names, current-institution-affiliation-name, past-institution-affiliation-name, credit-name, other-names).

csv_text = await client.expanded_search.csv(
    "family-name:hickey", fields=["orcid", "given-names", "family-name"], rows=100
)

docs.title: Query syntax
docs.text: The query is a Solr query string over indexed fields: family-name:Kucsko, given-names:Georg, text-and-title:magnetic, doi:10.1088/..., and so on. A plain word searches the default fields. An unknown field name makes the server answer HTTP 500 rather than a validation error, so quote field values and check spellings before paging through results.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text: Search shares the API-wide limits: 12 requests per second for anonymous and public API callers, 40 burst, and 503 above the burst. The client paces at 4 requests per second by default.

docs.title: Upstream quirks
docs.text: Findings from about 48 paced requests against the live ORCID Public API v3.0 on 2026-11-27, with the Public API guide, the swagger document, and the usage limits page as references. Where a quirk affects orchis, the behavior of the client is noted.

docs.title: Representations
docs.text:
• Accept: application/json and Accept: application/vnd.orcid+json both answer JSON. No Accept header and Accept: application/xml answer XML. orchis sends Accept: application/json on every request; representation() methods ask for application/xml and return the body as text.
  • Accept: application/ld+json answers 406 with a generic ORCID error body, both for /{orcid}/record and for a single work. No JSON-LD method exists, because the representation is not served today.

docs.title: Missing data answers 404
docs.text:
• /{orcid}/biography answers 404 with error code 9041 ("Biography for the given record is null") when the record has no biography. /{orcid}/emails answers 404 the same way when the record has no public email. Both readers return None.
  • Empty lists differ: keywords, peer-reviews, and addresses answer 200 with an empty list for the same record.
  • An unused activities section was inconsistent across runs. /{orcid}/distinctions answered 404 in the study run and 200 with an empty affiliation-group in a later run on the same day. Every section reader therefore treats 404 as an empty section (None), and callers should handle both shapes.

docs.title: Routes and shapes
docs.text:
• Single-item routes use the singular segment (/{orcid}/work/145464015). The plural segment (/{orcid}/works/145464015) answers the same body with status 200. orchis sends the singular form.
  • Nearly every scalar is wrapped as {"value": ...}, and timestamps are epoch milliseconds in the same wrapper. Field names mix singular and plural: the person section has family-name, expanded search has family-names; the summary element is work-summary inside group, while affiliation summaries sit in affiliation-group[].summaries[] wrapped per type. The models keep the API structure and alias it to snake_case.
  • display-index is a number in person elements and a string in activity elements. The models accept both.
  • Every element carries put-code, path, visibility, and a source block with source-orcid and/or source-client-id, so provenance survives grouping.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
• /expanded-search/ answers {"expanded-result": [...], "num-found": N}. A start past the total answers {"expanded-result": null, "num-found": N}; the unwrapper turns that into an empty result list with the total intact.
  • rows=1000 answers HTTP 500 with a Solr RemoteSolrException in developer-message. So does an unknown field name (bogus-field:xyz). Keep rows at 100 or below, which is the dialect maximum.
  • /search/ answers the Solr envelope {"result": [{"orcid-identifier": ...}], "num-found": N} and accepts the same q, rows, and start parameters.
  • Both routes are unauthenticated. The client maps start to an offset and rows to the page size.

docs.title: Rate limits and credentials
docs.text:
• ORCID documents 12 requests per second for anonymous and public API callers and 24 for the member API, with a burst of 40 and a 503 above the burst. Daily quotas are 25,000 reads per IP address anonymously and 100,000 per client id for the public API. orchis defaults to 4 requests per second.
  • The token and the client credentials on hand are public API credentials. The member API answered 403 ("error": "forbidden") for both on a read of https://api.orcid.org/v3.0/{orcid}/record on 2026-11-27 and 2026-11-28, so the member API is not wrapped. The client-credentials grant at https://orcid.org/oauth/token with scope /read-public and the client id and secret in the form body mints a token (HTTP 200), which orchis does when ORCHIS_CLIENT_ID and ORCHIS_CLIENT_SECRET are set (verified live on 2026-11-28).

docs.title: Bulk data
docs.text: The public data file is documented at Working with the Public Data File and hosted on orcid.figshare.com. The 2025 edition is a 17.4 GB tar.gz of XML. This package does not download or parse it; use the search routes or the data file directly.

docs.title: prodromus
docs.text:
prodromus is not yet published on PyPI; until its first release it installs from the bibliofabric workspace.

prodromus is a Python client for the bioRxiv and medRxiv API, built on bibliofabric. One client serves both preprint servers. It reads preprint metadata by DOI and by date range, the links from preprints to the journal articles they became, preprints by funder, and the content and usage statistics. It ships an async client and a generated sync twin with the same API. The API needs no credentials.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
from prodromus import ProdromusClient

async with ProdromusClient() as client:
    versions = await client.details.get("10.1101/339747")
    [(version.version, version.date) for version in versions]

    async for preprint in client.details.iterate("medrxiv", "2026-11-01", "2026-11-01"):
        preprint.doi, preprint.category, preprint.published_doi

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
Method Route Returns details.get(doi, server=) /details/{server}/{doi}/na/json every version as Preprint details.search(server, start, end, cursor=, category=) /details/{server}/{start}/{end}/{cursor} a page of 30 details.iterate(server, start, end, category=) the same, every page Preprint details.recent(server, posts= or days=) /details/{server}/{N} or /{N}d one answer, no paging published.get(doi, server=) /pubs/{server}/{doi}/na/json PublishedArticle list; preprint or journal DOI published.search / iterate(server, start, end) /pubs/{server}/{start}/{end}/{cursor} pages of 100 published.by_publisher / iterate_by_publisher(prefix, start, end) /publisher/{prefix}/{start}/{end}/{cursor} bioRxiv only published.biorxiv(start, end, cursor=) /pub/{start}/{end}/{cursor} bioRxiv only, fewer fields funders.search / iterate(server, ror_id, start, end) /funder/{server}/{start}/{end}/{ror}/{cursor} Preprint with funder declarations statistics.content(interval) /sum/{m,y} ContentStatistic list statistics.usage(server, interval) /usage/{m,y}/{server} UsageStatistic list

server is biorxiv or medrxiv. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. category filters by subject category, written with spaces or underscores (cell biology). The funder route covers posts from 2025-04-10 on.

docs.title: Upstream quirks
docs.text:
Checked against the live API on 2026-11-28.

  • Errors come back with HTTP 200 and the reason in messages[0].status, for example Both dates must be in yyyy-mm-dd format. The client raises ConfigurationError for them, and treats no posts found and no articles found as empty answers.
  • The newest-posts forms (/details/biorxiv/45, /details/biorxiv/2d) take no cursor, and the funder route takes no Nd form; with them the API answers the date-format error.
  • cursor is a number on the first page and a string on later pages, and total is often a string.
  • authors is one string with ; between names (Preprint.author_list splits it), published is a journal DOI or NA (Preprint.published_doi reads it), and version is a string.
  • The API publishes no rate limit; the client defaults to one request per second over one connection (PRODROMUS_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND).

docs.title: quiddita
docs.text:
quiddita is not yet published on PyPI; until its first release it installs from the bibliofabric workspace.

quiddita is a Python client for Wikidata, built on bibliofabric. It covers Wikidata's three read interfaces: the MediaWiki Action API (wbgetentities, wbsearchentities, wbgetclaims), the Wikibase REST API (items, properties, statements, per-language term routes), and the SPARQL query service. It types every payload with Pydantic models, batches wbgetentities id requests at the API's 50-id limit, and ships an async client plus a generated sync twin with the same API. The API needs no credentials, but all three services ask for a descriptive User-Agent with contact information, which the client builds for you.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv add quiddita

Requires Python 3.12 or newer.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import asyncio
from quiddita import QuidditaClient


async def main():
    async with QuidditaClient() as client:
        entity = await client.entities.get("Q42")
        print(entity.description(), entity.sitelinks["enwiki"].title)

        batch = await client.entities.batch_get(["Q42", "P31", "L1"])
        print(sorted(batch))

        page = await client.search.search(query="douglas adams")
        print([hit.id for hit in page.results])

        result = await client.sparql.query(
            "SELECT ?item WHERE { ?item wdt:P31 wd:Q5 } LIMIT 5"
        )
        print(result.rows())


asyncio.run(main())

client.entities exposes get(), batch_get(), and iterate_ids(). client.search exposes search(), iterate(), collect(), and the REST routes search_items() and search_properties(). client.claims, client.sitelinks, client.items, client.properties, and client.statements cover the Action API and REST read routes. client.sparql talks to the query service on query.wikidata.org.

docs.title: Sync usage
docs.text:
QuidditaSyncClient is generated from the async source and behaves the same. The sync client uses plain httpx.Client and never starts or touches an event loop, so it works in scripts, in Jupyter, in threads, and when called from inside a running event loop.

from quiddita import QuidditaSyncClient

with QuidditaSyncClient() as client:
    entity = client.entities.get("Q42")
    print(entity.claims["P31"][0].mainsnak.datavalue)

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: QuidditaSettings loads from environment variables prefixed with QUIDDITA_ and from a .env file in the working directory. The defaults follow the pace Wikidata's own guides ask for: serial requests at 2 per second against www.wikidata.org, and one SPARQL query every 2 seconds in the separate sparql rate class. QUIDDITA_USER_AGENT and QUIDDITA_MAILTO feed the User-Agent; QUIDDITA_TIMEOUT, QUIDDITA_MAX_RETRIES, and the other shared fields of bibliofabric.config.BaseApiSettings also apply.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Entities covers wbgetentities, batching, id iteration, and the Special:EntityData routes.
  • Search covers wbsearchentities, the REST search routes, and the REST suggest routes.
  • Claims and statements covers wbgetclaims and the REST statement routes.
  • Site links covers the site link resources.
  • Lexemes covers the WikibaseLexeme REST read routes.
  • SPARQL covers the query service and how the two hosts share one rate limiter.
  • Utility modules covers badges, HTML formatting, value parsing, property suggestions, and constraint checks.
  • Upstream quirks lists what the live services do differently from their documentation.
  • The API reference is generated from the source.

docs.title: Claims and statements
docs.text: Wikidata serves statements in two shapes. The Action API shape lives in client.entities and client.claims; the REST shape lives in client.statements.

docs.title: wbgetclaims (Action API)
docs.text:
claims = await client.claims.get("Q42", property="P569", rank="preferred")
claim = claims["P569"][0]
print(claim.mainsnak.datavalue.value)  # the raw Wikidata value shape
print(claim.qualifiers, claim.references)

get() returns a ClaimsByProperty dict keyed by property id. rank accepts "deprecated", "normal", and "preferred"; other values are rejected locally because the API would answer badvalue. Each claim is a Claim model with mainsnak, rank, qualifiers (dict of property id to Snak), and references.

docs.title: REST statements
docs.text:
statements = await client.statements.for_entity("Q42", property="P31")
statement = statements["P31"][0]
print(statement.value.content)  # the typed REST content
print(statement.qualifiers, statement.references)

statement = await client.statements.get("Q42$F078E5B3-F9A8-480E-B7AC-D97778CBBEF9")

for_entity() accepts item and property ids and returns a StatementsByProperty dict. get() fetches one statement by its id (the $ is URL-encoded). REST qualifiers and references are RestQualifier records whose property is a {id, data_type} object and whose value is a {type, content} object; content is None for somevalue and novalue snaks.

docs.title: Entities
docs.text: client.entities wraps the wbgetentities module of the MediaWiki Action API. It returns one entity, a bounded batch, or an unbounded id list, typed as Entity.

docs.title: One entity
docs.text:
entity = await client.entities.get("Q42")
entity = await client.entities.get("https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q42")  # same

The id accepts Q, P, and L ids in any letter case, the wiki URL form, and the entity URL form; anything else raises ConfigurationError before a request is sent. Unknown ids raise NotFoundError.

Pass entity parts with select= (mapped to the API's props parameter) and the remaining parameters through params:

entity = await client.entities.get(
    "Q42",
    select=["labels", "descriptions"],
    params={"languages": ["en", "nl"], "sitefilter": ["enwiki"], "redirects": "no"},
)

redirects accepts "yes" and "no" (default "yes"). With "no", a redirect id answers as a stub entity with info only.

docs.title: Batches
docs.text:
batch_get() chunks ids at the API's limit of 50 ids per request and returns a dict keyed by the normalized id. An id that the API answers with a missing stub, such as a deleted item, is absent from the dict. An id that makes the API reject the whole request (no-such-entity, for example an item number above the highest one) raises NotFoundError; use iterate_ids(on_error="skip") to drop such ids and keep the rest.

batch = await client.entities.batch_get(["Q42", "P31", "L1"], select=["labels"])

batch_get() inherits the framework's concurrency bound, deduplication, and on_error="skip" failure handling.

docs.title: Iterating many ids
docs.text:
iterate_ids() walks an unbounded id list in order, 50 ids per request:

async for entity in client.entities.iterate_ids(ids, props=["claims"]):
    ...

Ids are normalized and deduplicated first. An unknown id raises NotFoundError. With on_error="skip" the client drops the id, repeats the request without it, and records the id in failures with its NotFoundError:

failures = []
async for entity in client.entities.iterate_ids(
    ids, on_error="skip", failures=failures
):
    ...

docs.title: EntityData: the full entity per format
docs.text:
client.entity_data reads wiki/Special:EntityData/{id}.{format}, which serves the full entity in one serialization without the 50-id limit of wbgetentities:

result = await client.entity_data.get("Q42")  # json
print(result.entity.id, result.entity.claims)

ttl = await client.entity_data.get("Q42", format="ttl")
print(ttl.document.content_type, len(ttl.document.text))

old = await client.entity_data.get("Q42", revision=2575435918)  # an old revision

get() returns an EntityDataResult. For format="json" the entity field carries the parsed Entity (the payload is the same shape as wbgetentities). For jsonld, rdf, nt, ttl, and n3 the document field carries an EntityDataDocument with the raw text and the answered content_type. Other suffixes answer 415, so format is validated client-side. revision= serves an old revision id; an unknown revision answers 404. An invalid id is rejected client-side.

negotiate() walks the content-negotiation route for callers who want it: https://www.wikidata.org/entity/{id} answers 303 to Special:EntityData based on the Accept header, and the client follows the redirect:

document = await client.entity_data.negotiate("Q42", accept="text/turtle")

docs.title: Models
docs.text: Entity carries type, id, labels, descriptions, aliases, claims, sitelinks, datatype (properties), and the page metadata (pageid, lastrevid, modified). Claim carries mainsnak, rank, qualifiers, and references; Snak.datavalue keeps the value untyped (DataValue.value) so every Wikidata value shape survives. Sitelink carries site, title, badges, and url when sitelinks/urls was requested. Unknown fields are kept (extra="allow"), so lexeme payloads survive validation.

docs.title: Lexemes
docs.text: client.lexemes reads lexemes through the WikibaseLexeme REST API at /w/rest.php/wikibaselexeme/v0. The same paths under wikibase/v1 answer 404 (verified 2026-11-27).

docs.title: Get a lexeme
docs.text:
lexeme = await client.lexemes.get("L2")
print(lexeme.lemmas["en"])  # 'first'
print(lexeme.lexical_category)  # 'Q1084', a bare item id
print(lexeme.forms[0].representations)  # {'en': 'firsts'}
print(lexeme.forms[0].grammatical_features)  # ['Q146786']
print(lexeme.senses[0].glosses["en"])

get() returns a RestLexeme with lemmas, lexical_category, language, statements, forms, and senses. lexical_category and language are bare item ids here, unlike the wbgetentities lexeme payload where they are nested objects. Each form carries representations, grammatical_features, and statements; each sense carries glosses and statements. The statement models are the same RestStatement shapes the item routes return.

There are no per-form or per-sense routes: /entities/forms/{id} and /entities/senses/{id} answer rest-no-match (verified 2026-11-27), so forms and senses come inside the lexeme payload. Lexemes, forms, and senses through wbgetentities stay available through client.entities.

Bases: BaseApiSettings

Wikidata-specific client settings.

Inherits timeout, max_retries, max_retry_wait, max_requests_per_second, max_concurrency, user_agent and mailto from :class:bibliofabric.config.BaseApiSettings. The API needs no credentials, but the MediaWiki Action API, the Wikibase REST API, and the SPARQL query service all ask for a descriptive User-Agent with contact information: effective_user_agent() builds it from user_agent or the package metadata, and mailto is appended when it is set.

Client for the wbgetentities module.

The API answers at most 50 ids per request (toomanyvalues above 50, verified on 2026-11-27). :meth:batch_get chunks through :class:~bibliofabric.ResourceClient; :meth:iterate_ids walks an unbounded id list one chunk at a time, in order.

docs.title: iterate_ids(ids, *, props=None, languages=None, sitefilter=None, on_error='raise', failures=None) async
docs.text:
Iterate over many ids, fetching up to 50 per request, in order.

Ids are normalized and deduplicated first. An id the API does not know raises NotFoundError; with on_error="skip" it is dropped and recorded in failures instead. props, languages, and sitefilter pass through to wbgetentities.

docs.title: _fetch_batch_chunk(field, chunk, *, select=None) async
docs.text:
Fetch one id chunk.

An id that the API answers with a missing stub (a deleted item, an unknown lexeme or property) is absent from the result, as the :meth:batch_get contract says. An id that makes the API reject the whole request (no-such-entity) raises NotFoundError.

docs.title: quiddita._async.sparql.SparqlClient
docs.text:
Client for SPARQL SELECT, ASK, and CONSTRUCT queries.

The query service is a second host, so the :class:QuidditaQueryClient behind this resource is a second API client instance. It shares the settings object and the rate limiter with the main client: SPARQL requests run in the sparql rate class, Action API and REST requests in the default class, and one limiter inside the main client paces both classes. See docs/quiddita/sparql.md.

The service answers malformed or overlong queries with HTTP 400 and a plain-text Java stack trace; those raise :class:~bibliofabric.exceptions.APIError with the text as the body.

docs.title: __init__(query_client)
docs.text: Build the resource client on the second-host query client.

docs.title: query(query, *, timeout=None) async
docs.text: Run a query with GET and return the typed SPARQL 1.1 JSON result.

docs.title: query_post(query, *, timeout=None) async
docs.text:
Run a query with POST and return the typed SPARQL 1.1 JSON result.

Long queries belong in a POST body: URL length limits do not apply. The POST is read-only, so the request carries retry=True for the framework's transient-failure retries.

docs.title: query_text(query, *, format='json', timeout=None) async
docs.text:
Run a query with GET and return the raw body as text.

format selects the representation through the Accept header: the service ignores a non-JSON format query parameter and answers SPARQL-result XML unless asked otherwise (verified 2026-11-27). Supported values: json, xml, csv, tsv, turtle. The body passes through as text; only :meth:query and :meth:query_post parse the typed SPARQL 1.1 JSON shape.

docs.title: quiddita.dialect
docs.text:
Query dialect and endpoint paths for Wikidata.

All requests go to two hosts. www.wikidata.org serves both the MediaWiki Action API (w/api.php) and the Wikibase REST API (w/rest.php/wikibase/v1), so one client with one rate limiter covers both. The SPARQL query service lives on query.wikidata.org and is served by a second client instance that shares the settings object and the limiter through the sparql rate class.

docs.title: Search
docs.text: client.search wraps wbsearchentities and the REST search routes.

docs.title: wbsearchentities
docs.text:
page = await client.search.search(query="douglas adams", language="en", type="item")

search() returns a Page[EntitySearchResult]. The language, uselang, type, and strict_language options map to the module's parameters; page, page_size, and iterate()'s paging use the module's limit and continue parameters.

wbsearchentities reports no total, so count() raises ConfigurationError. iterate() and collect() walk continue offset pages until the API returns an empty page:

async for hit in client.search.iterate(query="adams", page_size=50, limit=200):
    ...

EntitySearchResult carries id, label, description, match, aliases, and concepturi.

docs.title: REST search
docs.text:
The Wikibase REST API answers search/items and search/properties with a language-fallback display label:

items = await client.search.search_items("Douglas Adams", language="en", limit=3)
props = await client.search.search_properties("instance", language="en", limit=5)

Both return RestSearchResult records with id, display_label (language, value), description, and match.

docs.title: REST suggestions
docs.text:
The REST suggest routes answer the same result shape as the search routes and match aliases too:

items = await client.search.suggest_items("einstein", language="en", limit=3)
props = await client.search.suggest_properties("instance", language="en")

Their query parameter is q; a search= parameter answers 400 parameter-validation-failed (verified 2026-11-28). The client sends q.

docs.title: Site links
docs.text:
client.sitelinks reads the site links of an item through wbgetentities, without the rest of the entity.

links = await client.sitelinks.get("Q42", sites=["enwiki", "dewiki"], with_urls=True)
print(links["enwiki"].title, links["enwiki"].url)

get() returns a SitelinkMap dict keyed by site id. sites maps to the sitefilter parameter; with_urls=True asks for the sitelinks/urls property so each Sitelink carries the resolved article URL.

The REST shape is available through client.items.sitelink("Q42", "enwiki"), which returns one RestSitelink from the /entities/items/{id}/sitelinks/{site_id} route.

docs.title: SPARQL
docs.text: client.sparql talks to the SPARQL query service at https://query.wikidata.org/sparql. The service is a second host, so it runs on its own client instance behind the resource.

docs.title: Running queries
docs.text:
result = await client.sparql.query(
    "SELECT ?item ?label WHERE { ?item wdt:P31 wd:Q5 } LIMIT 5"
)
print(result.head.vars)
for row in result.rows():  # plain {variable: value} strings
    print(row["item"])

query() sends GET with format=json and returns a typed SparqlResult (the SPARQL 1.1 JSON result: head.vars and results.bindings with typed SparqlBindingValue terms carrying type, value, xml_lang, and datatype).

Long queries belong in a POST body, where URL length limits do not apply:

result = await client.sparql.query_post(long_query)

query_post() sends a read-only POST and therefore passes retry=True so the framework retries transient failures.

docs.title: Other formats
docs.text:
query_text() passes the raw body through as text. The representation is selected through the Accept header (the service ignores a non-JSON format query parameter): json, xml, csv, tsv, or turtle.

csv_body = await client.sparql.query_text(query, format="csv")

docs.title: Two hosts, one pace
docs.text: QuidditaClient owns one rate limiter built from QuidditaSettings. client.sparql builds a QuidditaQueryClient for query.wikidata.org that receives the same settings object and the main client's limiter instance. Requests are paced by rate class inside that shared limiter: Action API and REST requests use the default class (2 requests per second by default), SPARQL requests use the sparql class (one query every 2 seconds by default), and one concurrency bound covers both hosts. The result: the two clients together never exceed the pace the settings describe, and no separate coordination is needed.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Malformed or overlong queries answer with HTTP 400 and a plain-text Java stack trace; the framework raises APIError with that text attached as the body. The service cancels queries that run longer than its timeout.

docs.title: Upstream quirks
docs.text: Findings from the live study of Wikidata's three read interfaces on 2026-11-27, at about 60 paced requests, with the Action API self-documentation, the Wikibase REST OpenAPI document, and the data access guides as references. Where a quirk affects quiddita, the behavior of the client is noted.

docs.title: Read modules that exist
docs.text: The module index of action=help lists these read modules: wbgetentities, wbsearchentities, wbgetclaims, wbformatentities, wbformatvalue, wbparsevalue, wbavailablebadges, wbcheckconstraints, and wbsgetsuggestions, plus the write modules. The modules wbsearchbytitle and wbformatentitiesdata do not exist on Wikidata; both answer Unrecognized value for parameter "action".

docs.title: Action API error reporting
docs.text: All Action API errors, soft and hard, answer with HTTP 200 and an {"error": {code, info}} body. Unknown module, unknown parameter value, too many ids, and no-such-entity all came back with 200. quiddita raises on that shape in the unwrapper: no-such-entity becomes NotFoundError, everything else ConfigurationError.

docs.title: Parameter facts
docs.text:
• wbgetentities accepts at most 50 ids per request (toomanyvalues, lowlimit 50). batch_get() and iterate_ids() chunk at 50.
  • Unknown ids answer in two ways (verified 2026-11-28). An item id above the highest item number, and an unknown form or sense id, fail the whole wbgetentities request with no-such-entity, and the error body names the id as id. A deleted or never-used item id below that number (Q54446106), and an unknown lexeme or property id, answer with success and a {"id": ..., "missing": ""} stub. get() raises NotFoundError for both. batch_get() leaves stub ids out of its result and raises for a rejected request; iterate_ids() with on_error="skip" drops and records both kinds.
  • redirects accepts yes and no (default yes); the values 0, 1, and the empty string answer badvalue. With redirects=no a redirect id answers as a stub entity (info only).
  • wbgetclaims's rank accepts deprecated, normal, and preferred. The value valid answers badvalue, so ClaimsClient rejects it before sending.
  • wbsearchentities reports no total: searchinfo carries search and offset only. count() is therefore not supported, and iterate() walks continue offsets until an empty page.
  • wbformatentities returns HTML links per id; wbparsevalue parses values against a datatype; wbavailablebadges takes no titles or site parameters (it warns and returns all badges).
  • Multi-value parameters accept pipe-joined values (ids=Q42|P31); quiddita joins sequences with |.

docs.title: Special:EntityData (verified 2026-11-28)
docs.text:
• wiki/Special:EntityData/{id}.{format} serves the full entity per format: json (200 application/json, same shape as wbgetentities), jsonld, rdf, nt, ttl, and n3. The suffixes nquads, trig, and svg answer 415.
  • revision=<old revid> serves that revision; an unknown revision answers 404 with an HTML page, an invalid id answers 400 with Invalid ID: .... The route works for items, properties, and lexemes (L2.json).
  • Special:EntityData?ids=Q42|Q5&format=json answers HTML: the ids parameter is not a JSON route, so the client fetches one entity per request.
  • https://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q42 answers 303 to Special:EntityData/Q42.ttl under Accept: text/turtle; client.entity_data.negotiate() follows that redirect.
  • https://query.wikidata.org/bigdata/ld/wd/Q42, .ttl, and .jsonld all answer 404 (verified 2026-11-28): the linked-data endpoint of the query service is gone.

docs.title: REST suggest and lexeme routes (verified 2026-11-28)
docs.text:
• /suggest/items and /suggest/properties answer the same result shape as /search/items (match type can be alias). The query parameter is q; search= answers 400 parameter-validation-failed.
  • The lexeme routes live only under /w/rest.php/wikibaselexeme/v0: /entities/lexemes/L2 answers 200 with {id, lemmas, lexical_category, language, statements, forms, senses}, where lexical_category and language are bare item ids. The same path under wikibase/v1 answers 404, and /entities/forms/{id} and /entities/senses/{id} answer rest-no-match.

docs.title: Action utility modules (verified 2026-11-27/28)
docs.text:
• wbavailablebadges answers {"badges": [...]} with no parameters.
  • wbformatentities answers wbformatentities: {id: html}; the props and languages parameters are ignored with a warning, so the client does not offer them.
  • wbformatvalue takes datavalue as the JSON {"type": ..., "value": ...} object and datatype; without the type key it answers baddatavalue.
  • wbparsevalue answers results: [{raw, value, type}] for values and datatype.
  • wbsgetsuggestions answers search: [{id, url, rating, label, description}] and requires entity or properties; without both it answers propertysuggester-wbsgetsuggestions-either-entity-or-properties. With entity=Q42 the suggester answered an empty list on 2026-11-27.
  • wbcheckconstraints takes the entities in an id parameter (maximum 50, pipe-joined); entity and entityid answer the no-data error. The report is keyed by entity, then property, with per-claim mainsnak.results entries carrying status, constraint, and message HTML.

docs.title: Term data on 2026-11-27
docs.text: The item Q42 answered with no English label in any read shape (Action API with and without languages=en, REST item payload, and the REST /labels/en route answering resource-not-found), while wbsearchentities still matched it on the English label and the English description answered normally. The client's label() helpers return None in that case; they never fall back silently.

docs.title: REST API paths
docs.text:
The Wikibase REST API on Wikidata lives at https://www.wikidata.org/w/rest.php/wikibase/v1/. The bare https://wikidata.org/... spelling 301-redirects to www, and /items/Q42 answers rest-no-match; the real entity routes are /entities/items/{id}, /entities/properties/{id}, and /statements/{statement_id}. The read routes are the entity GETs, the per-language labels, descriptions, aliases (plus *_with_language_fallback), sitelinks (plus per-site), statements (plus per-statement), property-data-types, and search/items and search/properties.

The _fields query parameter that the OpenAPI document lists for the entity GET is rejected by the live API with invalid-query-parameter (HTTP 400). The client therefore always fetches full payloads.

The labels_with_language_fallback and descriptions_with_language_fallback routes answer HTTP 307 when another language serves the term (a request for simple redirected to the fallback chain). The term methods follow redirects.

The REST statement payload differs from the Action API claim: property arrives as a {id, data_type} object in entity payloads and as a string in the per-statement route, and value content is absent for somevalue and novalue snaks. The models accept both shapes. Lexemes live under a separate prefix (/w/rest.php/wikibaselexeme/v0), where client.lexemes.get() reads one lexeme. wbgetentities reads lexemes by id too.

docs.title: SPARQL query service
docs.text:
• GET and POST both answer format=json with the SPARQL 1.1 JSON result (head.vars, results.bindings, typed terms with uri/literal, xml:lang, and datatype).
  • Without an Accept header, the default answer is a SPARQL-result XML document. A non-JSON format query parameter is ignored; other representations (csv, tsv, turtle) are selected through Accept (verified 2026-11-27).
  • A malformed query answers with HTTP 400 and a plain-text Java stack trace starting with SPARQL-QUERY: queryStr=..., not a JSON error envelope.
  • Under load the service answers HTTP 429 with a Wikimedia error page instead of its usual error shapes; the framework maps that to RateLimitError and honors Retry-After. The live smoke set observed 429s on 2026-11-27 after several consecutive runs.
  • The service requires a descriptive User-Agent with contact information and asks readers to run one query at a time; the sparql rate class defaults to one query every 2 seconds.

docs.title: Rate defaults and sources
docs.text:
• Action API and REST: the guides at Wikidata:Data_access and Wikidata:Data_access/Large_volume ask readers to make requests in series with a delay, roughly one request every 500 milliseconds. Default: max_requests_per_second=2.0, max_concurrency=1.
  • SPARQL: Wikidata:SPARQL_query_service asks readers to run one query at a time and cancels overlong queries. Default: rate_limits={"sparql": 0.5} (one query every 2 seconds) under the shared concurrency bound.
  • All three services ask for a descriptive User-Agent with contact information; effective_user_agent() builds it from user_agent or the package metadata, and mailto is appended when set.

docs.title: Utility modules
docs.text: client.utilities wraps the small read modules of the Action API: wbavailablebadges, wbformatentities, wbformatvalue, wbparsevalue, wbsgetsuggestions, and wbcheckconstraints. Parameter facts come from the live study of 2026-11-27 and 2026-11-28; see upstream quirks.

docs.title: Badges
docs.text:
badges = await client.utilities.available_badges()  # ['Q17437798', ...]

available_badges() returns every badge id usable on site links.

docs.title: HTML formatting
docs.text:
links = await client.utilities.format_entities(["Q42", "P31"])
html = await client.utilities.format_value(
    {"type": "string", "value": "hello"}, "string"
)

format_entities() returns an HTML <a> link per id. The module ignores props and languages with a warning, so the client does not offer them. format_value() takes the {"type": ..., "value": ...} datavalue shape; without the type key the service answers baddatavalue.

docs.title: Parsing values
docs.text:
parsed = await client.utilities.parse_value(["Q42"], datatype="wikibase-item")
print(parsed[0].value["id"], parsed[0].type)  # Q42 wikibase-entityid

parse_value() returns ParsedValue records with the raw input, the parsed value, and the value type.

docs.title: Property suggestions
docs.text:
suggestions = await client.utilities.suggestions(entity="Q42", limit=10)
suggestions = await client.utilities.suggestions(properties=["P31"])

suggestions() wraps wbsgetsuggestions. The module answers propertysuggester-wbsgetsuggestions-either-entity-or-properties without entity or properties, so the client rejects that case before sending. Each PropertySuggestion carries id, url, rating, label, and description.

docs.title: Constraint checks
docs.text:
report = await client.utilities.check_constraints(["Q42"])
checks = report["Q42"]["P3192"][0]
print(checks.mainsnak.results[0].status)

check_constraints() wraps wbcheckconstraints. Its entity parameter is id (entity and entityid answer the no-data error, verified 2026-11-28). It returns a report keyed by entity id, then property id, with CheckedClaim records per claim; each carries the claim id and a mainsnak with the constraint check results (status, constraint, and message HTML). Pass claim_ids=, constraint_ids=, or statuses= to narrow the check.

docs.title: Ecosystem Roadmap & Architecture
docs.text:
The bibliofabric monorepo is designed as a three-layer open scholarly infrastructure stack:

Layer 3: Canonical Entity Fusion (working name: bibliocanon)
         Multi-source PID resolution, per-field Claim provenance,
         license governance, SQLite/DuckDB cache, lossy exporters
                              ▲
Layer 2: Modular Single-Source Client Libraries
         Original: aireloom (OpenAIRE), aletheca (OpenAlex), stavrophora (Crossref)
         Wave 1 (built, not yet released): ROR v2, Zenodo, DataCite,
                  OpenCitations, DOI RA/ConNeg, Semantic Scholar, ORCID v3,
                  Europe PMC, Wikidata, DOAJ v4, ISSN Portal
         Wave 2:  Domain indexes, repositories, funder APIs, protocol adapters
                              ▲
Layer 1: bibliofabric Core Framework
         Async + generated sync HTTP, auth, retries, throttling, paging,
         batching, streaming, identifier normalizers, typed ResourceClient[E]

Each single-source library stays lean, typed, and faithful to its upstream API schema. Cross-source entity deduplication, conflict resolution, and citation export live strictly in the canonical fusion layer above them.

docs.title: 2025–2026 Academic API Ecosystem Shifts
docs.text:
API choices and build order reflect concrete platform changes across the scholarly metadata ecosystem in 2025–2026:

  • OpenAlex credit tiers (2025–2026): Moved to usage-based daily budgets. A free API key grants $1.00/day (resetting at midnight UTC and required for cursor paging past page 1), alongside prepaid credits and institutional tiers, exposing X-RateLimit-Credits-Used and cost_usd. Free/CC0 complementary sources (DataCite, Europe PMC, OpenCitations, Semantic Scholar, ROR, DOAJ) are increasingly valuable so pipelines avoid spending OpenAlex budget on metadata and crosswalks served elsewhere for free.
  • Crossref transitions (2026):
  • The Crossref Event Data public API was sunset on April 23, 2026 (historical dump archived on Academic Torrents), replaced by the Crossref Data Citation API (/beta/datacitations/, targeting GA late 2026).
  • Retraction Watch data is now integrated into Crossref REST (updated-by / update-type:retraction with source: retraction-watch) alongside a daily GitLab CSV (crossref/retraction-watch-data).
  • Crossref's Open Funder Registry is formally transitioning into ROR (2024–2026); keep /funders for legacy 10.13039/... → ROR crosswalks.
  • ROR v2: API and schema v1 were sunset in late 2025. ROR v2 (api.ror.org/v2/organizations, with v2.1 adding continents, domains, timestamps, and streamlined single_search affiliation matching) is required and now serves as the canonical registry for both organizations and funders.
  • Open Policy Finder (Jisc): Replaced legacy Sherpa RoMEO & Juliet (v2.sherpa.ac.uk retired July 2026) at api.openpolicyfinder.jisc.ac.uk using x-api-key header authentication under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. OpenDOAR migrated onto the same API and paused new submissions/updates pending review until January 2027.
  • OpenCitations consolidation: Legacy COCI, POCI, and /index/v1 are deprecated/archived in favor of unified Index v2 (api.opencitations.net/index/v2) and Meta v1 (api.opencitations.net/meta/v1).
  • Unpaywall (September 2026): Retired /v2/search (410 Gone, redirecting callers to OpenAlex). Single-DOI lookup (GET /v2/{doi}?email=...) remains active (100k calls/day).
  • DOAJ v4: API v1–v3 are deprecated; API v4 (doaj.org/api/v4) is the active CC0 endpoint.
  • arXiv (October 2026): Completed its cloud/database migration (arXiv-CE) and spun out as an independent nonprofit; Atom 1.0 XML and OAI-PMH remain the primary machine interfaces.

docs.title: Gaps in the Original Three Clients
docs.text:
aireloom (OpenAIRE), aletheca (OpenAlex), and stavrophora (Crossref) already provide broad scholarly literature coverage, but leave five gaps. The Wave 1 libraries cover most of the first four gaps with public read clients. The other sources named below stay Wave 2 candidates.

  1. Authority registries & PID crosswalks: Canonical organization/funder hierarchies (ROR v2, GLEIF LEI), researcher-asserted profiles (ORCID v3), journal OA/APC/preservation metadata (DOAJ v4, ISSN Portal / Keepers, Open Policy Finder), universal PID bridging (Wikidata), and DOI Registration Agency routing (doi.org/ra).
  2. Research data & software: Crossref is literature-centric and OpenAlex lacks file manifests, concept↔version DOIs, checksums, and intrinsic code identifiers. DataCite, Zenodo (InvenioRDM), Dryad, Dataverse, Figshare, and Software Heritage fill this gap.
  3. Abstracts & full-text / bio-annotations: Crossref lacks abstracts for many publishers and OpenAlex omits restricted abstracts. Europe PMC, Semantic Scholar, PubMed, and CORE v3 provide rich abstracts, full-text links, and text-mined entities.
  4. Auditable citations & citation semantics: OpenCitations provides 100% CC0 auditable citation links (OCIs) and OMID crosswalks; Semantic Scholar adds influential citations, TLDRs, citation intents, and SPECTER2 embeddings.
  5. Preprint versioning & research integrity: arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv track preprint versions and preprint↔journal publication links; Retraction Watch + Crossref Crossmark provide safety-critical retraction coverage.

docs.title: Phase 0 — Core Enablers & Existing-Client Extensions
docs.text:
1. Six targeted bibliofabric core additions (detailed in Wave 1 Client Specs & Core Enablers): default per-client Accept headers, header-aware ResponseUnwrapper / RFC 5988 Link pagination, POST-body search dialect, sliding/fixed-window rate limiter + daily quota hooks, pluggable non-JSON (XML/SRU/Atom) decoder hook, and expanded bibliofabric.ids normalizers. Status on 2026-11-27: per-client headers and the JSON:API unwrapper are in bibliofabric 0.8, together with identifier normalizers for ISBN, ISNI, Wikidata, GND, and VIAF. The rest is listed in Deferred work.
  2. Existing client enhancements:
  3. stavrophora (Crossref): Add the Crossref Data Citation API (/beta/datacitations/) and Retraction Watch (updated-by / update-type:retraction) helpers.
  4. aletheca (OpenAlex): Expose OpenAlex credit/budget telemetry headers (X-RateLimit-Credits-Used, cost_usd) cleanly via on_response().

Status on 2026-11-28: all three are done. stavrophora has client.data_citations for the beta route and Work.retractions / Work.is_retracted for the Retraction Watch data, and the aletheca docs describe the credit and cost headers.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Wave 1: Authorities & Open Scholarly Graphs
docs.text:
Highest canonical ROI, open/free access, and permissive licensing (predominantly CC0 / ODC-By / Public Domain):

  • Authorities & Routers: ROR v2 (+ Zenodo dump loader & FundRef crosswalk), ORCID v3.0, DOAJ v4, DOI RA/ConNeg + ISSN Portal ConNeg, Wikidata (REST + wbgetentities batch).
  • Works, Citations, Data & Software: DataCite REST (+ optional GraphQL), Semantic Scholar (Graph + Bulk + POST batch), OpenCitations (Index v2 + Meta v1), Europe PMC, Zenodo (reusable InvenioRDM pattern).

Status on 2026-11-28: all eleven libraries are built under their final names and cover the public read endpoints of their APIs. See Wave 1 libraries for the roster and Deferred work for what was left out.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Canonical Entity Fusion MVP
docs.text:
Build the fusion library (bibliocanon) above bibliofabric and the Wave 1 clients:

  • Ten first-class canonical Pydantic models (Work, Person, Organization, Venue, Publisher, Funder, Grant, Dataset, Software, Concept).
  • Claim-based per-field provenance, Union-Find PID equivalence clustering, declarative FusionPolicy with license gating (commercial_safe=True).
  • Hybrid Waterfall + Scatter-Gather DAG planner with single-flight coalescing and per-source circuit breakers.
  • SQLite OLTP + DuckDB OLAP local store, bulk snapshot loaders (ROR, DOAJ, Retraction Watch CSV, SPDX, CRediT), and lossy exporters (CSL-JSON, BibTeX, Schema.org JSON-LD, MLCommons Croissant, RIS, Parquet).

docs.title: Phase 3 — Wave 2: Specialists & Shared Protocol Adapters
docs.text:
• Preprints, Data, Software & OA: arXiv, bioRxiv/medRxiv, CORE API v3, Dryad v2, Harvard Dataverse (reusable across 100+ Dataverse instances), Figshare v2, Software Heritage, re3data, Unpaywall (lightweight lookup).
  • Domain Indexes & Registries: DBLP, INSPIRE-HEP, NASA ADS / SciXplorer, HAL, ClinicalTrials.gov v2, PubMed / NCBI E-utilities, OSF Preprints, ChemRxiv, GLEIF LEI, Open Policy Finder (with CC-BY-NC-ND license guard), Open Library, Lobid-GND, VIAF, Mir@bel, HK-dir, JUFO, NIH RePORTER v2, NSF Award Search, UKRI GtR, RAiD, Identifiers.org, MeSH RDF.
  • Shared Protocol Adapters: Generic OAI-PMH XML harvester mixin, FAIR Signposting HEAD/Link resolver, and CodeMeta / CITATION.cff software metadata parsers.

Status on 2026-11-28: two Wave 2 libraries are built. archeion covers the arXiv query API (search, lookups by id, paging) with an Atom parser of its own; its OAI-PMH interface waits for the shared harvester above. prodromus covers every route of api.biorxiv.org for bioRxiv and medRxiv. See Deferred work.

docs.title: Restricted, Commercial & Do-Not-Build List
docs.text:
Keep the open core free of legal/licensing blockers and deprecated endpoints:

  • Do not build (sunset/deprecated): Crossref Event Data (sunset April 23, 2026), ROR v1 (sunset late 2025), Sherpa v2 (v2.sherpa.ac.uk, retired July 2026), OpenCitations COCI/POCI//index/v1, Unpaywall /v2/search (retired September 2026), DOAJ v1–v3.
  • Do not scrape (closed/no public API): ResearchGate, Loop (Frontiers), DFG GEPRIS (consume via OpenAIRE/Crossref), Ringgold Identify (resolve legacy IDs passively via Wikidata/ORCID/ISNI crosswalks).
  • Optional user-credentialed plugins only (proprietary / restricted ToS): Lens.org, Dimensions, Scite, Altmetric, PlumX, PubPeer, OpenSyllabus, Elsevier Scopus/ScienceDirect, Springer Nature, IEEE Xplore, Wiley TDM, ACM DL, WorldCat v2, ISBNdb, OpenCorporates (ODbL + 50/day free cap), BASE (strictly non-commercial), OpenDOAR (CC BY-NC-ND + paused until Jan 2027), Google Books (non-redistributable caching ToS).
  • Periodic local tables (no live REST API): Latindex, Scimago (SJR), CWTS Journal Indicators, MIAR.

docs.title: Roadmap Guides
docs.text:
• Works, Citations, Preprints, Data & OA Catalog — Structured catalog of scholarly work, citation, preprint, repository, data, software, integrity, and protocol APIs.
  • Authority Registries, Organizations, Venues, Funders & Taxonomies — Structured catalog of researcher, organization, venue, funder, PID, and controlled-vocabulary APIs.
  • Wave 1 Client Specs & Core Enablers — Starter implementation specs for the 11 Wave 1 clients and the 6 bibliofabric core additions.
  • Wave 1 Libraries — The roster with the package names, their origins, and the release steps.
  • Deferred Work — Everything Wave 1 left out, with the reason and the condition that unblocks it.
  • Canonical Entity Fusion Architecture — End-to-end architecture blueprint for the canonical entity fusion library.
  • Building a client on bibliofabric — Practical guide to writing, testing, and shipping a new client package in this workspace.

docs.title: Academic APIs Catalog: Authority Registries, Organizations, Venues, Funders & Taxonomies
docs.text:
This catalog covers the canonical authority registries, persistent-identifier routers, and controlled vocabularies needed to anchor authors, institutions, journals, books, publishers, funders, grants, and subjects across scholarly graphs.

Priority Tiers:

  • P0 (Foundational Backbone): Required for canonical entity grounding; build first (Wave 1).
  • P1 (High Canonical Value): High-impact enrichment sources (Wave 2).
  • P2 (Domain / Regional Enrichment): Valuable regional or discipline authorities and lightweight helpers.
  • P3 (Bulk Table / Commercial / Skip): Periodic CSV lookup tables, paywalled services, or closed portals.

docs.title: Authors, Researchers & Contributors
docs.text: API Docs & Base URL Protocol Auth / Pricing License Rate Limits & Paging / Batching Unique Canonical Value-Add bibliofabric Fit / Gaps Priority ORCID API v3.0 DocsPublic: https://pub.orcid.org/v3.0Member: https://api.orcid.org/v3.0 REST JSON (Accept: application/vnd.orcid+json) or XML Anon (public); free Public Client OAuth2 (/read-public, non-commercial); paid Member API. Public API Terms (non-commercial); annual public data file CC0. 12 req/s (24 member), burst 40/s → 503; 25k/day anon / 100k/day public. Search start/rows (10k cap). No multi-ID batch. Author-asserted bio, verified employment/education timelines (ROR/Ringgold), curated works, cross-PID links (ISNI/Scopus/ResearcherID). Good fit (ClientCredentialsAuth(token_auth_method="post"), normalize_orcid). Needs default Accept header, daily quota guard, XML-style JSON unwrapper. P0 Wikidata (REST v1, Action, SPARQL) & Scholia DocsREST: https://www.wikidata.org/w/rest.php/wikibase/v1Action: https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.phpSPARQL: https://query.wikidata.org/sparql REST JSON, Action JSON, SPARQL Free (optional OAuth2). Descriptive User-Agent required or immediate 429. CC0 1.0 Action wbgetentities batches 50 QIDs/req. SPARQL 60s timeout, ~5 conc. Honor Retry-After. Universal PID crosswalk hub (ORCID, ISNI, VIAF, GND, LCCN, IdRef, ROR, ISSN, DOI, OpenAlex), multilingual labels, deceased dates, Scholia templates. Moderate fit (wbgetentities dict unwrapper, normalize_wikidata_qid, optional SPARQL helper). P0 Lobid-GND (hbz / DNB) Docshttps://lobid.org/gnd (/search, /{id}.json, /reconcile) REST JSON-LD + Reconcile API Free, no key. CC0 1.0 ES from/size + scroll; polite throttling (especially /reconcile). DACH/European researchers, corporate bodies, subjects, biographical dates, sameAs links to VIAF/ISNI/Wikidata/ORCID. Strong fit (offset_param="from", page_size_param="size", valid JSON). P1 VIAF (OCLC) Docshttps://viaf.org/viaf/ (/{id}/viaf.json, /AutoSuggest, /search) REST JSON/JSON-LD + SRU (XML) Free public read (modernized 2025–2026 OAS 3.0 infrastructure). ODC-BY 1.0 Polite limits; SRU startRecord/maximumRecords. No multi-ID batch GET. Global meta-authority clustering 60+ national libraries (humanities and historical authors lacking ORCIDs). Moderate fit (JSON cluster + AutoSuggest; SRU XML needed for /search). P1 Library of Congress Linked Data (id.loc.gov) Docshttps://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/ (/suggest2, /{lccn}.json) REST JSON (suggest2), JSON-LD, SKOS Free, no key. Public Domain / CC0 Strict IP bans: JSON 20 req/min (1h block); MARCXML 30 req/min (72h rolling block). Authoritative North American name authority (LCNAF) & subjects (LCSH) with exactMatch to VIAF/ISNI/Wikidata. Needs strict per-minute window limiter to prevent IP bans. docs.title: Academic APIs Catalog: Works, Citations, Preprints, Data, Software, OA & Integrity
docs.text:
This catalog evaluates scholarly literature, citation graph, preprint, research data, software, open-access, and research-integrity APIs against 2025–2026 platform status and bibliofabric 0.7 capabilities.

Priority Tiers:

  • Tier 1 (Wave 1 / Next Up): Highest canonical value, open/permissive licensing, clean REST/JSON (or essential preprint coverage).
  • Tier 2 (Wave 2 / High-Value Specialist): Strong domain/data/software authority or reusable protocol adapters.
  • Tier 3 (Restricted / Niche / Deprecated): Paywalled, non-redistributable ToS, narrow niche, or sunset endpoints.

docs.title: General Scholarly Indexes & Citation Graphs
docs.text: API Docs & Base URL Protocol Auth & Access License Rate Limits & Paging / Batching Unique Value-Add bibliofabric Fit Priority DataCite REST & GraphQL Docshttps://api.datacite.orghttps://api.datacite.org/graphql REST (JSON:API) + GraphQL (POST) Public read: none (User-Agent/mailto). Write: Member BasicAuth; Usage Reports: JWT. CC0 1.0 page[number]/page[size] (10k cap) + page[cursor]. GraphQL Relay cursors. 500 unid / 1,000 identified / 3,000 member per 5 min. Authoritative DOI agency for datasets, software, preprints, DMPs, grey lit, and PID Graph (relatedIdentifiers, versioning, usage stats). REST ready (JSON:API unwrapper + page[cursor]; BasicAuth ready for writes). Tier 1 Semantic Scholar (Graph + Bulk + Recs + Datasets) Docshttps://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/recommendations/v1, /datasets/v1 REST/JSON Free API key (x-api-key header); anonymous shares throttled global pool (frequent 429s). ODC-By 1.0 (corpus); AI2 API License (SPECTER2 Apache 2.0). Search offset/limit (1k cap); /paper/search/bulk (token cursor, cursor_start=None); POST /paper/batch (500 IDs), POST /author/batch. 1 RPS intro key. TLDRs, SPECTER2 embeddings, influential citations, citation contexts & intents, strong CS/biomed abstracts, author disambiguation. Ready today (HeaderAuth, cursor_start=None, _fetch_batch_chunk POST override with retry=True). Tier 1 OpenCitations (Index v2 + Meta v1) Docshttps://api.opencitations.net/index/v2https://api.opencitations.net/meta/v1 REST/JSON (+ SPARQL & dumps) Open/free; optional Access Token (authorization header). CC0 1.0 Path lookups (/citations/doi:..., /references/doi:..., /metadata/omid:...); __-separated path batching; unpaged (page_size_param=None). 180 req/min/IP. First-class auditable citation links (OCIs) & OMID crosswalks unifying Crossref, DataCite, NIH-OCC, OpenAIRE, JaLC. (COCI/POCI/Index v1 deprecated.) Ready today (page_size_param=None, custom item_path & _fetch_batch_chunk). Tier 1 Europe PMC (Articles + Annotations + Citations) Docshttps://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/annotations_api REST/JSON & XML Open/free, no API key. Metadata open; full-text per-article CC license. cursorMark (* → nextCursorMark), pageSize max 1,000. Citations/refs page/pageSize. Annotations batch 1–8 IDs. Polite ~1–10 RPS. Life-science articles, preprints, grants, JATS full text, text-mined bio-annotations (genes/UniProt, diseases, chemicals, data links), PMID/PMCID/DOI crosswalk. Ready today (cursorMark + pageSize). JATS XML needs XML helper. Tier 1 PubMed / NCBI E-utilities & PMC OA Docshttps://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/utils/oa/oa.fcgi REST XML & JSON (.fcgi) Free; optional api_key + tool/email query params. US Public Domain (metadata; PMC OA per-article CC). 2-step esearch (retstart/retmax, WebEnv history) → esummary (JSON) or efetch (XML only). 3 RPS keyless / 10 RPS with key. Authoritative MeSH indexing, MEDLINE curation, structured PubMed XML, NCT/grant tags, PMC OA tarballs. Needs XML decoder for efetch; QueryParameterAuth works for esearch/esummary. Tier 2 DBLP Docshttps://dblp.org/search/publ/api/author/api, /venue/api REST/JSON, XML, RDF Open/free, no API key. CC0 1.0 f (offset) + h (hits up to 1,000), format=json. Strict anti-burst throttling (keep ≤1 RPS or use XML/RDF dumps). Gold-standard CS publication & author disambiguation (PIDs) and conference/series hierarchy. Ready today (offset_param="f", page_size_param="h", result.hits.hit unwrapper). Tier 2 INSPIRE-HEP Docshttps://inspirehep.net/api/ REST/JSON (+ BibTeX/LaTeX) Open/free, no API key for read. CC0 (no bulk author email harvesting). page + size (up to 1,000; 10k ES cap) + links.next. 15 req / 5s per IP (429s count against rolling window — wait ≥5s). High-energy physics literature, collaborations/experiments, arXiv↔journal canonical records, HEP citations. Ready today (Invenio JSON; recommend ≥5s 429 cooldown). Tier 2 NASA ADS / SciXplorer Docshttps://api.adsabs.harvard.edu/v1/ REST/JSON (Solr) Free Bearer token (Authorization: Bearer). Open metadata (abstracts/full-text per publisher). Solr start/rows (max 2,000) + cursorMark; POST /metrics & /export/*. 5,000 req/day (X-RateLimit-*). Astronomy, planetary & Earth/heliophysics bibcodes, curated telescope/dataset links, full-text search, astro citation graph. Ready today for /search/query (StaticTokenAuth + cursorMark). Tier 2 Lens.org (Scholarly & Patent) Docshttps://api.lens.org/scholarly/searchhttps://api.lens.org/patent/search REST/JSON (POST DSL + GET) Paid / Member plan (14-day academic trial); Authorization: Bearer. Proprietary / Member ToS (no bulk redistribution). JSON POST (size, from, scroll). Tiered (~10–20 RPM basic); x-rate-limit-retry-after-millis. 250M+ works + 150M+ global patents + patent-to-scholarly NPL citations, clinical trials, funding. Needs POST search dialect + millisecond retry-after parsing. Tier 3 Dimensions (DSL v2) Docshttps://app.dimensions.ai/api/dsl/v2 Custom DSL POST Paid institutional or approved free non-commercial scientometrics grant only. API key → /auth.html → 2h JWT. Proprietary / Restricted ToS. DSL limit (1,000) + skip (50k cap); 30 req/min/IP. Publications, grants, patents, clinical trials, policy documents, orgs. Poor fit (custom DSL + non-OAuth JWT + restricted ToS). Tier 3
