docs.title: Canonical Entity Fusion Architecture
docs.text: (Working name: bibliocanon — an orchestration, entity-resolution, and fusion library layered cleanly above bibliofabric and all single-source sibling clients.)

docs.title: Design Synthesis from Scholarly Knowledge Graphs
docs.text:
The architecture borrows proven patterns from major scholarly knowledge graphs while keeping local-first Python SDK ergonomics (no Spark or RDF triplestore required):

System Pattern Adopted Pitfall Avoided OpenAIRE Graph Multi-stage deduplication (blocking → similarity → transitive closure) + explicit per-assertion provenance & trust scores (0.0–1.0). Heavy batch Hadoop/Spark coupling; must run both on-demand (async single-entity) and in local batch pipelines. OpenAlex Flat, ergonomic canonical Pydantic models grounded in ROR, ORCID, ISSN-L, and DOI; CC0 openness. Silent winner-takes-all overwrites where callers cannot inspect which source supplied a field or when. OpenCitations Meta (OMID) Internal stable IDs decoupled from external PIDs + versioned provenance snapshots. Triplestore/Blazegraph operational overhead; implement the data model in Pydantic + SQLite/DuckDB instead. Wikidata / Scholia Claim-centric model (value, qualifiers, source, confidence) so conflicting claims coexist transparently. Unbounded untyped schemas; preserve strict ty-checked Pydantic fields backed by a structured claims map. CERIF / Research Graph First-class temporal, role-typed relationships (Person —[employed_at, 2020–2024]→ Organization). CERIF-XML verbosity; represent edges as typed Pydantic models with optional export adapters. CSL-JSON, BibTeX, Schema.org, Croissant Standard lossy export projections tailored to downstream tools. Treating citation formats as the internal canonical schema (which drops affiliations, grants, OA policies, and provenance).

docs.title: Ten First-Class Canonical Entities
docs.text:
Every entity inherits from CanonicalEntity:

  • canonical_id: str — deterministic internal URN (e.g. urn:biblio:work:doi:10.1038/..., or content-addressed hash urn:biblio:work:sha256:... when no hard PID exists).
  • identifiers: IdentifierSet — normalized multi-PID registry (dict[PidScheme, list[PidValue]] with primary flag and source provenance).
  • same_as: list[str] — external canonical URIs (ror.org, orcid.org, wikidata.org, openalex.org, omid).
  • claims: dict[str, list[Claim]] — raw per-field assertions retained for auditability, offline re-fusion, and license filtering.
  • provenance: EntityProvenance — per-source fetch timestamps, fusion policy version, source degradations, has_conflict: bool, and effective minimum SPDX license.
Entity Primary Hard PIDs (Anchors) Secondary / Crosswalk PIDs Key Canonical Attributes Work (articles, preprints, books, chapters, proceedings) doi, isbn13, arxiv, pmid, pmcid, handle, ark openalex, openaire, s2, omid, wikidata, hal, oclc, lccn Title, subtitle, type (COAR/CSL), pub dates, abstract, language, ordered authorships (+ CRediT + affiliations), venue ref, citations/references, OA status/URLs, SPDX license, retraction/correction status, funding links, subjects. Grant / Project raid, doi (grant DOI), (funder_ror, award_number) cordis, nih_core_project, nsf_award, ukri_gtr, arc_grant, snsf, openaire_project Title, abstract, funder ref, award number, start/end dates, budget + currency, PIs (ORCID), administering/partner orgs (ROR), linked outputs. Dataset doi, accession (Identifiers.org CURIE), ark zenodo, dryad, figshare, openaire, openalex Work core + version chain (isVersionOf), files/distributions, checksums/format/size, SPDX license, funding, isSupplementTo, Croissant ML-structure fields. docs.title: Identity Clustering & Guarded Links
docs.text:
Entity resolution maintains a bipartite equivalence graph (EntityCluster) ↔ (PidScheme, normalized_value):

  1. Hard 1:1 merges (Union-Find): Normalized doi, orcid, ror, issn_l, lei, raid, swhid, pmid, and wikidata QID. Two records sharing any hard PID merge deterministically into one equivalence cluster.
  2. Guarded merges and version links (never collapsed destructively):
  3. Print vs. Electronic ISSN: Merge only through an authoritative ISSN-L from ISSN Portal or DOAJ, never blindly on title similarity.
  4. Preprint ↔ Version of Record (VoR): An arXiv ID or bioRxiv DOI and its published journal DOI link via explicit hasVersion / isVersionOf edges rather than destructive merge, preserving distinct dates, licenses, and abstracts.
  5. ISBN-10 / ISBN-13: Edition-level identifiers grouped under a parent Work cluster.
  6. Composite fallback keys:
  7. Grants lacking DOIs/RAiDs anchor on (funder_ror, normalized_award_code).
  8. Works lacking hard PIDs anchor on (normalized_title_hash, year, first_author_surname) with fuzzy verification (Jaro-Winkler / Levenshtein ≥ 0.92) before clustering.

docs.title: Claim Provenance, Conflict Resolution & License Governance
docs.text:
Every ingested upstream field is recorded as an immutable Claim:

Claim(
    field="title",
    value="...",
    source="crossref",
    source_record_id="10.1038/s41586-020-2649-2",
    retrieved_at=datetime(...),
    source_updated_at=datetime(...),
    confidence=1.0,
    license_spdx="CC0-1.0",
)

docs.title: Resolution Strategies (Declarative FusionPolicy)
docs.text:
1. authority_priority: Choose the claim from the highest-ranked source for that field (tie-breaking by confidence, then source_updated_at).
  2. freshest_timestamp: Choose the latest source_updated_at for mutable operational metadata (APCs, OA URL liveness, current employment flags).
  3. union_with_dedup: Merge normalized sets across sources (PIDs, aliases, OA locations, funding awards, references, subject terms), retaining the list of supporting sources per item. Never average incompatible citation counts across indexes; expose per-source counts side by side.
  4. safety_monotonic (any_true_with_evidence): For retractions, expressions of concern, and errata, any verified authoritative positive claim surfaces prominently with evidence rather than being outvoted.
  5. confidence_weighted: For inferred links (affiliation string → ROR, text-mined grants), accept claims at or above threshold (e.g. ROR chosen=True or OpenAIRE trust ≥ 0.8) and keep lower-confidence matches in tentative_claims.
  6. Raw claim retention & conflict surfacing: Non-winning claims stay in entity.claims[field] and set provenance.has_conflict = True when high-tier sources materially disagree (e.g., publication year off by >1, conflicting retractions, mismatched ISSN-L).

docs.title: License Governance (FusionPolicy)
docs.text:
Because upstream licenses differ materially — ROR, DOAJ, GLEIF, Wikidata, Lobid-GND, OpenAlex, Crossref bibliographic facts, DataCite, OpenCitations, and NIH/NSF are CC0/Public Domain, while Open Policy Finder is CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0, ORCID Public API carries non-commercial terms, and Google Books restricts persistent redistribution — FusionPolicy enforces licensing declaratively:

policy = FusionPolicy(
    commercial_safe=True,
    allowed_licenses={"CC0-1.0", "CC-BY-4.0", "ODC-By-1.0", "OGL-UK-3.0"},
)

Disallowed sources are skipped during planning (saving quota) or stripped during offline re-fusion and export, and every fused entity computes its effective minimum license in entity.provenance.

docs.title: Hybrid Waterfall + Scatter-Gather Execution Engine
docs.text:
Pure scatter-gather wastes API quota (e.g. querying Crossref for a DataCite DOI); pure sequential waterfall is too slow. The planner runs a staged DAG with three built-in profiles (fast, standard, deep):

  1. Stage 0 — Local & Static Resolution (0 HTTP calls): Normalize PIDs via bibliofabric.ids, query the local SQLite/DuckDB cache (with per-source TTLs, e.g. ROR/ISSN 30d, Work metadata 7d, Citations 1d), and consult static vocabularies (SPDX, CRediT, OECD FOS, ANZSRC) plus optional local ROR/DOAJ dumps (<1 ms).
  2. Stage 1 — Fast Anchor & Routing Call (1 call):
  3. For DOIs: check local prefix cache or call doi.org/ra/{doi} (batchable) to route straight to Crossref (stavrophora) vs. DataCite vs. ConNeg.
  4. Fetch the primary anchor record (Crossref/DataCite for Work, ORCID for Person, ROR for Org, ISSN/DOAJ for Venue) to harvest secondary PIDs (orcid, ror, issn, pmid, grant_id).
  5. Stage 2 — Bounded Async Scatter-Gather (run_bounded):
  6. Fan out in parallel across complementary sources unlocked by Stage 1 PIDs.
  7. Apply single-flight request coalescing so a batch of 50 works sharing 1 journal ISSN or 3 ROR IDs fires only 1 upstream fetch per unique anchor.
  8. Stage 3 — Optional Recursive Graph Expansion (depth=1..N): Hydrate linked Author, Organization, Venue, and Grant stubs into full canonical entities on demand.

docs.title: Partial Failure Tolerance
docs.text:
Every adapter runs inside a per-source timeout and isolated error boundary (on_error="degrade" by default, "raise" optional) with a per-source circuit breaker that opens after consecutive 5xx/429/timeout failures so a degraded registry (such as VIAF or LoC throttling) never stalls the pipeline. Each resolution returns FusionResult[E]:

  • entity: E — best canonical entity built from all succeeded sources
  • sources_succeeded: list[str]
  • source_errors: dict[str, SourceFailure] — typed status, retryable flag, and sanitized message
  • completeness: float — fraction of target field groups populated

docs.title: Local Caching, Persistence & Bulk Snapshots
docs.text:
Persistence is organized into three tiers:

  • Tier 1 — Raw HTTP ETag/TTL Cache (SQLite): Stores (source, canonical_request_key) → (etag, last_modified, status, gzip_json, fetched_at, ttl) to enable If-None-Match conditional revalidation for slow-changing authorities (ROR, Wikidata, MeSH, SPDX).
  • Tier 2 — Claim & Entity Graph Store (SQLite OLTP + DuckDB OLAP):
  • entities(canonical_id, entity_type, payload_json, updated_at, schema_version)
  • identifiers(scheme, value, canonical_id, primary_flag, source) — indexed for O(1) PID crosswalk and Union-Find cluster lookups.
  • claims(canonical_id, field, value_json, source, source_record_id, confidence, license_spdx, retrieved_at) — retaining raw claims allows callers to re-run FusionEngine offline under a different FusionPolicy (e.g. toggling commercial_safe=True or changing source priority) without re-querying any API.
  • relations(src_id, rel_type, dst_id, qualifiers_json, source, confidence) — CERIF-style typed temporal edges.
  • DuckDB bridge: Zero-copy SQL analytics and Parquet export over millions of fused entities and claims.
  • Tier 3 — Local Bulk Snapshot Loaders: First-class loaders for compact, high-value open dumps — ROR Zenodo dump (~115k orgs), DOAJ journal dump (~21k journals), Retraction Watch daily GitLab CSV (~50k+ rows), plus static SPDX, CRediT, and ANZSRC tables — turning the highest-hit lookups into <1 ms zero-network calls.

docs.title: Lossy Export Adapters
docs.text:
All exporters live under exports/ with zero network I/O and optional license-compliance validation before serialization:

Exporter Output Format Primary Target to_csl_json(work) CSL-JSON Pandoc, Zotero, Citeproc (id, type, DOI, ISSN, ISBN, author, issued.date-parts, container-title) to_bibtex(work) BibTeX / BibLaTeX LaTeX workflows (deterministic citekeys, LaTeX escaping, @article/@inproceedings/@book/@software/@dataset) to_schema_org(entity) Schema.org JSON-LD Web/SEO & knowledge graphs (ScholarlyArticle, Person, Organization, Periodical, Grant, SoftwareSourceCode, Dataset with @id & sameAs) to_croissant(dataset) MLCommons Croissant JSON-LD ML-ready dataset metadata (schema.org/Dataset + cr:distribution, cr:recordSet, cr:field) to_ris(work) RIS Legacy reference managers & systematic review tools (EndNote, RefWorks, Rayyan, Covidence) to_parquet(entities) Apache Parquet / Arrow Columnar bibliometrics & ML pipelines (flattened entities, PID crosswalks, and edge tables via PyArrow/DuckDB)

docs.title: Deferred work
docs.text: This page lists everything that the Wave 1 and Wave 2 libraries left out, with the reason and the condition that unblocks it. An item leaves this page only when it is done.

docs.title: Core framework
docs.text:
Wave 1 needed two of the six planned core additions. BaseApiClient.default_headers sends per-client headers such as an Accept type, and JsonApiUnwrapper reads JSON:API envelopes. bibliofabric.ids gained normalizers for ISBN, ISNI, Wikidata, GND, and VIAF. The rest stays open.

Item Why it is deferred Unblocked by RFC 5988 Link header parser for paging No Wave 1 read route pages through headers only. DOAJ and Zenodo carry their page links in the response body. A Wave 2 client that pages through headers, such as Software Heritage, OSF, or GLEIF. POST-body search dialect Every Wave 1 read route works with GET. The Semantic Scholar batch routes are POST requests that only read, and its client sends them directly. NIH RePORTER, Figshare, CORE, or SPARQL endpoints with a POST interface. Window limiter and daily quota hooks No Wave 1 API enforces a window or daily quota that the per-second limiter cannot respect. LoC, GLEIF, or NASA ADS, which ban or throttle by minute or by day. Pluggable non-JSON decoder The DOI client returns XML and BibTeX representations as text and parses the JSON ones. arXiv Atom, PubMed efetch, SRU, or a generic OAI-PMH harvester. Identifier normalizers for LEI, ARK, RAiD, SWHID, and SPDX No Wave 1 payload carries these identifiers as first-class fields. GLEIF LEI, arXiv, DataCite (RAiD), or Software Heritage clients.

docs.title: Release
docs.text: Item Why it is deferred Unblocked by PyPI trusted publishers for the new names PyPI registers a pending publisher only through its web interface, signed in as the owner. Adding a pending publisher for each name, as described in Wave 1 libraries. Release of the new libraries Each first release needs its trusted publisher. bibliofabric 0.8.0, which they require, is on PyPI since 2026-11-28, with aireloom 0.9.1, aletheca 0.5.1, and stavrophora 0.5.0. The trusted publishers above, then one <name>-v0.1.0 tag per library.

docs.title: ROR (rorifer)
docs.text: Item Why it is deferred Unblocked by Client identification ROR paused registration for client ids. The API needs no credentials and documents a limit of 2,000 requests per 5 minutes per IP address; the client paces itself to 6 requests per second. ROR reopening registration. The client id then goes into default_headers. Complete lists through the API The API reaches at most 10,000 records per query and cannot OR two different filter keys. This is an upstream limit. Nothing on our side. Use the data dumps, which the client reads. Searching external ids that contain a quote, a backslash, or a colon The query parser of ROR rejects such values. An upstream change. Pass bare ids.

docs.title: Zenodo (zenotheca)
docs.text: Item Why it is deferred Unblocked by Write routes (deposits, drafts, file upload, publish, community management) Wave 1 covers reads only. Anonymous requests answer 403, so there is no way to test a write. An access token in .env and a decision to support writes. Typed facet aggregations Search answers aggregations with a different bucket shape per facet. The client returns them as plain dicts in Page.meta, so no data is lost. A decision on which facets need typed models. Typed models for OAI-PMH metadata schemas The metadata element depends on the metadata prefix (eight prefixes on 2026-11-27). Each record carries the metadata as raw XML. A decision on which prefixes need typed models. Live check of the token settings No Zenodo token exists. The Authorization header and the page size of 100 with a token are covered by offline tests only. A Zenodo access token in .env. GET /api/records/{id}/files-archive (every file of a record as one zip) and GET /api/names Both answer 403 without a token (verified 2026-11-28). download_file() fetches each file of a record. A Zenodo access token in .env.

docs.title: DataCite (dataphora)
docs.text: Item Why it is deferred Unblocked by DOI writes (create, update, delete, publish) and media mutations Wave 1 covers reads only. The write routes belong to the MDS API and need repository credentials. A DataCite repository account and a decision to support writes. Read routes media, url, views, and downloads under /dois/{id} They answer 404 without a login (verified 2026-11-27). A DataCite account. The client then sends its credentials. Usage Reports API and API-key management Both need a login, and no account exists. A DataCite account. GraphQL mutations Queries are public and wrapped. Mutations need a bearer token, and none exists. A DataCite account and a decision to support writes.

docs.title: OpenCitations (opcitato)
docs.text: Item Why it is deferred Unblocked by Access Token in the authorization header No token exists to test, and both APIs answer without one. The token is free, counts unique users, and does not change the limit. A caller can send one through a prepared httpx.AsyncClient, which an offline test covers. A token from OpenCitations, then an optional setting and a live check. json=array(...) and json=dict(...) row transformations The plain rows carry every field. These parameters only reshape a row. A caller that needs the reshaped rows. Database dumps at download.opencitations.net The dumps are many gigabytes and serve bulk harvest, not lookups. A decision to ship a dump loader, as the ROR client has. Legacy Index API v1 (/index/v1/...) It is the predecessor of v2. Its rows carry bare DOIs and a subset of the v2 fields, and it still answers 200 (verified 2026-11-28). A caller that needs a field only v1 returns. OCI Resolver (oci.opencitations.net) It is a web page that returns information about one citation for any OCI. index.citation() covers the citations of the Index. A caller that must resolve the OCIs of other datasets.

docs.title: DOI (hodoi)
docs.text: Item Why it is deferred Unblocked by Resolver parameters noredirect, urlappend, locatt, ignore_aliases, and nols noredirect answers an HTML page, not an API (verified 2026-11-28). The other four reshape the redirect for multiple-resolution links. locations() lists the redirect targets, and handle() returns the record that holds them. A caller that needs the reshaped redirect. Handle API parameters callback and recursive callback asks for a JSONP body, which no Python client needs. recursive is not in the factsheet, and the proxy accepted it without changing the answer (verified 2026-11-27). A decision to expose them. ?pretty=true on /ra/ and on the Handle API It only indents the JSON (verified 2026-11-28). A caller that reads the raw JSON text. Content negotiation for EIDR, JaLC, and OP These agencies answer /ra/, but no sample DOI was exercised, so AGENCY_SUPPORT does not list them. A sample DOI from each agency and a few live requests.

docs.title: Semantic Scholar (scholiast)
docs.text: Item Why it is deferred Unblocked by Live check of the keyed paths The API key on hand answers HTTP 403. A new key, then one live run with SCHOLIAST_API_KEY set. Live check of /paper/search, /snippet/search, and the URL: id form The anonymous pool answered 429 for these three on 2026-11-27 and 2026-11-28. The client wraps them from the published specification. /paper/search/match, /paper/autocomplete, /patent/search, the recommendations, and the release listing passed a live check without a key on 2026-11-28. A key, or a quiet hour on the anonymous pool. Dataset file downloads and diffs The file listing answers 401 without a key. A download is a plain HTTP GET of a pre-signed URL. A key, then a decision to wrap the download. Live check of the paper fields openAccessDoi and embedding and the author fields normalizedAffiliations and aliases They answer 400 without a key. The models carry the fields. A key with access to those fields.

docs.title: ORCID (orchis)
docs.text: Item Why it is deferred Unblocked by Member API on api.orcid.org The token and the client credentials on hand are public API credentials: the member API answered 403 for both on 2026-11-28. The member read routes have the same paths as the public ones. ORCID member credentials, then a base URL setting and a live run. Write routes (POST, PUT, and DELETE on record sections) They need a member token and are out of scope for this wave. A member token. application/ld+json representations The API answers 406 for that media type. The API serving JSON-LD. The /{orcid}/invited-to-peer-review route The public API answers 404 for it (verified 2026-11-28). The activities summary lists peer reviews under peer-reviews, which the client wraps. ORCID serving the route on the public API. Download of the public data file The 2025 edition is a 17.4 GB archive of XML files. A decision to ship a bulk loader, as the ROR client has.

docs.title: Europe PMC (europaea)
docs.text: Item Why it is deferred Unblocked by format=xml and format=dc on the search, and format=xml on the per-article routes The client requests format=json. The other formats return the same records in XML or Dublin Core. A caller that needs those formats, then typed wrappers for them. Typed parsing of the JATS full text and the book XML The XML routes return the document as text in XmlDocument. A decision on which JATS elements need models. The /preprint/{source}/{id} routes of older documentation The service answers 404 for all of them (verified 2026-11-27). A preprint record is available through /article/PPR/{id} and the SRC:PPR search, which the client wraps. The service adding the routes. Bulk downloads of the full-text corpus and the supplementary files They are archives for bulk harvest, not REST routes. A decision to ship a bulk loader. Annotation writes on the annotations API Wave 1 covers reads only. They need an OAuth token. An account and a decision to support writes.

docs.title: Wikidata (quiddita)
docs.text: Item Why it is deferred Unblocked by Action API write modules (wbeditentity, wbsetlabel, wbsetdescription, wbsetaliases, wbsetclaim, wbremoveclaims, wbsetreference, wbmergeitems, wbcreateredirect, wblinktitles, and the lexeme wbl* writes) Wave 1 covers reads only. They need a bot account. An account and a decision to support writes. REST write methods (POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE on items, properties, lexemes, forms, senses, and statements) Wave 1 covers reads only. They need a bot account. An account and a decision to support writes. Batches above 50 ids on wbgetentities The API answers toomanyvalues above 50 ids, and the client chunks at 50. The higher limit needs an approved bot flag. Several entities per Special:EntityData request The route serves one entity per request. The service adding a multi-id JSON route. Per-form and per-sense REST routes The lexeme REST API has no route for a single form or sense (404 on 2026-11-28). The lexeme payload carries its forms and senses. The lexeme REST API adding the routes. SPARQL UPDATE The query service is read-only. Nothing on our side. The service has no update endpoint. Linked-data endpoint of the query service (/bigdata/ld/...) The endpoint is gone (404 on 2026-11-28). Nothing on our side. Wikibase submodules of the MediaWiki query API (meta=wbcontentlanguages, list=wblistentityusage, prop=wbentityusage, list=wbsubscribers, prop=pageterms, list=wbsearch) They describe wiki pages and the use of entities on other wikis, not the entities themselves, and list=wbsearch repeats wbsearchentities (checked 2026-11-28). client.request("GET", "w/api.php", params=...) reaches them today. A caller that needs typed results for one of them.

docs.title: DOAJ (diurnalia)
docs.text: Item Why it is deferred Unblocked by Applications search (GET /api/v4/search/applications/{query}) The route answers 401 without an admin key (verified 2026-11-27). A DOAJ admin key in .env. Write routes (POST /api/articles, PUT and DELETE on /api/articles/{id} and /api/journals/{id}, POST /api/applications, and GET, PUT, DELETE on /api/applications/{id}) Wave 1 covers reads only. They need an admin key. A DOAJ admin key and a decision to support writes. Bulk upload routes (POST and DELETE on /api/bulk/articles, GET /api/bulk/articles/{upload_id}, and POST and DELETE on /api/bulk/applications) They manage article uploads by publishers and need a publisher key. A DOAJ publisher account. Download of the full journal and article data dumps DOAJ grants access to the dumps case by case, and the dump routes answer 401 without it (verified 2026-11-28). The public journal CSV export is wrapped by journals.download_csv(). An access grant from DOAJ, then a dump loader like the ROR one.

docs.title: ISSN Portal (seriatim)
docs.text: Item Why it is deferred Unblocked by SRU Search API It is a paid service. /sru answers 404 without an account. A subscription and its API key. OAI-PMH access It is a paid service. /oai and oai.issn.org answer 404 without an account. A subscription. ISSN-H families (/resource/ISSN-H/{issn}) The page says they are reserved to subscribers (verified 2026-11-28). A subscription. /ltwa-export CSV export The route answers 502 with the page parameters (2026-11-27 and 2026-11-28). The HTML table is wrapped. The portal serving the export again. Search export and browse (/internal/search/export, /internal/browse) Both answer 404 without a session. A full-access account. ROAD record views and publishers.issn.org They answer HTML only and add no machine-readable read route. The ISSN Centre publishing machine-readable answers for them.

docs.title: arXiv (archeion)
docs.text: Item Why it is deferred Unblocked by OAI-PMH interface (https://oaipmh.arxiv.org/oai, formats arXiv, arXivRaw, and oai_dc) It is the bulk harvest route and answers XML with resumption tokens. The roadmap plans one shared OAI-PMH harvester in bibliofabric for arXiv, EarthArXiv, and repositories; zenotheca has its own OAI-PMH client today. The shared harvester, then an oai resource on archeion. RSS and Atom announcement feeds (https://rss.arxiv.org/rss/{category}) They list the daily announcements, which the query API returns too with sortBy=submittedDate. A caller that needs the announcement order of one day. Bulk data on Amazon S3 (PDF and source tarballs) The buckets are requester-pays and need AWS credentials. An AWS account and a decision to ship a loader.

docs.title: bioRxiv and medRxiv (prodromus)
docs.text: Item Why it is deferred Unblocked by The XML (OAI-PMH style) and HTML formats of details and funder, and the CSV downloads of pub, sum, and usage They carry the same records as the JSON format the client reads. A caller that needs one of these formats. Full text (the jatsxml URL of each version) It is a download per preprint, not an API route. Preprint.jatsxml holds the URL. A decision to wrap the download, as europaea does for Europe PMC. The reports pages (https://api.biorxiv.org/reports) They are HTML pages for people. A machine-readable form of the reports.

docs.title: Wave 1 Client Specs & Core Enablers
docs.text:
This guide provides the starter specifications that the 11 Wave 1 client libraries were built from, the 6 targeted bibliofabric core additions, and the 2 extensions to existing clients that were planned with them.

For the step-by-step recipe to scaffold, type-check, generate sync twins, and test any client package in this workspace, see Building a client on bibliofabric.

Status on 2026-11-28: all eleven libraries are built under their final names (see Wave 1 libraries). These specs were the starting point. Where the live API differs from a spec, the client follows the live API, and the upstream-quirks page of the package records the difference. Corrections carry the date on which they were verified.

docs.title: bibliofabric Core Enablers
docs.text:
bibliofabric 0.8 already provides retry=bool, _fetch_batch_chunk(), page_size_param: str | None, max_offset, per-instance dialect=, BasicAuth, ClientCredentialsAuth(token_auth_method="post"), RefreshTokenAuth, automatic 401 token refresh, on_response(), stream(), follow_redirects, connect_timeout, and cached TypeAdapter(list[E]) validation.

Six lightweight, backwards-compatible core additions unlock Wave 2 without per-client workarounds. Two of them are in bibliofabric 0.8: the default_headers property of BaseApiClient (addition 1) and JsonApiUnwrapper (the JSON:API part of addition 2), together with five of the identifier normalizers (ISBN, ISNI, Wikidata, GND, and VIAF from addition 6). The deferred list has the rest with the reason for each:

  1. Default per-client Accept / static headers: Add an optional default_headers: Mapping[str, str] | None parameter (or Accept default on BaseApiSettings/BaseApiClient) merged into owned and caller-supplied requests unless overridden per call.
  2. Unlocks: ORCID (Accept: application/vnd.orcid+json), UKRI GtR (Accept: application/vnd.rcuk.gtr.json-v7), GLEIF (Accept: application/vnd.api+json), DOI Content Negotiation (Accept: application/vnd.citationstyles.csl+json).
  3. Header-aware ResponseUnwrapper & RFC 5988 Link parser: Allow ResponseUnwrapper.next_cursor() (or an optional companion method) to read httpx.Headers, and ship a small parse_link_header() helper plus a reusable JSON:API unwrapper mixin (data[].attributes + links.next).
  4. Unlocks: Software Heritage (Link: <...>; rel="next"), DataCite REST, OSF v2, Zenodo links.next, GLEIF LEI, and ARC NCGP.
  5. POST-body search & pagination dialect: Allow ResourceClient subclasses to declare search_method = "POST" with a build_search_body() hook that places filters, page size, and offset/cursor in the JSON request body instead of query parameters (with retry=True for read-only search POSTs).
  6. Unlocks: NIH RePORTER v2, Figshare /articles/search, ETER v4, CORE v3 POST search, Lens.org, and SPARQL endpoints.
  7. Fixed / sliding-window rate limiter & daily quota hooks: Extend Limiter alongside req/s spacing to enforce explicit (max_requests, window_seconds) caps and optional daily budget/quota callbacks.
  8. Unlocks: LoC (20 req/min to prevent 1h–72h IP bans), GLEIF (60 req/min), ROR (2,000 / 5 min), DataCite (500–3,000 / 5 min), ORCID (25k–100k / day), NASA ADS (5,000 / day).
  9. Pluggable non-JSON decoder hook: Generalize BaseApiClient.parse_json() with a pluggable decoder hook (parse_response(response) defaulting to JSON) for XML, Atom 1.0, OAI-PMH, SRU, ANVL, and BibTeX/plain text.
  10. Unlocks: arXiv Atom XML, PubMed efetch, re3data, VIAF/LoC SRU, DOI BibTeX ConNeg, ARK/N2T, and generic OAI-PMH harvesting.
  11. Expanded bibliofabric.ids normalizers: Add canonical normalizers and check-digit validators alongside existing normalize_doi, normalize_orcid, normalize_ror, and normalize_issn:
  12. normalize_isbn (ISBN-10 ↔ ISBN-13 + check digits)
  13. normalize_isni, normalize_lei, normalize_wikidata_qid
  14. normalize_gnd, normalize_viaf, normalize_ark
  15. normalize_raid, normalize_swhid, normalize_spdx

docs.title: Immediate Extensions to Existing Clients
docs.text:
Before starting new packages, two high-value additions belong in existing packages:

  • stavrophora (Crossref):
  • Add a resource client for the Crossref Data Citation API (/beta/datacitations/ → GA late 2026), replacing the sunset Event Data API.
  • Add typed helpers for Retraction Watch records embedded in Crossref /works (updated-by / update-type:retraction with source: retraction-watch).
  • aletheca (OpenAlex):
  • Document and optionally surface OpenAlex credit/budget headers (X-RateLimit-Credits-Used, cost_usd) via BaseApiClient.on_response() alongside existing daily_budget 429 retry vetoing.

Status on 2026-11-28: all three are done. The Data Citation API is still beta upstream (/beta/datacitations, its own pool at 3 requests per second), so stavrophora labels client.data_citations as beta.

docs.title: 1. ROR v2 (Organizations & Funders)
docs.text:
• Base URL: https://api.ror.org/v2 (primary path: organizations)
  • Auth: NoAuth() by default; optional HeaderAuth("Client-Id", ...) for the registered 2,000 req / 5 min tier.
  • QueryDialect: page_param="page", page_start=1, page_size_param=None (fixed 20/page), max_page_size=20, default_page_size=20, max_offset=9980, query_param="query", sort_param=None, select_param=None.
  • ResponseUnwrapper: results -> body["items"], total -> body["number_of_results"], item -> body, next_cursor -> None, meta -> body["meta"].
  • Batching & Rate Limits: No native multi-ID batch endpoint; use bounded concurrent get() or the Zenodo dump. Verified 2026-11-27: ROR publishes no limit for anonymous callers and has paused registration, so the client sends no client identification.
  • License: CC0 1.0 (API and Zenodo data dumps).
  • Upstream Quirks:
  • API/schema v1 was sunset in late 2025; target v2.1 fields (names, locations, domains, external_ids incl. fundref).
  • Expose a dedicated match_affiliation(affiliation: str) method using ?affiliation=... (mid-2026 default single_search), trusting entries with chosen: true.
  • Provide an optional Zenodo JSON dump loader (~115k records) for offline <1 ms lookups and legacy Crossref Funder ID (10.13039/...) → ROR crosswalks.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: the dump holds about 152,000 records. A rejected request (unknown filter key, page above 500, malformed query.advanced) answers HTTP 200 with an errors body. query and query.advanced cannot be combined. The keyword search does not find an ISNI, so the external-id lookup goes through external_ids.all in query.advanced.

docs.title: 2. ORCID API v3.0 (Researchers)
docs.text:
• Base URL: https://pub.orcid.org/v3.0 (Public) or https://api.orcid.org/v3.0 (Member)
  • Auth: NoAuth() for anonymous public reads, or ClientCredentialsAuth(client_id, client_secret, "https://orcid.org/oauth/token", scope="/read-public", token_auth_method="post") for Public/Member clients.
  • QueryDialect: Search (/expanded-search or /search): offset_param="start", page_size_param="rows", max_page_size=200, default_page_size=25, max_offset=10_000, query_param="q", page_param=None, sort_param=None.
  • ResponseUnwrapper: Search returns body["expanded-result"] (or body["result"]) and total -> body["num-found"]; single profile sub-routes (/{orcid}/record, /works, /employments, /educations, /external-identifiers) return item -> body.
  • Batching & Rate Limits: No multi-ID batch GET. 12 req/s public (24 req/s member), burst 40/s returns 503; daily caps 25k/day anon, 100k/day Public Client, unlimited Member.
  • License: ORCID Public API Terms (non-commercial restriction on Public API); annual public data file is CC0. Tag accordingly in fusion policies.
  • Upstream Quirks:
  • Requires Accept: application/vnd.orcid+json (default is XML; relies on core Enabler #1 or explicit per-request headers until landed).
  • JSON preserves XML-derived {"value": "..."} wrapper dicts throughout; normalize cleanly inside Pydantic field validators.
  • Normalize IDs with bibliofabric.ids.normalize_orcid.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: Accept: application/json and application/vnd.orcid+json both answer JSON, and application/ld+json answers 406. The client sends application/json on every request.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: /expanded-search/ answers {"expanded-result": [...], "num-found": N} and /search/ answers {"result": [...], "num-found": N}. rows=1000 answers HTTP 500, as does an unknown field name in q, so the client caps rows at 100.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: /{orcid}/biography and /{orcid}/emails answer 404 with error code 9041 when the record has none, and an unused activities section answered 404 in one run and 200 with an empty group in another. Every section reader maps 404 to None.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: the member API token on hand was rejected with 403 on api.orcid.org, so the client is not built for the member API and does not mint tokens. It sends an optional ORCHIS_ACCESS_TOKEN as a bearer header. The member read routes have the same paths as the public ones.

docs.title: 3. DataCite REST API (Datasets, Software, Preprints & PID Graph)
docs.text:
• Base URL: https://api.datacite.org (paths: dois, clients, providers, prefixes, events; optional GraphQL at /graphql)
  • Auth: NoAuth() for public read (send descriptive User-Agent / mailto for identified tier); BasicAuth(repository_id, password) for Member writes/drafts.
  • QueryDialect: page_size_param="page[size]", max_page_size=1000, default_page_size=25, page_param="page[number]", max_offset=10_000, cursor_param="page[cursor]", cursor_start="1", query_param="query", sort_param="sort", select_param=None.
  • ResponseUnwrapper: JSON:API envelope: results -> body["data"], item -> body["data"], total -> body["meta"]["total"], next_cursor -> extract page[cursor] query param from body.get("links", {}).get("next"), meta -> body.get("meta", {}).
  • Batching & Rate Limits: Verified 2026-11-27: filters take one parameter per criterion, and a comma list inside one filter means OR. Rate: 500 unid / 1,000 identified / 3,000 member per 5 min per IP; the API sends no rate-limit headers. The client defaults to 1.5 requests per second.
  • License: CC0 1.0.
  • Upstream Quirks:
  • Deep pagination past 10,000 records requires page[cursor]=1 on the first request (not *) and following links.next.
  • Normalize DOIs with normalize_doi; preserve relatedIdentifiers and version fields for dataset/software lineage.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: page[size] accepts 1 to 1000 (1001 is cut to 1000); numbered paging stops at 10,000 records with a 400; a cursor walk always orders by created ascending, whatever sort says; sort accepts relevance, name, created, updated, published, view-count, download-count, citation-count, and title (a - prefix reverses it); date filters take years; fields[dois] silently drops resourceTypeGeneral. /dois/{id}/media, /views, /downloads, and /url answer 404 without a login, and /prefixes/totals answers 204.

docs.title: 4. Semantic Scholar (Graph, Bulk Search & Batch)
docs.text:
• Base URL: https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1 (plus optional /recommendations/v1, /datasets/v1)
  • Auth: HeaderAuth("x-api-key", api_key) strongly recommended (anonymous pool suffers frequent 429 throttling).
  • QueryDialect:
  • Standard search (/paper/search): offset_param="offset", page_size_param="limit", max_page_size=100, default_page_size=25, max_offset=1_000, query_param="query", select_param="fields", page_param=None, sort_param=None.
  • Bulk search (/paper/search/bulk, via per-instance dialect=): cursor_param="token", cursor_start=None, page_size_param=None (fixed 1,000/page), query_param="query", select_param="fields", sort_param="sort".
  • ResponseUnwrapper: results -> body["data"], item -> body, total -> body.get("total"), next_cursor -> body.get("token"), meta -> remaining keys.
  • Batching & Rate Limits: Override _fetch_batch_chunk() to call POST /paper/batch (up to 500 IDs per chunk, json={"ids": chunk}, params={"fields": ...}, retry=True) and POST /author/batch. Intro API key: 1 req/s (max_requests_per_second=1.0).
  • License: ODC-By 1.0 (datasets/corpus); AI2 API License (attribution required; SPECTER2 embeddings Apache 2.0).
  • Upstream Quirks:
  • Accepts prefixed IDs (DOI:..., ARXIV:..., PMID:..., CorpusId:..., or bare 40-char S2 paper ID); preserve prefix during normalize_id() and match back in record_keys().
  • POST /paper/batch returns null entries in the JSON array for missing IDs; filter None items inside _fetch_batch_chunk().
  • Always specify select= (fields=) explicitly; default response is minimal (paperId, title).
  • Verified 2026-11-27: the API key on hand answers HTTP 403, so the client was built and tested without a key. Without a key, /paper/search, /paper/search/match, /snippet/search, the URL: and PubMedCentral: id forms, and the patent search routes answered 429 during the whole study. The client wraps them from the published specification, and the docs page lists them as unverified.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: POST /paper/batch and POST /author/batch take a bare JSON array of ids and answer a bare array with null in the place of an unknown id. fields is a query parameter on both. The client sends at most 500 ids per paper call and 1000 ids per author call.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: fields=openAccessDoi and fields=embedding answer 400 without a key, and a dataset file listing answers 401 without a key. /paper/autocomplete answers {"matches": [...]}, and GET /dataset/releases answers a plain array of release ids.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: the published limits are 1000 requests per second for the shared anonymous pool and 1 request per second for an introductory key. The pool is contended, so the client defaults to 1 request per second and concurrency 1.

docs.title: 5. DOAJ API v4 (Gold & Diamond OA Journals)
docs.text:
• Base URL: https://doaj.org/api/v4 (paths: search/journals/{query}, search/articles/{query}, journals/{id}, articles/{id}; verified 2026-11-27 that journals and articles have no list route)
  • Auth: NoAuth() for public read/search.
  • QueryDialect: page_param="page", page_start=1, page_size_param="pageSize", max_page_size=50, default_page_size=10, sort_param="sort", query_param=None (search query is embedded in the path).
  • ResponseUnwrapper: results -> body["results"], item -> body, total -> body.get("total"), next_cursor -> None, meta -> envelope minus results.
  • Batching & Rate Limits: Batch ISSN lookups via Lucene OR query (issn:1234-5678 OR issn:8765-4321) in /search/journals/{query}. Rate: ~2 req/s (max_requests_per_second=1.5 conservative default). Verified 2026-11-27: pageSize above 50 is cut to 50 and the default is 10.
  • License: CC0 1.0.
  • Upstream Quirks:
  • API v1–v3 are deprecated; always target /api/v4/.
  • Search encodes the Lucene query as a URL-encoded path segment (/search/journals/{query}); handle via a resource method or path-building override.
  • Capture bibjson.apc, bibjson.license, bibjson.preservation, bibjson.editorial.review_process, and bibjson.seal for canonical Venue records.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: /api/search/... and /api/v4/search/... answer the same envelope. The client wraps v4.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: the API answers 400 beyond the first 1000 records of a query, because (page - 1) * pageSize + pageSize must be at most 1000. page=0 is treated as page 1.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: wildcards answer 400. AND, OR, ANDNOT, quoted phrases, and ranges work. A license filter needs the stored spelling, such as license:"CC BY".
  • Verified 2026-11-27: an unknown DOI answers 200 with total of 0. The client raises NotFoundError on an empty envelope.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: the documentation states a limit of 2 requests per second with bursts of five. The client defaults to 1 request per second.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: GET /api/journals/{id} and GET /api/articles/{id} answer 200 without a key for a DOAJ record id, with more fields than a search result (es_type, last_manual_update, and a fuller admin section).

docs.title: 6. OpenCitations (Index v2 + Meta v1)
docs.text:
• Base URL: https://api.opencitations.net/index/v2 and https://api.opencitations.net/meta/v1
  • Auth: NoAuth(). The optional OpenCitations Access Token is not in the client yet (see the deferred list).
  • QueryDialect: Unpaged dialect: page_size_param=None, page_param=None, offset_param=None, cursor_param=None, sort_param=None, query_param=None, select_param=None.
  • ResponseUnwrapper: Endpoints return a top-level JSON list[dict]: results -> body, item -> body[0] (raising NotFoundError when empty), total -> len(body), next_cursor -> None, meta -> {}.
  • Batching & Rate Limits: Verified 2026-11-27: the Meta API accepts __-delimited ids (/metadata/doi:a__doi:b, one row per id); the Index API answers [] for a multi-id path, so it takes one id per request. Rate: 180 req/min/IP documented; the client defaults to 3 requests per second.
  • License: CC0 1.0.
  • Upstream Quirks:
  • Legacy COCI, POCI, and /index/v1 are deprecated/archived; target only /index/v2 and /meta/v1.
  • Missing IDs return HTTP 200 with an empty JSON list [] rather than 404; map empty responses cleanly in get() / unwrapper.item().
  • Index v2 exposes oci, citing, cited, creation, timespan, journal_sc, and author_sc (self-citation flags).
  • Verified 2026-11-27: Index v2 has six operations (/citation/{oci}, /citations/{id}, /references/{id}, /citation-count/{id}, /reference-count/{id}, /venue-citation-count/{issn}), and Meta v1 has three (/metadata/{ids}, /author/{id}, /editor/{id}). The rows accept require, filter, sort, and format=csv (the Accept header alone does not switch the format). Counts arrive as strings.

docs.title: 7. Europe PMC (Articles, Preprints, Citations & Annotations)
docs.text:
• Base URL: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest (plus https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/annotations_api)
  • Auth: NoAuth().
  • QueryDialect: Search (/search): cursor_param="cursorMark", cursor_start="*", page_size_param="pageSize", max_page_size=1000, default_page_size=25, iterate_page_size=1000, query_param="query", sort_param="sort", page_param=None, select_param=None (use resultType="core" or "lite").
  • ResponseUnwrapper: results -> body["resultList"]["result"], total -> body["hitCount"], next_cursor -> body.get("nextCursorMark"), meta -> request, version.
  • Batching & Rate Limits: Batch PMIDs/DOIs via Lucene OR query (EXT_ID:12345 OR EXT_ID:67890) in /search; annotations API batches 1–8 article IDs per request. No hard key cap; polite ~5–10 req/s.
  • License: Open metadata; full-text reuse governed by explicit per-article CC license field.
  • Upstream Quirks:
  • Always pass format=json (XML is the default otherwise!).
  • cursorMark echoes the current cursor when exhausted — already handled automatically by ResourceClient._iterate_cursor().
  • Pass resultType="core" to retrieve full abstracts, grants, MeSH headings, and full-text URLs (lite omits them).
  • Verified 2026-11-27: pageSize accepts at most 1000, and a larger value answers 404. nextCursorMark repeats unchanged when the list is exhausted. A search can take about ten seconds and answers transient 503 errors, which the client retries.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: the data links route is /{source}/{id}/datalinks in lower case, and dataLinks answers 404. The routes comments, correctionsAndErratum, and textMinedTerms answer 404 and are absent from the OpenAPI document. Comments and corrections are part of the core record, and text-mined terms moved to the annotations API.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: fullTextXML and supplementaryFiles take a bare id such as PMC13810549. They answer 406 to Accept: application/json and need application/xml. bookXML answers 200 with a message element for a book without open access XML.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: the grants API is the Grist API at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/GristAPI/rest/get/query=<q>&format=json&page=N. The parameters must follow & and not ?, because ? makes the route answer 406 to a JSON Accept header. HitCount is a JSON string.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: the annotations API has five routes. Four of them page with a float cursorMark and signal exhaustion with a nextCursorMark of -1.0. annotationsBySectionAndOrType without a filter returns about 24 MB.

docs.title: 8. Zenodo / InvenioRDM (Datasets & Software Releases)
docs.text:
• Base URL: https://zenodo.org/api (generalizable to any InvenioRDM instance by swapping base_url)
  • Auth: NoAuth() for public read (mandatory User-Agent, otherwise 403); optional StaticTokenAuth(token) for higher page size (100 vs 25) and private/deposit access.
  • QueryDialect: Use per-instance dialect= based on auth presence: page_param="page", page_start=1, page_size_param="size", max_page_size=25 (unauth) or 100 (auth), default_page_size=25, and page * size at most 10,000 (Elasticsearch max_result_window, verified 2026-11-27), query_param="q", sort_param="sort".
  • ResponseUnwrapper: results -> body["hits"]["hits"], item -> body, total -> body["hits"]["total"], next_cursor -> None (or links.next), meta -> {"aggregations": body.get("aggregations", {})}.
  • Batching & Rate Limits: Batch concept/version DOIs with an OR clause in q, which uses the Elasticsearch query-string syntax. Rate: verified 2026-11-27, about 78 requests at 2 per second met no limit and the API sent no rate-limit headers. The client defaults to 2 requests per second.
  • License: Metadata CC0; record files per declared SPDX license (default CC-BY 4.0).
  • Upstream Quirks:
  • Always distinguish conceptdoi (all versions) vs. doi (specific version) and preserve files[].checksum (md5:...).
  • Use BaseApiClient.stream() for downloading dataset/software archives so auth, throttling, and typed errors apply automatically.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: the API serves the legacy record schema (recid, conceptrecid, metadata), not the InvenioRDM schema that the documentation describes. A concept id answers 302 to the newest version, mostrecent orders by last update, and all_versions=true returns every version instead of one record per concept.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: /api/vocabularies/{vocabulary} serves the resourcetypes, licenses, languages, communitytypes, funders, and affiliations vocabularies in a hits envelope; /api/communities/{id}/subcommunities answers the RDM-shaped hits envelope; and https://zenodo.org/oai2d answers all six OAI-PMH verbs (a ListRecords call without a match answers 422 with noRecordsMatch).

docs.title: 9. DOI RA / Content Negotiation + ISSN Portal ConNeg
docs.text:
Two small lookup clients: hodoi for the DOI proxy at doi.org and seriatim for the ISSN Portal.

  • Base URLs:
  • https://doi.org/ra/{doi1},{doi2} — batch DOI Registration Agency lookup (returns JSON list of {"DOI": ..., "RA": "Crossref" | "DataCite" | ...}).
  • https://doi.org/api/handles/{doi} — raw Handle.net JSON record.
  • https://doi.org/{doi} — HTTP Content Negotiation with follow_redirects=True and Accept: application/vnd.citationstyles.csl+json (or application/vnd.schemaorg.ld+json, application/x-bibtex).
  • Verified 2026-11-27: Crossref answers CSL JSON, Unixref XML, BibTeX, and RIS, and answers 406 for schema.org JSON-LD and DataCite JSON; DataCite answers all of them; mEDRA answers CSL JSON, BibTeX, and RIS. The client keeps the catalog in hodoi.media_types.
  • https://portal.issn.org/resource/ISSN/{issn} with Accept: application/ld+json — JSON-LD lookup. Verified 2026-11-27: without that Accept header ?format=json answers with HTML, and the JSON-LD is a single node.
  • Auth: NoAuth().
  • Batching & Rate Limits: /ra/{doi1},{doi2} accepted a list of 200 DOIs and answered 414 for 500 (verified 2026-11-27), so the client chunks at 100. /doiRA/ serves the same route. doi.org publishes no limit; the client defaults to 2 requests per second. ISSN Portal free ConNeg is individual lookup only (polite pacing, aggressive local caching).
  • License: Open resolution infrastructure; individual DOI metadata license follows its Registration Agency; ISSN Portal free ConNeg is non-bulk.
  • Upstream Quirks:
  • doi.org redirects content negotiation to the data server of the registration agency (Crossref api.crossref.org/v1/works/{doi}/transform, DataCite data.crosscite.org/{doi}). The Accept header survives the redirect. The client follows redirects on the content request only, so that a caller can still read the 302.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: without an Accept header the proxy redirects to the landing page; HEAD answers 302 with the same Location; the Handle REST API accepts index, type, auth, and recursive; the old Handbook URL for resolution now redirects to a landing page, and the current reference is the DOI resolution documentation that the package cites.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: the ISSN Portal JSON-LD is one node per resource, not a @graph array as this spec assumed.
  • Verified 2026-11-27: the ISSN Portal answers JSON-LD for /resource/ISSN/{issn} and /resource/ISSN-L/{issn} only. The free search (/search) and the Title Word Abbreviation list (/ltwa) are HTML pages, which the client reads with the standard library parser. The portal has no SPARQL endpoint. The SRU Search API, OAI-PMH access, and the ISSN-H families need a paid subscription.

docs.title: 10. Wikidata (Universal PID Crosswalk Hub)
docs.text:
• Base URLs:
  • REST API v1: https://www.wikidata.org/w/rest.php/wikibase/v1
  • Action API (batch): https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php
  • Optional SPARQL: https://query.wikidata.org/sparql
  • Auth: NoAuth() (optional OAuth2). Descriptive User-Agent with contact URL/email is strictly mandatory (BaseApiSettings.mailto handles this cleanly; generic user agents receive immediate 429).
  • QueryDialect: Action wbsearchentities: offset_param="continue", page_size_param="limit", max_page_size=50, default_page_size=25, query_param="search", page_param=None, sort_param=None.
  • ResponseUnwrapper: Action wbgetentities returns a dict keyed by QID (body["entities"]); convert list(body["entities"].values()) (filtering "missing" in item) in results().
  • Batching & Rate Limits: Override _fetch_batch_chunk() to call Action wbgetentities with ids=Q1|Q2|... (up to 50 QIDs per request). Honor Retry-After; keep SPARQL queries under the 60s timeout and ≤5 concurrent.
  • License: CC0 1.0.
  • Upstream Quirks:
  • Extract external IDs from well-known properties (P496 ORCID, P6782 ROR, P213 ISNI, P214 VIAF, P227 GND, P244 LCCN, P269 IdRef, P1278 LEI, P236 ISSN, P356 DOI, P6179 / P10283 OpenAlex).
  • Cache entity responses aggressively with ETag / If-None-Match when revalidating crosswalks.
  • Verified 2026-11-27 and 2026-11-28: the Action API answers every error with HTTP 200 and an error object, and wbgetentities takes at most 50 ids. wbsearchentities reports no total. Special:EntityData/{id}.{format} serves one entity as json, jsonld, rdf, nt, ttl, or n3, and https://www.wikidata.org/entity/{id} redirects to it. The REST API adds /search/*, /suggest/*, and /statements/*. The lexeme routes live under /w/rest.php/wikibaselexeme/v0, and the linked-data endpoint of the query service is gone. The client wraps all of these read routes.

docs.title: Wave 1 libraries
docs.text:
Wave 1 adds eleven single-source client libraries to the three existing ones. Each library covers every public read endpoint of its upstream API and models every field the API returns. Write endpoints are out of scope for this wave. The deferred list records what was left out and why.

The libraries are not yet published on PyPI. The release section lists what each first release needs.

docs.title: Roster
docs.text: Library Package Covers Upstream docs ROR rorifer Organization records, search, filters, affiliation matching, registry dumps on Zenodo REST API Zenodo zenotheca Record search, record versions, files and downloads, communities, vocabularies, OAI-PMH harvesting REST API DataCite dataphora DOIs, activities, clients, providers, repositories, prefixes, events, GraphQL queries REST API OpenCitations opcitato Citation links, references, citation counts, and metadata API documentation DOI RA and content negotiation hodoi Registration agency lookup, metadata by media type, handle records DOI resolution documentation Semantic Scholar scholiast Papers, authors, citations, references, search, batch lookup, recommendations, patents, snippets, and dataset releases API docs ORCID orchis Researcher records, person sections, activities, and both public search routes Public API guide Europe PMC europaea Literature search, article records, full text, references, citations, data links, evaluations, annotations, grants, profiles, and preprints Web services Wikidata quiddita Entities, claims, sitelinks, lexemes, search, entity data in RDF formats, utility modules, and SPARQL Action API DOAJ diurnalia Journal and article search, journal and article records API v4 docs ISSN Portal seriatim ISSN and ISSN-L records as JSON-LD, the free search, and the Title Word Abbreviation list ISSN Portal

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
The names follow the existing family. aireloom weaves OpenAIRE, aletheca is a library of truth for OpenAlex, and stavrophora is Greek for "cross bearer", after Crossref. Each Wave 1 name is a Latin or Greek word that points at its source.

Package Origin rorifer Latin for "dew bearing" (ros, roris), and it starts with ROR. zenotheca Zeno plus theca (library). Zenodo is named after Zenodotus, the first librarian of Alexandria. dataphora "Data bearer", the DataCite counterpart of stavrophora. opcitato From opere citato ("in the work cited"), the "op. cit." of footnotes. hodoi Greek for "roads" or "ways". The client routes a DOI to its registration agency, and the word contains "doi". scholiast A scholar who writes scholia, the notes in the margins of a text. orchis The Greek and botanical name of the orchid, after ORCID. europaea Latin for "European", after Europe PMC. quiddita From quidditas ("whatness"), for the Q identifiers of Wikidata. diurnalia Latin for daily records, the root of "journal", after the Directory of Open Access Journals. seriatim Latin for "one after another", for serials and their ISSNs.

Each name has three spellings: the distribution and import name (rorifer), the prefix of the settings environment variables (RORIFER_MAX_CONCURRENCY), and the prefix of the class names (RoriferClient).

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
1. Register a pending trusted publisher on PyPI for each name: owner utsmok, repository bibliofabric, workflow ci.yml, environment pypi. The publish job reads the package name from the tag <name>-v<version>, so the workflow needs no change.
  2. Tag each Wave 1 library as <name>-v0.1.0, following the release flow in the root AGENTS.md. Every library requires bibliofabric>=0.8,<0.9; bibliofabric 0.8.0 is on PyPI since 2026-11-28.

docs.title: rorifer
docs.text:
rorifer is not yet published on PyPI. Until the first release, use it from a checkout of the bibliofabric workspace, where uv sync --all-packages installs it together with the bibliofabric 0.8 it needs.

rorifer is a Python client for the ROR API v2, built on bibliofabric. It types the organizations endpoint with Pydantic models, serializes the ROR filter syntax for you, and reads the registry dumps that ROR publishes on Zenodo. It ships an async client and a generated sync twin with the same API. The API needs no credentials.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv sync --all-packages

The command runs in a checkout of the bibliofabric workspace and installs rorifer with the bibliofabric 0.8 it needs. uv add rorifer works once the package is on PyPI. Requires Python 3.12 or newer.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import asyncio
from rorifer import RoriferClient


async def main():
    async with RoriferClient() as client:
        org = await client.organizations.get("006hf6230")
        print(org.display_name, org.status)

        page = await client.organizations.search(query="university of twente")
        print(page.total, [org.display_name for org in page.results])

        chosen = [
            match.organization
            for match in await client.organizations.match_affiliation(
                "University of Twente, Enschede, Netherlands"
            )
            if match.chosen
        ]
        print(chosen[0].id)


asyncio.run(main())

client.organizations exposes get(), exists(), search(), iterate(), collect(), first(), and count(), plus match_affiliation(), find_by_external_id(), and find_by_funder_doi(). client.dumps lists the registry dumps on Zenodo and downloads one.

docs.title: Sync usage
docs.text:
RoriferSyncClient is generated from the async source and behaves the same. The sync client uses plain httpx.Client and never starts or touches an event loop, so it works in scripts, in Jupyter, in threads, and when called from inside a running event loop.

from rorifer import RoriferSyncClient

with RoriferSyncClient() as client:
    org = client.organizations.get("https://ror.org/006hf6230")
    print(org.display_name)

    for org in client.organizations.iterate(
        {"types": ["education", "nonprofit"], "country.country_code": "NL"}, limit=200
    ):
        print(org.id, org.established)

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: RoriferSettings loads from environment variables prefixed with RORIFER_ and from a .env file in the working directory. RORIFER_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND (default 6) and RORIFER_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 5) set the request pace. Requests to Zenodo, which lists the data dumps, run in their own rate class: RORIFER_RATE_LIMITS is a JSON object of requests per second per class and defaults to {"zenodo": 0.5}, because the anonymous Zenodo search accepts 30 requests per minute. A RORIFER_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND that you set applies to every class, unless you also set RORIFER_RATE_LIMITS. The shared fields of bibliofabric.config.BaseApiSettings also apply, such as RORIFER_TIMEOUT, RORIFER_MAX_RETRIES, RORIFER_MAX_RETRY_WAIT, and RORIFER_USER_AGENT.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Organizations covers records, search, filters, affiliation matching, and the identifier lookup.
  • Data dumps covers the Zenodo dumps and how to read all 150,000 records.
  • Upstream quirks lists what the live API does differently from its documentation.
  • The API reference is generated from the source.

docs.title: Data dumps
docs.text: ROR publishes a dump of the whole registry with every release, in the ror-data community on Zenodo. The dump of 2026-11-19 (v2.16) holds 152,297 records in a 40.9 MB zip file. Use it when you need every record, because the API reaches at most 10,000 records per query.

docs.title: List, pick, and download
docs.text:
dumps = await client.dumps.list(limit=5)
for dump in dumps:
    print(dump.publication_date, dump.version, dump.zip_url)

latest = await client.dumps.latest()
path = await client.dumps.download(latest, "ror-data.zip")

list() reads the Zenodo search API with all_versions=true, so every ROR release is one RorDump record. Without that parameter, Zenodo answers a release series with its newest version only. The records come ordered by last update, 25 per page, which is the largest page for callers without a Zenodo account. limit (default 5) caps the number of records; list() stops when the releases run out.

latest() reads the Zenodo concept record of the dumps (6347574). Zenodo redirects that record to the newest release, so the answer is the newest release and not the record that was last updated.

download() streams the zip to disk, creates missing parent directories, and returns the path. A dump record also exposes record_id, concept_id, doi, metadata, files, and links.

The anonymous Zenodo search accepts 30 requests per minute. The client paces its Zenodo requests to one every 2 seconds (see RORIFER_RATE_LIMITS), so list() with a large limit takes a while.

docs.title: Read the records
docs.text:
from rorifer import iter_dump_records

for org in iter_dump_records(path):
    print(org.id, org.display_name)

iter_dump_records() reads the JSON member of the zip one record at a time and yields Organization models, the same models as client.organizations.get(). It never loads the whole file. On a 2026 test machine, parsing and validating the full dump took 14 seconds. The function raises ConfigurationError when the zip has no .json member, when the member is not a JSON array, or when the member is truncated.

iter_dump_records() is a plain function, so the same call works with the sync client and without a client at all.

docs.title: Index by external id
docs.text:
from rorifer import index_external_ids, iter_dump_records

records = list(iter_dump_records(path))
fundref = index_external_ids(records, "fundref")
nsf = fundref["100000001"][0]

index_external_ids() groups records by every external_ids.all value of one scheme. Keys drop whitespace and lower case, so an ISNI matches in both spellings. The full dump yields about 30,000 FundRef ids. compact_external_id() returns one id in that key form.

docs.title: Crosswalk to Crossref funder DOIs
docs.text:
from rorifer import fundref_doi_from_id, fundref_id_from_doi

fundref_id_from_doi("https://doi.org/10.13039/100000001")  # "100000001"
fundref_doi_from_id("100000001")  # "10.13039/100000001"

Every Crossref Funder Registry DOI has the prefix 10.13039/ followed by the FundRef id. Both functions raise ValueError for input in any other form.

docs.title: Organizations
docs.text: client.organizations talks to /organizations and returns Organization models. Pages hold 20 records, and the API serves pages 1 to 500, so one query reaches at most 10,000 records. A query with more results raises ConfigurationError when page 501 would be needed. To read the whole registry, use a data dump.

docs.title: Get one record
docs.text:
org = await client.organizations.get("006hf6230")
org = await client.organizations.get("https://ror.org/006hf6230")  # same record
org = await client.organizations.get("ror.org/006hf6230")  # same record
found = await client.organizations.exists("006hf6230")

The bare ROR id, the record URL, and the form ror.org/006hf6230 work. get() returns records of every status, including inactive and withdrawn ones, and raises NotFoundError for an id that does not exist. exists() returns False for a missing record. It sends GET, because the ROR gateway answers HEAD with 403.

docs.title: The record model
docs.text:
Field Content id The record URL, such as https://ror.org/006hf6230 names Name entries with value, lang (which may be None), and types (ror_display, label, alias, acronym) display_name The ror_display name, else the first label, else the first name types Any of archive, company, education, facility, funder, government, healthcare, nonprofit, other status active, inactive, or withdrawn established The year as an integer domains Website domains links Link entries of type website or wikipedia, with the URL in value locations Location entries with geonames_id and geonames_details (continent, country, subdivision, lat, lng, name) external_ids ExternalId entries with type (grid, isni, wikidata, fundref), all, and preferred relationships Relationship entries with type (parent, child, related, successor, predecessor), the other record's id, and a label admin created and last_modified, each with date and schema_version

external_ids_of_type("fundref") returns every id of one scheme. Fields that ROR adds later are kept in model_extra.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
page = await client.organizations.search(query="university of twente")
page.total  # 132 on 2026-11-27
page.results  # up to 20 Organization records
page.meta  # facet counts: types, countries, continents, statuses

query is a keyword search over names and external ids. It finds a FundRef id (query=100000001) and a Wikidata id (query=Q1547084, in upper case), but it does not find an ISNI.

advanced takes an Elasticsearch query string for the query.advanced parameter, for example names.value:"University of Twente" or established:[1900 TO 2000]. ROR rejects a request that carries both query and advanced; the client raises ConfigurationError with ROR's message.

Only active records answer by default. Pass all_status=True to include inactive and withdrawn records.

page = await client.organizations.search(
    {"types": ["education", "nonprofit"], "country.country_code": "NL"},
    advanced="established:[1900 TO 2000]",
    all_status=True,
    page=2,
)

ROR has no sort, field selection, cursor, or page-size parameters. Passing sort=, select=, cursor=, or page_size= raises ConfigurationError without a request.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Filters travel in one filter parameter as key:value pairs. A list value repeats its key, which means OR, and different keys are joined with commas, which means AND. Pass a plain dict or the OrganizationFilters model. The model accepts the dot notation of the API (country.country_code) and the Python attribute name (country_country_code).

Key Matches status active, inactive, or withdrawn types One or more of the nine organization types country.country_code ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, such as NL country.country_name Country name in the spelling of ROR locations.geonames_details.country_code Country code of one location locations.geonames_details.country_name Country name of one location locations.geonames_details.continent_code Continent code, such as eu locations.geonames_details.continent_name Continent name, such as Europe

Any other key is a rejected request. The filter models allow extra fields, so a key that ROR adds later still works. Prefer the codes over the names, because a name must match the spelling of ROR exactly.

docs.title: Iterate and count
docs.text:
async for org in client.organizations.iterate(
    {"types": "education", "country.country_code": "NL"}, limit=1_000
):
    print(org.id)

total = await client.organizations.count(query="university of twente")

iterate() fetches page after page and stops at limit, at an empty page, or when number_of_results records were seen. A query with more than 10,000 results raises ConfigurationError at page 501; it does not stop with the first 10,000 records. count() returns number_of_results; ROR has no count-only route, so it fetches one page. collect() and first() accept the same arguments as iterate().

ROR warns that a paged query without a filter can repeat or skip records between pages. For a complete list, narrow the query with a filter or read a data dump.

docs.title: Affiliation matching
docs.text:
matches = await client.organizations.match_affiliation("Dept of Physics, MIT")
chosen = next(match.organization for match in matches if match.chosen)

ROR returns up to 10 AffiliationMatch candidates. Each carries the matched substring, a score from 0 to 1, a matching_type, and chosen, which is true for exactly one candidate. The full record is in organization.

docs.title: Identifier lookup and the funder crosswalk
docs.text:
from rorifer import fundref_id_from_doi

# By any external id, in any spelling the client knows
await client.organizations.find_by_external_id("0000000403998953", id_type="isni")

# By a Crossref Funder Registry DOI
nsf = await client.organizations.find_by_funder_doi("10.13039/100000001")
fundref_id_from_doi("10.13039/100000001")  # "100000001"

find_by_external_id() searches the stored spelling exactly, so it tries every spelling ROR may keep. An ISNI is searched in its grouped and its compact form, and a Wikidata id in lower and upper case. id_type restricts the result to one scheme (fundref, grid, isni, wikidata). The lookup includes inactive and withdrawn records. ROR cannot search a value that contains a double quote, a backslash, or a colon, so pass the bare id; anything else raises ConfigurationError.

find_by_funder_doi() runs the same lookup for a Crossref Funder Registry DOI. fundref_id_from_doi() and fundref_doi_from_id() convert between the DOI and the FundRef id.

Bases: BaseApiSettings

ROR-specific client settings.

Inherits timeout, max_retries, max_retry_wait, max_requests_per_second, max_concurrency, rate_limits, user_agent and mailto from :class:bibliofabric.config.BaseApiSettings and sets ROR defaults: 6 requests per second, concurrency 5, and a zenodo class at one request every 2 seconds for the data dump helper, because the anonymous Zenodo search accepts 30 requests per minute. The API needs no credentials.

docs.title: Resource clients
docs.text: Each resource client inherits the generic operations from bibliofabric.ResourceClient (get, search, iterate, collect, first, count) through rorifer._async.dialect.RoriferResourceClient. Only the members that ROR changes or adds are shown here.

docs.title: rorifer._async.organizations.OrganizationsClient
docs.text:
Bases: RoriferResourceClient[Organization]

Client for the /organizations endpoint.

Pages hold 20 records and the API serves pages 1 to 500, so one query reaches at most 10,000 records. For the whole registry, download a data dump through :attr:RoriferClient.dumps.

docs.title: search(filters=None, *, query=None, sort=None, select=None, page=None, page_size=None, cursor=None, on_error='raise', failures=None, params=None, advanced=None, all_status=False) async
docs.text:
Fetch one page of organizations as a typed :class:Page.

query is a keyword search over names and external ids; advanced is an Elasticsearch query-string over record fields (query.advanced, for example names.value:"University of Twente"). ROR rejects a request that carries both. all_status includes inactive and withdrawn records; by default only active records answer. :attr:Page.meta carries ROR's facet counts (types, countries, continents, statuses) and time_taken.

Raises:

Type Description ConfigurationError

page_size, sort, select, or cursor is set. ROR has no such parameter, so the client sends no request.

docs.title: iterate(filters=None, *, query=None, sort=None, select=None, page_size=None, limit=None, cursor=None, on_error='raise', failures=None, on_page=None, params=None, advanced=None, all_status=False)
docs.text:
Iterate over all matching organizations, page by page.

Accepts the same arguments as :meth:search. Iteration stops at limit, on an empty page, or when number_of_results records were seen. A query with more than 10,000 matches raises :class:~bibliofabric.exceptions.ConfigurationError when it asks for page 501, so pass a limit of at most 10,000 for broad queries.

Raises:

Type Description ConfigurationError

page_size, sort, select, or cursor is set. ROR has no such parameter, so the client sends no request.

docs.title: collect(filters=None, *, limit=None, query=None, sort=None, select=None, page_size=None, cursor=None, on_error='raise', failures=None, on_page=None, params=None, advanced=None, all_status=False) async
docs.text: Collect the output of :meth:iterate into a list, bounded by limit.

docs.title: first(filters=None, *, query=None, sort=None, select=None, page_size=None, cursor=None, on_error='raise', failures=None, params=None, advanced=None, all_status=False) async
docs.text:
Return the first matching organization, or None when there is none.

ROR fixes pages at 20 records, so the call reads one page and returns its first record. It accepts the same arguments as :meth:iterate except limit and on_page.

docs.title: count(filters=None, *, query=None, params=None, advanced=None, all_status=False) async
docs.text:
Return number_of_results of the query.

ROR has no count-only route, so this fetches one full page.

docs.title: match_affiliation(affiliation) async
docs.text:
Match a free-text affiliation string to organizations.

Runs ROR's affiliation matcher (?affiliation=) and returns up to 10 candidates, each with a score from 0 to 1; ROR marks one candidate chosen. The matched input is in substring.

docs.title: find_by_external_id(value, *, id_type=None) async
docs.text:
Return the organizations that carry value as an external id.

id_type restricts the match to one scheme (fundref, grid, isni, wikidata); None checks every scheme. ROR matches the stored spelling exactly, so an ISNI is searched in its grouped and its compact form and a Wikidata id in either case. Inactive and withdrawn records are included, because a withdrawn record can still be the target of a crosswalk.

docs.title: find_by_funder_doi(doi) async
docs.text:
Return the organizations registered under a Crossref funder DOI.

doi is a Crossref Funder Registry DOI such as 10.13039/100000001; the search uses its FundRef id.

docs.title: rorifer.OrganizationFilters
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Filter model for the /organizations route.

A sequence value ORs its items (types=["education", "nonprofit"]) and different keys AND. status is active, inactive, or withdrawn. Country codes are ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 in any case; country and continent names must match ROR's spelling exactly (The Netherlands), so prefer the codes.

docs.title: rorifer.filters.external_id_query(value, *, id_type=None)
docs.text:
Return the query.advanced clause that matches one external id.

ROR compares external_ids.all with the stored spelling and case, so the clause ORs every spelling ROR may store: the value as given, an ISNI in its grouped and its compact form, and a Wikidata id in upper case. ROR's query parser cannot search a value that contains ", \ or :, so those raise :class:ConfigurationError; pass the bare id.
