docs.title: Upstream quirks
docs.text: Findings from about 110 requests against the live ROR v2 API on 2026-11-27 and a second round on 2026-11-28 that also covered Zenodo, with the REST API documentation as the reference. Where a quirk affects rorifer, the behavior of the client is noted.

docs.title: Rejected requests return HTTP 200
docs.text:
An unknown filter key, a page above 500, malformed query.advanced syntax, and a request that carries both query and query.advanced all answer with status 200 and a body such as {"errors": ["..."]}. A client that only checks the status code reports an empty result. rorifer raises ConfigurationError with the messages of ROR whenever an envelope carries errors.

An unknown query parameter is different. It answers with status 400.

docs.title: Paging is fixed and capped
docs.text:
Pages hold exactly 20 records and the API serves pages 1 to 500. There is no page-size parameter, no cursor, no sort, and no field selection. One query therefore reaches at most 10,000 records.

ROR's documentation warns that a paged query without a filter can repeat or skip records between pages. The warning is real. A 60-record iteration of query=university of twente returned 52 distinct records on 2026-11-27. Use a dump for a complete list.

docs.title: The keyword search does not find an ISNI
docs.text:
query searches names and external ids, and it finds a FundRef id (query=100000001 returns the National Science Foundation) and a Wikidata id in upper case (query=Q1547084). It does not find an ISNI in either spelling. Both query=0000000403998953 and query=0000 0004 0399 8953 return zero records.

The exact lookup works through query.advanced with the field external_ids.all, as in external_ids.all:"0000 0004 0399 8953". The match is exact and case-sensitive: external_ids.all:"Q1547084" finds the record and external_ids.all:"q1547084" finds nothing, while the grouped ISNI finds the record and the compact spelling does not (2026-11-28). That is why rorifer searches every spelling. The fields external_ids.all.value and _everything_ are rejected as illegal field names. A clause such as external_ids.type:isni matches a record that has any id of that type, not the value next to it, so rorifer applies id_type to the returned records. names.value is different: names.value:twente and names.value:Twente answer the same records.

ROR's query parser cannot search a value that contains a double quote, a backslash, or a colon. A GRID URL fails, while the bare grid.52788.30 works.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text: The eight documented keys work as described. A repeated key means OR, and a comma between keys means AND. The pipe character does not mean OR. Repeating the whole filter parameter also means AND, but rorifer sends one parameter.

docs.title: Records and representations
docs.text:
• id is a URL (https://ror.org/006hf6230). The API accepts three forms in the path: the bare id, the URL, and ror.org/006hf6230. rorifer strips the domain from the last two.
  • A single GET returns inactive and withdrawn records. A search returns active records only, unless all_status=true is sent.
  • external_ids is a list of objects with type, all, and preferred. The dump and the API use the same schema.
  • HEAD answers with 403, so exists() sends GET.
  • Accept: application/ld+json answers with 406. The client asks for application/json.
  • query.name redirects with 302.

docs.title: Affiliation matching
docs.text: The affiliation parameter answers with items of {substring, score, matching_type, chosen, organization}. It returns up to 10 candidates and marks one as chosen.

docs.title: Data dumps
docs.text:
The dumps live in the ror-data community on Zenodo (concept record 6347574). The zip holds a JSON file with a top-level array of records in the API schema, plus a CSV file. The download URL follows the pattern /api/records/{id}/files/{key}/content and honors Range.

Three details of Zenodo matter for the dump helper (checked on 2026-11-28):

  • The search q=communities:ror-data&type=dataset answers three records without all_versions=true, because Zenodo collapses a release series into its newest version. With all_versions=true it answers every release (99 on that day). rorifer sends the parameter, so dumps.list() returns one record per release.
  • The search orders by last update, not by publication date, so the first hit is not always the newest release. GET /api/records/6347574 (the concept record) answers 302 to the newest release. rorifer reads the concept record for dumps.latest().
  • Callers without a Zenodo account get 25 records per search page. A larger size answers 400 (Page size cannot be greater than 25). The search route accepts 30 requests per minute for such callers; the 31st answers 429 with {"message": "30 per 1 minute"} and a Retry-After header. The record route accepts about 133 requests per minute. rorifer pages by 25 and paces its Zenodo requests to one every 2 seconds.

docs.title: Rate limits and health check
docs.text:
The REST API documentation gives a limit of 2,000 requests per 5 minutes per IP address, about 6.7 requests per second. The API sends no rate-limit headers. Registration for a client id is paused, and ROR enforces no client-id-based limit until it reopens (client id page). rorifer defaults to 6 requests per second.

GET https://api.ror.org/heartbeat answers the text OK with content type text/html. The route lies outside /v2. RoriferClient.heartbeat() calls it and returns True for that answer.

docs.title: scholiast
docs.text:
scholiast is not yet published on PyPI; until its first release it installs from the bibliofabric workspace.

scholiast is a Python client for the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph API, the Recommendations API, and the Datasets API, built on bibliofabric. It types papers, authors, citations, patents, snippets, recommendations, and dataset releases with Pydantic models, paces itself at 1 request per second by default, and works with or without an API key. It ships an async client and a generated sync twin with the same API.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv add scholiast

Requires Python 3.12 or newer.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: The API key is optional. Set SCHOLIAST_API_KEY (or pass api_key to ScholiastSettings) and the client sends it as the x-api-key header on every request, which moves you from the shared anonymous pool to your own 1 request per second allocation. Without a key the client runs on the shared pool, where any request can answer HTTP 429. Some fields (embedding, openAccessDoi) and some routes (dataset file listings, diffs, snippet search) need a key regardless; the API answers 400 or 401 without one.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import asyncio
from scholiast import ScholiastClient


async def main():
    async with ScholiastClient() as client:
        paper = await client.papers.get("DOI:10.1038/nature12373")
        print(paper.title, paper.year, paper.citationCount)

        page = await client.papers.search(
            query="photosynthesis", fields=["title", "year"], page_size=10
        )
        print(page.total, [paper.title for paper in page.results])

        papers = await client.papers.batch(
            ["DOI:10.1038/nature12373", "ARXIV:1304.1068"], fields=["title"]
        )
        print(len(papers))


asyncio.run(main())

client.papers exposes get(), exists(), search(), iterate(), collect(), first(), count(), batch(), bulk_search(), bulk_iterate(), citations(), references(), authors(), autocomplete(), and search_match(). client.authors exposes get(), search(), iterate(), papers(), and batch(). client.recommendations exposes for_paper() and for_list(). client.datasets exposes releases(), latest(), release(), dataset(), and diffs(). client.snippets and client.patents expose search() and get() respectively. Start with papers and authors.

docs.title: Sync usage
docs.text:
ScholiastSyncClient is generated from the async source and behaves the same. The sync client uses plain httpx.Client and never starts or touches an event loop, so it works in scripts, in Jupyter, in threads, and when called from inside a running event loop.

from scholiast import ScholiastSyncClient

with ScholiastSyncClient() as client:
    paper = client.papers.get("DOI:10.1038/nature12373")
    print(paper.title)

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text: Semantic Scholar publishes 1000 requests per second for the whole unauthenticated pool and 1 request per second for an API key. The pool is contended, so keyless callers see HTTP 429 often. The client defaults to 1 request per second and concurrency 1, which is safe in both modes. Raise SCHOLIAST_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND only if you know your key's tier. See upstream quirks for what the live API actually did on 2026-11-27.

docs.title: Links
docs.text:
• Papers
  • Authors
  • Recommendations
  • Datasets
  • Other routes (snippets, patents)
  • Upstream quirks
  • API reference

docs.title: Authors
docs.text: client.authors talks to the /author routes and returns Author models.

docs.title: Get one author
docs.text:
author = await client.authors.get("1741101", select=["name", "hIndex", "paperCount"])
found = await client.authors.exists("1741101")

Without fields the API answers with authorId only. externalIds and papers are key-gated upstream: a keyless request that asks for them answers HTTP 400.

docs.title: The author model
docs.text:
Field Content authorId The Semantic Scholar id name, aliases Names affiliations Affiliation strings homepage, url Links paperCount, citationCount, hIndex Counters externalIds Catalog ids; needs a key papers Papers linked to the author; needs a key

Fields the API adds later are kept in model_extra.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
page = await client.authors.search(
    query="adam smith", fields=["name", "affiliations"], page_size=20
)
page.total
page.results
page.next_cursor  # the next offset as a string

search(), iterate(), collect(), first(), and count() come from the resource base; paging uses offset and limit like the paper search.

docs.title: Papers of one author
docs.text:
page = await client.authors.papers(
    "1741101", fields=["title", "year", "citationCount"], limit=100
)

Returns one page of Paper records. The route serves at most the most recent 10,000 papers of an author.

docs.title: Batch
docs.text:
authors = await client.authors.batch(
    ["1741101", "1780531", "99999999"], fields=["name", "hIndex"]
)

One POST /author/batch call fetches up to 1000 authors; the client chunks longer lists. The API answers null for unknown ids and the client drops those entries. The POST is a read and is sent with retries.

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
client.datasets talks to the /datasets/v1 routes. A release is a dated snapshot of the whole Academic Graph, refreshed weekly. The old /datasets/v1/datasets route is gone; the release routes are the current API, and they use snake_case field names.

releases = await client.datasets.releases()
# ['2022-05-10', '2022-05-17', ..., '2026-11-24']

release = await client.datasets.latest()
release.release_id  # '2026-11-24'
release.datasets  # DatasetSummary entries
release.datasets[0].name  # 'abstracts'
release.datasets[0].description

release = await client.datasets.release("2026-11-24")  # or any id, or 'latest'

docs.title: One dataset with file URLs
docs.text:
dataset = await client.datasets.dataset("abstracts")
dataset.files  # temporary pre-signed download links

This route needs an API key and answers HTTP 401 without one. The client sends the request anyway and lets the API decide. Downloading the files themselves is plain HTTP against the pre-signed URLs and is not wrapped.

docs.title: Diffs between two releases
docs.text:
diffs = await client.datasets.diffs("abstracts", "2026-11-17", "2026-11-24")
diffs.diffs[0].from_release
diffs.diffs[0].update_files  # files to insert or update
diffs.diffs[0].delete_files  # files whose records to delete

Applying every diff in order brings a local copy from the start release to the end release. This route also needs an API key.

docs.title: Other routes
docs.text: Snippets and patents live on the graph base URL alongside papers and authors.

docs.title: Snippets
docs.text:
client.snippets.search() talks to /snippet/search. Snippets are excerpts of roughly 500 words drawn from a paper's title, abstract, and body text. The route needs an API key with snippet access.

result = await client.snippets.search("protein folding", fields=["text"], limit=10)
result.retrievalVersion
for match in result.data:
    match.score
    match.snippet.text
    match.snippet.snippetKind  # bodyText, title, abstract, ...
    match.snippet.annotations.sentences
    match.snippet.annotations.refMentions  # with matchedPaperCorpusId
    match.paper.title  # minimal paper record
    match.paper.openAccessInfo

The default limit is 10 and the API maximum is 1000.

docs.title: Patents
docs.text:
client.patents talks to the /patent routes.

patent = await client.patents.get("US10296086B2", fields=["title", "abstract"])
patent.ucid
patent.title

page = await client.patents.search("neural network", fields=["title"], limit=100)
page.results  # Patent records
page.next_cursor  # next offset as a string

citations = await client.patents.outbound_citations(
    "CorpusId:4314121", fields=["title"], limit=100
)
citations.citingPaperInfo  # the cited paper
citations.data  # the citing patents

get() answered keyless on 2026-11-27 with a minimal record (title, ucid). search() and outbound_citations() are in the published API spec; the study could not observe their keyless behavior because the shared pool answered 429 in that window. The Patent model declares the documented fields (applicationUcids, cpcCodes, claims, citedUcids, filingDate, publicationDate, and more) and keeps unknown fields in model_extra.

docs.title: Papers
docs.text: client.papers talks to the /paper routes and returns Paper models.

docs.title: Get one paper
docs.text:
paper = await client.papers.get("DOI:10.1038/nature12373")
paper = await client.papers.get("ARXIV:1304.1068")
paper = await client.papers.get("PMID:23903748")
paper = await client.papers.get("CorpusId:4314121")
paper = await client.papers.get("MAG:2159974629")
paper = await client.papers.get("ACL:W12-1905")
paper = await client.papers.get("649def34f8be52c8b66281af98ae884c09aef38b")  # S2 id
found = await client.papers.exists("DOI:10.1038/nature12373")

Every documented id form works in the path: a bare S2 paper id, DOI:, ARXIV:, PMID:, PMCID:, MAG:, ACL:, PubMedCentral:, CorpusId:, and URL: (percent-encode the URL value). Ids travel verbatim; the client does not rewrite them. An unknown id raises NotFoundError.

Without fields the API answers with paperId only. Select fields with select=:

paper = await client.papers.get(
    "DOI:10.1038/nature12373",
    select=["title", "year", "citationCount", "externalIds", "tldr"],
)

The API needs a key for embedding and openAccessDoi; a keyless request that asks for them answers HTTP 400.

docs.title: The paper model
docs.text:
Field Content paperId, corpusId The Semantic Scholar ids externalIds ExternalIds with DOI, ArXiv, MAG, PubMed, PubMedCentral, DBLP, ACL, Medline, and the integer CorpusId title, abstract, venue, year, publicationDate Bibliographic fields publicationVenue Normalized venue: id, name, type, alternate_names, url referenceCount, citationCount, influentialCitationCount Graph counters isOpenAccess, openAccessPdf, openAccessDoi Open-access status, the PDF (url, status, license, disclaimer), and the DOI fieldsOfStudy, s2FieldsOfStudy Field labels and S2FieldOfStudy entries (category, source) publicationTypes Such as Journal Article, Review journal name, volume, pages authors Author stubs (authorId, name) citationStyles, textAvailability Kept permissive; shape varies tldr Tldr (model, text) embedding Embedding (model, vector); needs a key matchScore Set only on a title match

Fields the API adds later are kept in model_extra.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
page = await client.papers.search(
    query="photosynthesis",
    fields=["title", "year", "citationCount"],
    page_size=10,
    page=2,
)
page.total
page.results  # up to 10 Paper records
page.next_cursor  # the next offset as a string, None on the last page

search(), iterate(), collect(), first(), and count() come from the resource base. page and page_size map to the API's offset and limit; one query reaches at most 10,000 records because the API caps offset + limit at 10,000.

Filters are their own query parameters. Pass them as a model or a mapping:

from scholiast import PaperSearchFilters

page = await client.papers.search(
    PaperSearchFilters(
        year="2020-2023",
        fieldsOfStudy="Biology",
        openAccessPdf="true",
        minCitationCount=50,
    ),
    query="photosynthesis",
)
# the same keys work as a plain mapping
page = await client.papers.search({"venue": "Nature"}, query="crispr")

docs.title: Bulk search
docs.text:
page = await client.papers.bulk_search("crispr", fields=["title", "year"], limit=1000)
page.next_cursor  # continuation token, None when done

# or let the client follow tokens
papers = [paper async for paper in client.papers.bulk_iterate("crispr", limit=5000)]

Bulk search returns up to 1000 records per call, ordered by corpus id rather than relevance. It accepts the same filters as search().

docs.title: Batch
docs.text:
papers = await client.papers.batch(
    ["DOI:10.1038/nature12373", "ARXIV:1304.1068", "DOI:10.9999/nope"],
    fields=["title", "year"],
)

One POST /paper/batch call fetches up to 500 papers; the client chunks longer lists. The API answers null for unknown ids and the client drops those entries, so the result can be shorter than the id list. The POST is a read and is sent with retries.

docs.title: Citations and references
docs.text:
citations = await client.papers.citations(
    "DOI:10.1038/nature12373",
    fields=["title", "contexts", "intents", "isInfluential"],
    limit=100,
)
for citation in citations.results:
    citation.citingPaper.title
    citation.contexts  # text snippets where the citation appears
    citation.isInfluential

references = await client.papers.references(
    "DOI:10.1038/nature12373", fields=["title", "contexts"], limit=100
)
authors = await client.papers.authors("DOI:10.1038/nature12373")

Each call returns one page as a Page; next_cursor is the next offset or None on the last page. The routes serve at most the most recent 10,000 edges per paper.

docs.title: Autocomplete and title match
docs.text:
candidates = await client.papers.autocomplete("semanti")
# candidates[i].id, .title, .authorsYear

match = await client.papers.search_match(
    "Nanometer scale thermometry in a living cell", fields=["title", "year"]
)
match.paper  # the best-matching paper
match.matchScore

search_match() raises NotFoundError when no candidate passes the relevance threshold.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text: client.recommendations talks to the /recommendations/v1 routes and returns Paper models. Both routes answer {"recommendedPapers": [...]}.

docs.title: For one paper
docs.text:
papers = await client.recommendations.for_paper(
    "DOI:10.1038/nature12373", fields=["title", "year"], limit=10
)

The id takes the same forms as a paper get (DOI:, ARXIV:, a bare S2 id, and so on). This route works without an API key.

docs.title: For a list of papers
docs.text:
papers = await client.recommendations.for_list(
    positive_paper_ids=["ARXIV:2106.15928"],
    negative_paper_ids=["DOI:10.1038/nature12373"],
    fields=["title", "year"],
    limit=10,
)

positive_paper_ids steers toward these papers and negative_paper_ids steers away; at least one id is required. The route is a read-only POST and is sent with retries. It is more restricted upstream than the single-paper route and may answer 400 on the anonymous pool.

docs.title: scholiast.ScholiastSettings
docs.text:
Bases: BaseApiSettings

Semantic Scholar client settings.

Inherits timeout, max_retries, max_retry_wait, max_requests_per_second, max_concurrency, user_agent and mailto from :class:bibliofabric.config.BaseApiSettings. The defaults pace the client at 1 request per second with concurrency 1, matching the guaranteed per-key limit of the API.

api_key is optional. When set, it travels in the x-api-key header and the caller gets its own rate allocation; without it the client runs on the shared anonymous pool, where any request may answer HTTP 429.

docs.title: Resource clients
docs.text: Each resource client inherits the generic operations from bibliofabric.ResourceClient (get, search, iterate, collect, first, count) through scholiast._async.resources.ScholiastResourceClient. Only the members that Semantic Scholar changes or adds are shown here.

docs.title: scholiast._async.papers.PapersClient
docs.text:
Bases: ScholiastResourceClient[Paper]

Client for the /paper routes.

get, search, iterate, collect, first, count, and exists come from the resource base; fields is the select argument everywhere. get accepts every id form the API documents (S2 id, DOI:, ARXIV:, PMID:, PMCID:, MAG:, ACL:, PubMedCentral:, CorpusId:, URL:).

docs.title: authors(id, *, fields=None, limit=None, offset=None) async
docs.text: Fetch one page of the authors of id.

docs.title: autocomplete(query) async
docs.text:
Return completion candidates for a partial query.

Candidates carry a minimal record (id, title, authorsYear). The API returns an empty list for no matches.

docs.title: batch(ids, *, fields=None) async
docs.text:
Fetch many papers in one or more POST /paper/batch calls.

Ids use the same forms as :meth:get. The API answers null for unknown ids; those entries are dropped. Requests chunk at 500 ids (the API maximum) and are sent with retries.

docs.title: bulk_iterate(query=None, filters=None, *, fields=None, limit=None, params=None)
docs.text: Iterate over every matching paper by following the bulk token.

docs.title: bulk_search(query=None, filters=None, *, fields=None, token=None, params=None) async
docs.text:
Fetch one page of up to 1000 papers from /paper/search/bulk.

Bulk search returns basic paper data ordered by corpus id, not by relevance, and has no limit parameter: a page holds up to 1000 records whatever the caller asks for. When more papers match, page.next_cursor carries the continuation token; pass it back as token. params adds query parameters the method does not name, such as sort (citationCount:desc or publicationDate:asc).

docs.title: citations(id, *, fields=None, limit=None, offset=None, params=None) async
docs.text:
Fetch one page of the papers citing id.

Each record carries the citing paper plus contexts, intents, contextsWithIntent, and isInfluential. page.next_cursor is the next offset, or None on the last page. params adds query parameters the method does not name, such as publicationDateOrYear (2020:2021). The papers of an author see only their most recent 10,000 citation and reference edges.

docs.title: references(id, *, fields=None, limit=None, offset=None) async
docs.text:
Fetch one page of the papers id cites.

Each record carries the cited paper plus the citation contexts of the source paper, which page.meta["citingPaperInfo"] describes.

docs.title: search(filters=None, *, query=None, sort=None, select=None, page=None, page_size=None, cursor=None, on_error='raise', failures=None, params=None, fields=None) async
docs.text:
Fetch one page of relevance-ranked papers.

fields selects the returned fields (the API's fields parameter; the same list select accepts).

docs.title: search_match(query, *, fields=None, filters=None) async
docs.text:
Return the paper whose title matches query best.

filters narrows the candidates with the same criteria :meth:search accepts. Raises :class:NotFoundError when no candidate passes the relevance threshold. matchScore sits on the returned match.

docs.title: search_path(query)
docs.text: Return paper/search; the query always travels on the search route.

docs.text:
Fetch many authors in one or more POST /author/batch calls.

The API answers null for unknown ids; those entries are dropped. Requests chunk at 1000 ids (the API maximum) and are sent with retries.

docs.title: papers(id, *, fields=None, limit=None, offset=None, params=None) async
docs.text:
Fetch one page of the papers written by author id.

The route serves at most the most recent 10,000 papers. page.next_cursor is the next offset, or None on the last page. params adds query parameters the method does not name, such as publicationDateOrYear (2020:2021).

docs.title: scholiast._async.recommendations.RecommendationsClient
docs.text:
Client for the /recommendations/v1 routes.

Both routes answer {"recommendedPapers": [...]} and work without an API key; for_list is more restricted upstream and may answer 400 on the anonymous pool.

docs.title: for_list(positive_paper_ids, negative_paper_ids=(), *, fields=None, limit=None) async
docs.text:
Return recommendations for a list of papers (POST /papers/).

positive_paper_ids steers toward these papers; negative_paper_ids steers away. Both take the same id forms as a paper get. The POST is read-only and is sent with retries.

docs.title: for_paper(id, *, fields=None, limit=None, params=None) async
docs.text:
Return papers related to id (GET /papers/forpaper/{id}).

id takes the same forms as a paper get (DOI:, ARXIV:, a bare S2 id, and so on). params adds query parameters the method does not name, such as from (recent, the default, or all-cs).

docs.title: scholiast._async.datasets.DatasetsClient
docs.text:
Client for the /datasets/v1 routes.

A release is a dated snapshot of the whole Academic Graph. Listing releases and reading a release's dataset summaries works without a key. Reading a dataset's file URLs and fetching diffs need an API key and answer HTTP 401 without one.

docs.title: dataset(name, *, release_id='latest') async
docs.text:
Return one dataset of one release, with its file URLs.

files holds temporary pre-signed download links. This route needs an API key.

docs.title: diffs(dataset_name, start_release, end_release) async
docs.text:
Return the diffs between two releases of one dataset.

Applying updateFiles and deleteFiles in order brings a local copy from start_release to end_release. This route needs an API key.

docs.title: latest() async
docs.text: Return the newest release with its dataset summaries.

docs.title: release(release_id='latest') async
docs.text:
Return one release with its dataset summaries.

release_id is a date string or latest.

docs.title: releases() async
docs.text:
Return every release id (GET /release).

The ids are date strings such as 2026-11-24, oldest first.

docs.title: scholiast._async.snippets.SnippetsClient
docs.text:
Client for the /snippet/search route.

Snippet search needs an API key with snippet access; keyless requests answered HTTP 429 on the anonymous pool on 2026-11-27 and 2026-11-28.

docs.title: search(query, *, fields=None, limit=None, params=None) async
docs.text:
Return the snippets that match query best.

Each match carries the snippet text, its annotations, a score, and a minimal paper record. fields picks parts of the snippet, such as snippet.text or snippet.annotations.sentences. The default limit is 10 and the API maximum is 1000. params adds query parameters the method does not name, such as paperIds, authors, year, or venue.

docs.title: scholiast._async.patents.PatentsClient
docs.text:
Client for the /patent routes.

All three routes answered without an API key on 2026-11-28. search and outbound_citations are paged like the paper lists.

docs.title: get(ucid, *, fields=None) async
docs.text:
Return one patent by its UCID (for example US10296086B2).

Without fields the answer holds ucid and title; ask for abstract, claims, inventors, and the other names of the Patent model for the full record. claims is served by this route only.

docs.title: outbound_citations(paper_id, *, fields=None, limit=None, offset=None) async
docs.text:
Return the patents that cite paper paper_id.

paper_id takes the paper id forms (DOI:, CorpusId:, a bare S2 id, and so on). A paper that no patent cites answers HTTP 404, which raises :class:NotFoundError. claims is not served here.

docs.title: search(query, *, fields=None, limit=None, offset=None) async
docs.text:
Search patents by plain-text query, ranked by BM25 relevance.

The answer holds ucid and title only unless fields names more. A page holds at most 100 patents, and claims is not served here: ask :meth:get for it.

docs.title: scholiast.ScholiastUnwrapper
docs.text: Extracts results, totals, and metadata from Semantic Scholar JSON.

docs.title: item(body)
docs.text: Return the record itself; single-entity routes are unwrapped.

docs.title: meta(body)
docs.text:
Return the envelope minus the result list.

Keeps offset, next, token, total, retrievalVersion and any other envelope extras the API adds.

docs.title: next_cursor(body)
docs.text:
Return the continuation for a follow-up request.

Offset-paged envelopes carry next (the next offset value); bulk search carries token. Both are returned as strings. On the last page the key is absent or null.

docs.title: results(body)
docs.text:
Return the data records (or matches), in order.

A body without either key (a single record, a plain release-id list) yields no results; those routes read the body directly.

docs.title: total(body)
docs.text:
Return total of a search envelope, or None when absent.

The published schema types total as a string, so a numeric string is read as the number it holds.

docs.title: Upstream quirks
docs.text: Findings from 67 requests against the live Semantic Scholar APIs on 2026-11-27, with the Academic Graph API reference, the product page, and the published OpenAPI documents of the graph, recommendations, and datasets services as the reference. Where a quirk affects scholiast, the behavior of the client is noted.

docs.title: Rate limits and the anonymous pool
docs.text:
The published limits are 1000 requests per second shared among all unauthenticated callers, and 1 request per second guaranteed for an API key (the introductory tier). The shared pool is contended in practice. During the study, keyless requests answered HTTP 429 at a steady 1 request per second and stayed lossy even at 3 to 5 seconds between requests, while other requests in the same window answered 200. The 429s are not proportional to pacing; the pool throttles unevenly.

scholiast therefore defaults to 1 request per second with concurrency 1, which works with and without a key. The live test suite sends at most one request per second and skips with pytest.skip("rate limited") on a 429 instead of failing, because the pool is shared and often exhausted.

docs.title: The API key on hand is inactive
docs.text: The optional API key stored in the repository .env answered HTTP 403 on 2026-11-27 in two separate checks, with the key sent as x-api-key. The key is probably no longer active. scholiast accepts any key and sends it as the x-api-key header, so the setting needs no change once a new key is issued. All live tests run without a key.

docs.title: Key-gated fields answer 400, not 401
docs.text: GET /paper/{id}?fields=openAccessDoi keyless answers HTTP 400 with {"error": "Unrecognized or unsupported fields: [openAccessDoi]"}. The same happens for embedding, and on the author routes for normalizedAffiliations and aliases (2026-11-28). The fields exist and are documented; they are only served to keys with the right access. scholiast models these fields and lets the API decide.

docs.title: Paper ids
docs.text:
• Every documented prefix answered 200 keyless on 2026-11-27: a bare S2 paper id, DOI:, ARXIV:, PMID:, MAG:, ACL:, and CorpusId:.
  • URL: needs percent-encoding of the whole value (URL:https%3A%2F%2Fdoi.org%2F...); it answered 429 in the study window, so the encoded form is implemented per the API docs but its 200 was not observed.
  • PMCID:PMC4221854 answered 404 twice even though the same paper's externalIds lists that PubMedCentral id. PubMedCentral: was not verifiable for the same reason. scholiast passes all id forms through unchanged; the API decides what it accepts.
  • Unknown ids answer HTTP 404 with {"error": "Paper with id ... not found"}, which the client maps to NotFoundError.

docs.title: Batch routes answer a bare array
docs.text:
POST /paper/batch and POST /author/batch answer a JSON array, not an envelope. Unknown ids hold the position with null. scholiast reads the array (and tolerates an envelope for safety) and drops the null entries. The fields parameter is a single-value query parameter, not part of the POST body. Both POSTs are reads and are sent with retries (retry=True).

Limits: 500 ids per paper batch call, 1000 ids per author batch call. The client chunks automatically.

docs.title: Search paging
docs.text:
• /paper/search answers {total, offset, next, data} and caps offset + limit at 10,000, so one relevance query reaches at most 10,000 records. The client sets max_offset to 9900.
  • /paper/search/bulk answers {total, token, data} and returns up to 1000 records per call (a limit above 1000 is rejected client-side). Continuation works: the opaque token was passed back and the next 1000-record page came back with a fresh token on 2026-11-27. The last page answers "token": null, which ends bulk_iterate().
  • The relevance-search route stayed at 429 through the whole study window (10 attempts, without a key), so its envelope comes from the API documentation alone. No successful answer was captured for that route.

docs.title: Field selection
docs.text: fields is a comma-joined single-value query parameter on every graph route, including the batch POSTs (where it goes into the query string). Without fields, a paper answers with paperId only (plus title and year on some routes). citationStyles and textAvailability are documented as objects; the models keep them permissive because their inner shape varies.

docs.title: Other routes
docs.text:
• GET /paper/{id}/citations and /references answer {data, next, offset}; /references also carries citingPaperInfo. The routes serve at most the most recent 10,000 citation and reference edges per paper (documented limit).
  • GET /paper/autocomplete answers {"matches": [...]} with minimal records (id, title, authorsYear), not the data key the other routes use. The unwrapper reads both.
  • GET /paper/search/match answers {"data": [record]} where the record is the paper itself with matchScore beside it.
  • GET /author/search answers {total, offset, next, data}.
  • GET /patent/{ucid} answered 200 keyless. The detail record carries claims as one text and the party names (assignees, applicants, inventors) as lists of strings (2026-11-28).
  • GET /patent/outbound-citations/{paper_id} answers {total, offset, next, data}. A paper that no patent cites answers HTTP 404, not an empty list, which the client raises as NotFoundError.
  • GET /snippet/search is documented with a 1000 max limit; keyless it stayed at 429 in the study, so the client wraps it but the payload shape comes from the spec only.
  • The recommendations routes live on their own base URL (/recommendations/v1). GET /papers/forpaper/{id} and POST /papers/ both answered 200 keyless on 2026-11-27 and answer {"recommendedPapers": [...]}.
  • The datasets routes also have their own base URL (/datasets/v1). GET /release answered a plain array of release id strings, and GET /release/latest answered {release_id, datasets: [...]} (11 datasets on 2026-11-24). The old /datasets/v1/datasets route answers 404; it is gone. GET /release/latest/dataset/abstracts answered HTTP 401 keyless, so dataset file listings and diffs need an API key. The client sends the requests anyway and lets the API decide.

docs.title: Model field names
docs.text: The datasets service uses snake_case (release_id, from_release, update_files), unlike the graph service's camelCase (paperId, openAccessPdf). The models keep the API's own names.

docs.title: seriatim: Python client for the ISSN Portal (async and sync)
docs.text:
seriatim is not yet published on PyPI; until its first release it installs from the bibliofabric workspace.

seriatim is a Python client for the ISSN Portal, built on bibliofabric. It reads ISSN and ISSN-L records as JSON-LD, wraps the free search over the Portal's HTML result page, and reads the list of Title Word Abbreviations. It ships an async client and a generated sync twin with the same API. All wrapped routes are free and need no credentials.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv add seriatim

Requires Python 3.12 or newer.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import asyncio
from seriatim import SeriatimClient


async def main():
    async with SeriatimClient() as client:
        record = await client.records.get("0028-0836")
        print(record.main_title, record.format)  # Nature. medium:Print

        cluster = await client.issn_l.get("0028-0836")
        print([(p.identifier, p.format) for p in cluster.has_part])

        page = await client.search.page("0028-0836")
        print(page.total, [hit.title for hit in page.hits])

        entry = await client.ltwa.page(search="journal")
        print(entry.entries[0])


asyncio.run(main())

The client sends Accept: application/ld+json on every request. Record models keep unknown keys, and record.raw holds the untouched JSON-LD node when the Portal publishes a field the model does not know yet.

docs.title: Sync usage
docs.text:
The generated sync twin has the same API and works without an event loop.

from seriatim import SeriatimSyncClient

with SeriatimSyncClient() as client:
    record = client.records.get("0028-0836")
    for hit in client.search.iterate("nature", limit=20):
        print(hit.issn, hit.title)

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Settings come from environment variables prefixed with SERIATIM_ or a .env file. There is no credential field; the SRU Search API and OAI-PMH need a paid subscription and are not wrapped.

Field Default Meaning timeout 30.0 Request timeout in seconds max_retries 3 Automatic retries for idempotent requests max_requests_per_second 1.0 Courtesy pace; the Portal publishes no limit max_concurrency 2 Parallel request bound user_agent, mailto None Contact information for the User-Agent

docs.title: Package pages
docs.text:
• ISSN and ISSN-L records
  • Free search
  • Title Word Abbreviations
  • Upstream quirks
  • Reference

docs.title: Title Word Abbreviations
docs.text:
The list of Title Word Abbreviations lives at https://portal.issn.org/ltwa. The page renders one HTML table per request, so client.ltwa reads that table with the standard library. This is a scrape of a public page, not a machine-readable API. The Portal's own /ltwa-export CSV route answered 502 Bad Gateway when probed on 2026-11-27 and is not wrapped.

page = await client.ltwa.page(search="journal", languages=["eng"])
for entry in page.entries:
    print(entry.word, entry.abbreviation, entry.language)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Values Notes search free text Filters by word text languages ISO 639-2 codes, for example ger, fra Repeatable page, page_size any page; 20 default The Portal serves at most 100 rows per page sort word, abbreviation Default word order asc, desc Default asc

A page_size above 100 makes the Portal answer a page with an error alert and no table; the parser returns an empty list for it.

docs.title: Rows
docs.text: Each LtwaEntry holds word, abbreviation and language. The Portal renders an empty abbreviation cell as the literal text None; the parser maps that cell to None.

docs.title: Iterating the table
docs.text:
The page carries no total, so client.ltwa.iterate(...) stops on the first page without rows. Each page costs one paced request.

async for entry in client.ltwa.iterate(sort="abbreviation"):
    print(entry.word, entry.abbreviation)

docs.title: ISSN and ISSN-L records
docs.text:
The Portal serves one JSON-LD node per record at https://portal.issn.org/resource/ISSN/{issn} and https://portal.issn.org/resource/ISSN-L/{issn}. The node arrives through content negotiation with the Accept: application/ld+json header, which the client sends on every request.

record = await client.records.get("0028-0836")

Identifiers travel in any spelling the helpers accept. The compact form 00280836 and URL forms such as https://portal.issn.org/resource/ISSN/0028-0836 normalize to 0028-0836. A value that fails the check digit raises ConfigurationError before a request leaves the process. A valid but unregistered ISSN raises NotFoundError; the Portal answers those with a 404 and a JSON error body.

docs.title: Record fields
docs.text:
SeriatimRecord models the fields the Portal publishes today. Every model allows extra keys, so new fields stay reachable as model extras, and record.raw holds the untouched node.

Field JSON key Content issn, issn_l, key_title identifiedBy Properties that read the #ISSN, #ISSN-L and #KeyTitle nodes format format medium:Print or medium:Online type type The bf:Work, bf:Instance, schema:Periodical set type_dct typeDct The DCT form-of-material code, for example formofmaterial:a main_title, name, alternate_name, title same keys Title variants; title mixes id references and language-tagged title objects identified_by identifiedBy The identifier nodes, including hasCancelledISSN lists is_part_of isPartOf Cluster memberships with ISSN-L and ISSN-H links spatial spatial Country URIs url url Access URLs has_cancelled_issn_l, has_incorrect_issn hasCancelledISSN-L, hasIncorrectISSN Related ISSN lists main_entity_of mainEntityOf Record status, modification date, ISSN centre attribution, creation activity

Cancelled records answer a much smaller node with @context, id, identifiedBy and mainEntityOf only. The flat identifier node then carries cancelledInFavorOf and the status idStatus:Cancelled; the same model covers both shapes, and record.issn works for both.

cancelled = await client.records.get("0302-2889")
print(cancelled.issn)  # 0302-2889
print(cancelled.main_entity_of.status)  # recordStatus:Cancelled

docs.title: Raw node access
docs.text:
node = await client.records.raw("0028-0836")
print(node["mainEntityOf"]["modified"])

raw returns the parsed JSON object as sent. Use it when the Portal publishes a field that the model does not carry yet.

docs.title: ISSN-L clusters
docs.text:
client.issn_l takes an ISSN value and returns the cluster node. The hasPart array lists every medium that shares the ISSN-L, print and online alike, each with its identifier and format.

cluster = await client.issn_l.get("0028-0836")
for part in cluster.has_part:
    print(part.identifier, part.format)

docs.title: The ISSN-L table
docs.text:
The ISSN Centre publishes the whole ISSN to ISSN-L mapping as a zip at /public/issnltables.zip (about 27 MB zipped and 2.6 million ISSNs on 2026-11-28). client.issn_l.download_table() streams it to a file, and two readers stream its members without unpacking the zip.

from seriatim import iter_issn_l_clusters, iter_issn_to_issn_l

path = await client.issn_l.download_table("issnltables.zip")
for link in iter_issn_to_issn_l(path):
    link.issn, link.issn_l, link.medium  # "0028-0836", "0028-0836", "ta"
for issn_l, issns in iter_issn_l_clusters(path):
    ...

iter_issn_to_issn_l() yields one IssnLink per ISSN. Its medium comes from a third column that the readme of the zip does not mention; the values are the medium codes of MARC 21 field 007, positions 00 and 01 (ta printed text, cr online resource, co optical disc). iter_issn_l_clusters() yields each ISSN-L with every ISSN that links to it, the ISSN-L included.

docs.title: Existence checks
docs.text: client.records.exists(issn) performs a GET and returns False on 404. Check-digit failures never reach the network; they raise ConfigurationError.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text: Classes, methods, and models of seriatim. All names are importable from the package top level.

docs.title: SeriatimClient
docs.text:
The async client. SeriatimSyncClient exposes the same API synchronously.

Member Kind Purpose records property RecordsClient for /resource/ISSN/{issn} issn_l property IssnLClient for /resource/ISSN-L/{issn} search property SearchClient for the HTML search ltwa property LtwaClient for the LTWA table default_headers property {"Accept": "application/ld+json"}

Constructor arguments: settings (defaults to get_settings()), base_url override for tests, and an optional caller-owned http_client.

docs.title: RecordsClient and IssnLClient
docs.text:
Both share the same shape; the model differs.

Method Returns Notes get(id) SeriatimRecord or IssnLRecord Typed model; record.raw holds the node raw(id) dict The untouched JSON-LD node exists(id) bool GET based; False on 404

IssnLClient.download_table(dest) streams the public ISSN-L table zip to dest and returns the path.

Identifiers normalize through require_issn; invalid values raise ConfigurationError without a request, unregistered values raise NotFoundError.

docs.title: SearchClient
docs.text: Method Returns Notes page(query, ...) SearchPage One page of parsed rows; see the search page for parameters iterate(query, ...) async iterator of SearchHit Walks pages; stops at limit, an empty page, or the total count(query, ...) int or None The data-hits total

docs.title: LtwaClient
docs.text: Method Returns Notes page(...) LtwaPage One table page; at most 100 rows iterate(...) async iterator of LtwaEntry Walks pages; stops on the first empty page

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
• SeriatimRecord: one ISSN record node. Properties issn, issn_l, key_title; fields for titles, identifiers, cluster membership, provenance, url, and the cancelled and incorrect ISSN lists. Extra keys stay reachable, raw holds the node.
  • IssnLRecord: one ISSN-L node with hasPart entries (HasPart: format, id, identifier) and the issn_l property.
  • SearchPage: total, page, page_size, hits.
  • SearchHit: issn, issn_l, issn_h, title, detail_path, medium, medium_label, country, country_label, category, category_label, cancelled_issns, other_media.
  • OtherMedium: label, href.
  • LtwaPage: entries, page, page_size, search, languages, sort, order.
  • LtwaEntry: word, abbreviation, language.
  • IdentifiedBy, LangString, TitleValue, IsPartOf, RecordProvenance, GenerationActivity, RecordAttribution: the nested node models of a record.

docs.title: Helpers
docs.text: Name Purpose is_valid_issn(value) Modulo 11 check digit validation require_issn(value) Normalize to the hyphenated form or raise ConfigurationError parse_issn_record(node) Validate one record node, setting raw parse_issn_l(node) Validate one ISSN-L node, setting raw record_issn(record) Normalized ISSN of a record parse_search_page(html, page=, page_size=) Parse one search result page parse_ltwa_page(html) Parse one LTWA table page SeriatimSettings, get_settings() Settings with the SERIATIM_ prefix iter_issn_to_issn_l(zip_path) Stream IssnLink(issn, issn_l, medium) rows from the ISSN-L table iter_issn_l_clusters(zip_path) Stream (issn_l, issns) pairs from the ISSN-L table

docs.title: Free search
docs.text:
The Portal search at https://portal.issn.org/search answers a server-rendered HTML page for every Accept header and format parameter; there is no machine-readable variant. client.search fetches that page and parses the result rows with the standard library, so this resource is an HTML scrape of the public search form, not an API. When the Portal changes its markup, the parser raises APIError with a body excerpt instead of returning guesses.

page = await client.search.page("0028-0836")
print(page.total)  # the data-hits value of the result list
for hit in page.hits:
    print(hit.issn, hit.medium, hit.title)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
The parameters mirror the public search form. Every criterion is optional, but at least one is required.

Parameter Values Notes query free text The search field; also matches ISSNs fuzzy flag The fuzzy search checkbox chinese_script flag The Chinese script checkbox partner_repositories kee, roa, tra Repeatable iso_country ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes Repeatable media ta (print), cr (online) Repeatable category reg (confirmed record) Repeatable page, page_size page_size 20, 30, 50, 100 Defaults 1 and 20 sort_field, sort_order search score, title, country, issn; asc, desc

Unknown values travel to the Portal untouched, and the Portal decides whether to accept them.

docs.title: Result rows
docs.text:
Each SearchHit carries what the row displays.

Field Content issn The record ISSN title The key title shown in the heading detail_path The link target under /resource, without the search session parameters issn_l, issn_h The ISSN-L and ISSN-H cluster identifiers medium, medium_label The medium code and its label, for example ta and Print country, country_label The country code and its label category, category_label The record badge, for example reg and Confirmed record cancelled_issns Cancelled ISSNs of the record other_media The sibling medium links of the cluster, each with label and href

docs.title: Paging and counting
docs.text:
client.search.iterate(...) accepts the same criteria and walks the pages one paced request at a time. It stops at limit, on an empty page, or when the data-hits total has been reached. client.search.count(...) returns the total of one request.

async for hit in client.search.iterate("nature", limit=50):
    print(hit.issn, hit.country_label)

Because iterate is an async iterator, async for consumes it directly, one paced request per page.

docs.title: Upstream quirks
docs.text: Facts verified against the live ISSN Portal with curl on 2026-11-27, in about 55 paced requests. The portal publishes no rate limit; the client defaults to one request per second.

docs.title: Record routes
docs.text:
• GET /resource/ISSN/{issn} with Accept: application/ld+json answers 200 application/ld+json. The body is one JSON-LD node, not an @graph array. ?format=json answers the same node; a .json suffix answers 400 application/json.
  • Accept: application/json, text/turtle, application/rdf+xml, and a missing Accept header answer the HTML page instead of JSON-LD.
  • The route requires the hyphenated ISSN. The compact spelling (/resource/ISSN/00280836) answers 404 with a JSON error body.
  • A value with a wrong check digit or a malformed shape answers 400 with a generic HTML error page. A value with a valid check digit that is not registered answers 404 with a JSON error body. The client validates the check digit before sending, so 400 never happens through the library.
  • Lowercase check digit x works (/resource/ISSN/2434-561x answers the same node as 2434-561X).
  • GET /resource/ISSN-L/{issn} with the JSON-LD Accept header answers one node with a hasPart array listing every medium of the cluster.
  • /resource/ISSN-H/9048-0007 answers HTML only; the ISSN-H route does not serve JSON-LD through content negotiation.
  • Full records share one key set: @context, alternateName, format, hasCancelledISSN-L, hasIncorrectISSN, id (often the empty string), identifiedBy, identifier, isPartOf, issnBibo, issnSchema, mainEntityOf, mainTitle, name, spatial, title, type, typeDct, url. Cancelled records answer only @context, id, identifiedBy, mainEntityOf.
  • Identifier nodes cluster under #ISSN, #ISSN-L and #KeyTitle keys. Key titles carry language tags of the und-Latn shape. Cancelled records answer one flat identifier node with cancelledInFavorOf instead.
  • Observed format values are medium:Print and medium:Online; typeDct was formofmaterial:a on every full record sampled, print and online alike.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
• /search answers server-rendered HTML for every probe: the Accept headers application/ld+json and application/json, format=json, format=jsonld, format=rdf, and with a python-httpx user agent.
  • The result container holds the total in data-hits; each record row is an article.search-results__record with data-issn, data-key-title, data-issnl, data-issnh, data-cancelled-issn, data-medium (ta print, cr online), data-country, and a data-category badge (reg confirmed record).
  • The form fields are search, fuzzy and chinese_script (checkboxes with the value True), partner_repositories (kee, roa, tra), iso_country, media, category, page, page_size (20, 30, 50, 100), and sort_field (search score, title, country, issn) with sort_order (asc, desc).
  • page=2 works without the search_id session parameter the page embeds in its own links.
  • The site runs Anubis bot protection. Requests with a browser-like User-Agent (tested with Mozilla/5.0) receive a proof-of-work challenge page; the library's default user agent passes.

docs.title: Title Word Abbreviations
docs.text:
• /ltwa renders the table with page, page_size, order, sort plus the form fields search and languages (ISO 639-2 codes).
  • page_size=100 answers 100 rows; page_size=500 answers a page with the generic error alert and no table. 100 is the practical cap.
  • The page carries no total row count.
  • /ltwa-export?page=1&page_size=20&order=asc&sort=word answers 502 Bad Gateway (probed twice on 2026-11-27); without parameters it answers 400. The CSV export is therefore not wrapped.

docs.title: Other services
docs.text:
• No SPARQL endpoint: /sparql answers 404 and data.issn.org did not answer.
  • ROAD (road.issn.org) is a separate Drupal site. Its record paths redirect to publishers.issn.org/resource/issn/... and answer HTML only, even with the JSON-LD Accept header.
  • /internal/search/export and /internal/browse answer 404 without a session.
  • The ISSN-L table downloads as /public/issnltables.zip (about 27 MB on 2026-11-28) from the /issnl-table page. Its ISSN-to-ISSN-L file has a third column with MARC 21 field 007 medium codes (ta, cr, ...), which the readme in the zip does not describe.
  • The menu lists the SRU Search API and OAI-PMH access as paid services. portal.issn.org/sru and portal.issn.org/oai answer 404, and oai.issn.org answers a 404 page, so no public endpoint exists without a subscription.

docs.title: Stavrophora
docs.text: Stavrophora is a Python client for the Crossref REST API, with an async variant and a generated sync twin. It is built on bibliofabric and covers the works, journals, funders, members, types, prefixes, and licenses routes with typed Pydantic models, plus the beta Data Citations API.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Requires Python 3.12 or newer.

uv add stavrophora

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import asyncio

from stavrophora import StavrophoraClient


async def main() -> None:
    async with StavrophoraClient(mailto="you@example.org") as client:
        work = await client.works.get("10.1038/nature12373")
        print(work.primary_title)

        page = await client.works.search(
            query="proteomics", select=["DOI", "title"], page_size=5
        )
        for work in page.results:
            print(work.doi, work.primary_title)


asyncio.run(main())

search() returns a Page with .results (typed models), .total, .next_cursor, and .meta (the response envelope minus the results).

docs.title: Sync usage
docs.text:
Every class has a generated sync twin: StavrophoraClient pairs with StavrophoraSyncClient, and each resource class pairs with a Sync-prefixed twin (WorksResource -> SyncWorksResource). Both variants take the same parameters, raise the same errors, retry and page the same way, and enforce the same per-class rate limits.

from stavrophora import StavrophoraSyncClient

with StavrophoraSyncClient(mailto="you@example.org") as client:
    work = client.works.get("10.1038/nature12373")
    page = client.works.search(query="proteomics", select=["DOI", "title"], page_size=5)
    for work in page.results:
        print(work.doi, work.primary_title)

The sync client uses httpx.Client, time.sleep, and threads, and never starts or touches an event loop, so it works in plain scripts, in Jupyter, and when called from inside a running event loop. See Sync usage for when to pick which variant.

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
The Crossref API needs no authentication. Two optional credentials change how requests are sent:

Credential How to set it What it does Polite pool email mailto= or STAVROPHORA_MAILTO Sent as a mailto query parameter; raises your rate limits Metadata Plus key plus_token= or STAVROPHORA_PLUS_TOKEN Sent as a crossref-api-key: Bearer <key> header

A plus_token replaces mailto as the credential when both are set. An explicit auth_strategy= argument overrides both.

When rate limits are not explicitly configured, StavrophoraClient applies pool-aware defaults (Public: 5/1 req/s, Polite: 10/3 req/s, Metadata Plus: 50/50 req/s) and tracks Crossref's x-api-pool / x-rate-limit-* response headers via client.last_pool and client.last_rate_limit_headers.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Works: search, filters, cursor iteration, batch DOI lookup, facets, sample, agency, and scoped works routes.
  • Errors, retries, rate limits.
  • Crossref quirks: behavior the client defends against.
  • API reference.

docs.title: Data citations (beta)
docs.text:
client.data_citations covers the Crossref Data Citations API at https://api.crossref.org/beta/datacitations. Each record links a citing work (subject) to a cited dataset, software, or other work (object) with a relation type such as references. Crossref marks the route as beta: its contents and output format may change.

page = await client.data_citations.search(object_id="10.3886/ICPSR01132.v1", rows=20)
page.total  # 57 on 2026-11-28
citation = page.results[0]
citation.subject.id  # DOI of the citing work
citation.subject.member  # Crossref member of the citing work
citation.object.type  # "dataset"
citation.relation  # "references"
citation.timestamp  # when Crossref added the relationship

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Every filter is optional, and the filters combine with AND.

Argument Query parameter Matches subject_id subject-id DOI of the citing work object_id object-id DOI of the cited object member_id member-id Crossref member ID of the citing work relation relation Relation type, for example references from_created_date from-created-date Added on or after this date or time until_created_date until-created-date Added on or before this date or time

The DOI filters accept a bare DOI or a https://doi.org/ URL and send the DOI in lower case. The date filters take 2025, 2025-01, 2025-01-01, 2025-01-01T12, or 2025-01-01T12:00.

docs.title: Paging
docs.text:
The route pages by a 0-based page number. search() takes page= and rows= (1 to 1000, default 20), and page.next_cursor holds the next page number as a string, or None after the last page. iterate() follows the pages with 1000 rows each, and count() reads the total with one 1-row request.

async for citation in client.data_citations.iterate(
    member_id=78, from_created_date="2026-11"
):
    ...

await client.data_citations.count(relation="references")

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text: The route runs in its own Crossref pool. On 2026-11-28 it answered x-api-pool: datacitations, x-rate-limit: 3, and x-concurrency-limit: 3 with and without mailto. The client sends these requests in the datacitations rate class at 3 requests per second for every credential type; change it through STAVROPHORA_RATE_LIMITS.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
All errors subclass bibliofabric.BibliofabricError (re-exported from stavrophora):

Exception When NotFoundError 404 response RateLimitError 429 response after retries AuthError 401 or 403 response APIError any other error status; .body holds the parsed error payload NetworkError connection failed TimeoutError request exceeded timeout ValidationError a response record failed model validation; .raw holds the payload ConfigurationError a request the API would reject with 400, raised before sending

Records that fail validation raise ValidationError during iterate(). Pass on_error="skip" with a failures list to drop them instead:

failures = []
async for work in client.works.iterate(filters, on_error="skip", failures=failures):
    ...

docs.title: Retries
docs.text:
The client retries 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504 responses, plus network failures and timeouts. A Retry-After header is honored; other failures back off with jittered exponential waits capped at max_retry_wait (60 seconds by default). 403 and 404 are never retried. max_retries defaults to 3 and is configurable through STAVROPHORA_MAX_RETRIES.

A 403 from Crossref means the account was blocked, not throttled; stop and inspect the request rather than retrying.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text:
When rate_limits, max_concurrency, and max_requests_per_second are not explicitly set on StavrophoraSettings, StavrophoraClient picks pool-aware defaults based on your credentials:

Pool Credentials rate_limits (req/s) max_concurrency Public neither mailto nor plus_token {"single": 5.0, "list": 1.0, "datacitations": 3.0} 1 Polite mailto set (no plus_token) {"single": 10.0, "list": 3.0, "datacitations": 3.0} 3 Metadata Plus plus_token set {"single": 50.0, "list": 50.0, "datacitations": 3.0} 10

Pacing follows the 2026-07 Crossref split per request class: top-level /works searches run in the list class, the beta data citations route runs in the datacitations class, and single records, scoped /.../works routes, and all other routes run in the single class. The concurrency bound is shared across classes. Override each class through STAVROPHORA_RATE_LIMITS (a JSON object such as {"single": 10.0, "list": 3.0, "datacitations": 3.0}) and the shared bound through STAVROPHORA_MAX_CONCURRENCY.

Every response is inspected by StavrophoraClient.on_response(), which captures Crossref's x-api-pool, x-rate-limit-limit, x-rate-limit-interval, and x-concurrency-limit headers into the read-only client.last_pool and client.last_rate_limit_headers properties.

On 429 the client backs off and retries automatically.

docs.title: Funders
docs.text:
client.funders covers /funders and /funders/{doi}.

from stavrophora import FunderFilters

funder = await client.funders.get("10.13039/100000001")
funder.hierarchy_names  # child funder ids and names, on single records only
funder.hierarchy  # nested child tree, on single records only

page = await client.funders.search(
    FunderFilters(location="Netherlands"), query="university"
)

location is a case-sensitive country name. The route accepts query plus filter; sort and select raise ConfigurationError client-side.

funders.works(doi) returns a works client bound to /funders/{doi}/works; see Works. The scoped route already includes descendants' works. With include_descendants=True, the funder's id plus its descendant registry ids are ORed into every request's funder filter, which pins the result set to the listed ids:

scope = client.funders.works("10.13039/100000002", include_descendants=True)
page = await scope.search(page_size=5)

The id set comes from the funder record and is fetched once per scope. Requests that carry their own funder filter raise ConfigurationError, since the two would silently AND together.

funders.descendants(doi) returns the descendant registry ids from the funder record, in Crossref's bare form ("100000025"); it returns an empty list for funders without a hierarchy:

descendants = await client.funders.descendants("10.13039/100000002")

docs.title: Journals
docs.text:
client.journals covers /journals and /journals/{issn}.

journal = await client.journals.get("20493630")  # ISSN normalized to 2049-3630
journal.primary_title  # scalar title on this route
journal.counts.total_dois

page = await client.journals.search(query="neurology", page_size=5)

The route accepts only plain query. sort, select, and filter raise ConfigurationError client-side, because the API answers 400 to them.

journals.dois_by_year(issn) returns DOI counts per issued year from the journal record's breakdowns.dois-by-issued-year, as a dict[int, int]:

counts = await client.journals.dois_by_year("20493630")  # {2026: 838, 2020: 729, ...}

journals.works(issn) returns a works client bound to /journals/{issn}/works; see Works.

docs.title: Licenses
docs.text:
client.licenses covers the /licenses list route. Crossref has no single-license route, so licenses.get() and licenses.exists() raise ConfigurationError.

page = await client.licenses.search(query="creativecommons", page_size=10)
page.results[0].url
page.results[0].work_count

licenses.iterate() pages with offset and rows (Crossref does not support cursor on /licenses).

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
client.members covers /members and /members/{id}. Member ids are plain integers.

from stavrophora import MemberFilters

member = await client.members.get(297)
member.primary_name
member.prefix  # list of {name, value} prefix entries

page = await client.members.search(MemberFilters(prefix="10.1038"))

The route accepts query plus the member filters (prefix, backfile-doi-count, current-doi-count). sort and select raise ConfigurationError client-side.

members.works(id) returns a works client bound to /members/{id}/works; see Works.

docs.title: Prefixes
docs.text:
Crossref serves no /prefixes list route, so prefixes are addressable only one at a time. prefixes.search(), count(), and iterate() raise ConfigurationError.

prefix = await client.prefixes.get("10.1038")
prefix.member  # "297"; the API returns a full URI, the model keeps the bare value
prefix.name

page = await client.prefixes.works("10.1038").search()

prefixes.works(prefix) returns a works client bound to /prefixes/{prefix}/works; see Works.

docs.title: Crossref quirks
docs.text: Behavior of the live API that shapes how the client works. Each item is verified against the live service.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
• filter=doi:a|b returns zero results. The supported OR form is repeated keys: filter=doi:a,doi:b. Batch lookups use that form.
  • Crossref has no publisher filter. Scope by prefix, member, or ror-id instead.
  • Unknown query parameters are rejected with 400, not ignored. The client sends only rows, offset, query, filter, sort, order, select, cursor, and mailto, and rejects per-route unsupported ones client-side.

docs.title: Paging
docs.text:
• There is no page parameter. Paging is offset plus rows, with offset + rows <= 10000 and rows <= 1000. search() raises ConfigurationError before sending a request past the cap.
  • Deep paging uses cursor on /works and scoped */works routes; non-works list routes (/journals, /funders, /members, /licenses) reject cursor with 400 and use offset paging instead. Cursor exhaustion is implicit: the last non-empty page still returns a next-cursor; only the following request returns empty items.
  • Cursor requests reject the issued and published* sorts with a sort-criteria-incompatible-with-cursor 400 (since 2026-08-24). Cursor result sets are no longer stable under index-date windows, so incremental sync should prefer from-created-date / until-created-date windows over from-index-date.
  • sample caps at 100 and cannot combine with rows or offset; sample() handles both.
  • The API serves both https://api.crossref.org and https://api.crossref.org/v1 with identical payloads; stavrophora pins /v1.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
• /prefixes has no list route (404); only /prefixes/{prefix} and /prefixes/{prefix}/works exist. /licenses has no single-item route (404); only the list exists.
  • /types ignores rows and offset and always returns the complete list (about 30 types).
  • /journals/{issn} returns title as a bare string while /journals returns a list; the Journal model accepts both.
  • /prefixes/{prefix} returns member and prefix as full https://id.crossref.org/member/297-style URIs; the Prefix model normalizes them to bare values.

docs.title: Response shapes
docs.text:
• Every response wraps in one message level: single items live in message, lists in message.items with totals in message.total-results. Page.meta carries the envelope minus the results, so facets and totals stay reachable.
  • The published spec is incomplete: several returned fields are absent from it. All models use extra="allow", so unknown fields survive parsing.
  • Reference entries, license entries, and funder entries vary in shape between publishers; every field is optional and tolerant types (SafeList, SafeStr, SafeInt) absorb nulls and scalar-vs-list differences.
  • event.sponsor is a string for one sponsor and a list for several (ACM GECCO proceedings print two sponsors). The Event model accepts both and always yields a list.

When rate_limits, max_concurrency, and max_requests_per_second are not explicitly set on settings, pool-aware defaults apply: Metadata Plus (50/50 req/s, concurrency 10), Polite Pool (10/3 req/s, concurrency 3), or Public Pool (5/1 req/s, concurrency 1).

class StavrophoraClient(BaseApiClient):
    """Client for the Crossref API.

    ``StavrophoraClient`` drives async code and its generated twin
    ``StavrophoraSyncClient`` drives synchronous code; both expose the same
    resources and methods.

    Credentials are resolved in the constructor: an explicit ``auth_strategy``
    wins, then a Metadata Plus key (``crossref-api-key`` header), then
    ``mailto`` (polite pool via query parameter). When ``rate_limits``,
    ``max_concurrency``, and ``max_requests_per_second`` are not explicitly
    set on ``settings``, pool-aware defaults apply: Metadata Plus
    (``50/50`` req/s, concurrency ``10``), Polite Pool (``10/3`` req/s,
    concurrency ``3``), or Public Pool (``5/1`` req/s, concurrency ``1``).
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        settings: StavrophoraSettings | None = None,
        *,
        mailto: str | None = None,
        plus_token: str | None = None,
        base_url: str | None = None,
        auth_strategy: AuthStrategy | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        resolved = settings or get_settings()
        mailto = mailto or resolved.mailto
        plus_token = plus_token or resolved.plus_token

        if plus_token:
            pool_rate_limits = _PLUS_RATE_LIMITS
            pool_concurrency = _PLUS_CONCURRENCY
        elif mailto:
            pool_rate_limits = _POLITE_RATE_LIMITS
            pool_concurrency = _POLITE_CONCURRENCY
        else:
            pool_rate_limits = _PUBLIC_RATE_LIMITS
            pool_concurrency = _PUBLIC_CONCURRENCY

        fields_set = resolved.model_fields_set
        updates: dict[str, Any] = {}
        if mailto and resolved.mailto != mailto:
            updates["mailto"] = mailto
        if (
            "rate_limits" not in fields_set
            and "max_requests_per_second" not in fields_set
        ):
            updates["rate_limits"] = dict(pool_rate_limits)
        if "max_concurrency" not in fields_set:
            updates["max_concurrency"] = pool_concurrency
        if updates:
            resolved = resolved.model_copy(update=updates)

        if auth_strategy is not None:
            auth = auth_strategy
        elif plus_token:
            auth = HeaderAuth(PLUS_TOKEN_HEADER, f"Bearer {plus_token}")
        elif mailto:
            auth = QueryParameterAuth("mailto", mailto)
        else:
            auth = NoAuth()
        super().__init__(
            base_url=base_url or CROSSREF_API_BASE_URL,
            settings=resolved,
            unwrapper=CrossrefUnwrapper(),
            auth=auth,
        )
        self._last_pool: str | None = None
        self._last_rate_limit_headers: dict[str, str] = {}

    @property
    def last_pool(self) -> str | None:
        """The ``x-api-pool`` header value from the most recent response, if any."""
        return self._last_pool

    @property
    def last_rate_limit_headers(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Crossref rate-limit headers captured from the most recent response."""
        return dict(self._last_rate_limit_headers)

    def on_response(self, response: httpx.Response) -> None:
        """Capture Crossref pool and rate-limit headers from each response."""
        captured: dict[str, str] = {}
        for header in _RATE_LIMIT_HEADERS:
            value = response.headers.get(header)
            if value is not None:
                captured[header] = value
        self._last_rate_limit_headers = captured
        self._last_pool = captured.get("x-api-pool")

    @cached_property
    def works(self) -> WorksResource:
        """The ``/works`` resource (search, iterate, batch DOI lookup, agency)."""
        return WorksResource(self)

    @cached_property
    def journals(self) -> JournalsResource:
        """The ``/journals`` resource."""
        return JournalsResource(self)

    @cached_property
    def funders(self) -> FundersResource:
        """The ``/funders`` resource."""
        return FundersResource(self)

    @cached_property
    def members(self) -> MembersResource:
        """The ``/members`` resource."""
        return MembersResource(self)

    @cached_property
    def types(self) -> TypesResource:
        """The ``/types`` resource."""
        return TypesResource(self)

    @cached_property
    def prefixes(self) -> PrefixesResource:
        """The ``/prefixes`` resource."""
        return PrefixesResource(self)

    @cached_property
    def licenses(self) -> LicensesResource:
        """The ``/licenses`` resource (list/iterate only)."""
        return LicensesResource(self)

    @cached_property
    def data_citations(self) -> DataCitationsResource:
        """The beta ``/beta/datacitations`` route (search, iterate, count)."""
        return DataCitationsResource(self)

    #: Only the top-level ``/works`` route is array-class. Everything else —
    #: single records, scoped ``/.../works`` routes, and all other routes —
    #: reports the ``polite-single`` pool in Crossref's ``x-api-pool`` header
    #: (2026-07-21 rate split; see the README and the phase 2 research). The
    #: beta data citations route reports its own ``datacitations`` pool.
    _TOP_LEVEL_WORKS = re.compile(r"^(/v1)?/works/?$")

    def rate_class(self, request: httpx.Request) -> str:
        """Map the request onto Crossref's polite pools (D-19)."""
        path = request.url.path
        if path.rstrip("/") == DATACITATIONS_PATH:
            return "datacitations"
        if self._TOP_LEVEL_WORKS.search(path):
            return "list"
        return "single"

Crossref-specific tunables.

Loaded from environment variables prefixed with STAVROPHORA_ (or a .env file): STAVROPHORA_MAILTO for the polite pool, and STAVROPHORA_PLUS_TOKEN for a Metadata Plus key. Generic behavior (timeout, retries, pacing) is inherited from :class:bibliofabric.config.BaseApiSettings.

class StavrophoraSettings(BaseApiSettings):
    """Crossref-specific tunables.

    Loaded from environment variables prefixed with ``STAVROPHORA_`` (or a
    ``.env`` file): ``STAVROPHORA_MAILTO`` for the polite pool, and
    ``STAVROPHORA_PLUS_TOKEN`` for a Metadata Plus key. Generic behavior
    (timeout, retries, pacing) is inherited from
    :class:`bibliofabric.config.BaseApiSettings`.
    """

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        env_prefix="STAVROPHORA_", env_file=".env", extra="ignore"
    )

    #: Defaults for the Crossref polite pool: top-level ``/works`` searches
    #: are the ``list`` class at 3 requests/s, the beta data citations route
    #: the ``datacitations`` class at 3 requests/s, everything else (single
    #: records, scoped ``/.../works`` routes, other routes) the ``single``
    #: class at 10 requests/s; ``max_concurrency`` is shared. When left unset,
    #: :class:`StavrophoraClient` selects pool-aware defaults for Public,
    #: Polite, or Metadata Plus credentials.
    rate_limits: dict[str, float | None] = Field(default_factory=_default_rate_limits)
    max_requests_per_second: float | None = Field(default=3.0, gt=0)
    max_concurrency: int = Field(default=3, gt=0)

    #: Contact email; sent as the ``mailto`` query parameter so requests land
    #: in the Crossref polite pool.
    mailto: str | None = None

    #: Metadata Plus key, sent as ``crossref-api-key: Bearer <token>``.
    plus_token: str | None = None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _apply_uniform_rate_limit(self) -> Self:
        """Honor an explicit ``max_requests_per_second`` when ``rate_limits`` is unset.

        Setting ``max_requests_per_second=None`` (or a single uniform rate)
        without also specifying ``rate_limits`` clears the per-class map so
        every request class falls back to ``"default"`` (unthrottled or that
        uniform rate).
        """
        if (
            "max_requests_per_second" in self.model_fields_set
            and "rate_limits" not in self.model_fields_set
        ):
            self.rate_limits = {}
        return self

class WorksResource(_WorksListResource):
    """Typed client for the Crossref ``/works`` route."""

    def item_path(self, id: str | int) -> str:
        """Return the single-work path with the DOI percent-encoded."""
        return self._resource.item_path(id)

    async def get(
        self,
        id: str | int,
        *,
        select: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> Work:
        """Fetch one work by DOI; 404 raises :class:`NotFoundError`."""
        return await self._resource.get(id, select=select, params=params)

    async def exists(self, id: str | int) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` when the DOI exists (HTTP HEAD); 404 returns ``False``."""
        return await self._resource.exists(id)

    async def agency(self, doi: str) -> WorkAgency:
        """Look up the DOI registration agency for a work."""
        response = await self._client.request("GET", f"{self.item_path(doi)}/agency")
        data = self._client.unwrapper.item(self._client.parse_json(response))
        return validate_model(
            WorkAgency, data, request=response.request, response=response
        )

    async def latest_version(
        self,
        doi: str,
        update_types: Collection[str] | None = DEFAULT_VERSION_UPDATE_TYPES,
    ) -> Work:
        """Resolve a DOI to the newest record in its Crossmark update chain.

        Older records of an update chain carry ``updated-by`` entries naming
        the works that updated them, each with a ``type`` and a timestamp or
        date parts. By default only ``("new_version", "new_edition")`` entries
        are followed so retractions and corrections are not mistaken for newer
        versions; pass ``update_types=None`` to follow all Crossmark updates.
        A DOI without matching update data is returned unchanged.
        """
        allowed = set(update_types) if update_types is not None else None
        work = await self.get(doi)
        seen = {self.normalize_id(doi)}
        if work.doi:
            seen.add(self.normalize_id(work.doi))
        while work.updated_by:
            candidates = (
                [entry for entry in work.updated_by if entry.type in allowed]
                if allowed is not None
                else work.updated_by
            )
            if not candidates:
                break
            newest = max(candidates, key=_update_timestamp)
            target = newest.doi
            if not target or self.normalize_id(target) in seen:
                break
            seen.add(self.normalize_id(target))
            work = await self.get(target)
            if work.doi:
                seen.add(self.normalize_id(work.doi))
        return work
