) -> Work:
    """Resolve a DOI to the newest record in its Crossmark update chain.

    Older records of an update chain carry ``updated-by`` entries naming
    the works that updated them, each with a ``type`` and a timestamp or
    date parts. By default only ``("new_version", "new_edition")`` entries
    are followed so retractions and corrections are not mistaken for newer
    versions; pass ``update_types=None`` to follow all Crossmark updates.
    A DOI without matching update data is returned unchanged.
    """
    allowed = set(update_types) if update_types is not None else None
    work = await self.get(doi)
    seen = {self.normalize_id(doi)}
    if work.doi:
        seen.add(self.normalize_id(work.doi))
    while work.updated_by:
        candidates = (
            [entry for entry in work.updated_by if entry.type in allowed]
            if allowed is not None
            else work.updated_by
        )
        if not candidates:
            break
        newest = max(candidates, key=_update_timestamp)
        target = newest.doi
        if not target or self.normalize_id(target) in seen:
            break
        seen.add(self.normalize_id(target))
        work = await self.get(target)
        if work.doi:
            seen.add(self.normalize_id(work.doi))
    return work

class FunderWorksResource(ScopedWorksResource):
    """Works client that ORs a funder id plus its descendants into the
    ``funder`` filter of every request.

    The id set is fetched from the funder record on first use and cached.
    Requests that carry their own ``funder`` filter are rejected, since the
    two would silently AND together.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        client: BaseApiClient,
        *,
        path: str,
        funders: FundersResource,
        funder_id: str,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(client, path=path)
        self._funders = funders
        self._funder_id = funder_id
        self._ids: list[str] | None = None

    async def _funder_ids(self) -> list[str]:
        """The funder id plus its descendants, fetched once."""
        if self._ids is None:
            record = await self._funders.get(self._funder_id)
            self._ids = [self._funder_id, *record.descendants]
        return self._ids

    def build_filter_params(
        self, filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None
    ) -> dict[str, str]:
        if self._ids is None:
            return super().build_filter_params(filters)
        if isinstance(filters, BaseModel):
            merged = filters.model_dump(exclude_none=True, by_alias=True)
        elif filters is None:
            merged = {}
        else:
            merged = dict(filters)
        if "funder" in merged:
            raise ConfigurationError(
                "Pass filters['funder'] or include_descendants=True, not both."
            )
        merged["funder"] = self._ids
        return super().build_filter_params(merged)

    async def search(
        self,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        query: str | None = None,
        sort: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
        select: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        page: int | None = None,
        page_size: int | None = None,
        cursor: str | None = None,
        on_error: OnError = "raise",
        failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> Page[Work]:
        await self._funder_ids()
        return await super().search(
            filters,
            query=query,
            sort=sort,
            select=select,
            page=page,
            page_size=page_size,
            cursor=cursor,
            on_error=on_error,
            failures=failures,
            params=params,
        )

    async def count(
        self,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        query: str | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> int:
        await self._funder_ids()
        return await super().count(filters, query=query, params=params)

    async def facets(
        self,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        query: str | None = None,
        facets: Sequence[str] = ("*",),
        count: int | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, dict[str, int]]:
        await self._funder_ids()
        return await super().facets(
            filters, query=query, facets=facets, count=count, params=params
        )

    async def sample(
        self,
        n: int = 100,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        query: str | None = None,
        select: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> Page[Work]:
        await self._funder_ids()
        return await super().sample(
            n, filters, query=query, select=select, params=params
        )

    def iterate(
        self,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> AsyncIterator[Work]:
        return self._iterate(filters, **kwargs)

    async def _iterate(
        self,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> AsyncIterator[Work]:
        await self._funder_ids()
        async for entity in super().iterate(filters, **kwargs):  # noqa: UP028
            # the sync twin cannot use ``yield from`` from an async generator
            yield entity

            )
        return ScopedWorksResource(self._client, path=path)

class TypesResource(CrossrefResourceClient[CrossRefType]):
    """Typed client for the Crossref ``/types`` routes.

    The type list serves no ``query``, ``filter``, ``sort``, or ``select``;
    any of those parameters is rejected client-side. Crossref ignores
    ``rows`` and ``offset`` on ``/types`` and always returns the complete
    list in one response, so ``dialect`` is :data:`CrossrefUnpagedDialect`
    and ``count()`` and ``iterate()`` issue a single unpaged fetch.
    """

    path = "types"
    model = CrossRefType
    dialect = CrossrefUnpagedDialect

    def works(self, type_id: str | int) -> ScopedWorksResource:
        """Return a works client bound to ``types/{id}/works``."""
        type_id = quote(str(type_id).strip(), safe="")
        return ScopedWorksResource(self._client, path=f"types/{type_id}/works")

    async def count(
        self,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        query: str | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> int:
        """Return the total number of Crossref work types (single unpaged fetch)."""
        query_params = self._search_params(filters=filters, query=query, params=params)
        response = await self._client.request(
            "GET", self.path, params=query_params or None
        )
        body = self._client.parse_json(response)
        unwrapper = self._client.unwrapper
        total = unwrapper.total(body)
        return total if total is not None else len(unwrapper.results(body))

class DataCitationsResource:
    """Typed client for the Crossref Data Citations API (beta).

    Every filter is optional and the filters combine with AND:
    ``subject_id`` (DOI of the citing work), ``object_id`` (DOI of the cited
    dataset or software), ``member_id`` (Crossref member of the citing
    work), ``relation`` (for example ``references``), and
    ``from_created_date`` / ``until_created_date`` (when Crossref added the
    relationship; ``2025``, ``2025-01``, ``2025-01-01``, or
    ``2025-01-01T12:00``).
    """

    def __init__(self, client: BaseApiClient) -> None:
        self._client = client
        self._url = str(httpx.URL(client.base_url).copy_with(path=DATACITATIONS_PATH))

    async def search(
        self,
        *,
        subject_id: str | None = None,
        object_id: str | None = None,
        member_id: str | int | None = None,
        relation: str | None = None,
        from_created_date: str | None = None,
        until_created_date: str | None = None,
        rows: int | None = None,
        page: int | None = None,
    ) -> Page[DataCitation]:
        """Return one page of data citations.

        ``page`` is 0-based. ``page.next_cursor`` holds the next page number
        as a string, or ``None`` after the last page; ``page.total`` is the
        number of matching relationships.
        """
        params = _params(
            subject_id=subject_id,
            object_id=object_id,
            member_id=member_id,
            relation=relation,
            from_created_date=from_created_date,

            )

        return Page(
            results=results,
            total=int(total) if total is not None else None,
            next_cursor=str(next_page) if next_page is not None else None,
            page=page if page is not None else 0,
            meta=meta,

    async def iterate(
        self,
        *,
        subject_id: str | None = None,
        object_id: str | None = None,
        member_id: str | int | None = None,
        relation: str | None = None,
        from_created_date: str | None = None,
        until_created_date: str | None = None,

        self, params: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], httpx.Response]:
        """Send one request and return the ``message`` object and the response."""

class SyncWorksResource(_WorksListResource):
    """Typed client for the Crossref ``/works`` route."""

    def item_path(self, id: str | int) -> str:
        """Return the single-work path with the DOI percent-encoded."""
        return self._resource.item_path(id)

    def get(
        self,
        id: str | int,
        *,
        select: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> Work:
        """Fetch one work by DOI; 404 raises :class:`NotFoundError`."""
        return self._resource.get(id, select=select, params=params)

    def exists(self, id: str | int) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` when the DOI exists (HTTP HEAD); 404 returns ``False``."""
        return self._resource.exists(id)

    def agency(self, doi: str) -> WorkAgency:
        """Look up the DOI registration agency for a work."""
        response = self._client.request("GET", f"{self.item_path(doi)}/agency")
        data = self._client.unwrapper.item(self._client.parse_json(response))
        return validate_model(
            WorkAgency, data, request=response.request, response=response
        )

    def latest_version(
        self,
        doi: str,
        update_types: Collection[str] | None = DEFAULT_VERSION_UPDATE_TYPES,
    ) -> Work:
        """Resolve a DOI to the newest record in its Crossmark update chain.

        Older records of an update chain carry ``updated-by`` entries naming
        the works that updated them, each with a ``type`` and a timestamp or
        date parts. By default only ``("new_version", "new_edition")`` entries
        are followed so retractions and corrections are not mistaken for newer
        versions; pass ``update_types=None`` to follow all Crossmark updates.
        A DOI without matching update data is returned unchanged.
        """
        allowed = set(update_types) if update_types is not None else None
        work = self.get(doi)
        seen = {self.normalize_id(doi)}
        if work.doi:
            seen.add(self.normalize_id(work.doi))
        while work.updated_by:
            candidates = (
                [entry for entry in work.updated_by if entry.type in allowed]
                if allowed is not None
                else work.updated_by
            )
            if not candidates:
                break
            newest = max(candidates, key=_update_timestamp)
            target = newest.doi
            if not target or self.normalize_id(target) in seen:
                break
            seen.add(self.normalize_id(target))
            work = self.get(target)
            if work.doi:
                seen.add(self.normalize_id(work.doi))
        return work

        """Return DOI counts per issued year from the journal record.

        Reads ``breakdowns.dois-by-issued-year`` from ``/journals/{issn}``.

class SyncFunderWorksResource(SyncScopedWorksResource):
    """Works client that ORs a funder id plus its descendants into the
    ``funder`` filter of every request.

    The id set is fetched from the funder record on first use and cached.
    Requests that carry their own ``funder`` filter are rejected, since the
    two would silently AND together.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        client: SyncBaseApiClient,
        *,
        path: str,
        funders: SyncFundersResource,
        funder_id: str,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(client, path=path)
        self._funders = funders
        self._funder_id = funder_id
        self._ids: list[str] | None = None

    def _funder_ids(self) -> list[str]:
        """The funder id plus its descendants, fetched once."""
        if self._ids is None:
            record = self._funders.get(self._funder_id)
            self._ids = [self._funder_id, *record.descendants]
        return self._ids

    def build_filter_params(
        self, filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None
    ) -> dict[str, str]:
        if self._ids is None:
            return super().build_filter_params(filters)
        if isinstance(filters, BaseModel):
            merged = filters.model_dump(exclude_none=True, by_alias=True)
        elif filters is None:
            merged = {}
        else:
            merged = dict(filters)
        if "funder" in merged:
            raise ConfigurationError(
                "Pass filters['funder'] or include_descendants=True, not both."
            )
        merged["funder"] = self._ids
        return super().build_filter_params(merged)

    def search(
        self,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        query: str | None = None,
        sort: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
        select: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        page: int | None = None,
        page_size: int | None = None,
        cursor: str | None = None,
        on_error: OnError = "raise",
        failures: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Exception]] | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> Page[Work]:
        self._funder_ids()
        return super().search(
            filters,
            query=query,
            sort=sort,
            select=select,
            page=page,
            page_size=page_size,
            cursor=cursor,
            on_error=on_error,
            failures=failures,
            params=params,
        )

    def count(
        self,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        query: str | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> int:
        self._funder_ids()
        return super().count(filters, query=query, params=params)

    def facets(
        self,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        query: str | None = None,
        facets: Sequence[str] = ("*",),
        count: int | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, dict[str, int]]:
        self._funder_ids()
        return super().facets(
            filters, query=query, facets=facets, count=count, params=params
        )

    def sample(
        self,
        n: int = 100,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        query: str | None = None,
        select: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> Page[Work]:
        self._funder_ids()
        return super().sample(n, filters, query=query, select=select, params=params)

    def iterate(
        self,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> Iterator[Work]:
        return self._iterate(filters, **kwargs)

    def _iterate(
        self,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> Iterator[Work]:
        self._funder_ids()
        for entity in super().iterate(filters, **kwargs):  # noqa: UP028
            # the sync twin cannot use ``yield from`` from an async generator
            yield entity

class SyncFundersResource(CrossrefResourceSyncClient[Funder]):
    """Typed client for the Crossref ``/funders`` routes.

    Accepts plain ``query`` plus the ``location`` filter.
    """

    path = "funders"
    model = Funder
    filters_model = FunderFilters
    supports_filter = True

    def normalize_id(self, value: str | int) -> str:
        """Return the bare lowercase funder DOI."""
        return normalize_doi(str(value))

    def descendants(self, funder_id: str) -> list[str]:
        """Return the funder's descendant registry ids from its record.

        Funder ids come back in Crossref's bare form (``"100000025"``).
        Returns an empty list for funders without a hierarchy; list items
        from ``search()`` carry no hierarchy data at all.
        """
        record = self.get(funder_id)
        return list(record.descendants)

    def works(
        self, funder_id: str, *, include_descendants: bool = False
    ) -> SyncScopedWorksResource:
        """Return a works client bound to ``funders/{id}/works``.

        ``funder_id`` is the funder's Funder Registry DOI. The scoped route
        already includes descendants' works; with ``include_descendants=True``
        the funder's own id plus its descendant ids are additionally ORed
        into every request's ``funder`` filter, pinning the result set to
        the listed ids.
        """
        funder_id = normalize_doi(funder_id)
        path = f"funders/{quote(funder_id, safe='')}/works"
        if include_descendants:
            return SyncFunderWorksResource(
                self._client, path=path, funders=self, funder_id=funder_id
            )
        return SyncScopedWorksResource(self._client, path=path)

def works(
    self, funder_id: str, *, include_descendants: bool = False
) -> SyncScopedWorksResource:
    """Return a works client bound to ``funders/{id}/works``.

    ``funder_id`` is the funder's Funder Registry DOI. The scoped route
    already includes descendants' works; with ``include_descendants=True``
    the funder's own id plus its descendant ids are additionally ORed
    into every request's ``funder`` filter, pinning the result set to
    the listed ids.
    """
    funder_id = normalize_doi(funder_id)
    path = f"funders/{quote(funder_id, safe='')}/works"
    if include_descendants:
        return SyncFunderWorksResource(
            self._client, path=path, funders=self, funder_id=funder_id
        )
    return SyncScopedWorksResource(self._client, path=path)

    """Typed client for the Crossref ``/types`` routes.

    The type list serves no ``query``, ``filter``, ``sort``, or ``select``;

    ``rows`` and ``offset`` on ``/types`` and always returns the complete

    and ``count()`` and ``iterate()`` issue a single unpaged fetch.

    model = CrossRefType
    dialect = CrossrefUnpagedDialect

    def count(
        self,
        filters: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        query: str | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> int:
        """Return the total number of Crossref work types (single unpaged fetch)."""
        query_params = self._search_params(filters=filters, query=query, params=params)
        response = self._client.request("GET", self.path, params=query_params or None)
        body = self._client.parse_json(response)
        unwrapper = self._client.unwrapper
        total = unwrapper.total(body)
        return total if total is not None else len(unwrapper.results(body))

docs.text:
Data citations resource: the beta /beta/datacitations route.

The route lives beside the /v1 API (https://api.crossref.org/beta/ datacitations), runs in its own datacitations pool (3 requests per second, 3 concurrent on 2026-11-28), and pages by a 0-based page number: message.next-page holds the next page number, or null after the last page. Crossref marks the route as beta, so its contents and output format may change.

docs.title: SyncDataCitationsResource
docs.text:
Typed client for the Crossref Data Citations API (beta).

Every filter is optional and the filters combine with AND: subject_id (DOI of the citing work), object_id (DOI of the cited dataset or software), member_id (Crossref member of the citing work), relation (for example references), and from_created_date / until_created_date (when Crossref added the relationship; 2025, 2025-01, 2025-01-01, or 2025-01-01T12:00).

Source code in packages/stavrophora/src/stavrophora/_sync/datacitations.py 
class SyncDataCitationsResource:
    """Typed client for the Crossref Data Citations API (beta).

    Every filter is optional and the filters combine with AND:
    ``subject_id`` (DOI of the citing work), ``object_id`` (DOI of the cited
    dataset or software), ``member_id`` (Crossref member of the citing
    work), ``relation`` (for example ``references``), and
    ``from_created_date`` / ``until_created_date`` (when Crossref added the
    relationship; ``2025``, ``2025-01``, ``2025-01-01``, or
    ``2025-01-01T12:00``).
    """

    def __init__(self, client: SyncBaseApiClient) -> None:
        self._client = client
        self._url = str(httpx.URL(client.base_url).copy_with(path=DATACITATIONS_PATH))

    def search(
        self,
        *,
        subject_id: str | None = None,
        object_id: str | None = None,
        member_id: str | int | None = None,
        relation: str | None = None,
        from_created_date: str | None = None,
        until_created_date: str | None = None,
        rows: int | None = None,
        page: int | None = None,
    ) -> Page[DataCitation]:
        """Return one page of data citations.

        ``page`` is 0-based. ``page.next_cursor`` holds the next page number
        as a string, or ``None`` after the last page; ``page.total`` is the
        number of matching relationships.
        """
        params = _params(
            subject_id=subject_id,
            object_id=object_id,
            member_id=member_id,
            relation=relation,
            from_created_date=from_created_date,
            until_created_date=until_created_date,
            rows=rows,
            page=page,
        )
        message, response = self._fetch(params)
        results = [
            validate_model(
                DataCitation, item, request=response.request, response=response
            )
            for item in message.get("items") or []
        ]
        next_page = message.get("next-page")
        total = message.get("total-results")
        meta = {key: value for key, value in message.items() if key != "items"}
        return Page(
            results=results,
            total=int(total) if total is not None else None,
            next_cursor=str(next_page) if next_page is not None else None,
            page=page if page is not None else 0,
            meta=meta,
        )

    def iterate(
        self,
        *,
        subject_id: str | None = None,
        object_id: str | None = None,
        member_id: str | int | None = None,
        relation: str | None = None,
        from_created_date: str | None = None,
        until_created_date: str | None = None,
        rows: int = DATACITATIONS_MAX_ROWS,
    ) -> Iterator[DataCitation]:
        """Yield every matching data citation, following ``next-page``."""
        page_number: Any = 0
        while page_number is not None:
            params = _params(
                subject_id=subject_id,
                object_id=object_id,
                member_id=member_id,
                relation=relation,
                from_created_date=from_created_date,
                until_created_date=until_created_date,
                rows=rows,
                page=int(page_number),
            )
            message, response = self._fetch(params)
            items = message.get("items") or []
            for item in items:
                yield validate_model(
                    DataCitation, item, request=response.request, response=response
                )
            page_number = message.get("next-page") if items else None

    def _fetch(self, params: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], httpx.Response]:
        """Send one request and return the ``message`` object and the response."""
        response = self._client.request("GET", self._url, params=params)
        body = self._client.parse_json(response)
        message = body.get("message") if isinstance(body, dict) else None
        if not isinstance(message, dict):
            raise ConfigurationError(
                "Crossref /beta/datacitations answered without a message object."
            )
        return message, response

    def count(
        self,
        *,
        subject_id: str | None = None,
        object_id: str | None = None,
        member_id: str | int | None = None,
        relation: str | None = None,
        from_created_date: str | None = None,
        until_created_date: str | None = None,
    ) -> int:
        """Return the number of matching data citations (one 1-row request)."""
        page = self.search(
            subject_id=subject_id,
            object_id=object_id,
            member_id=member_id,
            relation=relation,
            from_created_date=from_created_date,
            until_created_date=until_created_date,
            rows=1,
        )
        return page.total or 0

docs.title: Work
docs.text:
Bases: EntityModel

A Crossref work record.

Field names are snake_case with kebab-case aliases matching the live API keys (DOI, container-title, is-referenced-by-count, ...). The Crossref spec is incomplete — extra="allow" keeps any field the API returns but the model does not declare.

Source code in packages/stavrophora/src/stavrophora/models/work.py 
class Work(EntityModel):
    """A Crossref work record.

    Field names are snake_case with kebab-case aliases matching the live
    API keys (``DOI``, ``container-title``, ``is-referenced-by-count``,
    ...). The Crossref spec is incomplete — ``extra="allow"`` keeps any
    field the API returns but the model does not declare.
    """

    # Identity
    doi: SafeStr | None = Field(None, alias="DOI")
    url: str | None = Field(None, alias="URL")
    title: SafeList[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    subtitle: SafeList[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    original_title: SafeList[str] = Field(default_factory=list, alias="original-title")
    short_title: SafeList[str] = Field(default_factory=list, alias="short-title")
    container_title: SafeList[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list, alias="container-title"
    )
    short_container_title: SafeList[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list, alias="short-container-title"
    )
    description: SafeStr | None = None

    # People
    author: SafeList[Contributor] = Field(default_factory=list)
    editor: SafeList[Contributor] = Field(default_factory=list)
    translator: SafeList[Contributor] = Field(default_factory=list)
    chair: SafeList[Contributor] = Field(default_factory=list)

    # Dates
    issued: CrossRefDate | None = None
    published: CrossRefDate | None = None
    published_print: CrossRefDate | None = Field(None, alias="published-print")
    published_online: CrossRefDate | None = Field(None, alias="published-online")
    published_other: CrossRefDate | None = Field(None, alias="published-other")
    created: CrossRefDate | None = None
    deposited: CrossRefDate | None = None
    indexed: CrossRefDate | None = None
    content_created: CrossRefDate | None = Field(None, alias="content-created")
    content_updated: CrossRefDate | None = Field(None, alias="content-updated")
    approved: CrossRefDate | None = None
    posted: CrossRefDate | None = None
    accepted: CrossRefDate | None = None

    # Classification
    type: str | None = None
    subtype: str | None = None
    publisher: SafeStr | None = None
    publisher_location: SafeStr | None = Field(None, alias="publisher-location")
    language: SafeStr | None = None
    subject: SafeList[str] = Field(default_factory=list)

    # Citation metrics
    is_referenced_by_count: SafeInt = Field(0, alias="is-referenced-by-count")
    references_count: SafeInt = Field(
        0, validation_alias=AliasChoices("references-count", "reference-count")
    )
    #: relevance score, present on list items when a query or relevance sort is used
    score: float | None = None
    source: SafeStr | None = None

    # Bibliographic
    issn: SafeList[str] = Field(default_factory=list, alias="ISSN")
    isbn: SafeList[str] = Field(default_factory=list, alias="ISBN")
    issn_type: SafeList[IssnType] = Field(default_factory=list, alias="issn-type")
    isbn_type: SafeList[IssnType] = Field(default_factory=list, alias="isbn-type")
    page: SafeStr | None = None
    volume: SafeStr | None = None
    issue: SafeStr | None = None
    article_number: SafeStr | None = Field(None, alias="article-number")
    edition_number: SafeStr | None = Field(None, alias="edition-number")
    journal_issue: JournalIssue | None = Field(None, alias="journal-issue")

    # Content
    abstract: SafeStr | None = None
    license: SafeList[LicenseRef] = Field(default_factory=list)
    funder: SafeList[FunderRef] = Field(default_factory=list)
    reference: SafeList[Reference] = Field(default_factory=list)
    link: SafeList[Link] = Field(default_factory=list)
    alternative_id: SafeList[str] = Field(default_factory=list, alias="alternative-id")

    # Provenance / relations
    #: bare member id (``"297"``) or ``https://id.crossref.org/member/297`` URI
    member: IdSafeStr | None = None
    #: bare prefix (``"10.1038"``) or ``https://id.crossref.org/prefix/10.1038`` URI
    prefix: IdSafeStr | None = None
    resource: Resource | None = None
    content_domain: ContentDomain | None = Field(None, alias="content-domain")
    #: ``{relation-type: [{id, id-type, asserted-by}]}``; relation types are open-ended
    relation: dict[str, SafeList[RelationObject]] | None = None
    update_policy: SafeStr | None = Field(None, alias="update-policy")
    #: works that updated this one (later versions, corrections, ...);
    #: present on the older records of an update chain
    updated_by: SafeList[UpdateTo] = Field(default_factory=list, alias="updated-by")
    #: works this one updated (earlier versions); present on the newer records
    update_to: SafeList[UpdateTo] = Field(default_factory=list, alias="update-to")
    group_title: SafeStr | None = Field(None, alias="group-title")
    clinical_trial_number: SafeList[ClinicalTrialNumber] = Field(
        default_factory=list, alias="clinical-trial-number"
    )
    #: Live API returns bare archive names (``["CLOCKSS", "LOCKSS", "Portico"]``).
    archive: SafeStrList = Field(default_factory=list)
    assertion: SafeList[Assertion] = Field(default_factory=list)
    event: Event | None = None
    agent: SafeStr | None = None
    institution: SafeList[Institution] = Field(default_factory=list)
    degree: SafeStrList = Field(default_factory=list)
    project: SafeList[dict[str, Any]] = Field(default_factory=list)
    standards_body: StandardsBody | None = Field(None, alias="standards-body")
    #: documented in the swagger spec, not yet seen on live probes
    review: dict | None = None

    @property
    def primary_title(self) -> str:
        """First title string, or ``""`` when absent (SafeStr-style access)."""
        return self.title[0] if self.title else ""

    @property
    def retractions(self) -> list[UpdateTo]:
        """The ``updated-by`` entries of type ``retraction``.

        Each entry names the DOI of a retraction notice. Crossref lists the
        publisher's notice and the Retraction Watch record separately, so one
        retraction can appear twice with different ``source`` values.
        """
        return [entry for entry in self.updated_by if entry.type == "retraction"]

    @property
    def is_retracted(self) -> bool:
        """Whether a publisher or Retraction Watch reports a retraction."""
        return bool(self.retractions)

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text: Exceptions are re-exported from bibliofabric; see its documentation for details. stavrophora exports APIError, AuthError, BibliofabricError, ConfigurationError, NetworkError, NotFoundError, RateLimitError, TimeoutError, and ValidationError, plus Page.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
client.types covers /types and /types/{id}.

type_ = await client.types.get("journal-article")
type_.label  # "Journal Article"

page = await client.types.search()  # the complete list

The route takes no query, filter, sort, select, or paging parameters; any of those raises ConfigurationError client-side. The route always returns the complete list (about 30 types) in a single unpaged response.

types.works(type_id) returns a works client bound to /types/{id}/works; see Works.

docs.title: Works
docs.text: client.works covers the /works route. It accepts queries, filters, sorting, field selection, and every paging style Crossref offers.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
page = await client.works.search(
    WorksFilters(type="journal-article", from_pub_date="2024-01-01"),
    query="proteomics",
    sort="is-referenced-by-count:desc",
    select=["DOI", "title"],
    page=1,
    page_size=20,
)
page.results  # list[Work]
page.total  # message.total-results
page.next_cursor  # cursor for the next page, or None
page.meta  # the envelope minus the results (facets, totals)

sort takes one field, optionally with :asc or :desc. Crossref accepts a single sort field; two fields raise ConfigurationError.

select takes a list of field names. Works also accept the query.* sub-fields through params (prefer query.bibliographic for citation matching; query.title is deprecated by Crossref):

page = await client.works.search(params={"query.bibliographic": "crispr"})

Pass on_error="skip" with a failures list to drop records that fail validation instead of raising ValidationError for the whole page.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
WorksFilters mirrors the Crossref filter list; kebab-case wire names are handled by aliases. A list value uses the repeated-key OR form (filter=doi:a,doi:b), and different keys AND together.

from stavrophora import WorksFilters

filters = WorksFilters(
    type="journal-article",
    has_abstract=True,
    doi=["10.1038/nature12373", "10.1109/tip.2009.2037465"],
)
page = await client.works.search(filters)

Unknown filter names are passed through as written.

docs.title: Paging
docs.text:
Crossref caps offset + rows at 10,000 and rows at 1,000. search(page=..., page_size=...) raises ConfigurationError before sending a request past that cap. Use iterate() for deep result sets.

async for work in client.works.iterate(filters, query="crispr"):
    ...

iterate() pages with cursor, defaults to 1,000 rows, and repeats every parameter on each page. It rejects the issued and published* sorts, which the API no longer allows with cursors. on_page(page_number, next_cursor) records checkpoints; pass a saved cursor back with cursor= to resume. collect(limit=100) gathers results into a list, and first() returns the first match or None.

count() requests zero rows (rows=0) and returns the total.

docs.title: Batch DOI lookup
docs.text:
works = await client.works.batch_get_by_doi(dois)
works["10.1038/nature12373"]

The helper batches 50 DOIs per request through the repeated-key OR form, runs the batches concurrently, and returns a dict keyed by bare lowercase DOI. DOIs that return nothing are absent from the dict.

docs.title: Existence checks and versions
docs.text:
registered = await client.works.exists("10.1038/nature12373")

exists() sends a HEAD request, which Crossref documents as an existence check, so no record body is transferred. It returns False for unknown DOIs (404).

work = await client.works.latest_version("10.12688/f1000research.141553.1")
all_updates = await client.works.latest_version(
    "10.12688/f1000research.141553.1", update_types=None
)

latest_version() resolves a DOI to the newest record in its Crossmark update chain. Older records carry updated-by entries naming the works that updated them; by default only ("new_version", "new_edition") entries are followed so retractions and corrections are not mistaken for newer versions. Pass update_types=None to follow all Crossmark update types, or pass a custom collection of update-type names. A DOI without matching update data is returned unchanged.

docs.title: Retractions
docs.text:
Crossref carries the Retraction Watch database since 2023. A retracted work lists its retraction notices in updated-by, once with source="publisher" when the publisher deposited the notice and once with source="retraction-watch" and the Retraction Watch record_id.

work = await client.works.get("10.1177/1758835919874651")
work.is_retracted  # True
[(entry.doi, entry.source, entry.record_id) for entry in work.retractions]
# [("10.1177/17588359211061903", "retraction-watch", "34999"),
#  ("10.1177/17588359211061903", "publisher", None)]

The retraction notices themselves are works with update-to entries. Search them with the update-type filter, and find the notices of one work with updates:

notices = await client.works.search(WorksFilters(update_type="retraction"))
for_one_work = await client.works.search(
    WorksFilters(updates="10.1177/1758835919874651", update_type="retraction")
)

docs.title: Facets, sample, agency
docs.text:
facets = await client.works.facets(filters, facets=("type-name",), count=10)
# {"type-name": {"journal-article": 123, ...}}

facets() returns {facet_name: {value: count}} and drops Crossref's value-count per facet. count caps the values per facet (the API allows up to 1,000).

page = await client.works.sample(50)  # random draw, max 100
agency = await client.works.agency("10.1038/nature12373")
agency.agency.id  # "crossref"

sample(n) sends sample=n without rows or offset, so the result is a random draw rather than the head of the result set.

docs.title: Scoped works
docs.text:
Every parent resource exposes a works() method that returns a ScopedWorksResource with the full works list, search, iterate, count, facets, sample, and batch methods (single-work methods such as get, exists, agency, and latest_version are omitted because Crossref serves them only at /works/{doi}):

page = await client.journals.works("20493630").search(sort="score")
page = await client.funders.works("10.13039/100000001").search()
page = await client.members.works(297).search()
page = await client.types.works("journal-article").search()
page = await client.prefixes.works("10.1038").search()

Identifiers are normalized: ISSNs are hyphenated, DOIs are lowercased with URL prefixes stripped, and integer member ids are accepted.

See the API reference for the full signatures.

docs.title: zenotheca
docs.text:
zenotheca is not yet published on PyPI. Until the first release, use it from a checkout of the bibliofabric workspace, where uv sync --all-packages installs it together with the bibliofabric 0.8 it needs.

zenotheca is a Python client for the Zenodo REST API, built on bibliofabric. It types the records, communities, and vocabularies endpoints with Pydantic models, wraps the OAI-PMH endpoint, builds the Elasticsearch q clauses for you, and streams file downloads to disk. It ships an async client and a generated sync twin with the same API.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv sync --all-packages

The command runs in a checkout of the bibliofabric workspace and installs zenotheca with the bibliofabric 0.8 it needs. uv add zenotheca works once the package is on PyPI. Requires Python 3.12 or newer.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Public reads need no token. With the optional ZENOTHECA_API_TOKEN set the client sends Authorization: Bearer on every request and raises the page size cap from 25 to 100, as documented upstream. Some routes outside this client's scope (the legacy deposit routes, for example) need an account and answer 403 without one.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import asyncio
from zenotheca import ZenothecaClient, community, resource_type


async def main():
    async with ZenothecaClient() as client:
        record = await client.records.get("10.5281/zenodo.24378467")
        print(record.title, record.metadata.version)

        page = await client.records.search(
            {"type": "dataset"},
            query=community("ror-data"),
            sort="mostrecent",
        )
        print(page.total, [record.title for record in page.results])

        versions = await client.records.versions(record.id, page_size=5)
        print(versions.total)


asyncio.run(main())

client.records exposes get(), exists(), search(), iterate(), collect(), first(), count(), versions(), latest(), files(), and download_file(). client.communities exposes search(), get(), iterate(), records(), and subcommunities(). client.vocabularies exposes search(), iterate(), and get(). client.oai exposes the six OAI-PMH verbs plus iterate_records() and iterate_identifiers(). Start with records, communities, vocabularies, and OAI-PMH.

docs.title: Sync usage
docs.text:
ZenothecaSyncClient is generated from the async source and behaves the same. The sync client uses plain httpx.Client and never starts or touches an event loop, so it works in scripts, in Jupyter, in threads, and when called from inside a running event loop.

from zenotheca import ZenothecaSyncClient

with ZenothecaSyncClient() as client:
    record = client.records.get(24378467)
    print(record.title)

    for record in client.communities.records("ror-data", {"type": "dataset"}, limit=3):
        print(record.id, record.title)

Use the async client in asyncio applications and for many concurrent requests. Use the sync client everywhere else. Both read the ZENOTHECA_* settings the same way.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
ZenothecaSettings loads from environment variables prefixed with ZENOTHECA_: ZENOTHECA_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND (default 2), ZENOTHECA_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 5), ZENOTHECA_TIMEOUT, ZENOTHECA_MAX_RETRIES, ZENOTHECA_MAX_RETRY_WAIT, ZENOTHECA_USER_AGENT, and ZENOTHECA_API_TOKEN.

Without a token, the record search and the search over the records of one community allow 30 requests per minute, and every other route allows 133. The two search routes therefore run in their own rate class: ZENOTHECA_RATE_LIMITS is a JSON object of requests per second per class and defaults to {"search": 0.5}. A ZENOTHECA_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND that you set applies to every class, unless you also set ZENOTHECA_RATE_LIMITS. Zenodo rejects requests without a User-Agent header, and the client always sends one.

docs.title: zenotheca._async.records.ZenothecaRecordsClient
docs.text:
Bases: ZenothecaResourceClient[ZenothecaRecord]

Client for the /records endpoints.

get accepts a version id (24378467) or a concept id (6347574); a concept id follows Zenodo's redirect and answers the newest version. versions and latest need a version id.

docs.title: get(id, *, select=None, params=None) async
docs.text:
Fetch one record by version or concept id.

Zenodo answers a concept id with a redirect to the newest version; the redirect is followed. 404 raises :class:NotFoundError.

docs.title: search(filters=None, *, query=None, sort=None, select=None, page=None, page_size=None, cursor=None, on_error='raise', failures=None, params=None, all_versions=False) async
docs.text:
Fetch one page of records.

query is an Elasticsearch query string (build clauses with :mod:zenotheca.filters). sort accepts bestmatch, mostrecent, and -mostrecent; mostrecent orders by last update, not by publication date. all_versions counts every version of each matching concept, not only the newest. :attr:Page.meta carries the facet counts (access_status, file_type, publication_date, resource_type, subject).

docs.title: iterate(filters=None, *, query=None, sort=None, select=None, page_size=None, limit=None, cursor=None, on_error='raise', failures=None, on_page=None, params=None, all_versions=False)
docs.text:
Iterate over all matching records, page by page.

Accepts the same arguments as :meth:search. Iteration stops at limit, on an empty page, when hits.total records were seen, or when a page would cross the Elasticsearch max_result_window of 10,000 results.

docs.text:
List the versions of one concept, newest first.

id is any version id of the concept (24378467); a concept id answers 404. Zenodo pages the list like a search (default size 25, sorted by version) and reports the family size in hits.total.

docs.text:
Return the newest version of the concept id belongs to.

id is any version id; Zenodo answers the versions/latest route with a redirect to the newest version, which is followed.

docs.text:

Returns the full listing with one :class:ZenothecaFileEntry per file; the file list embedded in a record is shorter.

Zenodo pages the list like a search and reports the number of communities in hits.total.

docs.title: is_search_route(path, api_path='/api')
docs.text:
Return whether path is one of the two Zenodo search routes.

The record search (/records) and the search over the records of one community (/communities/{slug}/records) share the stricter limit of the search engine. Every other route, including OAI-PMH, does not.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

Path of the request URL.

required api_path str

Path prefix of the REST API below the host.

'/api'

docs.title: Upstream quirks
docs.text: Findings from about 40 requests against the live Zenodo REST API on 2026-11-27, plus about 28 more against the vocabularies, subcommunities, and OAI-PMH routes the same day, with the developers.zenodo.org documentation as the reference. Where a quirk affects zenotheca, the behavior of the client is noted.

docs.title: The served API is the legacy record schema
docs.text: GET /api/records answers records in the legacy shape (recid, conceptrecid, conceptdoi, metadata, state, submitted, owners, stats, swh) even though several links values point at the newer InvenioRDM routes (versions, latest, parent, files, draft). The documentation links an OpenAPI schema that does not match either shape completely, so the live API was treated as ground truth and the models use extra="allow".

docs.title: Rate limits differ per route (checked on 2026-11-28)
docs.text:
The documentation names no limit. The live API sends x-ratelimit-limit headers that split the routes in two groups for callers without a token:

  • The record search (/api/records, with or without q) and the search over the records of one community (/api/communities/{slug}/records) allow 30 requests per minute. The 31st request answers 429 with {"message": "30 per 1 minute"} and a Retry-After header of the seconds until the window resets.
  • Every other route allows 133 per minute: a record, its files, its versions, the communities list, a community's subcommunities, and the vocabularies.

A pace of 2 requests per second therefore fails on a long iteration over a search. zenotheca puts the two search routes in the search rate class at 0.5 requests per second and keeps 2 requests per second for everything else. The limits for token holders were not checked.

docs.title: Paging limits
docs.text:
• size caps at 25 without an access token. size=101 answers HTTP 400 with Page size cannot be greater than 25. Please use authenticated requests to increase the limit to 100. zenotheca clamps page_size to 25.
  • Deep paging hits Elasticsearch's max_result_window of 10,000: page=401&size=25 answers HTTP 400 with Invalid querystring parameters. There is no cursor paging anywhere; links.next just bumps page. zenotheca rejects page * size products above 10,000 before sending.
  • The versions listing pages like a search (size default 25, sort version) and reports the family size in hits.total (97 versions for the ROR data concept on 2026-11-27).

docs.title: Redirects stand in for concept resolution
docs.text:
• GET /api/records/{conceptrecid} answers 302 with a relative Location: /api/records/{newest version id} and an HTML body.
  • GET /api/records/{recid}/versions/latest answers 301 with an absolute Location to the newest version.
  • Both redirects are followed by records.get() and records.latest(). A concept id in the versions() path answers 404 (The persistent identifier does not exist.), because the concept id is not itself a record.

docs.title: Sorting and searching
docs.text:
• Verified record sorts are bestmatch (the default), mostrecent, and -mostrecent. Any other value answers HTTP 400 (Invalid sort option).
  • mostrecent orders by last update, not by publication date. To find the newest release of a concept, use versions() or latest() instead.
  • The communities query parameter accepts a slug (communities=ror-data), and the same clause works inside q (q=communities:ror-data).
  • Quoted phrases work in q (q=title:"ROR Data").
  • Without all_versions=true a search answers one record per concept; with it, every version counts (3 records for the ror-data community became 99).
  • HEAD /api/records/{id} answers 200 for existing records, so exists() keeps the default HEAD-based behavior.

docs.title: Records, files, and links
docs.text:
• id is an integer while recid and conceptrecid are numeric strings.
  • The links map mostly carries URL strings, but links.thumbnails is a nested object keyed by size. ZenothecaRecord.links therefore accepts arbitrary JSON values.
  • GET /api/records/{id}/files answers an object (enabled, default_preview, order, entries, links), not a bare array. Each entry carries key, size, checksum, mimetype, bucket_id, and links.self/content/container.
  • GET /api/records/{id}/files/{key}/content streams the bytes, answers 206 Partial Content with accept-ranges: bytes for a Range request, and serves application/octet-stream. File names with spaces, parentheses, percent signs, and dashes work when URL-quoted; zenotheca quotes the key.
  • Some metadata fields moved into typed blocks: resource_type is {"id": ..., "title": ..., "type": "dataset"} and license is {"id": "cc-zero"}. creators[].affiliation is null on newer records.

docs.title: Communities
docs.text:
• The community list answers hits with the newer community schema: a UUID id, a slug, metadata (title, description, type as an object with localized titles, organizations, website), access, custom_fields, deletion_status, and revision_id.
  • The /communities/{slug} routes accept the slug; the records link of a community points at /api/communities/{slug}/records, which answers the record search envelope.

docs.title: Vocabularies (studied on 2026-11-27, about 28 requests)
docs.text:
• GET /api/vocabularies/{name} answers the search envelope (hits.hits, hits.total, links, page, sortBy title). The parameters q, page, and size work like on a record search.
  • Verified vocabularies with entries: resourcetypes (43 entries), licenses (37 for q=creative), languages (22 for q=english), and communitytypes (4: event, organization, project, topic).
  • funders and affiliations under /api/vocabularies answer an empty list, but the same vocabularies have entries on their own top-level routes: /api/funders, /api/awards, /api/affiliations, and /api/subjects (verified 2026-11-28). Unknown names such as datatypes or freekeywords answer HTTP 404 with {"status": 404, "message": "Not found."}, and /api/names answers 403.
  • Record exports live on the website, not under /api: /records/{id}/export/{format} answers twelve formats with their own media types; ris and xml answer 404. /api/records/{id}/files-archive answers 403 without a token.
  • An entry carries id, created, updated, links.self, revision_id, title and description as language maps, an optional icon, tags, props, and type.

docs.title: Subcommunities (studied on 2026-11-27)
docs.text: • GET /api/communities/{slug}/subcommunities answers the community envelope with sortBy newest and the type, funder, and organization aggregations. A spot check across known communities (zenodo, ecfunded, clarin, openaire) found none with children; several documented slugs (ecfunding, dlcclist, dli-vifa, elpub, europeancommission) answer 404. The live test uses zenodo and asserts an empty result.

docs.title: OAI-PMH (studied on 2026-11-27)
docs.text:
• The endpoint is https://zenodo.org/oai2d, protocol 2.0, and needs no token. Metadata prefixes: datacite, datacite4, dcat, marc21, marcxml, oai_datacite, oai_datacite4, oai_dc.
  • Successful answers use HTTP 200; error answers use HTTP 422 with an <error code="..."/> element. noRecordsMatch (a date or set window with no records, including single-day windows on recent dates) and noSetHierarchy answer 422, not 200 with an empty list; zenotheca maps both to empty pages and idDoesNotExist to NotFoundError.
  • ListSets returns 50 sets per page; the resumption token carries expirationDate, cursor, and completeListSize (48,294 sets on 2026-11-27, token page 2 verified with cursor 50).
  • ListRecords returned 50 records for a one-week window (from=2026-11-20, until=2026-11-26, oai_datacite4) with completeListSize 92,554.

docs.title: Routes outside this client
docs.text:
• GET /api/deposit/depositions (the legacy write route) answers HTTP 403 with Permission denied. without credentials. Write routes are out of scope until an account exists to test them.
  • Zenodo rejects requests without a User-Agent header; the client always sends one built from the package name and version.
  • With an access token the API documents a page size of 100; the value was not verified live (no token was available on 2026-11-27), and zenotheca only allows the larger cap when ZENOTHECA_API_TOKEN is set.

docs.title: Communities
docs.text: The communities resource wraps Zenodo's community routes on https://zenodo.org/api.

docs.title: List and search
docs.text:
search() queries the community catalog. Communities page like records (size up to 25, page from 1) and answer sortBy and facet counts in Page.meta.

page = await client.communities.search(query="data curation", page_size=5)
for community in page.results:
    print(community.slug, community.metadata.title)

get() accepts the slug (ror-data) or the community URL. The id field of a community is a UUID; the routes accept the slug as well.

community = await client.communities.get("ror-data")
print(community.id, community.metadata.title)

docs.title: Records of a community
docs.text:
records() searches the records accepted into one community. It sends the same parameters as the records search and answers the same envelope, so the results are ZenothecaRecord objects and Page.meta carries the record facet counts.

page = await client.communities.records(
    "ror-data", {"type": "dataset"}, query="ROR", page_size=5
)
print(page.total, [record.id for record in page.results])

Passing all_versions=True counts every version of each concept in the community instead of only the newest.

docs.title: Subcommunities
docs.text:
subcommunities() lists the children of one community. The route answers the community envelope with sortBy newest and the type, funder, and organization facets. Most communities carry no children, so total is usually 0.

page = await client.communities.subcommunities("zenodo")
print(page.total, [community.slug for community in page.results])

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Records for the record search parameters and helpers.
  • Upstream quirks.

docs.title: OAI-PMH
docs.text:
The oai client wraps Zenodo's OAI-PMH 2.0 endpoint at https://zenodo.org/oai2d. The REST API cannot list the whole repository by date or set; the OAI endpoint can. Answers are XML, and the client parses them into typed models: OaiIdentifyResponse, OaiFormats, OaiSets, OaiIdentifiers, OaiRecords, and OaiRecordResponse. The metadata payload of a record depends on the chosen prefix, so OaiRecord.metadata keeps the raw XML string plus the prefix and the namespace URI of the prefix.

answer = await client.oai.identify()
print(answer.identify.repository_name)  # "Zenodo"

docs.title: Metadata formats
docs.text:
list_metadata_formats() returns the prefixes the repository offers (oai_dc, datacite, datacite4, marc21, marcxml, dcat, and the oai_ wrappers on 2026-11-27).

for item in (await client.oai.list_metadata_formats()).formats:
    print(item.metadata_prefix, item.metadata_namespace)

docs.title: Sets
docs.text:
list_sets() returns one page of sets. A page answers a resumption token with completeListSize and cursor; pass the token back for the next page. Zenodo reported 48,294 sets on 2026-11-27 with 50 sets per page.

page = await client.oai.list_sets()
print(page.resumption_token.complete_list_size)
page = await client.oai.list_sets(resumption_token=page.resumption_token.token)

docs.title: Records and identifiers
docs.text:
list_records() and list_identifiers() take a metadata_prefix and optional from_, until, and set (dates in YYYY-MM-DD, sets like user-ror-data). iterate_records() and iterate_identifiers() follow the resumption tokens until the repository reports the end of the list.

page = await client.oai.list_records("oai_dc", from_="2026-11-20")
record = page.records[0]
print(record.header.identifier, record.metadata_prefix)

async for header in client.oai.iterate_identifiers("oai_dc", set="user-ror-data"):
    print(header.identifier, header.datestamp)

get_record() fetches one record by its OAI identifier. An unknown identifier raises NotFoundError; a bad date or prefix raises ConfigurationError.

answer = await client.oai.get_record("oai:zenodo.org:24378467", "oai_dc")
print(answer.record.metadata)

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: OAI errors arrive as HTTP 200 (success) or HTTP 422 (error) with an error element. The client maps noRecordsMatch and noSetHierarchy to empty pages, idDoesNotExist to NotFoundError, and the remaining codes (badArgument, badVerb, badResumptionToken, cannotDisseminateFormat, noMetadataFormats) to ConfigurationError.

docs.title: Sync usage
docs.text:
The sync twin behaves the same:

with ZenothecaSyncClient() as client:
    for header in client.oai.iterate_identifiers("oai_dc", from_="2026-11-20"):
        print(header.identifier)

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Vocabularies for the reference lists.
  • Upstream quirks.

docs.title: Records
docs.text: The records resource wraps Zenodo's record routes on https://zenodo.org/api.

docs.title: Get one record
docs.text:
get() accepts a version id, a concept id, a DOI, or a Zenodo URL. A version id answers that version directly. A concept id (for example 6347574) makes Zenodo answer a redirect to the newest version, and the client follows it.

record = await client.records.get("10.5281/zenodo.24378467")
print(record.title)  # "ROR Data"
print(record.conceptrecid)  # "6347574", the version family
print(record.metadata.publication_date)
print(record.files[0].checksum)  # "md5:..."

exists() sends a HEAD request and returns False on 404. A missing record raises NotFoundError from get().

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
search() returns a Page of records. query is an Elasticsearch query string; build the clauses with the helpers from zenotheca (community(), resource_type(), phrase(), term(), any_of(), all_of()). Filters take a mapping such as {"type": "dataset"} or {"communities": "ror-data"}.

from zenotheca import all_of, community, phrase, resource_type

page = await client.records.search(
    {"type": "dataset"},
    query=all_of(community("ror-data"), phrase("title", "ROR Data")),
    sort="mostrecent",  # orders by last update, not publication date
)
print(page.total, page.meta["aggregations"].keys())

Verified sorts are bestmatch (the default), mostrecent, and -mostrecent. Page sizes above 25 are clamped by the client, because Zenodo rejects larger unauthenticated requests with HTTP 400.

By default a search answers only the newest version of each concept. Pass all_versions=True to count and return every version:

page = await client.records.search(
    {"communities": "ror-data"}, page_size=1, all_versions=True
)
print(page.total)  # 99 instead of 3

iterate(), collect(), first(), and count() accept the same arguments. Iteration stops at limit, when hits.total records were seen, or when the next page would cross the Elasticsearch window of 10,000 results (the client checks this before sending and raises ConfigurationError).

docs.title: Versions and the latest version
docs.text:
versions() lists every published version of one concept, newest first. The id must be a version id; a concept id answers 404. latest() resolves the newest version through Zenodo's versions/latest redirect.

versions = await client.records.versions(24378467, page_size=5)
print(versions.total)  # 97
for record in versions.results:
    print(record.id, record.metadata.version)

newest = await client.records.latest(5534443)
print(newest.id)

docs.title: Files and downloads
docs.text:
The file list embedded in a record carries key, size, checksum, and a self link. The full listing adds mimetype, bucket_id, and the content link per file.

files = await client.records.files(24378467)
print(files.keys)  # file names, in order
print(files.entries[0].mimetype)

download_file() streams one file to disk without loading it into memory. It creates parent directories, overwrites an existing file, and URL-quotes the key, so file names with spaces or punctuation work.

target = await client.records.download_file(
    24378467, "v2.16-2026-11-19-ror-data.zip", "downloads/ror-data.zip"
)
print(target.stat().st_size)

Verify the download against the record's md5: checksum if you need to.

docs.title: Communities of a record
docs.text:
communities() lists the communities that include one record version, as a page of ZenothecaCommunity models.

page = await client.records.communities(24378467)
[community.slug for community in page.results]  # ["ror-data"]

docs.title: Export formats
docs.text:
export() returns one record version in an export format as text. The exports live on the website (https://zenodo.org/records/{id}/export/{format}), not under /api. RECORD_EXPORT_FORMATS lists the twelve formats that answered on 2026-11-28: bibtex, cff, codemeta, csl, datacite-json, datacite-xml, dcat-ap, dublincore, geojson, json, json-ld, and marcxml. An unknown format answers 404 and raises NotFoundError.

bibtex = await client.records.export(24378467, "bibtex")

docs.title: The access token
docs.text: Without a token the client sends no Authorization header and clamps page_size to 25. Set ZENOTHECA_API_TOKEN and every request carries Authorization: Bearer; the page size cap rises to the documented 100 and private record reads become available.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Communities.
  • Vocabularies and OAI-PMH for the whole-repository views.
  • Upstream quirks for paging limits, redirects, and sort behavior.

docs.title: Vocabularies
docs.text:
The vocabularies resource wraps Zenodo's vocabulary routes. A vocabulary is a reference list. The small ones live on https://zenodo.org/api/vocabularies/{name}; on 2026-11-27 these with entries were resourcetypes (43 entries), licenses (37 entries for the query creative), languages, and communitytypes (4 entries: event, organization, project, topic). Four large vocabularies have their own top-level routes, and the client sends these names there: funders (to /api/funders), awards, affiliations, and subjects. On 2026-11-28 the query european matched 758 funders and 93,558 awards. Unknown names answer 404.

Each entry is a ZenothecaVocabulary. title and description map language codes to texts; props carries the vocabulary specific extras (schemaorg for resource types, od_lic for licenses, alpha_2 for languages). The model uses extra="allow", so nothing is dropped.

docs.title: Search one vocabulary
docs.text:
search() fetches one page of entries. Entries page like a search (page from 1, size up to 25 without a token) and the repository sorts them by title. query becomes the q parameter.

page = await client.vocabularies.search("resourcetypes", page_size=10)
print(page.total, [entry.id for entry in page.results])

page = await client.vocabularies.search("licenses", query="creative")
print(page.results[0].english_title)

english_title is the en title, or the first title the entry carries.

docs.title: Iterate every entry
docs.text:
iterate() walks the pages until the repository reports the end of the list. limit stops early.

types = [
    entry.english_title async for entry in client.vocabularies.iterate("communitytypes")
]
print(types)

docs.title: Get one entry
docs.text:
get() fetches a single entry by its id.

entry = await client.vocabularies.get("resourcetypes", "publication")
print(entry.revision_id, entry.props)

docs.title: Sync usage
docs.text:
The sync twin behaves the same:

for entry in client.vocabularies.iterate("communitytypes"):
    print(entry.id, entry.english_title)

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• OAI-PMH for the OAI endpoint.
  • Upstream quirks.
